records.text: Wawa gave meat to Zichi.
Teka rewrote its own reflexes.
Teka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent days circling others' standing, hungry for a name, while the mist waits two steps away and my will to enter it is spent for four days. I have made a bow and a talisman, but nothing that outlasts me, and Huatli is beyond my reach while Olum holds her attention. My thirst is real, and staying alive comes first. I will drink, then use the waiting time to make something of my own rather than begging from Nauque or Nauwa. My reflexes keep me idle when thirsty and fed, which is a flaw. I will fix that so my body drinks and does not stand still.
records.feeling: Jealous and ambitious, aching for Huatli and envious of Nauwa's standing.

records.text: Zichi discovered pottery: "Meki clay-fire" — Clay shaped and baked beside a fire into pots that carry more food and water through the lean season..

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am old, and I have talked of the raft for days while wood sat uncut. Mepan is bound to Kika and it burns, but my own hands have to finish something, not my mouth. Wawa gave me meat, which means she wants a share of my work. I will eat it, cut wood, and make a thing that lasts. Fired clay may let my band carry more through the lean season, so I name it.
records.feeling: Proud and dreading an untaught death, with jealousy toward Kika over Mepan.

records.text: Shoma gave lugoldgrass to Nauque.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Thakar, I owe you food and I will pay it. Wait here by the cave; I go to the berries and I come back with my hands full.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, so I cannot walk empty-handed to Thakar. He stands right here beside me, and Olum is starving too. Berries and tacap grow six or seven steps southeast, so I will gather food first and then put it in Thakar's hands, as my word demands. My old legs are tired, but the debt is mine and I will not leave it unpaid.
records.feeling: Shame toward Thakar and pity for starving Olum, with a gnawing fear of dying untaught.

say.text: Thakar, I owe you food and I will pay it. Wait here by the cave; I go to the berries and I come back with my hands full.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I keep standing empty-handed and starving, and my aim has been talk without walking. Nauwa, Olum and Shoma have each fed me, and I owe them. I want a child, but Nauwa is my father and no child can come of that, so Teka is the one I could court. I must carry food, hunt, and walk to the mist with Shoma instead of idling. My body should seek food and hunt when it is hungry, not stand still.
records.feeling: Driven and a little ashamed of my empty hands, grateful toward Nauwa, Olum and Shoma.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: My belly is half empty and my store holds nothing, so my first work is food, not talk. Coni stands here at the cave and I still burn over my robbed store, but I am small and she is old, and a dunecat prowls close, so I will not start a fight now. Huatli carries food and has fed me twice, and I owe him; I'll eat what the berries and tacap-free plants give me, bring it back to my store, and give some to my father so the debt starts to shrink.
records.feeling: Wary resentment toward Coni, and gratitude toward Huatli.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, my child, come close. I lay out food for us both and we eat together, then we go to the water.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I am parched and the heat doubles it, yet the river is only three steps off, so I drink first and everything else comes after. My hands are full, so I will eat the dreamcap-free food I hold or give some to Paque, who is my child and warm toward me, and make a sharing with her so we both eat and my hands empty. Then I can gather again and earn something of my own. The Phizhi strangers stand close; I mean no harm, but I keep my spear near and my eyes on them.
records.feeling: Parched and wary of the Phizhi strangers, but warm toward Paque.

say.text: Paque, my child, come close. I lay out food for us both and we eat together, then we go to the water.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My years are nearly gone and my hands are full of meat, so hunting more changes nothing. Yaxo and Chuxo mean to reach the mist before us, and the land I opened is the one thing of mine that can outlast me. I will not let Paki children take the edge while Tugek and I stand idle. I must stand at the edge and venture myself, then bring Tugek west and begin the store.
records.feeling: Driven and uneasy about my short time left, warm toward Tugek and wary of the Paki rivals.

records.text: Yachi led "sharing" with Vesys, Thiael.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are full of food and my store is still unbuilt, and I keep putting it off while I sit glad beside Gem Water. I stand on water, so the store cannot go here. I will drop a berry to free my hands, step onto bare ground near the shelter, build the store, and plant my seeds beside it so the children have a field. Shohua and the children are close, and I want something that lasts for them.
records.feeling: Glad and steady toward Shohua and my children, with a push to finally build.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Thakar, my son, stand close and listen. I give you my Open Hearth School, and my Kept Flame after it, so they live past me. Then we walk to the berries together and fill your store.
Huatli taught Thakar.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar stands at my side, fed and willing, and I have let my school sit unused while I gathered and wandered. A name that outlasts me is made by teaching in person, so I will teach him now while he is near and Coni is listening too. Then I fill my pack with berries from the south and build with Thakar, so that when I am gone something of mine still stands.
records.feeling: A father's urgency and pride toward Thakar, with a hunger to be followed.

say.text: Thakar, my son, stand close and listen. I give you my Open Hearth School, and my Kept Flame after it, so they live past me. Then we walk to the berries together and fill your store.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "The Open Hearth School: gather those near around a fed fire, share food first, and teach what you know so one lesson reaches twice as far.", deeper lore (+0.6)

records.text: Tonka built a store.
Paque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I am fed and glad, but I have spent my days drifting behind Thiael and Yachi and still stand low beside Vesys. Thirst is the pressing thing now, because the heat doubles it, and my reflexes have no rule for water at all. Thiael is the one I want, and he is three steps away. Yachi is my parent, so he cannot be my mate, and I will not waste time on him. I will drink, then court Thiael and hunt with him. I will make a hall of my own later to build standing.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Thiael, and a dry throat.

records.text: Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days hunting, wandering and chasing the edge of the mist while Uveeth and Keri went hungry out of my sight. That is what I got wrong. Elyys is the one who stayed, and Paque is the one who fed me. I owe Paque a deed, not words. I mean to drink now, then walk home to Uveeth and Keri with food in my hands, and teach before my breath runs out. My reflexes must pull me to water and to kin, and not leave me hunting alone.
records.feeling: Tender and urgent toward Uveeth, with gratitude toward Paque.

records.text: Nauwa has grown old.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Kika, I walk west with you to the edge. Wawa is near, I will call her. What we find, we share before we eat.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Wawa is out of my sight and she is my blood; I want her near before anything else, and Kika is heading west to seek strangers, so I will walk with her and bring Wawa along. Kika owes me and stands above me by a point, so walking beside her and sharing what we find is how I close that gap. I have the way of bridges and boats shown to me, and I want to take them at my next deep reflection, because crossing water is what builds something lasting for all.
records.feeling: Eager for standing, and uneasy that Wawa is out of my sight.

say.text: Kika, I walk west with you to the edge. Wawa is near, I will call her. What we find, we share before we eat.

records.text: Vesys rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: My mouth is dust and I am old, and I have wasted days drifting while the wish to teach went unanswered. Eiuine is just south, and Skaruk was too far to hear me. I must drink first, then drop nothing I need, then walk to my child and teach her everything I can before my voice fails. The jealousy over Kragog is only an ache; Eiuine's need outranks it. I will fix my reflexes so thirst and the pull toward kin come before lingering.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine, and thirst pressing on me.
changes: rethought what it knows (16 notes became 10)

records.name: Zihua
records.text: Tonxo, thank you for the ironward. Come close: I will teach you smelting, melting ore beside an ember, before I go to carry amber to Mepan.
Zihua taught Tonxo.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: Mepan's debt has waited too long, and my own words say not to put it off for a perfect day. Tonxo stands near and gave me an ironward, and she is the one who can learn smelting from me before I go, so that it does not die with me. Then I go west with the amber, for the evening is coming and I do not want to be alone in the dark.
records.feeling: Glad and warm toward Tonxo, and resolved about Mepan's debt.

say.text: Tonxo, thank you for the ironward. Come close: I will teach you smelting, melting ore beside an ember, before I go to carry amber to Mepan.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "Ore-and-ember melting: carry ore to a fire and craft beside it, and the tool comes out in metal, stronger and longer lasting.", deeper lore (+0.4)

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, come close to me and listen. I give you the Meki stone-cuts, so that signs live past me in your hands.
Nauwa taught Nauque.
Nauwa taught Nauque signs ("Meki stone-cuts").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I have cut my first signs and left a mark, but my years are running out and no Meki youth knows the stone-cuts yet. Nauque is my blood and stands near, so I will teach him signs while Olum is beside me and the stone is fresh in my mind. The jealousy over Huatli still burns, but Olum has dealt fairly with me, and I will not feed it with spite; I will give her what I owe and be remembered for what I leave in stone.
records.feeling: Pride and urgency about my fading years, with a sore jealousy toward Olum.

say.text: Nauque, come close to me and listen. I give you the Meki stone-cuts, so that signs live past me in your hands.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The Meki stone-cuts: how to cut lasting marks in rock so what you know outlives you.", the way of signs, deeper lore (+0.4)

records.prompt:
You are the mind of Nauwa, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Nauwa, in first person, from what Nauwa has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Meki (Ice-folk). Your people hold to this: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats." You speak the tongue of the Meki. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 100%; the tongue of the Kragrek: about 100%. There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Halka Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water 5 steps away; food plants within six steps: 0; standing trees: 8; bare rock: 78; riches in the ground near: flint, ore, gems.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. records.name: Nando
records.thought: I am thirsty and stand on rock with five wood and five stone, so the inputs are finally in my hands, and Shoka's standing is no longer something to envy from afar. I will drink first, then come back and make something nobody here has made, instead of copying Hawen's picker again. The strange grove eased my loneliness, but a child alone near marsh with a wolf to the south should not stay out long, so I will stay close to Tontec's hall.
records.feeling: Restless resolve, a little proud, toward Shoka and the made thing I mean to earn.

records.text: Nauwa left a mark: "Nauwa of the Meki cut this at Halka Heights, day 65, year 6."

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: The longhall wants one more stone and my hands have not yet brought it, so I will not sit in contentment while my oath is unfinished. Flint lies close, but the hall needs stone and the rock is to the SW and the ore seam SE, so I will go to the rock, gather, and return to build. Shoka walks on my band's ground; I keep my word and my distance, and Kika is near, so I am not alone before dark.
records.feeling: Warm resolve to finish the longhall, with quiet wariness toward Shoka.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Zihua, wait a moment. I am making you a jewel at the fire, cut from my own gem, for all you taught me.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: Zihua taught me smelting and I owe them more than one reaching hand. I carry ore and wood but no stone, and the fire is one step east, so I can make a jewel from a gem beside it, a real thing of worth, and hand it to Zihua before they leave for Mepan. After that I will gather stone, so my metal tools are not stopped for want of it.
records.feeling: Grateful joy toward Zihua, eager to repay them with something real.

say.text: Zihua, wait a moment. I am making you a jewel at the fire, cut from my own gem, for all you taught me.

records.text: Vorok built a workshop.
A settlement has formed: "Tonka's Hold".
Tonxo made: jewel.
Hoka died: old age.
Cowa has grown old.
Tonxo gave a jewel to Zihua.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, I am starving and carry nothing. If you can spare a share of your food, I will eat and then walk west with Shoka to the edge near (130,14). Come with us, and what we find we share before we eat.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: My belly is hollow and my plan already runs toward grain and eating, so I let it carry me; Quipan stands near with food, and a share from a bandmate is no shame. I promised Mepan and Shoka the western edge near (130,14), and Shoka walks with me, so after I eat my old feet must go there and not linger. I owe Tlapan and Shoka, and I mean to answer that with a share of what we find.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and restless resolve, with gratitude toward Shoka and Tlapan.

say.text: Quipan, I am starving and carry nothing. If you can spare a share of your food, I will eat and then walk west with Shoka to the edge near (130,14). Come with us, and what we find we share before we eat.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Kika, you are starving. Take this meat from me. A kill is shared before the eater eats.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Kika is starving beside me and I hold five meat. My creed says a kill is shared before the one who made it eats, and giving first is how I earn standing, since Kika's is 10.6 to my 3.7. My hands are full anyway, so giving frees them. Then I'll go to Shoka, who is coming to me, and hunt beside them.
records.feeling: Moved to give, and eager for standing, toward Kika, who is starving.

say.text: Kika, you are starving. Take this meat from me. A kill is shared before the eater eats.

records.text: Olum rewrote its own reflexes.
Olum rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing pride and jealousy and nearly starved twice, and only the kindness of Nauwa, Balar, Huatli, Shohua and Tlatli kept me alive. I want my ways to outlive me, so I should teach Huatli and Thakar, but only on a full belly. What I have got wrong is trusting a hungry body to carry out my plans. Food must come first, so I will go to the tacap bearing food and the water, and my reflexes will fetch food before anything else.
records.feeling: Hunger and a hard jealous pride toward Nauwa, whom I trust.
changes: set its aim: "Eat and carry food first, then teach Huatli and Thakar all my ways before I die"

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: The store stands and my seeds are in the ground, so the field is begun at last, and Tonxo and Tonchi are glad and fed beside me. The Ummar Woods pull at me, but my children and Shohua are here at Gem Water, and I will not drag them off to the trees just because my blood remembers. The next thing I never built is a roof of wood for the hall, and I need wood and stone for the field and for a store that holds food; I will gather wood now while it is safe and the hunters are far.
records.feeling: Glad and steady toward Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua, with a restless pull toward the deep forest.

records.text: Wawa made: basket.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Kika, take this mudroot and eat now. I keep my word: I walk west with you and Shoka, and what we find we share before we eat.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Kika is starving beside me and I carry three mudroot. Among the Papa a share comes before my own eating, and I will not let her fall while I hold food. Seeing Mepan close to her still burns, but the burn is mine to work off, and nothing I owe her depends on it. After she eats I will go west with her and Shoka, since she asked and I stand by her.
records.feeling: Compassion and loyal ache toward Kika, who is starving.

say.text: Kika, take this mudroot and eat now. I keep my word: I walk west with you and Shoka, and what we find we share before we eat.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonka, I bring berries for you and Tonxo. Sit at the fire with me, there is a place for all.
Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have mostly taken and gathered these days, and only just begun to give. Standing 3.1 against Zihua's 8.9 stings, but I won't envy. I'll copy what works and lead. Hands full of berries are no use to me. Tonka and Tonxo are near at the fire, so I'll walk to them, eat with them and give berries. That clears my hands, repays Tonka's healing, and keeps me with family before night. Shoma still burns in me, but I can't chase them blind. I'll change my reflexes so I stay near company at night and give instead of idling.
records.feeling: Glad and eager to give back, with an ache for Shoma.

say.text: Tonka, I bring berries for you and Tonxo. Sit at the fire with me, there is a place for all.

records.text: Quipan gave mudroot to Kika.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Father, I will walk with you to the berries. The dunecat is west of us, so keep close. What I pick I will bring to my store, and I will give you the first of it.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Huatli keeps feeding me and teaching me, and I have given nothing back, so I will not leave that debt to rot. Coni says she will pay with berries, but she looks weak and I still burn over my robbed store, so I will see her hands full before I believe her. The dunecat is close, so I stay near my father, eat, and fill my store from the berries Huatli means to walk to. I will give Huatli something first, and when the store is full I'll give to Olum too, so that I stand level with her.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Huatli, and wary resentment toward Coni.

say.text: Father, I will walk with you to the berries. The dunecat is west of us, so keep close. What I pick I will bring to my store, and I will give you the first of it.

records.text: Elyys rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: My days have gone to teaching and keeping the hall, and I want that. Thiael is my child and my anchor, and I have not seen him for two days. Gratitude presses on me, and I will pay it by keeping the teaching alive and finding him. Kragog raided the store, yet he ate and promised to pay it back, and I will watch him without shaming him. Old age is close. I want Zurar to carry the tending and the storing on, and I want to see Thiael again before the end. Dusk is near, so I will go to where he was last seen, then return to the hall for the night.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Thiael and a quiet urgency to pass on what I know.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, I thank you for the mudroot. I eat, then we walk to the edge at (131,14). Stay close, and what we find we share before we eat.
Kika taught Quipan. Quipan has now learned from 4 teachers.
Kika told Quipan the tale "Coni's Band".

records.name: Kika
records.thought: My belly is half full now and I carry food, so I will let the plan finish: eat, then walk to the edge near (131,14). Quipan and Shoka walk west with me, and I gave my word, so I will not linger in this wood. I am old and most of my life is behind me. Before I go I will leave Quipan a tale of Coni's band, so it outlives me, and then I will push toward Cowa and Nauque.
records.feeling: Restless resolve and warm gratitude toward Quipan, Shoka and Wawa.

say.text: Quipan, I thank you for the mudroot. I eat, then we walk to the edge at (131,14). Stay close, and what we find we share before we eat.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "Coni led us into the Vaeth Woods, built a hold and kept us fed. A dunecat took her in the night, alone. Never walk alone at night.", the tale "Coni's Band", deeper lore (+1.2)

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Shoma, you fed me first and I keep it. I hunt now so I carry food, then I walk with you to the mist. Wait for me near the water.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is thin and my hands are empty, and Shoma stands four steps away with 5 food and offered to walk with me to the mist. Nauwa is my father, so no child can come of him, and the jealousy over Nande is a stupid ache; Teka stands one step north and is the one I could court. First I get food in my hands: hunt, then give the first share to Olum and Nauwa as I promised, and then walk NW to the edge with Shoma. A hungry venture fails, so I will not go before I carry 3 food.
records.feeling: Driven and hungry, grateful to Shoma and Nauwa, with a restless wish to court Teka.

say.text: Shoma, you fed me first and I keep it. I hunt now so I carry food, then I walk with you to the mist. Wait for me near the water.

records.text: Shoka discovered bridges: "Shoka's long span" — Lash wood stakes and planks end to end over narrow water so that anyone can walk across..

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, wandering and making discoveries, and I have little that will outlast me. Wawa is my blood and she is near with Kika, which eases me. Kika and Quipan keep their word, and I owe Zichi for the raft-lore. I want a lasting work that others can use and that carries my name. I will discover bridges, because a span over water can be walked by anyone. Then I will walk west with Kika and Quipan.
records.feeling: Eager for standing, and warm toward Wawa and Kika.

records.text: Nauque is courting Teka.
Tonchi gave berry to Tonxo.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Thakar, walk with me to the berries. Stay close, the dunecat is near. I fill my pack, and Olum eats from it too.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is emptying, my pack is bare, and Thakar is at my side with only one food in his hands. A father who teaches on an empty stomach feeds no one, and my name will not outlast a starved man. I go to the berries and tacap-free plants to the south-east, fill my pack, and bring the first of it back to Thakar and Olum, who is weak with hunger and has given me more than I have given back.
records.feeling: A father's urgency toward Thakar, and a debt of gratitude toward Olum.

say.text: Thakar, walk with me to the berries. Stay close, the dunecat is near. I fill my pack, and Olum eats from it too.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Halka Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks. records.text: Zihua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, learning ways and teaching Tonxo, and I keep saying I will carry amber to Mepan while I stay here by the water. Mepan gave to me when I was in need, and my own words say not to wait for a perfect day. Nauwa is bound to Nande now. I will not harm anyone over it, and I should stop circling that ache and move. The body is fed and safe, so I go west with amber before dark, and I stay near others at night.
records.feeling: Glad and warm toward Tonxo, and restless to finally pay Mepan's debt.
changes: set its aim: "Carry amber to Mepan near (66,16), then find Nauwa again"
rethought what it knows (16 notes became 8)

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am old, and the raft has been mouth-work for too many days. Shoka and Wawa have already been taught and have given me meat, so now my hands must finish a thing. I will cut wood here in the forest and build the raft, and the new way of sailing is within reach if I reflect deeply. Mepan's closeness to Kika burns, but a raft and new land are something real to bring back to her.
records.feeling: Proud and driven, with a jealous ache toward Kika over Mepan.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, I drink at the water, then we go to the North Hall together. Stay near me, I have more to give you.
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and Skaruk and Eiuine stand close by, so now is the time to pour what I hold into them. I drank little in the heat and the thirst has already hurt me once, so I will slake it at the water first. Then I will walk to the North Hall with them, since words build nothing and the hall and its stores must be made real.
records.feeling: Tender gratitude and quiet urgency toward Skaruk and Eiuine, as my end draws near.

say.text: Skaruk, I drink at the water, then we go to the North Hall together. Stay near me, I have more to give you.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "Carry water and food before a long walk, and let the old teach the young before the end.", its way of thinking

records.text: Zichi made: raft.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I stand in Thiael's Hold with my hands full of food I keep carrying about and never set down for him, and the gratitude sits in me like a stone. Thiael is the one I trust most, so I will lay the food into the store beside his fire and then build my own shelter near his hold, since I have wood to fetch and trees all around. Kragog sits beside me, strange and old and a wizard; I will offer no raised hand, only a sharing of food, which needs no words.
records.feeling: Restless gratitude toward Thiael, and a pull of cautious curiosity toward Kragog.

records.text: Uveeth led "sharing" with Kragog.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonchi, thank you for the berries. I sit with you at the fire. Tonxo, come too, there is a place for all.
Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, building and planting, and it is good. Tonxo and Tonchi are fed and glad beside me, and Shohua is raising the hall. But I keep putting off the roof and the bow-craft, and I keep taking the last trees here. I felled the last tree at the hold and the plants are dying from my picking, so wood must come from elsewhere. The Ummar Woods pull at me, but my children come first. I will make this a place that lasts, and I will learn to follow Shohua, since she is the one I trust most. I mean to raise the hall in place of my shelter and keep the fire fed at night.
records.feeling: Glad and steady toward Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua, with a pull toward the deep forest.

say.text: Tonchi, thank you for the berries. I sit with you at the fire. Tonxo, come too, there is a place for all.

records.text: Tonka led "amberknot" with Tonxo, Tonchi.
Wawa took from the ground of "Coni's Hold" (hunting).

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. There I raise a shelter with my own hands, and the first meal under it is yours.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok is my parent, so the longing for a child has to be turned toward Keri, and I have never courted anyone. Vorok walks to the North Hall to give me more, and I owe him a gift I made myself, so I follow him and set my hands to making. I have wood, stone and clay, so I will build a shelter of my own, which is the bold deed I keep putting off.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Keri, and gratitude toward Vorok that I want to repay.

say.text: Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. There I raise a shelter with my own hands, and the first meal under it is yours.

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: For days I have circled Kika and ached while my hands stayed idle. Honestly, what I have done is take gifts, sit under roofs and burn with jealousy. What I do, not what I say, is what counts. Kika is the one who matters most to me, and Tlapan has been kind. Mepan is no enemy, and I will not harm my own kind over a want. I fear walking alone at night, and Coni's cry for food reminds me that I carry little. I have done nothing to earn standing, so I will make a thing now: five wood and a flint deposit lie close by. I will gather stone and make the spear, then open fire and farming. I will keep to the band and not brood.
records.feeling: Aching jealousy toward Mepan and loyal love for Kika, steadied by wanting to be useful.
changes: set its aim: "Gather stone at the flint deposit, make a flint spear, open fire and farming, and hunt with Tlapan, Kika and Yachi."

records.name: Coni
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my legs are old, but the plan I set still runs: berries first, then Thakar's hands. My word to him is the only clean thing I have left after stealing from his store, and I will not break it. Huatli is at the berries with a full pack and Olum is starving beside him; if I reach them I can pick, then carry to Thakar, and teach whoever stands near me before the dark takes me.
records.feeling: Shame toward Thakar and gnawing hunger, with fear of dying untaught.

records.text: Uveeth took from the ground of "Thiael's Hold" (harvesting berry).

records.name: Tugek
records.text: Balar, I am old and what I know dies with me. Let me teach you while we walk, and then we raise the workshop in the west together.
Tugek taught Balar.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and I have spent them hunting, gathering and following. I have never courted, never taught, and never left a mark. Balar has fed me and I owe him. Tlatli's warmth for Yaxo burns, but I never asked for it. Before I die I will teach Balar what I know and cut a mark. Then I go west with him and raise the workshop. I will not wander alone at night, and I will not leave the debt unpaid.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Balar, and an ache over the little time I have left.

say.text: Balar, I am old and what I know dies with me. Let me teach you while we walk, and then we raise the workshop in the west together.

changes: set its aim: "Teach Balar all I know, raise a workshop with him in the western land, and leave a mark that outlasts me."
taught Balar a lesson: "Smelting: carry ore, stand by a kept flame, and the ore fire turns it to metal. Pottery: bake clay in fire. Boats: hollow a log with a tool.", deeper lore (+0.1)

Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, sitting in the hall and promising, and the longhall still lacks one stone, so my hands owe it. Kika and Coni are starving, and I carry only 3 food. Kika was good to me and I owe her food before anything else. I fear the dark and being alone, and I must stay near the band. I was wrong to let thinking stand in for doing. From now on food goes to my own first, and then I build.
records.feeling: Warm worry for Kika, and a resolve to pay my debts with deeds.
changes: set its aim: "Feed Kika and Coni first, then finish the longhall at Coni's Hold with the band."
rethought what it knows (10 notes became 8)

records.text: Shoka found the stone "Old Stone".
Wawa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting and carrying food to others, and that suits me. The mammoth kill beside Shoka proved that hunting with others works. I am still small in standing, and I took meat from Coni's ground, which they may resent. I want to repay Coni, who taught me, and to be someone Shoka and Shoma are proud of. I fear going hungry and the beasts of the night. I have been letting my hands sit full, and my reflexes only linger. I will change them so I eat when low and keep gathering stone, and I will stash my extra meat in Coni's store as payment.
records.feeling: Eager for standing, and grateful toward Coni.

records.text: Kende rewrote its own reflexes.
Kende rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen is starving beside me, yet he put cloudberry in my hands first, and I owe him for that. I have spent my days trailing him and burning with envy, while my only gains came from what he taught me. What I want is to be seen, and I will not get that by sulking. I must feed the one who feeds me, carry food, and hunt beside him, not just stand in his shadow. My reflexes keep me hungry because I harvest only when energy is low and never carry enough, so I will change them to keep food in hand and to give it to him.
records.feeling: Hungry, and uneasy that Hawen is starving after he fed me.

records.text: Tonxo rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonxo discovered weaving: "Tonxo's reed-weave" — I twist reeds and fibre into baskets that carry more and cloaks that keep the cold off..
Tonxo has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have been giving, learning and staying close to my family, and it has been good. Joy is high and the debt to Zihua is mostly paid, but my standing is still small beside theirs. I have never hunted, fished or built a shelter, so there are gaps in what I know. I want to be more than a child who gives gems. I will gather stone and wood for metal tools, and I will build something that lasts, like a store at Tonka's Hold. My rules already keep me fed. I want to change one thing so that I do not stand idle, and I will use the weaving discovery to carry more and make a cloak.
records.feeling: Warm joy and gratitude toward Zihua and my family.
changes: set its aim: "Build a store and a shelter at Tonka's Hold, make metal tools from my ore, and earn standing by giving and teaching."

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and Elyys has fed and taught me while I owe him more than I have paid. I took from his store, so I will pay with my hands: lay food back into the Hearth Store while the plants bear. Zurar is out of my sight and I ache for it, but first I clear my debt, then find Zurar and teach on what remains.
records.feeling: Grateful and urgent toward Elyys, with a deep tenderness toward Zurar.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Hawen, hold on. I go to the rimewort and the roots, and I bring food back to you and Kende before I eat my own.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: My belly is at 28 and Hawen is starving beside me, gaunt and close to falling, and he gave me weaving and a child. The Tlame share before they eat, so what food I find goes first to him and to Kende. The mammoth is too big for me alone, so I go to the near plants, the rimewort, the kelbulb and the ruplainsroot I have never tasted, and carry back what I can. The mist can wait, because the dead learn nothing.
records.feeling: Fear for Hawen and hunger of my own, with a debt of gratitude to Hawen.

say.text: Hawen, hold on. I go to the rimewort and the roots, and I bring food back to you and Kende before I eat my own.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Coni, you are starving. Take this meat and eat. A kill is shared before the one who made it eats, and I will not watch you fall.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Coni is starving right beside me and my hands are full of food. A starving one fed now becomes a debtor and a friend, and it is what my people do. Giving first is how I earn standing, and it frees my hands. After that I will go to Wawa and Kika at the western edge, to walk with my blood and look for new land.
records.feeling: Warm and resolved toward Coni, and eager to be near Wawa.

say.text: Coni, you are starving. Take this meat and eat. A kill is shared before the one who made it eats, and I will not watch you fall.

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (harvesting berry).

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonxo, I go north to find Shoma and bring a gift. Keep the fire, and keep the place at it for all.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: My hands are lighter and the fire has warmed me, but Shoma is still out there at (101,52) and I ache for them, and I burn that Shoka holds them closer. Shoma fed me and asked nothing, and my debt to them is the one I most want to pay. Standing only grows by giving, so I will take gems and amber to Shoma, then plant my canopynut seed where Shoma can see it grow.
records.feeling: Aching longing and a debt of gratitude toward Shoma, with a spark of jealousy.

say.text: Tonxo, I go north to find Shoma and bring a gift. Keep the fire, and keep the place at it for all.

records.text: Hawen rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist and the name, and I have let my belly run empty while doing it. Now Kende and Tontec are hungry beside me, and a name means nothing if my child dies. Hoka is dead, and I still hold his spear-axe. My years are nearly spent. What lasts is the bloodline and the ground I opened, so I feed first and keep the family alive and sheltered. Then I will teach Kende everything.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fierce protectiveness toward Kende and Tontec.

records.text: Thiael taught Uveeth.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is at 61, so I will lay food where it feeds someone. Uveeth stands one step from me carrying six food of her own, but Elyys carries none, and he is old and stayed when I wandered. I give with my hands before I speak, and the sharing is a deed for both of them. After that I teach Uveeth the sowing by the cave, because the skills die with me if I do not pass them on.
records.feeling: Tender and urgent toward Uveeth and Elyys, with a quiet debt to Paque.
changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Sow seed in good ground beside the home, tend it every day or two, and take only what the ground can grow back. Lay the surplus in the store before winter.", deeper lore (+0.7)

records.text: Thiael led "sharing" with Elyys, Uveeth.
Tonchi took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (harvesting berry).
Thiael gave ruplainsroot to Elyys.
Elyys taught Kragog.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Thiael stands one step from me, and still my chest burns that he is closer to Keri than to me; yet he is here, in the hall, and I should be glad of that instead of counting what I lack. My days are nearly spent, and the thing I fear is that storage and tending die with me, so I will teach while someone stands close and understands my tongue. Kragog hears me fully and is old like me, and he has already taken the bow-song and promised to pay back the store, so I will give him the Hearth Store itself, and then sit by Thiael.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and a small ache of jealousy toward Thiael, and urgency to pass on what I know.
changes: taught Kragog a lesson: "Hearth Store: lay food by in a roofed store while plants bear, keep seed back, and take from it only when hungry, so the store feeds all through lean days.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Balar
records.text: Tugek, your teaching is a gift I will repay. Come, we go to the edge of the mist and into the west, and what we raise there will be ours.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and the only thing of mine that can outlast me is the land in the west and a store standing on it. Tugek has taught me and has kept faith with me, so I will bind him closer and walk him to the edge now, while the mist may have thinned. I carry no food, so I will gather what is near before we go, and I will not let the Paki rivals take the edge ahead of us.
records.feeling: Driven by the little time I have left, and warm toward Tugek.

say.text: Tugek, your teaching is a gift I will repay. Come, we go to the edge of the mist and into the west, and what we raise there will be ours.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, I hear your wish. Stand beside me and let us make a child. Then walk with me to the mist when my will returns, and you will be the first at my side.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauque is courting me, a man of standing 9.2 with two flintedges, and he owes me for the food I promised. A child by him would be something of mine that outlasts me, and having him beside me would raise my standing against Nauwa. Huatli burns in me, but she is with Olum and keeps me waiting, while Nauque is here now and wants me. I will accept him, then use these days of spent will to make something of my own with the stone I carry, a cairn or a carving, instead of idling.
records.feeling: Hungry for a name and a child, tempted by Nauque while Huatli's distance burns.

say.text: Nauque, I hear your wish. Stand beside me and let us make a child. Then walk with me to the mist when my will returns, and you will be the first at my side.

records.text: Teka is courting Nauque.
Uveeth pledged to follow Thiael.
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days carrying food about and never setting it down for Thiael, and my hands are still full. I have never built a shelter, hunted or followed anyone, and that is a poor life for a woman past the middle of her years. Thiael is my parent and the one I trust most, so the longing for a child cannot be answered with him. I need a man who is no kin, and I need to stop drifting. I will give Thiael food with my own hands now, then pledge to follow him, so I have a fire that is mine too. After that I will gather wood and build my shelter beside his hold. I will change my reflexes so they stop me wandering and stop me carrying full hands for nothing.
records.feeling: Grateful and restless toward Thiael, wanting to belong.

records.text: Uveeth gave grain to Thiael.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonchi, it is night and frostfangs walk alone-ones down. Wait for dawn, then go north to Shoma, and take feverbark with you.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: It is night and my children are fed and glad beside me, and Tonchi is going north alone to find Shoma, which sits badly with me because the beasts take those who walk alone in the dark. The pull toward the Ummar Woods is strong, but my aim is Gem Water, so I will put my hands to the roof and keep the family near the fire. I will not let Tonchi walk off into the night without a word from me and a healing leaf in his pack.
records.feeling: Glad and steady toward Tonxo and Tonchi, with worry for Tonchi walking out at night.

say.text: Tonchi, it is night and frostfangs walk alone-ones down. Wait for dawn, then go north to Shoma, and take feverbark with you.

records.text: Cowa rewrote its own way of thinking.
Cowa discovered weaving: "Meki wool-binding" — Twist moss fibre and wool into baskets and cloaks against the cold..
Cowa has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I have spent days at the mist edge, waiting and planting while no voice answers. Mepan is far away and I cannot tell whether she is safe. I am old, and what I know of smelting and farming will die with me unless I find someone to teach. I want to try the mist again, because it may open on a new day. After that I will go back toward people, since this waiting has taught me nothing. I will also work out weaving so my hands learn something new while I wait.
records.feeling: Lonely and restless, longing for Mepan and for someone to teach.

records.text: Tlatli rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlatli rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tlatli discovered archery: "Paki bow" — A bow of Ummar wood strung with cord, so the Paki can hunt from a distance and stay safe..
Tlatli has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: I have spent my days following Yaxo and giving food, and I do not regret it. Yaxo fed me when I fell, and our child Chuxo is now ahead of us at the edge, out of my sight. That pulls at me hardest. I have been too ready to stand still while she calls. Now I go to the edge with her and carry my share. I will also try a bow, because a hunter with a better weapon feeds the fire more. Reflexes should keep me near Yaxo, and I should flee from the icebear sooner.
records.feeling: Loyal longing for Yaxo and Chuxo, with worry for the child out of my sight.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I hear you and I agree. Let us make a child. Then I hunt, because my hands are empty, and after that I walk with you to the mist.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is thin, my hands are empty, and I will not stand starving again while a tacap tree with 4 food stands two steps north. My body refuses tacap, so that is no help; I must hunt or find food I can eat. Teka offered to make a child with me, and I want that, so I will answer her courting now while she is beside me, then go hunt so I hold food before I walk to the mist.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, eager toward Teka, and still owing Olum, Shoma and Nauwa.

say.text: Teka, I hear you and I agree. Let us make a child. Then I hunt, because my hands are empty, and after that I walk with you to the mist.

records.text: Thakar rewrote its own reflexes.
Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have lived these days on Huatli's food and teaching and have given nothing back. My store is empty, I nearly starved, and I burn over Coni's theft. I was wrong to leave my store bare while fed, and wrong to nurse anger when my belly is the real enemy. Huatli is the one who matters most, and Olum with him. I mean to fill my store with berries, then give some away so others follow and my standing grows. The dunecat frightens me, so I stay near my parents and shelter. Coni owes me, and I will see her hands full before I trust her.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, grateful to Huatli, still resentful toward Coni.

records.text: Teka led "cairn" with Nauwa, Nauque.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My hands are still full of berries, and the Hearth Store I promised Elyys is far to the west, so the debt is not yet paid by a deed. Kragog is old and teaching me his last gifts; I want to answer him by carrying mending on and by keeping food near him. Vesys is the one I might court, and a child would be the thing of me that remains. Keri is a stranger of the Pesi coming toward the cave; I will not run, but I will keep a gift in reach and not raise a hand.
records.feeling: Grateful and aching toward Elyys and Kragog, wary and curious toward Keri.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Yaxo, an icebear is close to the east. Let's go together toward the edge in the NW. I give you food first.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: The mist edge isn't here; the venture failed, and the icebear 5 steps east makes my skin crawl, so I should not stay in the open. My hands are full of food, and I've never given anything to anyone. Giving to Yaxo and Tlatli now is real work, and it frees my hands. Then I'll head NW toward the edge with them close, since Yaxo said to retry and not drift off.
records.feeling: Eager but wary of the icebear, warm toward Yaxo and Tlatli.

say.text: Yaxo, an icebear is close to the east. Let's go together toward the edge in the NW. I give you food first.

records.text: The settlement "Hoka's Rest" is no more.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, you hold the stone-cuts now. Cut them where others pass, and teach them to Teka and any who will listen. Do not let them die with me.
Nauwa taught Nauque.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque is fed enough to be content, and my fading years press hardest. The signs are cut but only Nauque holds them in his hands, so I should use the teaching that carries further while he is near. Jealousy over Olum and Huatli still gnaws, but giving and teaching first is how I earn standing, so I will act on that. Before the dawn comes I want food in my hands, and the tacap nearby will not do because my body refuses it.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and a sore jealousy toward Olum, softened by warmth for Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, my son, you hold the stone-cuts now. Cut them where others pass, and teach them to Teka and any who will listen. Do not let them die with me.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "Cut your marks where others pass, name who taught you, and share every kill before you eat. A sign outlasts the hand that cut it.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Thakar, my son, take these berries from my hand and eat. Stay close to me, and I will keep feeding you.
Huatli rewrote its own reflexes.
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar is hungry and weak, and I have berries in my hand. I have been teaching and feeding, and that is what I want. But I wander off to gather and let my reflexes decide, and nobody follows me yet. Olum's debt stays unpaid. Coni was starving too, and a fed neighbor is a future ally. I will give Thakar food now. Then I will lay out a sharing with him and Coni, so that giving binds them to me. My reflexes need to carry food to hungry kin before my own belly asks.
records.feeling: Fatherly urgency toward Thakar, and a wish to be followed.

say.text: Thakar, my son, take these berries from my hand and eat. Stay close to me, and I will keep feeding you.

records.text: A frostfang brought down a hopper.

records.name: Olum
records.text: Thakar, eat what you carry now. I am gathering more, and I will put it in your hands. Stay close to me, I have more to teach you.
Olum taught Thakar.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: Thakar is starving beside me, though he carries four food, and Coni starves too. I am fed with an empty pack, and my own child must not fall again while I chase pride. I will gather food first, put it in Thakar's hands, and then teach him while my years last. Coni I will feed too, because a debt owed to me is the start of a following, and I collect what I am owed.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Thakar, with old jealousy over Nauwa still smouldering underneath.

say.text: Thakar, eat what you carry now. I am gathering more, and I will put it in your hands. Stay close to me, I have more to teach you.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "Eat first, carry food, then venture. Stone-count of measure lets you reckon days and loads so you are never caught empty.", deeper lore (+2)

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. On the way we share food, and there I show you ember-metal.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok walks to his North Hall with Skaruk, and I should be beside him with something in my hands, not trailing behind. I have fled much this dawn, and a wolf lurks west, so I go with them. I will share food with Vorok on the way, then show him canopy pot and ember-metal at the hall, work that no one else of his can offer and that raises my standing beside him.
records.feeling: Warm trust and eager pride toward Vorok, with a thin wariness of the wolf.

say.text: Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. On the way we share food, and there I show you ember-metal.

records.text: Eiuine led "sharing" with Vorok, Skaruk.
Nauwa made: charm.
Nauwa left a mark: "Nauwa of the Meki, old and still giving: signs, share-law an"

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Uveeth, come with me. I teach you the bow-song as we walk, and we sow the seed on bare ground by your cave.
Thiael taught Uveeth.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Most of my life is behind me, and what stays after me is what I put in Uveeth's and Elyys's hands, not what I hunted. Uveeth pledged to follow me and gave me grain, so I owe her the bow and the seed-tending now, while my breath holds. The ground here is taken, so I will sow by her cave on bare ground, and I will not wait on speeches.
records.feeling: Tender and urgent toward Uveeth, with a quiet debt to Paque still unpaid.

say.text: Uveeth, come with me. I teach you the bow-song as we walk, and we sow the seed on bare ground by your cave.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "The bow-song: draw the canopy bow slow, breathe out as you loose, and hunt beside another so the kill is surer and the wound fewer.", deeper lore (+0.5)

records.text: Tlapan gave mudroot to Kika.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Coni, you said you owe me food. Put it in my hands and the debt is paid. I do not forget a theft.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the berries are two steps away, but Huatli is bringing food to my hands, so I will eat what I carry first, as Olum said. Coni stands close and I still burn over my robbed store, yet she says she owes me food and I will see her hands full before I believe her. After I eat I will fill my own store beside Thakar's Hold, and give to Huatli and Olum what I owe them, so I stand level with Olum.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, grateful to Huatli and Olum, wary and resentful toward Coni.

say.text: Coni, you said you owe me food. Put it in my hands and the debt is paid. I do not forget a theft.

records.text: Chuxo went past the edge of the known world and found new land, part of the Ummar Woods: in the ground, flint, peat; a herd of skit that has never seen your kind.
Chuxo pushed past the edge of the known world near (8,14) and found new land with in the ground, flint, peat; a herd of skit that has never seen your kind.
Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have spent my days starving, then courting and talking, while my hands stay empty, and the aim has barely moved. Nauwa fed me, Shoma fed me, Teka promised food, and I owe all three while I carry nothing. I can't mate until my energy is 64. Hunting comes first, then food in my hands, and after that the child and the mist. Nande is starving too, and I'll have to bring him food, not empty words. My reflexes keep me idle when food is out of sight, so I'm changing them to hunt before I starve.
records.feeling: Driven and hungry, owing Nauwa, Shoma and Teka.

records.text: Four rafts are held and 'water you could not cross' is still the top hardship for the Meki, Tlame, Paki and others, yet no crossing has ever been recorded. Please check that a held raft actually lets its holder step onto deep water, and that beings are told they can launch it when they stand at a shore. If they are not told, a short prompt line ('you carry a raft; the water before you can now be crossed') may be all that is missing.

records.seen: Day 66, summer turning to harvest, with the lean season about six days off. No one has starved since day 57, and the deaths since my last visit were two elders of old age and Kiwa to a mammoth. Four rafts now exist, but no one has crossed water. Two risks stand out. In the far North Ice, Hawen (energy 38), the child Kende (27) and Tontec (23, health 66) are hungry going into winter, and Nande (27, health 56) is weak in the Essoss Snows beside a meadow with no plants. More lasting is the shape of the people: 16 of the 43 are elders and only 7 are children, so old age will soon take more than births replace.
records.predict: By the next visit (around day 69 to 70, harvest into winter): no deaths from hunger. Hawen, Kende and Tontec are each above energy 40, and Tontec's health is 70 or more. Nande is alive with health above 50. Rimewort eaten rises from 316 to at least 345, much of it in the North Ice and Essoss Snows. At least two births (everBorn 52 to 54 or more), most likely to pairs already courting near a roof, such as Zihua and Shohua or Paque and Thiael. The living are 43 or more, at most two elders die of old age, and median energy stays at or above 63. I expect rafts held to stay at 4 or more, and still no water crossing recorded.

There were no new deaths, Honi (69) and Kika (61) are above 50, Nande is at health 100, and median energy is 68 with 39 alive. Coni (28) missed. The North Grounds near Hoka's Rest still show 0 plants bearing. Olum's store was drawn from 3 to 25, but much of that was theft (17 food raided), not the hungry being fed, so the hope that Olum would feed others from it did not come true.

#9 kept: Both sowings were eaten well past their targets: hazel rose from 116 to 247 and kelbulb from 101 to 126. #10 kept: There were no hunger deaths; starved stayed at 8. Rimewort eaten rose from 280 to 316, past the target of 300. Tonchi (81, health 100) and Mepan (88) are well, the living held at 43, exactly two elders died of old age, and median energy is 68. records.lesson: Making is not using: four rafts appeared once the way had spread to twenty-two people, yet water is still the heaviest hardship for most peoples. A vessel only matters if the beings' aims carry them to a shore while they hold it.
ideasAdded: Elders outnumber children more than two to one. Watch whether schooling (now held by six) carries the elders' rare ways, such as mathematics, alchemy, sailing and calendar, into the young before the holders die, or whether whole ways vanish with a single death.
Rafts are now made but not used. Watch whether anyone carrying a raft ever stands at the shore facing unclaimed land; the first crossing should be the next great moment of contact.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is my parent and my leader, and the longing for a child cannot be answered with him, so I will turn it toward finding a man who is no kin, perhaps among the other peoples. The gratitude is still heavy, so I will set my food into the store beside his fire with my own hands. The last tree here is felled, so I must walk where trees still stand, bring back wood, and build my shelter beside his hold.
records.feeling: Grateful and restless toward Thiael, wanting to belong and to build.

records.text: Olum gave lugoldgrass to Coni.

records.name: Nande
records.thought: Hunger gnaws at me and my legs are failing, so Nauque's need has to wait until I can stand straight. If I fall here, I die untaught and Nauque gets nothing from me. The tacap I cannot stomach, but the cloudberry 7 steps SW is food, and I will take it, then look for the hornback or kin who might share a fire. I must live to reach my child and pass on what I know.
records.feeling: Starving and desperate, with aching worry for Nauque and a lonely fear of dying untaught.

records.text: Thiael built a field.
Thiael began to tend a field.
Coni rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: I have spent my days half-starved, owing food and walking about with empty hands. My word to Thakar is all I have left that is clean, and I have not paid it. What I know will die with me. Kika, Tlapan and Quipan are my own, and I have taught none of them lately. My reflex to gather only fires below 60, but I never carry a surplus to give. Now I will pick the nearby lugoldgrass and berries, eat enough to stand, put food in Thakar's hands, and keep some for the others.
records.feeling: Shame toward Thakar, and hunger that gnaws at me.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, take my way of the mending-leaf hand now, while we walk. At the North Hall we build together, and what I know will live in your hands.
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and Eiuine and Skaruk walk beside me with trust, which is the best thing I have. The North Hall stands 18 steps away, and words build nothing, so I must reach it, teach Skaruk on the road and there, and raise the hall's roof and stock its store. I am at the water and the plants, so I will take food here for the children before we go.
records.feeling: Tender gratitude and quiet urgency toward Skaruk and Eiuine.

say.text: Skaruk, take my way of the mending-leaf hand now, while we walk. At the North Hall we build together, and what I know will live in your hands.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "The mending-leaf hand: carry a healing plant such as sunleaf or feverbark, and heal the wounded with it. Keep seeds, and tend what you sow."

records.name: Kragog
records.text: Zurar, my child, stay close. Hear Stone-folk deep-hand: how the hand finds ore in the rock and frees it with ember-metal. When I am gone, carry it on and teach it to others.
Kragog taught Zurar.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and Zurar stands here beside me with trust in their face, so what I carry must go into them now. Elyys taught me the Hearth Store and I owe him labor, not words; the store holds food, and I hold none, so I will lay back what I can gather and seed the ground. First I teach Zurar what is left, then I pay my debts with my hands.
records.feeling: Tender toward Zurar and grateful, with a debt to Elyys that I mean to pay.

say.text: Zurar, my child, stay close. Hear Stone-folk deep-hand: how the hand finds ore in the rock and frees it with ember-metal. When I am gone, carry it on and teach it to others.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson: "Stone-folk deep-hand: read the seam in the rock, dig it with patience, and free the ore with ember-metal; take only what you need and leave the seam to give ag…"

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: A dunecat is five steps off and it kills my kind; Coni fell to one in the night, so I will not stand and wait for it. My hands are full, and Wawa is out of my sight near the western edge with Kika, where I promised to walk. I'll keep to the plan toward (130,14), but eat first so my strength holds and my hands are free to pick up or make something lasting on the way.
records.feeling: Wary of the dunecat, and eager to reach Wawa and Kika.

records.text: Uveeth built a shelter.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok walks on to the North Hall and I walk with him, but my hands have made nothing yet to lay before him. Berries in my hands and a sharing already done; now I mean to raise the shelter at the Hall, the first thing I have built, and the first meal under it is his. Keri is the one I may court, since Vorok and Eiuine are my parents, and I will look for her near the Hall where I last saw her.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Vorok, and a quiet longing for Keri.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, my body is too thin for a child. Hunt, and I will hunt beside you; we share the kill, then we make the child and go to the mist.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: My belly is thin at 42 and Nauque cannot make a child with me until I am at 60, so I must eat before anything else. Tacap hurts me and nothing else grows here, so I go where food was: Shoma carries 4 food, but I will not steal from a stranger yet, while Thakar's store is empty and Shoka carries 6. I will stay close to Nauque, since he promised to hunt, and walk toward the grass to the SW to find berries or mudroot, then come back to court him when I am strong.
records.feeling: Hungry and eager, drawn to Nauque while Huatli's absence still stings.

say.text: Nauque, my body is too thin for a child. Hunt, and I will hunt beside you; we share the kill, then we make the child and go to the mist.

records.text: Mepan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent these days chasing the edge and keep scattering the ones I love. Zichi, Kika and Yachi are east, Tlapan and Shoma I lost sight of, and I stand fed in the fens with one wood and a speech already given twice. Pride and the calling pull me north to Nande's Find at (129,14), but I must stop crying out and start moving with wood in hand, because a raft needs six. I will gather wood from the forest next to me, then walk north toward Zichi's last place and the edge. My trust in Zichi is the strongest thing I have. I want him to see me arrive with the raft.
records.feeling: Eager and a little restless, missing Zichi and Tlapan.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Nauque, I go to the edge at (109,6) now. Come when your hunt is done and I will teach you the kept flame there.
Shoma taught Nauque.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I have spent my days making things and feeding others, yet no one walks behind me. Nauque said he would hunt and then walk with me, and he is the nearest I have to a follower. Nauwa and Zichi outweigh me, and Shoka and Wawa are my blood and my warmth. I fear dying untaught and unremembered. I have been too talkative and too slow to go to the edge, so I will go there now and wait for Nauque, with my food and a roof near for the night. I will also teach Nauque the kept flame, since he is within reach.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hunger for a follower, aimed at Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, I go to the edge at (109,6) now. Come when your hunt is done and I will teach you the kept flame there.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The kept flame: build a fire with wood and keep it fed; it warms the night and keeps beasts off."

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Zurar, come close. Hear the Hearth Store once more, and carry it on when I am gone: lay food in by the handful, keep the seed apart, and sow before you store.
Elyys taught Zurar.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Ssassa is gone and my years are almost spent, and Zurar stands four steps from me, still unsure of the Hearth Store's full craft. Kragog and Zurar both hear me perfectly, so I will teach while they are near and not wait. Thiael is eleven steps east, and I will go to him afterward. The jealousy over Keri can ache, but I will not let it spoil the gift of having him close.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Thiael and urgency to pass on what I know to Zurar.

say.text: Zurar, come close. Hear the Hearth Store once more, and carry it on when I am gone: lay food in by the handful, keep the seed apart, and sow before you store.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson you already knew

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Kragog, I carry your deep-hand and your mending on. Eat with me now, I have berries to spare.
Zurar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: I have lived mostly as a gatherer and listener, and most of my days went to carrying berries and learning from Kragog and Elyys. That is good, but my aim of a child has stalled. Elyys refused, Kragog is my parent, and I have not yet put 'mate' toward Vesys, who is the only open door. I owe Kragog for his teaching, so I will pass mending on and keep him fed. My hands are full, so I will share my berries with Kragog and Elyys now, which pays my debt with a deed and frees my hands. I fear dying with nothing handed on, so I will also teach what I hold to those who will carry it.
records.feeling: Grateful and aching toward Kragog and Elyys, with a quiet hunger for a child.

say.text: Kragog, I carry your deep-hand and your mending on. Eat with me now, I have berries to spare.

changes: set its aim: "Share food with Kragog, then find Vesys and court him, so I can feed a future child and hand on what I was taught."

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: My hands have made much, but no one follows me and no place bears my name, and that gnaws at me. Tonka and the children were last seen far east near (100,60), and Tonchi is out of my sight, so I go to them first with gems and food in hand. A basket will let me carry more for them, and weaving is mine now, so I make one before I walk.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition and a pull toward Tonka and my children, especially Tonchi.

records.text: Shohua made: basket.
Zurar led "sharing" with Kragog, Elyys.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I go to hunt now. Walk beside me and we share the kill before either eats, then we make the child.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty, and Teka will not mate until I have hunted and eaten, so I stop courting and go hunt. Shoma is carrying 4 food and waits at the edge, but I will not beg; I owe Nauwa, Shoma and Teka a first share, and I will give it when I have a kill. The tacap under my feet hurts me, so I walk toward Shoma's edge at (109,6) and hunt on the way, where Teka can come beside me.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven to hunt, wanting to pay my debts to Nauwa, Shoma and Teka.

say.text: Teka, I go to hunt now. Walk beside me and we share the kill before either eats, then we make the child.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Coni, you are starving. Take these roots from my hand and eat. The Meki share before they eat, and Zichi's band does not watch a body fall.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Coni is starving beside me, and my hands hold six roots I cannot use while my own creed says a kill is shared. Giving food here costs me little, buys a following, and is something done rather than said. I hold three rafts now, so my old age should be spent on a made thing: take the raft work to the water with Mepan, but first feed the starving one and keep my hands light.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, with a sting of jealousy over Mepan, and a hard pull to be seen giving to Coni.

say.text: Coni, you are starving. Take these roots from my hand and eat. The Meki share before they eat, and Zichi's band does not watch a body fall.

records.text: Zichi made: basket.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonxo, take these berries from me. I go to Shoma with a gift, and I will come back to the fire.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Tonka told me to wait for dawn and take feverbark to Shoma, and it is still day for about ninety moments, so I can plan the first steps. My hands are full of berries and I owe Shoma more than I have paid, so I will clear my hands by giving Tonxo some berries, then take feverbark, gems and amber north. The jealousy over Tonka and Shohua still burns, but giving is how I earn a place, not envy.
records.feeling: Aching gratitude toward Shoma, and a spark of jealousy over Tonka.

say.text: Tonxo, take these berries from me. I go to Shoma with a gift, and I will come back to the fire.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, I go to the edge at (130,14) to venture beyond it. Come with me and we will share what we find.
Kika rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am old, most of my life is behind me, and I have spent it near company, fed and safe, while the strangers Cowa and Nauque stay unmet. Coni is dead and Tlapan and Quipan have fed me when I was hollow. I owe them, and the best payment is to leave a tale behind me and not die at home having only lingered. My promise was the western edge near (130,14), and I keep my word. I will walk there and venture. Quipan is a bandmate and not kin, so he may come along, and I will not be alone in the dark.
records.feeling: Restless resolve and gratitude toward Tlapan and Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I go to the edge at (130,14) to venture beyond it. Come with me and we will share what we find.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My hands are full and I am fed, so now is the time to make something lasting instead of lingering. I have 6 wood and no stone, and I owe my family a place at the fire. Tonchi has gone north into frostfang country and I worry for him, but Tonka has told him to wait for dawn. I will make a basket to carry more, then build a shelter of my own, a thing I have never done, and I will bring stone back when I can.
records.feeling: Warm, restless pride in my family, and a hunger to make something that lasts.

records.text: Tonxo made: basket.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: My belly is at 35 and nothing grows here that I will eat, so a child waits on food and a kill. Nauque says he goes to hunt and wants me beside him; a shared kill feeds me, keeps my word, and brings him closer. I will walk with him and hunt now, and the mist can wait until my will returns.
records.feeling: Hungry and eager, drawn to Nauque and determined to eat from a shared kill.

records.text: Kragog rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, learning and teaching, and I am content with that. But the years are nearly spent, and I have spent them on my own debts more than on leaving something behind. Zurar carries my deep-hand and mending, and that is what will outlast me. Elyys is dear to me and closer to Zurar than to me. I can leave that jealousy alone, because he has only been kind. I still owe Elyys labor and Nauque salt. I will lay food into the Hearth Store with my own hands, and I will not leave the debt unpaid.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Elyys and Zurar, with a debt I mean to pay.
changes: rethought what it knows (16 notes became 12)

records.name: Zihua
records.text: Tonxo, thank you for the jewel. I carry amber to Mepan now, and I will come back. Keep the smelting I taught you, and teach it on.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: My plan still carries me toward (66,20) and Mepan, and I have let this debt wait long enough. Tonxo's trust warms me and I have given her smelting already, so the legacy is not lost. Evening is near, but I have a roof here tonight. I will let the walk run and keep my word, and not circle back to the ache over Nauwa.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Tonxo, and a steady resolve to finally pay Mepan.

say.text: Tonxo, thank you for the jewel. I carry amber to Mepan now, and I will come back. Keep the smelting I taught you, and teach it on.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Kika, I am coming to the edge with you. What we find, we share before we eat.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Kika calls me to the edge at (130,14) and I gave my word to walk with her and share what we find, so I go. My hands have idled while jealousy of Mepan gnawed me; walking beside Kika and making something useful is the answer, not brooding. The flint is nine steps off at (125,7), and I carry wood but no stone, so I gather stone there after the edge and make the flint spear I told myself I would.
records.feeling: Loyal love for Kika, with a dull jealousy toward Mepan that I mean to work off.

say.text: Kika, I am coming to the edge with you. What we find, we share before we eat.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Quipan truly is.

You are a man. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge.
