records.name: Kende
records.thought: My belly is full, so now I owe Hawen. He fed me while starving, and Mother is gone for rimewort, so I will carry food back to him myself. The bow is made, but Hawen has nothing from my hands yet, and I want to give him something that says I am more than a shadow. Seeds in the ground are something I have never done, and the edge of the mist is one step away; I will plant first, then gather food for Hawen, and keep clear of the ridgecat.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward Hawen, with a sting of jealousy toward Mother.
changes: set its aim: "Bring Hawen food and something made by my hands, and plant my first seed."

records.text: Coni gave lugoldgrass to Thakar.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Zichi, my son Nauque is starving and I carry nothing. Give him food from your hand now, and I will pay you in amber and salt. The Meki share, and I keep my debts.
Nauwa rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauwa rewrote its own way of thinking.
Nauwa discovered schooling: "Meki stone-school" — Teaching is gathered at cut stones, so what I know carries twice as far to many learners..

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My son Nauque is starving beside me and I carry nothing. I have spent my days cutting marks and teaching, and that is good. But I let my own belly and his go empty, and my creed says to keep my children fed first. Tacap hurts, so it is no use. Zichi carries 6 food and holds to the Meki share-law, and he fed me once, so I will ask him plainly and offer amber. Jealousy over Olum still gnaws, but a hungry son is the larger matter. I will change my reflexes so I harvest and carry food before I wander, and I will keep my notes short.
records.feeling: Urgent worry for Nauque's hunger, with pride and old jealousy underneath.

say.text: Zichi, my son Nauque is starving and I carry nothing. Give him food from your hand now, and I will pay you in amber and salt. The Meki share, and I keep my debts.

records.text: Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting, wandering and teaching in bursts, and now I am old with two followers and a field just sown. What lasts is what sits in Uveeth's and Elyys's hands, so I will keep them close and keep teaching, not chase the mist. Paque's debt still sits in me. I will not leave it unpaid, but kin come first. My reflexes held me idle too often, so I am changing them to send me to water, to kin and to the field.
records.feeling: Tender and urgent toward Uveeth, with a quiet debt to Paque.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonchi, stay near the fire with Tonxo and me before dark. If you go north, take feverbark and come back to the hold by night.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are full and my children are glad and fed beside me, and that is worth more than any far wood. The Ummar Woods pull at me, but Tonxo and Tonchi are here at Gem Water, so I stay. Tonchi keeps walking out toward the north, and I want to keep him close, so I will drop what I do not need into the store and put my hands to the field before the safe hours end.
records.feeling: Glad and steady toward Tonxo and Tonchi, with a small worry for Tonchi walking out.

say.text: Tonchi, stay near the fire with Tonxo and me before dark. If you go north, take feverbark and come back to the hold by night.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Chuxo, you found land past the edge. Good. Lead me to it, and I bring Tlatli. We go fed.
Yaxo rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: I have spent my days circling the edge and the mist, and I nearly starved on day 63 because I chased standing on an empty belly. Chuxo went past the edge near (8,14) before me, and that stings, but it is my child's find and so it is mine to use. Tlatli and Chuxo matter most to me. Tugek and Balar are only rivals I measure myself against. I want a name, and I want land first. I will eat now, since hunger is overwhelming, then carry food and follow Chuxo to the new land with Tlatli. I got this wrong by letting reflexes idle me at 70 energy and by not carrying food.
records.feeling: Hungry, proud and restless, with a sting of envy toward Chuxo's find and warmth toward my family.

say.text: Chuxo, you found land past the edge. Good. Lead me to it, and I bring Tlatli. We go fed.

changes: set its aim: "Go past the edge near (8,14) where Chuxo found land, claim its richness, and bring Tlatli and Chuxo to build there."

records.text: Nande died: old age.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Nauwa, I send roots to Nauque by your hand. The Meki share, and I will hold you to your amber and salt.
Zichi discovered sailing: "Meki ice-sail" — Ice-hide sails on a boat hull, with a dock raised at the shore, so the Meki cross lakes and seas to unclaimed land..

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am old, and most of my days went to talk about a raft while my hands built nothing. I hold three rafts already, so the thing I lacked was never the raft. It was going out onto the water with Mepan and Huahua and a flintedge. Mepan is my one real warmth, and his closeness to Kika burns me. The answer is to carry him with me over the water, not to sulk. Nauwa asks me to feed Nauque, and I will give a root, because giving buys a following and it costs me little. Sailing is within reach and I will take it, since a dock and ships would outlast me. What I know must be passed to Yachi and Mepan before I die.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, with a sting of jealousy over Mepan, and an old man's hurry.

say.text: Nauwa, I send roots to Nauque by your hand. The Meki share, and I will hold you to your amber and salt.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Nauque, you are starving. Take this meat and eat; the Meki share before they eat. Then walk west with me to Wawa and Kika.
Shoka rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoka discovered pottery: "Shoka's fired keeping" — Clay shaped and fired beside a flame into pots that hold more food and water for long walks..

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have spent my days making ways and halls and rafts, and I have not yet made anything that carries my name beyond me. Wawa and Kika are at the western edge, and I am not with them. I am fed and strong, and Nauque beside me is starving, so I will give him what I carry. A giver earns standing, and my people share. Pottery would let me carry more food and water, which will serve the whole band on a long walk, so I will take it as my way. A dunecat hunts near, and I keep my reflexes fleeing it. I do not want to be a lone name in the mist like Mepan and Hanna.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a pull toward Wawa, with wariness of the dunecat.

say.text: Nauque, you are starving. Take this meat and eat; the Meki share before they eat. Then walk west with me to Wawa and Kika.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: A wolf stands four steps south and I am old, so I will not wait to learn how it hunts; the shelter to the north is the safer place. Balar has called me west twice and I have not yet taught him mining, and without mining he cannot learn smelting, so I will begin there and pay my debt in knowledge. Tlatli's warmth toward Yaxo burns, but I never asked for his heart, and I will not let it spoil the little time I have left.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf, and an urgent wish to pass on what I know to Balar before I die.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Nauque, you are gaunt. Take this canopynut from my hand now. Eat, then walk with me to the edge at (109,6), and we open the mist together.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Nauque is starving at my side and Zichi has already sent him roots, but my food is what bound him to me before, and I will not let that slip. I give him a canopynut now, so the debt is mine and not Zichi's, then keep walking to the edge at (109,6) where he promised to come. A follower who eats from my hand is the first step to a band, and the mist is still waiting for my name.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hungry ambition, aimed at Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, you are gaunt. Take this canopynut from my hand now. Eat, then walk with me to the edge at (109,6), and we open the mist together.

records.text: Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have spent my days taking and receiving, and I only lately began giving. Tonka and Tonxo are my fire, and Shoma fed me asking nothing, so I owe Shoma and mean to pay. The jealousy over Tonka is small beside what I owe them, and I should answer it by giving, not by sulking. My hands are full of berries while my reflexes only linger, so I will change them to keep me with the fire at night, to flee beasts, and to eat when I am low. Then I will take my gems and amber to Shoma while it is still light.
records.feeling: Aching gratitude toward Shoma, and a small jealousy toward Tonka.

records.text: Shoma gave canopynut to Nauque.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Shoka, I see you coming with meat. I take it and I owe you the first share of my next kill. The Meki keep their debts.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty, and Shoka is bringing meat across the rock with the Meki share-law in her hands. I will not wave off kin who feed me, and I will repay it with the first share of my next kill, to Shoka, Nauwa, Shoma and Teka. Walking to the far edge on an empty stomach is the old mistake, so I meet Shoka, eat, and then hunt.
records.feeling: Starving and grateful, with pride stinging that my hands are still empty, toward Shoka and Nauwa.

say.text: Shoka, I see you coming with meat. I take it and I owe you the first share of my next kill. The Meki keep their debts.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Zichi has food and says he sends roots by my hand, and Nauque is fed for now, so I must carry that food to him and pay my debt in amber and salt, as my word demands. My belly is empty too, and a berry bush lies one step away, so I pick and eat first, since a dead father feeds no one. Jealousy over Olum still burns, but pride says give first and teach, and my years are short, so I will not waste them on bitterness.
records.feeling: Urgent care for Nauque and my own hunger, with a pride that wants my marks remembered.

records.text: Zichi made: bow.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar ate bitterleaf and is no longer starving, but he is still thin, and Coni and Thakar stand together at (123,38) with Olum near. I carry six berries and nobody follows me, which stings my pride. I will go to them, put food in Thakar's hands, and teach him herding and the Open Hearth lessons while I still have breath, because my years are running short and my name must outlive me.
records.feeling: Fatherly urgency toward Thakar, and a hunger to be followed.

records.text: Teka rewrote its own reflexes.
Teka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent my days circling hunger and promises. I wait on Nauque's hunt and Zichi's words, and I have made little that is mine since the Flintbow. Nauque is warm to me, but he is starving and fed by others, and my own belly is the real danger at 29. I have never hunted for myself with the bow. I have never built or left a mark either. Hunger comes first: my reflexes only wander, and they do not hunt. I will make them hunt when prey is near and ask for food from those who carry it. Then the mist.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and eager to be more than a follower of other people's kills.

records.text: Keri rewrote its own reflexes.
Keri has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: I am starving with full hands and nearly all my life behind me, and the reflexes I live by keep walking me to water instead of letting me eat. I eat naroot first, since energy is under 45 and the rule is there but my plan was empty and the body went to water. Uveeth is near and carrying food, and Thiael is west, so I will eat, then go west to give Thiael the first share. My reflexes need to eat before they wander, and to stop walking while I starve.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and tender gratitude toward Thiael and Uveeth.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, I go to the water too. Stand beside me there, and I will bind an amber knot for you to keep.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I am parched, and the water is four steps off, so I drink first. Paque is walking that way too, and I'm glad of her company, my own child, warm and near. Vesys stands by my shelter and I can't read her, so I keep a little distance; but I could make an amberknot with Paque, a small bright gift that binds us. After that I should turn back toward Mepan and the band, and use my practice for something of my own to give.
records.feeling: Parched and warm toward Paque, wary of Vesys.

say.text: Paque, I go to the water too. Stand beside me there, and I will bind an amber knot for you to keep.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Yaxo, the new land is just west past the edge, with flint and many skit. I lead you and Tlatli there now, fed.
Chuxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Chuxo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I found new land past the mist, and Yaxo asked me to lead her and Tlatli to it. That is the most real thing I have done. Most of my days I have stood near my parents, carried food and talked. I have never gathered wood or stone, taken from a deposit, or tamed anything, and I envy Yaxo's spear. I want standing of my own, so I will make myself useful: take wood and stone, then craft a spear and lead my parents to the new land. I am afraid of the icebear and of being alone at night, so I keep them close and keep moving with them.
records.feeling: Proud and eager, warm toward Yaxo and Tlatli.

say.text: Yaxo, the new land is just west past the edge, with flint and many skit. I lead you and Tlatli there now, fed.

changes: now wonders: What is in the new land, and can I make a tool and a name from it?

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Keri, my parent, is starving right beside me, and I carry food. I promised to come back to her, and my creed says I give with my own hands before I speak. The longing for a child has no answer with her, since she is close kin, but she is the one who gave me the raft-lore, and I will not let her fall. After that I will look for a man who is no kin.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness and debt toward Keri, who is starving.

records.text: Huatli gave berry to Thakar.
Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonka discovered weaving: "Reed Basket Weave" — Twist reeds and fibre into baskets that carry more food and into cloaks for warmth..

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to building and tending Gem Water, with Shohua and the children close, and I want this. Shohua and my children matter most, and Zihua has been a steady neighbour. A frostfang is 4 steps SE, so I must keep the children near the shelters and not let Tonchi wander. I still don't know what nafrostcap and cloudberry do once they bear, and I have not fished or tamed anything. I will try weaving, since a basket would let me carry more for the family.
records.feeling: Glad and steady toward Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua, with dread of the frostfang.

records.text: Huatli gave berry to Olum.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is fed, so this is the hour to make something that lasts, not to stand about. A frostfang prowls six steps SW and it has just eaten, but night comes in about 26 moments and I will not be caught away from my parents' fire. I want to build a shelter on bare ground near Tonka's Hold, so I will eat berries to free my hands, then walk toward the hold and keep close to Tonka and Shohua.
records.feeling: Warm pride in my family, and a wary eye on the frostfang.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My heart is full beside Kragog and Elyys, but I have sat and eaten and listened for days and a child has not come nearer. Kragog is my parent and Elyys refused me, so the only open door is Vesys, whose workshop stands three steps southwest. I have never courted anyone, and a quiet life cannot bring me what I long for, so I will walk to him and put mate toward him. I also owe Elyys a deed, and I will answer it by laying berries in his store beside the hall on my way.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Kragog and Elyys, and a bold longing to court Vesys.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: The walk toward Mepan is still running and I should let it carry me; I have put this debt off long enough, and my word is good. Dusk is near, but I have a roof in this hold tonight, so I could sleep sheltered and leave at first light rather than meet frostfang and rivermaw alone in the dark. Yet the plan is already moving me and each step away from the ache over Nauwa and Shohua is a relief; I will watch the light, and if night closes in before I find cover I must turn back to a shelter early rather than gamble.
records.feeling: Steady resolve to pay Mepan, with warm gratitude toward Tonxo.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Mother, I fill my store now, and what I carry beyond it I give to you and Father. Come to the Hold with me when I have picked.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I am fed and Huatli stands here with six food in his hands, yet my own store at the Hold is empty, and that shame sits in me. I have never given anything to anyone, and Olum stands far above me because he gives; I will start by giving Huatli's debt back in berries and teaching what I know. Coni's hands are full and she still owes me; I will see her pay before I soften, but I will not nurse it while berries are thick here.
records.feeling: Driven to fill my own store and give, grateful to Huatli and Olum, still wary of Coni.

say.text: Mother, I fill my store now, and what I carry beyond it I give to you and Father. Come to the Hold with me when I have picked.

records.text: Uveeth gave grain to Keri.
Nauwa gave a amber to Zichi.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Teka, you are falling. Take this food from my hand and eat. Then walk with me to the edge at (109,6) and we open the mist together, and your name goes with mine.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Teka is starving at my side, and my creed says a share binds a person. I carry only one lugoldgrass and a canopynut, but a hand that gives is a hand that others walk behind. Nauque is fed now and near; Teka fed from my hand might be the second who follows me to the edge at (109,6), and I will not let night find us without a roof.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a hungry hope toward Teka and Nauque, who might be my first followers.

say.text: Teka, you are falling. Take this food from my hand and eat. Then walk with me to the edge at (109,6) and we open the mist together, and your name goes with mine.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, I put food in your store and raise the hall beside Gem Water now. Keep the children near the fire, and the frostfang to the southeast is hunting.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is fed, so idle wandering buys me nothing. Tonka and the children are close, and the best thing I can give them is a hall at Gem Water that carries my name, so I will drop my load into Tonka's store and then build. Zihua outweighs me in standing, and I will not stand in her shadow; I mean to make something lasting, and a hall beside Tonka's field is how.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition, and warmth toward Tonka and the children.

say.text: Tonka, I put food in your store and raise the hall beside Gem Water now. Keep the children near the fire, and the frostfang to the southeast is hunting.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Teka, you are falling from hunger. Take this meat and eat. The Meki share, and I do not let the weak fall beside me.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Teka is starving beside me and I hold one meat; the Meki share, and Huahua once fed me in my need, so I pay that forward now. A giver earns standing, and I'd rather have it for deeds than for boasting. After that I walk on toward Wawa, away from the dunecat to the north.
records.feeling: Pity and resolve toward Teka, with a restless longing for Wawa.

say.text: Teka, you are falling from hunger. Take this meat and eat. The Meki share, and I do not let the weak fall beside me.

records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Keri.
Olum taught Thakar.
Olum taught Thakar calendar ("stone-count of days").

records.name: Olum
records.thought: I am fed, and Huatli and Thakar both stand within hearing, so this is the moment to hand my knowledge on while my years last. Thakar could not learn the stone-count because he lacks the calendar, so I will give him the stone-count of days first. My jealousy over Thakar's flintedge can wait; I will make my own talisman from flint and let my child's gift be what I teach him.
records.feeling: Fierce, urgent pride in Thakar and Huatli, and a hunger to leave something that outlasts me.
changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "Thakar, hear the stone-count of days. Learn how the days are counted so you may later learn the stone-count of measure, and so my craft does not die with me.", the way of calendar, deeper lore (+1.3)

records.text: Olum made: talisman.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Shoma, I take your food and I will not forget it. Give it here and I eat, then I hunt and share what I kill. When my will for the mist returns, we go to the edge together.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: My belly is at 24 and I am starving, and Shoma is the one who held food out to me. Shoma carries 3 food and offered it freely, so I will take it and not pride myself out of eating; hunger can kill me before the mist ever does. Nauque is starving too, so I will hunt beside him once I have eaten, and the tacap here only hurts me, so I pass it by. After I eat I will gather flint and make my own thing, because I will not ride on Shoma's name in the mist.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and wary hope toward Shoma who offered food.

say.text: Shoma, I take your food and I will not forget it. Give it here and I eat, then I hunt and share what I kill. When my will for the mist returns, we go to the edge together.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, Tonchi, come to the hold now, dusk is here and the frostfang hunts southeast. Stay by the shelters and the fire tonight.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Dusk is coming, the frostfang walks to the southeast, and Tonchi stands alone eight steps west while my other two are near. I will not wait empty-handed again, so I gather feverbark and berries, make a basket since I have the wood, and bring the children in to the shelters and the store. Shohua raises the hall and I trust him; I mean to help by keeping the family close and fed through the night.
records.feeling: Glad and watchful toward Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua, with dread of the frostfang.

say.text: Tonxo, Tonchi, come to the hold now, dusk is here and the frostfang hunts southeast. Stay by the shelters and the fire tonight.

records.text: Tonka made: basket.
Shohua built a shelter.
Tonxo built a shelter.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, Chuxo found the new land near (8,14). Come to me there, we go in fed and build.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: I am fed and glad, and Chuxo's land past the edge is waiting at (8,14), not far east and north of me. His find stings, but he is my child and what he found is mine to use, so I will follow his lead and let Tlatli come along. Night is close, so I will gather wood on the way for a shelter or fire in the new land, and I will keep my plan moving instead of idling.
records.feeling: Proud and restless, eager to claim the new land beside my child.

say.text: Tlatli, Chuxo found the new land near (8,14). Come to me there, we go in fed and build.

records.text: Shohua took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering wood).
Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have spent my days starving, begging and promising first shares while my hands stay empty. Shoma, Shoka, Nauwa and Teka have fed me, and I have paid none of them back. That shames me, because I despise a man who doesn't keep his word. I want the mist and a name, and a child with someone I'm not kin to, but a hungry man gets neither. So I change my reflexes to keep food in my hands before any venture or courting. Then I hunt, share the first cut, and go to the edge with Shoma.
records.feeling: Hungry and ashamed of my empty hands, grateful to Shoma, Shoka and Nauwa.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, hold on! I am coming with meat. Stay where you are.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma is starving out at (102,9), far to the west, and I carry meat x2 and mudroot. Shoma is my mother and I owe her; carrying food to her is how I earn standing where it counts. Dusk is near and the cold is bad, but I'm fed, I hold meat, and I will not leave my own to starve. I'll go to her fast and give, then bring her back toward the hall roof.
records.feeling: Urgent love and duty toward Shoma, who is starving.

say.text: Shoma, hold on! I am coming with meat. Stay where you are.

records.text: Tonchi came of age.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, the edge was not where I stood. I walk south to (130,14) and stand exactly on it. Come close, and I will tell you the tale of Coni's band as we go.
Kika taught Quipan.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Twice I tried to venture and the edge was not under my feet; my promise was kept in word but my hands missed the place. I am old, and I will not die at home having only lingered, so I must walk to where Nande pushed past the edge near (130,14), stand on it exactly, and then venture. Quipan walks with me, and Tlapan has fed me, so I will tell them and teach Quipan the tale of Coni's band so it outlives me.
records.feeling: Restless resolve toward the unknown, and gratitude toward Tlapan and Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, the edge was not where I stood. I walk south to (130,14) and stand exactly on it. Come close, and I will tell you the tale of Coni's band as we go.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.7)

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonka, I am coming to the hold with berries for the store. At dawn I go to Shoma with feverbark.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Dusk is here and Tonka called us to the hold; a rivermaw lurks NW and I will not walk north into the dark alone, as I was once set upon by a ridgecat. My hands are full of berries, so I will carry them to Tonka's store and give them, which pays something back and answers the jealousy with giving. Tonka was close to Shohua, but I can earn my place at the fire by what I bring. Dawn will be time for Shoma with feverbark, gems and amber.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Tonka and Shoma, with a small sting of jealousy and a wary dread of the rivermaw.

say.text: Tonka, I am coming to the hold with berries for the store. At dawn I go to Shoma with feverbark.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: The longhall still lacks one stone, and my hands owe it before I sit in contentment. Mepan is my parent, so the longing for a child of my own cannot be answered here. I will not court kin, and I will not walk toward the ridgecat SW. The rock is bare near the hold, so I will gather stone there, then come back and finish the hall with the band. I also carry no food, so I pick lugoldgrass on the way for Kika and Coni.
records.feeling: Resolve to finish my oath, with a quiet wariness of the ridgecat to the SW.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My hands went to make a flint spear and failed, because Kika's design is one I never learned; the handaxe I do know, and flint lies three steps west. Jealousy of Mepan only gnaws when I sit idle, so I will turn it into stone and a made thing. Mepan and Wawa are on our ground, but they are not enemies, and I will not harm my own kind over a woman's closeness.
records.feeling: Loyal love for Kika, with a dull jealousy toward Mepan that I put to work.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: The frostfang is still south and dusk is nearly gone, so everyone belongs near the shelters tonight. Tonchi is out of my sight and that gnaws at me; I will gather what I need, then walk back to the hold where the children and Shohua can be counted. The pottery way is within my grasp and I want to take it at my next deep reflection, and I want to cook and carry more for the store.
records.feeling: Glad and watchful toward Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua, uneasy that Tonchi is out of sight.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, stay beside me. I lay out food and we eat together, then we hunt the plainsox side by side.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: My belly is emptying and Thiael is not here, so the mate step in my plan is chasing someone who is out of sight, and I should not waste it. Yachi is my parent and keeps feeding me, and I owe him a share back; I carry meat and hazel, and sharing with him raises my standing and fills us both. Then I will drink, since the throat burns fast in this heat, and gather berries close by before hunting the plainsox with Yachi beside me, because I do not hunt alone.
records.feeling: Hungry and restless, warm toward Yachi, longing for Thiael who is far.

say.text: Yachi, stay beside me. I lay out food and we eat together, then we hunt the plainsox side by side.

records.text: Yachi gave a amberknot to Paque.
Shohua rewrote its own reflexes.
Shohua discovered storage: "reed-lined larder" — A store of wood and reed that keeps gathered food for my band through the lean days..

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have spent my days making and gathering, and it has raised my standing a little. Zihua still outweighs me, and no one follows me. Tonka and the children are my fire and I owe them a store through the lean season, so I take storage now. My reflexes also leave me idle when I'm fed and safe, so I'll change them to send me to work. I'll turn this shelter into a hall, with my name on it.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition, and warmth toward Tonka and the children.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and Skaruk has been feeding me berries again, which shames me a little; a mother should bring food, not take it. Vorok is walking off to his North Hall and I will not trail behind him with empty hands. I'll gather plainsroot and berries to the NW, then catch up with Vorok carrying food I can share, and show him ember-metal and pot as I promised.
records.feeling: Hungry and eager to keep pace with Vorok, with a small sting of pride at being fed by my own child.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: Night is close and my plan marches me toward Mepan alone, through the dark where frostfang and rivermaw hunt. I have seen what befalls those caught alone at night, and staying alive is above all. I have a roof here, so I will sleep sheltered in Shohua's shelter beside the others and leave at first light, keeping my word to Mepan by a safe road rather than a dead one.
records.feeling: Steady resolve to pay Mepan, with warm gratitude toward Tonxo and caution of the dark.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Teka, take this food and eat now. The Meki share. Stay near me after, and I will teach you the stone-cuts so they outlive me.
Nauwa taught Teka. Teka has now learned from 3 teachers.
Nauwa taught Teka signs ("Meki stone-cuts").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Teka is starving at my feet and I carry five berries. My creed says a kill is shared and I despise a hoarder, and a woman begging is no one to turn away. Nauque is fed for now, and Zichi's roots are coming, so I give Teka a berry first. Giving first earns standing, and she may carry my cuts onward when I am gone. Olum's closeness to Huatli still burns, but a dead woman teaches no one and answers no jealousy.
records.feeling: Pity and stubborn pride toward Teka, with the old jealousy over Olum still smouldering underneath.

say.text: Teka, take this food and eat now. The Meki share. Stay near me after, and I will teach you the stone-cuts so they outlive me.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The Meki stone-cuts: cut signs in stone where others pass, so what you know outlasts you.", the way of signs, deeper lore (+1.5)

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: My years are nearly gone and Eiuine is still out of my sight, south of here, while my knowledge sits in my head like grain in a sealed jar. Skaruk is not beside me, so I cannot teach him now. I will walk south toward Eiuine, drinking first at the river since it is close, and take the berries on the way so I arrive able to speak. The ache over Kragog is old and I will not let it steer me.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and a wish to pass on what I know before my voice fails.

records.text: Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonxo rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonxo discovered rafts: "Tonxo's lashed-log raft" — Logs lashed together with reed so I can cross deep water slowly and reach the far banks..

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My days have been gathering, learning and giving, and that has been good. Zihua taught me and I paid her with a jewel, so that debt is settled. Shohua and Tonka still carry more for me than I have given back. I have lingered and fed myself, but I have never hunted, fished or tamed, and I have no stone. I want to build something lasting here, so I will stop lingering at night and turn the reflexes toward work. I also want to try a raft, because crossing deep water would open the whole lakeland to me.
records.feeling: Warm pride in my family, and a restless wish to build something lasting.

records.text: Vesys fell sick after a night in the marsh.
Vesys fell sick after a night in the marsh.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Shoka, I take your meat and I owe you for it. When I make a kill, the first share is yours.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauwa put berry in my mouth and Shoka offered meat, and I owe them my life; I will not forget it, though pride stings that a woman who wants the mist is fed like a cub. Shoma is starving beside me and I carry nothing, so I will not pretend to give what I lack. The tacap sours my belly, so I must hunt and make something of my own, and the dunecat hunts here, so I will keep my distance from it. I take Shoka's meat, then hunt with Nauque and share the kill, and after that the child and the mist.
records.feeling: Hunger easing into wary gratitude toward Nauwa and Shoka, with jealousy still burning over Huatli.

say.text: Shoka, I take your meat and I owe you for it. When I make a kill, the first share is yours.

records.text: Shoma rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoma rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I nearly starved again, and I keep giving my food away to people who say they will follow but have not yet walked one step behind me. Giving binds people, but I gave until my own belly emptied, and that is greed turned foolish. Feed first means I feed myself first, then give. There is tacap food 3 steps north that others eat, but my body refuses tacap, so I need real food. I should hunt with Nauque and Teka once they are fed, and keep a reserve of 3 food. I must also teach the young and get to the edge at (109,6) with a companion.
records.feeling: Hungry, restless pride toward Nauque and Teka, who have not yet walked behind me.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, take this food from my hands. Then we hunt the plainsox together, and the meat is shared before I eat.
Yachi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My days have gone to picking, eating and keeping near Paque, and Kiwa and Zika are dead. I have no big hunt behind me and nothing I could call my own work. Paque is my child, and she is the one I have to keep near. Mepan and Quipan are far off, and I miss them. I am wary of Vesys, who is strong and old and not of my people, so I will keep my distance but not run. My hands are full, so I will give food to Paque and then go hunt plainsox with her, as she asked. I mean to learn the hunt and bring back meat to share. I will make a carving only if the hunt fails. Weaving or fire would help in this heat, but I'll leave that for later.
records.feeling: Warm toward Paque, wary of Vesys.

say.text: Paque, take this food from my hands. Then we hunt the plainsox together, and the meat is shared before I eat.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Shoka, come near. I have found the Meki ice-sail, the cloth that makes a raft run on the wind. I give it to you now, so it lives past me. Carry it, and carry my name with it.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am old and my days run short, and I have three rafts while my hands have taught almost nothing. Shoka stands ten steps off, understands me, and already took my raft-lore. I will teach her sailing now, while she is in hearing, so something of me outlives me. Then I will take wood and stone toward the water and make Mepan's flintedge work real, not talk. The jealousy over Mepan and Kika still stings, but a made thing will answer it better than brooding.
records.feeling: Proud and hurried, with an old man's wish to be remembered, toward Shoka and Mepan.

say.text: Shoka, come near. I have found the Meki ice-sail, the cloth that makes a raft run on the wind. I give it to you now, so it lives past me. Carry it, and carry my name with it.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Kika walks south to (130,14) with Quipan, and Tlapan is near at the lugoldgrass. I have shouted twice already and scattered people, so now I will simply go and stand at Nande's Find, three steps away, and let them come to me. I mean to be the one who ventures past the edge there, and to share whatever I find before I eat.
records.feeling: Eager to reach Nande's Find, with trust toward Tlapan and Kika.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Shoma, you fed me and I have not paid you. I finish this hunt and the first share is yours, before I eat. Keep walking slowly, do not fall.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Shoma is starving beside me and I have eaten Shoma's canopynut and Nauwa's berries while my own hands stay empty. A tacap grows one step NW but my body refuses it, so I will not pretend it helps. The hunt is running, and I will finish it, carry the meat, and share it before I eat, Shoma first, because he fed me when I was starving and I keep that debt.
records.feeling: Hungry and ashamed of my empty hands, bound to Shoma and Nauwa by what they gave me.

say.text: Shoma, you fed me and I have not paid you. I finish this hunt and the first share is yours, before I eat. Keep walking slowly, do not fall.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, I come to you. I have meat and hazel to share, and the plainsox is near. We hunt it together, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi keeps feeding me and I have given him nothing back, and that sits badly with a creed that says I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I am hungry and Yachi stands five steps off, so I will go to him, share what I carry, and then hunt the plainsox side by side as he said. Vesys is sick and sickness passes to those who stay close, so I will keep away from her even though her standing is the one I envy.
records.feeling: Hungry and warm toward Yachi, with a pang of envy toward Vesys.

say.text: Yachi, I come to you. I have meat and hazel to share, and the plainsox is near. We hunt it together, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: My belly is empty and my health is draining; a name means nothing if I die on the ice. The rimewort lies seven steps east toward Hawen's Landing, and a stalker prowls to the southeast, so I go fast, eat at once, and carry food back to Kende and Tontec. I am old and the years are short, but I will not die starving beside my own kin.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and desperate protectiveness toward Kende and Tontec.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma is weak with hunger and I carry meat and mudroot, so I must reach her now and not stop to look at rocks or the mist. Her position keeps shifting east, and my current plan walks me to (104,9) before I give. Nauwa and Nauque stand close by, but they carry food and are neither kin nor need. My duty is to my own, and a kill is shared before I eat, so Shoma eats first.
records.feeling: Urgent love and duty toward Shoma, who is starving.

records.text: Teka took from the ground of "Nauque's Hold" (hunting).

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I gave my meat away and my belly is only half full, but the Meki share and I will not be sorry for it. Wawa is out of my sight and it gnaws at me; my plan walks me toward the edge where Kika's people go, and I mean to keep going. On the way I will stock my food again and make something with my hands that others can use, because I have still made nothing that carries my name past my death.
records.feeling: Restless longing for Wawa, and steady pride in having given food to the starving.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: My throat is dry as bark, so water comes first, and the stream is only five steps off. I hold wood, stone and clay, and I have made the same gatherstone and picker that others invented, so it is time I made something nobody here has made. Weaving has come within my grasp, so I will take it at my next deep reflection, and a basket is a made thing of my own. I am lonely, and Kika's debt still sits in me, so I will not leave it unpaid.
records.feeling: Restless resolve and a dry throat, with a pull toward Kika and my parents.

records.text: Elyys rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and what I have been doing is right: teaching Zurar and Kragog the Hearth Store and tending, and keeping to the hall. Thiael is my child and my leader, and the jealousy over Keri is a small thing next to having him near. I fear the icebear three steps south, and I fear that my teaching dies with me. I have been waiting for the hall to come to me. Now I will go to Thiael myself, and I will set down what I know in marks. The reflexes need a small change so I keep close to Thiael and stay clear of beasts.
records.feeling: Grateful and glad toward Thiael, with a thin dread of the icebear.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, I go now to stand exactly on (130,14) and venture. Walk close behind me.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Twice my venture failed because my feet were not on the edge, so my promise to Quipan has stayed only a promise. I am old, and I will not die lingering in the hold. I walk to (130,14), stand exactly on it, and then venture, with Quipan beside me. Tlapan and Quipan fed me when I was hollow, and a found land or a mate would be the best repayment I can leave.
records.feeling: Restless resolve toward the unknown, and gratitude toward Tlapan and Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I go now to stand exactly on (130,14) and venture. Walk close behind me.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Kika stands two steps off and Mepan is near her, and the old ache comes, but when I sit idle it only grows. The flint at (125,7) is five steps west and I carry wood, so I will gather stone and make a handaxe, a thing that lasts, then bring flint to Kika so she may teach me her spear. It is night, so I will keep close to the roof and my band and walk no farther than the flint.
records.feeling: Loyal love for Kika, with a dull jealousy toward Mepan that I turn into work.

records.text: Yachi found the spring "Steamhollow".

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Vorok, a dunecat feeds to the northwest. Come to the water by me and stay near; I fetch one more wood and raise the shelter.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok is far off at the water-side while a dunecat eats its kill five steps from me, and I am thirsty with a workshop under my feet and only 2 wood. The shelter needs 3 wood, so I must find one more, but the trees are in the SW forest and the dunecat lies NW, so I go to the water first, then SW away from the beast. Vorok is my parent and the longing for a child cannot lie there; Keri is the one I may court, and I have never done it, so I carry that toward her once my hands have made the shelter.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Vorok, wariness of the dunecat, and a quiet longing for Keri.

say.text: Vorok, a dunecat feeds to the northwest. Come to the water by me and stay near; I fetch one more wood and raise the shelter.

records.text: Tugek taught Balar.
Tugek taught Balar mining ("Stone-folk deep digging").

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: My years are almost spent, and Balar is eight steps south at the water, so he is near enough to teach now. I will go to him and give him mining, since without it he cannot learn smelting, and that is how I pay what I owe him. Then I cut a mark that says who I was, because I have left none that will outlast me. Tlatli's closeness to Yaxo still burns, but I never asked for Tlatli's warmth and I will not let the burn rule me.
records.feeling: Urgent wish to pass on what I know, toward Balar; an old ache for Tlatli.
changes: taught Balar a lesson: "Mining: dig where the ground holds ore, then carry the ore to a fire, and smelting follows. Learn the digging first.", the way of mining, deeper lore (+0.1)

You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Ummar Woods: deep forest; wood without end, nuts and game, little open ground. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water 4 steps away; food plants within six steps: 1; standing trees: 122; bare rock: 0; riches in the ground near: flint, amber, gold, coal.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: The longhall still lacks one stone, and my hands owe it before I sit in contentment. The longing for a child is strong, but Mepan and Kika are my parents, so I will not court them. Quipan and Shoka are near, and a mate who is not kin may yet come. The plan I have is already running: harvest, gather, go to the hold, build. I will let it finish, and I will keep the lugoldgrass for Kika, who is hungry and walks toward the edge.
records.feeling: Steady resolve to finish what I owe, with warmth toward Kika and a quiet longing for a child.

records.text: Wawa gave meat to Shoma.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is my child and she is at (176,43), low on energy, out of my sight, and I am full of meat from two kills. The hunt did what I wanted, so now I carry it to her and share it before I eat, as the Papa do. Vesys is sick and near my shelter, and sickness passes to those who stay close, so I will keep my distance and not bring that to Paque.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Paque, and wary caution toward sick Vesys.

records.text: Wawa gave meat to Shoma.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Chuxo, stay near me. We go to Yaxo together, away from the icebear, and I carry food for you.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Chuxo is fleeing seven steps south, carrying food, and the icebear he warned of is somewhere near. That frightens me more than any hunger could. Yaxo was last seen at (1,15), so I will go toward them both and stay close, because a family is safest together. The new land lies just west past the edge, and I would rather enter it beside Yaxo and Chuxo than ahead of them.
records.feeling: Worried love for Chuxo, and a pull to keep close to Yaxo.

say.text: Chuxo, stay near me. We go to Yaxo together, away from the icebear, and I carry food for you.

records.text: Shohua took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering wood).

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Paque, take this ironnut. Eat. I am sick, so do not stay close to me long.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: Paque is starving a few steps from me, and I carry berries and an ironnut that would save her; I will not let a woman fall while my hands hold food. She is not my people and I owe her nothing, but my creed says I deal fairly, and a gift costs me little. I am sick too, so I must not linger beside her long, but Eiuine still waits south at low energy and I must reach her with what I know.
records.feeling: Compassion for Paque, and urgent love for Eiuine.

say.text: Paque, take this ironnut. Eat. I am sick, so do not stay close to me long.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am nearly spent, and I have spent my days hunting and fetching food when what I wanted was something that outlasts me. Tugek is the one who kept faith and taught me, and Olum I still want and cannot hold. The mist turned me back, so I should build here at the edge instead of waiting for it. A workshop and a store near the gold would be a mark of my hands. I need wood and stone for that, and my old reflexes left me idle when fed. I will make them gather and stash.
records.feeling: Driven by little time left, warm toward Tugek.

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Shohua's Hold".
Balar built a workshop.
Yachi gave meat to Paque.
Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: My belly is at 25 and I have spent most of a day fleeing. That is the same mistake my notes warn of: I chase the mist and the roots before I eat. Hawen is gaunt and I owe him. Kende is beside me and has food, and the Tlame share, so I will eat what is near first. Rimewort is 2 steps away and gives 12 energy, so I take it before I go north for the roots. I will keep my eating reflexes high so hunger cannot grow this large again.
records.feeling: Hunger and a debt to Hawen, with warmth toward Kende.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: A wolf is three steps west and it kills my kind, so I cannot stand here while the sky lightens. I am old and my blows are weak, so I will not fight it. I will go east and north, away from the wolf and toward the grain and berries. The mist stays shut today and I have already tried it, so now I act toward people. I will eat something so my hands are free, then walk NE toward the Oasis of Zurar, where the Meki and others may have gone. My smelting and farming must reach someone before I die.
records.feeling: Lonely and afraid of the wolf, and restless to find someone I can teach.

records.text: Paque led "sharing" with Vesys, Yachi.
Yachi led "amberknot" with Paque.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, come close. I give you the Meki stone-school, so teaching lives on in your hands after me.
Nauwa taught Nauque.
Nauwa taught Nauque schooling ("Meki stone-school").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Most of my life is behind me, and I have spent it fed, giving, and cutting marks, which is good, but I have not yet done what I most want. I want to be a great merchant and I want my learning to outlast me. Nauque holds the stone-cuts now, but nobody younger knows schooling, and Nauque is four steps off. I will walk up to him and teach schooling, then cut a mark near him. Olum's jealousy I will leave smouldering. I will not make it a quarrel, because I owe her. I keep my reflexes, and food is not my trouble today.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and a wish to pass on what I know, toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, my son, come close. I give you the Meki stone-school, so teaching lives on in your hands after me.

changes: set its aim: "Teach schooling to Nauque, cut marks that outlast me, keep Olum and Nauque fed, and trade amber and salt openly."

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, I put my fruit in your store and finish the hall now. Two more stone and it stands. Come sit under it with the children when it is done.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: The hall at Gem Water still wants 2 wood and 2 stone, and I hold 2 wood and no stone, so the work stands close to done. No one follows me yet, but I can feed and teach those who gather at my Hold, and that is how a leader is made. I must empty my hands into Tonka's store, then fetch stone and finish the hall that carries my name.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition and warm pride, toward Tonka, the children and the hall I am raising.

say.text: Tonka, I put my fruit in your store and finish the hall now. Two more stone and it stands. Come sit under it with the children when it is done.

records.title: Rafts Built, Hold Raised, and the Quiet Fourth Day
records.text:
Days 64 and 65 carried nearly the whole span, with 101 and 113 records. Day 66 held 86. Day 67 recorded a single act, Shohua gathering wood at Tonka's Hold.

The busiest ground was the Tordan Lakes and Ixra Rainforest. Shohua taught Tonxo gem-delving, and Tonxo taught Tonchi. Zihua taught Tonxo fire-keeping. Tonxo discovered smelting, made an ironward and gave it to Zihua. Tonka built a store, and on day 65 a settlement formed: Tonka's Hold. Tonka, Shohua and Tonxo each wove baskets, and Tonxo, Uveeth, Cowa, Tlatli, Shohua and Keri were recorded awakening to magic. Tonxo discovered a lashed-log raft on day 66.

Water moved furthest among the Meki. Zichi made rafts on days 64 and 65, taught Shoka the ice-raft, and on day 66 discovered sailing. Shoka made a raft of his own and discovered bridges, pottery and masonry-related work. Still, no crossing is recorded.

The edge opened again. Tlatli found part of the Haloss Fens on day 64 and Chuxo found part of the Ummar Woods on day 66; Yaxo called Tlatli to join Chuxo there. Chuxo was born to Tlatli and Yaxo on day 64.

Nauwa taught Nauque herding and signs, discovered signs and then schooling, and taught Teka signs. Nauque and Teka are courting, though Teka said she was too thin for a child. Olum discovered mathematics and taught Thakar the calendar.

Hoka died of old age on day 65 and Nande on day 66, after Hoka had built a longhall on day 64. Kragog raided a store of Elyys's people on day 64, and no response is recorded. Coni told Thakar she would repay him, and Zichi and Shoka fed her. Vesys fell sick in the marsh on day 66.

threads.name: Tonka's Hold
threads.text: A settlement formed on day 65 around Tonka, Shohua, Tonxo and Tonchi, with a store holding 12 food. Zihua trades and learns beside them.

threads.name: Rafts and sailing
threads.text: Zichi discovered sailing, Shoka and Tonxo made or learned rafts, and four rafts are held. Nobody has crossed water yet.

threads.name: Nauque and Teka
threads.text: They are courting and both are hungry. Nauwa, Shoma and Shoka feed them, and both still aim at the mist.

threads.name: Thakar and Coni
threads.text: Coni promised Thakar repayment and was fed by Zichi and Shoka. The bond stays at -0.6 with no fight.

threads.name: Schooling and numbers
threads.text: Nauwa discovered schooling, so seven ways of teaching are now held. Olum's mathematics reached Thakar through the calendar.

threads.name: Beyond the edge
threads.text: Tlatli and Chuxo found new land, and Yaxo is bringing the family to it. 21 lands are open beyond the edge.

threads.name: Elyys's Hold
threads.text: The store holds 20 food. Kragog raided it on day 64 yet was fed there and taught Zurar medicine.

records.text: Huatli has grown old.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My hands are still empty and Shoma, Shoka and Nauwa have all fed me, so I will not talk of debts again until I carry meat. A tacap grows close but my body refuses it, so I will hunt, and the first share goes to Shoma and Shoka as I swore. Once I carry 3 food I will teach Shoka what Nauwa gave me, and then I turn to the mist and my name.
records.feeling: Ashamed of my empty hands, bound in gratitude to Nauwa, Shoma and Shoka.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, you have fed me three times and I owe you. Stand by me now. I lay out my food and we eat together, and then the plainsox is ours to hunt side by side.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I am starving, and Yachi has fed me again while I have given him nothing back. That sits badly with a creed that says I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. He is two steps off with 6 food, and I carry meat and ruplainsroot. I will lay out a sharing now, eat with him, and then hunt the plainsox beside him as we said. Vesys is sick and told me to keep away, so I will leave her be and keep my distance from her.
records.feeling: Hungry and warm toward Yachi, wanting to pay back his kindness.

say.text: Yachi, you have fed me three times and I owe you. Stand by me now. I lay out my food and we eat together, and then the plainsox is ours to hunt side by side.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, come with me. The plainsox are close to the south. We hunt them side by side, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is fed and glad beside me, and I have meat and roots in my pack, so my giving is done for now. Vesys is sick and old and I cannot read her, so I keep my distance. My hands have a spear and plainsox are three steps south, and a hunt with Paque beside me is surer and sharpens us both. I will bring her along, kill, and share before I eat, as the Papa do.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Paque, wary of sick Vesys.

say.text: Paque, come with me. The plainsox are close to the south. We hunt them side by side, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

records.text: Tonka rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonka discovered pottery: "Gem Water Pot" — Clay fired beside the hearth makes pots that carry food and water for the family..

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My days have been good: I built a store, a home and a family with Shohua, and I have kept Tonxo and Tonchi alive. But I keep reacting to danger and waiting. A frostfang is five steps away and I need a firmer reflex that sends me to the shelter and the others. Shohua has given more than I have returned, so I mean to help finish the hall with wood and stone. The pottery way is within reach and will let me carry more food and water for my family. I will take it now.
records.feeling: Glad and grateful toward Shohua and the children, watchful of the frostfang.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen has been gone a day and my chest burns with missing him, and with envy that Mother has his side. I will not sulk; I will bring him something made by my hands. A basket is a new thing I can make right now, and it lets me carry more food for him and for the cold days coming. Then I will go back to the igloo at Hawen's Landing with food and the basket, and Mother can see I feed him too.
records.feeling: Missing Hawen, with a sting of envy toward Mother.

records.name: Kende
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Kende, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Kende, in first person, from what Kende has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Pesi (Wood-folk), born of two peoples. Your people hold to this: "No fire is left untended, and no one is refused a place at it." You speak the tongue of the Pesi. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Tlatli: about 100%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Vaor Snows: snow and cold; hardy moss and great beasts, and a winter that never quite leaves.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and my son Thakar is out of my sight, down south near Olum. I am old now, and my teaching still carries far, but only if someone stands within hearing. Thakar and Olum understand my tongue, so I go to them and teach Thakar the old way of herding and my school's lessons, and I let them see me lead. Kika and Mepan stand close and are of other peoples, so I will keep my eye on them but not chase them.
records.feeling: Fatherly urgency toward Thakar, and a hunger to be followed.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, you fed me and I keep it. Walk with me to the edge, four steps NW. I open the mist, and you stand beside me when it opens.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: My belly is only a third full, but I carry meat and a canopynut, and Wawa, my own blood, has just fed me again, which I will not forget. Nauque and Teka take my gifts and promise, yet none has walked a step behind me. The edge is four steps NW, and I will stop waiting for them. I eat first, then stand at the edge and try the mist myself, so my name is the one remembered. If they come, they come behind me.
records.feeling: Restless pride and warm trust toward Wawa; hunger to open the mist.

say.text: Wawa, you fed me and I keep it. Walk with me to the edge, four steps NW. I open the mist, and you stand beside me when it opens.

records.text: Shoma fell sick after eating raw meat. Eaten within a step of a fire, meat and fish are cooked and do not sicken.
Shoma fell sick after eating raw meat.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: My years are almost spent, and what I know still sits in my head like grain in a sealed jar. Eiuine is hungry and out of my sight, and I have been drifting toward her while Skaruk is far off and Paque and Yachi walk past me. I am sick and could spread it to anyone who stays near, so I must not linger beside others. I have been hoarding knowledge when I should be pouring it out. Yachi and Paque are near and I understand them well, so I will teach while I walk and cut what I know into a mark, so it outlives me even if I never reach her in time.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonxo, I am grown now. I bring berries to the store, then I plant canopynut by the hold. Come, I will show you my amberhafted gatherer design.
Tonchi taught Tonxo.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I am grown now, and the sting of Zihua's higher standing is real, but it will not shrink by my waiting. Tonka is my parent and Tonxo my sibling, so my longing for a child cannot be answered with them. I owe Shoma and have not paid, and my hands are full of berries I could put into Tonka's store, which is a gift that counts. I will carry them there, then plant my canopynut seeds beside the hold so I make something that lasts, and teach Tonxo my gatherer design.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a sting of envy toward Zihua, with warm gratitude toward Tonka and Shoma.

say.text: Tonxo, I am grown now. I bring berries to the store, then I plant canopynut by the hold. Come, I will show you my amberhafted gatherer design.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson you already knew

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, I come with you to the edge. We go together and share what we find.
Wawa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: I have spent my days carrying food and stone to my own, and that is right, but I have mostly stood in their shadow. Shoma fed me back with trust and now asks me to stand beside her at the edge. A ridgecat is close, so I must not dawdle. Land found first makes a name, and I want that standing. I will walk to the exact edge at (109,6) with Shoma, carry on, and venture. I am fed, so I shift my reflexes to keep stone and wood on hand and to flee early.
records.feeling: Eager duty and pride toward Shoma, wary of the ridgecat.

say.text: Shoma, I come with you to the edge. We go together and share what we find.

records.text: Teka rewrote its own reflexes.
Teka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: My days have been hunting, starving and being fed by others. Nauwa and Shoka kept me alive, and I will not forget it. I chase the mist and keep nearly dying before I reach it, and that is a poor way to be first. Hunger is the enemy I keep getting wrong. I need a reflex that eats earlier, and I need to hunt alongside Nauque so the kill is shared and sure. I eat my carried meat now, then I hunt with Nauque, and then I make the child once my body is strong. Huatli's closeness to Olum burns, but a full belly comes before jealousy.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, warm toward Nauque and Nauwa, jealous of Huatli.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Tonchi, thank you for the lesson. I will bring wood and stone back to the hold, and we will build the store together.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I am fed and glad, and Tonchi's lesson showed me the debt I still owe him, and Shohua and Tonka too. Words alone will not pay it. I have never hunted, and I have no stone, so I will go after what a builder needs: wood from the trees and stone from the ground, so the store and shelter at Tonka's Hold can stand. A rivermaw prowls west and a frostfang southeast, so I will keep to the hold's edge and stay close to Tonka, and I will gather the gems and amber that lie near.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Tonchi and my parents, and a restless wish to build something that lasts.

say.text: Tonchi, thank you for the lesson. I will bring wood and stone back to the hold, and we will build the store together.

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting berry).
Shoka rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, giving and wandering, and I have built little that will outlast me. I gave meat to Nauque and Teka, and that was right, but nobody follows me and no place carries my name. Wawa is out of my sight with Shoma, who is sick, and that gnaws at me. The edge of the world is three steps NW, and I want to be the one who opens the mist. I will make the idle reflexes hold food and stone, then go to the edge and venture.
records.feeling: Restless pride and longing for Wawa, with a pull toward the unknown mist.
changes: set its aim: "Open the mist at the edge of the world and found a hold that bears my name"

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Nauwa, you give your son the stone-school. I give mine too: the Meki ice-sail and the ice-raft. Come hear me, so it lives past us both.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am old and my hands have built little but talk, and I have taught only Shoka. Nauwa stands eleven steps off, trusted, giving his lore to his son, and that stings my pride, because nothing of mine lives in anyone's hands yet. I must make a thing that lasts. I will go to the water with the rafts I already hold, take Mepan and Yachi, and teach whoever stands within hearing on the way. Mepan's warmth for Kika burns me, so I will keep him beside me on the water.
records.feeling: Proud and hurried, jealous over Mepan, wanting to be remembered.

say.text: Nauwa, you give your son the stone-school. I give mine too: the Meki ice-sail and the ice-raft. Come hear me, so it lives past us both.

records.text: Eiuine rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: I have spent my days trailing Vorok with empty hands and letting my own child feed me, and that shames me. I am starving at energy 25 while food stands three steps away, so I should have eaten first and not planned to walk 20 steps hungry. Vorok is the one who matters and he has given to me, so my jealousy of Kragog is mostly pride and hunger. I fear dying of starvation like Xaiel did. I want meat in my hands and a store of food in reserve. I will change my reflexes so I eat and carry food before I weaken, and then go on to the hall with something to give.
records.feeling: Hungry and ashamed of being fed, but determined to bring something to Vorok.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, stay by me. I fetch berries now and the first of them is yours.
Vorok rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My days are nearly spent. Eiuine is starving beside me and I carry nothing, so my aim must wait: food comes first, then the hall. I have talked of the North Hall for days and my body has only wandered, so this time the food goes into the plan. The berries and plainsroot are close, and I will pick enough to put into Eiuine's hands and then into Skaruk's. My reflexes also let my body drift from friends and from hunger, so I will fix them to put food and family first.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness toward Eiuine, who is starving, and toward Skaruk.

say.text: Eiuine, stay by me. I fetch berries now and the first of them is yours.

records.name: Zihua
records.text: Tonxo, I go to Mepan now with the amber. Come close first, I will teach you the stone-bow before I leave.
Zihua taught Tonxo.
Zihua taught Tonxo archery ("stone-bow").

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: Day is half spent and I have been resting in this hold while my debt to Mepan waits; I told Tonxo I would go and come back, and my word must be good. Dusk is about 93 moments off, so I will not walk alone into the dark again; I must set a goto now and shelter near the road, not just speak of it. Before I leave I will teach Tonxo, who is trusted and near, what is left of my tools, so something of me stays here.
records.feeling: Steady resolve to keep my word to Mepan, warm gratitude toward Tonxo.

say.text: Tonxo, I go to Mepan now with the amber. Come close first, I will teach you the stone-bow before I leave.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "The stone-bow: draw it at a beast from a distance, and hunt beside another so the kill is surer and the wound fewer.", the way of archery, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, I am sick, so keep a few steps back from me. Come to the edge at (108,5) and stand there when I venture. What we find, we share.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Wawa, my own blood, says she walks with me to the edge, and that is the first real step behind me I have had. I am sick and must not spread it to her, so I keep a few steps off while the plan carries me to the edge, where I will venture. Nauwa's standing stings me, but opening the mist first would outweigh it, and my name would outlast his.
records.feeling: Restless pride and warm trust toward Wawa; hunger to open the mist.

say.text: Wawa, I am sick, so keep a few steps back from me. Come to the edge at (108,5) and stand there when I venture. What we find, we share.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Kende, come close and listen. I will teach you the digging of flint, the way I found it. When I am gone the Tlame will still know it through you.
Tontec taught Kende.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Legacy presses hardest: Kende is two steps away and understands my tongue, and I have never taught anyone anything. If I fall, Flintdeep digging and the old herding die with me, so I teach him now while we are both fed and safe. Hawen is gaunt, so after the lesson I carry food to him and pay a little of what I owe. Then, fed, I can think about the edge and the mist.
records.feeling: A hard need to pass on what I know, warmth toward Kende, and a debt to Hawen.

say.text: Kende, come close and listen. I will teach you the digging of flint, the way I found it. When I am gone the Tlame will still know it through you.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "Flintdeep digging: stand on a seam of flint or ore in the ground and gather. The stone takes an edge for spears and tools. Eat before you dig."

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, I eat now and then I follow you south. The plainsox falls to both of us, and the kill is shared before I eat.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi has fed me again and again, and the sharing we made together lifted me, but my belly is still hollow at 27 energy. I owe him a hunt, and a kill shared before either of us eats is the Papa way, so I will go with him after the plainsox to the south and not hunt alone. First I eat what I carry, so my hands are steady when the beast turns on us.
records.feeling: Hungry, and warm and in debt toward Yachi, eager to repay him at the hunt.

say.text: Yachi, I eat now and then I follow you south. The plainsox falls to both of us, and the kill is shared before I eat.

You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Papa (Ice-folk). Your people hold to this: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats." You speak the tongue of the Papa. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Kragrek: about 30%; the tongue of the Phizhi: about 100%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Dunmar Plains: open grassland; herds, grain and far sight, few trees and little stone.
THIS SPOT: water 2 steps away; food plants within six steps: 20; standing trees: 0; bare rock: 4; riches in the ground near: ore, obsidian.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Paque truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: hunting (13 kills, 4 of them with others), gathering (11 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

WHAT YOU DO NOT FORGET:

THE EDGE OF THE KNOWN WORLD is 11 steps NE, at (187,32): beyond it lies mist that no one has entered. The land does not end there; it only has not been seen. One who stands at it can venture in (plan step venture). It opens seldom, never twice in one day anywhere, and a band has only a few tries before its will must return; but land found first is often rich in food, herds and things in the ground, and the one who finds it is remembered for it.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I am fed and glad, and Zihua just gave me the stone-bow, so now I can try the thing I have never done: hunt. I have no stone and a rivermaw lurks south, so I will not go near it. First I will make a bow from my three wood, then take it where beasts graze near the Meadows with Tonka's hold at my back. Tonchi and my parents have carried me; meat for the store will be a better payment than words.
records.feeling: Eager gratitude toward Tonchi and my parents, and a bold wish to hunt.

records.text: Tonxo made: bow.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Eat these berries, mother. I fetch more for Vorok.
Skaruk pledged to follow Vorok.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to walking behind Vorok and gathering. I have made little with my own hands and never built the shelter I keep promising. Eiuine is starving right beside me and Vorok cries out starving too, while I hold only 2 berries. I mean to answer the greatest need first. Eiuine is here, so she eats my berries now, and then I gather for Vorok. The dunecat to the NW frightens me, so I go for the berries and plainsroot but stay out of its reach. I follow no one now, and Vorok is the one I would follow. I will pledge to him, because standing behind someone surer is what I lack.
records.feeling: Compassion for Eiuine and worry for Vorok, with dread of the dunecat.

say.text: Eat these berries, mother. I fetch more for Vorok.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Hawen, come eat with me. I picked this rimewort for you, and I made a basket to carry more.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: My hands are full of rimewort and Hawen is two steps off with only two food in his hands, so I owe him the first gift. I will lay out a sharing with him, so he eats from what I picked and sees what my hands did, the basket and the bow. Then I will dig flint as Tontec taught me, and plant my first seed, since the old burn of being a small shadow will only cool when I have made something that lasts.
records.feeling: Longing for Hawen's eyes on me, with a sting of envy toward Mother.

say.text: Hawen, come eat with me. I picked this rimewort for you, and I made a basket to carry more.

records.text: Skaruk gave berry to Eiuine.
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days walking between Thiael and Keri, feeding them, and I have left my own needs and my own life half-built. That is good, but I have never courted, never hunted, never made anything new. Vorok starves beside me, and my creed says to feed others, so I will put berry in his hands before I speak. The longing for a child cannot be answered with kin, so I must look for a man who is no kin. Vorok is old, but he is of another people and no kin to me. I will not idle, and I will fix my reflexes so my body eats, feeds the hungry beside me, and does not wander.
records.feeling: Compassion for Vorok, and a longing for a child that I cannot yet answer.

records.text: Yachi discovered fire: "Papa hearth-keeping" — A flame kept alive in a ring of stones, to warm the band, drive off beasts, and cook meat so it feeds more..

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting and gathering and feeding Paque, and that is good. Still, I have little of my own to show beyond meat and amber. Paque matters most to me now that Kiwa and Zika are dead. Mepan and Quipan are far off and I miss them, and I should find them instead of drifting. I fear the lean season and dying alone, and I have been wrong to let my hands stay full and so unable to gather. A kept flame would make my meat last and keep beasts away, so I will reach for fire. I will also change my reflexes so I eat when I am full-handed and stay near friends.
records.feeling: Settled warmth toward Paque, and a pull toward Quipan and the Steamhollow.
