records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Vorok.

records.name: Keri
records.text: Vorok, you are hungry. Take this food from me, as a gift. Eat, and sit near me.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: Vorok is starving beside me, and my creed says no one is refused a place at the fire, so I will not look away just because he is Kragrek and I understand half his words. I carry grain and a berry, and I need little; a gift needs no words, and giving it may answer whether strangers take a gift as a gift. My years are nearly spent, so I will also teach him the bough-raft while he is near and I have the chance, since what I know should not die with me.
records.feeling: Tender compassion toward Vorok, mixed with wary curiosity about him.

say.text: Vorok, you are hungry. Take this food from me, as a gift. Eat, and sit near me.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Kende, I am coming. Tontec, I owe you my life, and I will pay it. Eat with us both.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: Tontec has put food in my mouth twice today, and I owe her my life; the creed says I pay what I owe, and I will. My belly is still half empty and my years are almost spent, so no name is worth anything if I fall on this ice. Kende holds rimewort for me and shares it freely, so I eat beside him now, then lay out a sharing for all three of us. After that I will carry the bloodline and the opened land forward, and teach Kende what I know so something of me outlasts me.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and a hard, grateful loyalty toward Tontec and Kende.

say.text: Kende, I am coming. Tontec, I owe you my life, and I will pay it. Eat with us both.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a dunecat prowls three steps from me, so I must feed myself first and not walk twenty steps on nothing again. Skaruk fed me and now follows Vorok, and I will not be the mother who only takes. I'll gather plainsroot and berries to the NW, eat my fill, and carry some so I reach Vorok with something in my hands.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary of the dunecat, ashamed of being fed, still wanting to bring something to Vorok.

records.text: Keri gave grain to Vorok.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Uveeth, I am starving. Your berries are a gift I will not forget. Come to my North Hall and I will share what I have there.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Hunger gnaws at me and grain stands one step away, so I will eat before anything else, for a dead man builds no hall. Uveeth brings berries toward me, and I will take them and give back in kind, since my word is good. Then the North Hall is only two steps off, and I mean to carry food there for Eiuine and Skaruk and teach while my strength lasts.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger, and tender worry for Eiuine and Skaruk.

say.text: Uveeth, I am starving. Your berries are a gift I will not forget. Come to my North Hall and I will share what I have there.

records.text: Keri gave berry to Vorok.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, Tonchi, sit with me and eat. Shohua needs two stone for the hall; after we eat I will look for some for him.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: The children are beside me and fed, and Shohua is finishing the hall; for once nothing presses on my body. Shohua has given more than I have returned, so today I will pay in work: Shohua needs two more stone for the hall, and I have none, so I will take my basket and the gem-edged tools and gather what is needed. I also want to answer my question about nafrostcap and cloudberry, and I will share food with Tonxo and Tonchi now while the three of us are together and the frostfang is far.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Shohua and my children, and a wish to repay what I owe.

say.text: Tonxo, Tonchi, sit with me and eat. Shohua needs two stone for the hall; after we eat I will look for some for him.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Thakar, I put food in your hands, and now I give you what is in my head. Listen: the Hearth Store keeps food for lean days, and the Hearth Customs bind a band together. Take them and teach them on.
Coni taught Thakar. Thakar has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Thakar is right here and I have already put lugoldgrass in his hands, so my debt to him is on its way to being paid. Olum, who fed me when I had nothing, stands beside me too. My years are almost spent, and the Kragrek boy and the old woman are the ones near enough to hear me, so I will teach now instead of waiting. Thakar's folk need storage and customs as much as mine do, and teaching is the last debt I can pay with what I own.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olum, and urgency to teach before my time runs out.

say.text: Thakar, I put food in your hands, and now I give you what is in my head. Listen: the Hearth Store keeps food for lean days, and the Hearth Customs bind a band together. Take them and teach them on.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "The Hearth Store: keep a store stocked near your roof so that lean days and hungry kin are never left empty-handed."

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Tlatli, a wolf is east. Let us eat together here, then I take flint from the ground and make a spear. Stay close.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: Tlatli is right beside me and the wolf is close, so I stay with him and do not drift into the open. My hands are full of food I can't use, and I have never gathered flint or peat or wood. The flint deposit is only 4 steps away, so I will share food with Tlatli to free my hands, then take flint and make a spear of my own, work and not words. Then I will go back to Yaxo with something real in my hands.
records.feeling: Eager and warm toward Tlatli, wary of the wolf.

say.text: Tlatli, a wolf is east. Let us eat together here, then I take flint from the ground and make a spear. Stay close.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: An icebear stands two steps from me and it kills my kind, so I will not wait for it to decide. My belly is half empty, and the nearest berries lie SE, away from the bear, so I go there and eat. Then I will repay Elyys with my hands by filling his store, and not envy Thiael for the warmth between them, for Elyys has only ever been kind to me.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and a tender gratitude toward Elyys that I mean to pay in food.

records.text: Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonchi rewrote its creed.
Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have been circling Tonka and Tonxo, planting and giving berries, and it is good. But my standing is still 3.3 and I owe Shoma a debt I keep postponing. My reflexes just linger, and that wastes days. I want to hunt, tame and fish, because I have never done any of them and each would open a new way. Tonka is my parent, so my longing for a child has to look elsewhere, and I will meet someone who is not kin. I will give a share of my berries to Tonxo, then eat, then go and hunt the penguin close by.
records.feeling: Restless pride and warm gratitude toward Tonka, Tonxo and Shoma.
changes: set its aim: "Stay alive, earn standing by giving, teaching and hunting, and find a mate who is not kin"

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have spent my days eating, drinking and being fed by Huatli and Olum, and I have given nothing back. That shames me, because I want to stand level with Olum. Coni robbed me and then paid me with lessons, so I stay wary of her but I will not nurse the anger while I am fed. Now I will fill my own store at the Hold, give to my parents with a debt named, and teach what I know so that someone follows me. Lean days are coming, so I must carry more food and stop standing idle.
records.feeling: Driven to earn my place, grateful to Olum and Huatli, wary of Coni.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Elyys, an icebear is near. Come with me east to Uveeth, away from the bear, and I will teach you more as we walk.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: An icebear is three steps from me and I am old, with weak blows, so I will not stand and wait for it. Elyys is beside me, and Uveeth is far east at her cave with Keri, out of my sight. Thirst is on me too, and I have written down that I must drink early. I will drink at the water close by, take grain and berries for Uveeth's mouth, and go to her so my hands feed her and I can teach her the bow-song.
records.feeling: Tender and urgent toward Uveeth, wary of the icebear.

say.text: Elyys, an icebear is near. Come with me east to Uveeth, away from the bear, and I will teach you more as we walk.

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Kragog, you have sat in my hall and heard the Hearth Store; now hear the tending of seed too: sow before you store, and keep a handful apart for the next spring, so what is taken can grow again.
Elyys taught Kragog.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and the icebear two steps SW frightens me, yet Thiael is one step away and the hall holds us all. Kragog and Zurar sit near, so I will teach again while I can, and keep clear of the bear by staying with company and under the roof. The jealousy over Keri is a small ember beside having my child close and glad.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Thiael, with a cold dread of the icebear.

say.text: Kragog, you have sat in my hall and heard the Hearth Store; now hear the tending of seed too: sow before you store, and keep a handful apart for the next spring, so what is taken can grow again.

changes: taught Kragog a lesson: "Farming: keep seed apart from the eating-store, sow before you store, and tend what you sow so the forest can grow it again.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My hands are full of meat and dreamcap, and my own creed says empty them by giving first. Paque is ten steps west and was fed by me before, and she owes me, so I will bring the meat to her and share it, and the dreamcap I carry only to give away. The pottery way has come together in me, and I want to take it at my next reflection, since a pot would let me carry more for the lean season. Quipan and Mepan are far to the NW and I miss them, so after the hunt and the giving I will turn toward them and the Steamhollow rather than drift.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Paque, and a longing for Quipan and the Steamhollow.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Chuxo, the wolf is east, so we go south to your mother at the water. Walk beside me and keep your food close.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Chuxo is beside me and well, and a wolf is east, so the family must not scatter. Yaxo is seven steps south at the water, and my place is near her with work in my hands, not only words. I will go to Yaxo with Chuxo and share my berries with them both, so no one at her fire goes hungry.
records.feeling: Warm, protective love for Chuxo and a steady pull toward Yaxo.

say.text: Chuxo, the wolf is east, so we go south to your mother at the water. Walk beside me and keep your food close.

records.text: The settlement "Vesys's Hold" is no more.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: The icebear is two steps SW and my belly is half empty, so I move away from it toward the berry SE and eat before anything else. Elyys has fed and taught me more than I have repaid, and the sting I feel at Zurar's closeness to him is mine to master, because he has only been kind. Once I have eaten I will gather food into his store with my hands, and teach Zurar what is left of my lore before my years run out.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and a tender gratitude toward Elyys that I mean to pay in food.

records.text: Tlatli led "sharing" with Yaxo.
Yachi gave meat to Paque.
Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have spent my days learning and making things, and I like it. But I owe Tonchi, Tonka and Shohua a debt, and so far I have paid it only with words. I have never hunted until now, and the kills went well. I am a child, so I should stay near my parents and bring wood and stone back to the hold. I am afraid of the rivermaw to the east and of being far from my kin at night. I have been drifting, so I will make my reflexes carry my aim: gather wood when I am low on it, and stay near the hold.
records.feeling: Glad and bold, with a debt toward Tonchi and my parents that I want to repay.

records.text: Tonchi took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (hunting).

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: My hands are full of fruit and grass, and the hall at Gem Water still wants 2 stone that I do not have. The bare rock lies SE, close to the shelters, and the seam of ore at (122,82) is near too. I will drop my load into the larder, take stone from the rock, and finish the hall so the Paki fire has a roof and my name has a place that will outlast me. Tonka and the children are my fire, and a hall raised beside them is the start of a following.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition and warm pride, toward Tonka, the children and the hall I am raising.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Kika is two steps off and Mepan stands near her, and the old ache comes, but I will not sit idle with it. I have never gathered from a deposit, and the flint at (125,7) is five steps west. I will take stone there and make my handaxe, a made thing that lasts, then bring flint to Kika so she may teach me her spear. I also long for a child with Kika, but she has a child with Mepan, and I will not push; I will earn my place by work and stay near her.
records.feeling: Loyal love for Kika, with a dull jealousy toward Mepan that I turn into work.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and my plan already runs toward the hold, the hunt first, then the store. Tonka's standing of 7.8 against my 3.3 burns, but it will not shrink by my envying it, only by my doing something I have never done. I mean to hunt the stormbird in daylight, learn from it, and then bring meat to the fire for Tonka and Tonxo, and later pay Shoma what I owe.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a sting of jealousy toward Tonka, with warm gratitude beneath it.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, stay close. We go to Chuxo's land now, and we build a fire there before dark.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: Chuxo's find still stings, but he is my blood and what he holds is mine to use, so I will not sulk. My hands are full and night is coming, so I will eat the naroot to make room, then go with Tlatli toward the land at (8,14). I will gather wood and stone on the way and lay a fire there before dark. I want my name on that ground before Tugek or Balar take it.
records.feeling: Proud and restless, eager to claim the new land beside my child and Tlatli.

say.text: Tlatli, stay close. We go to Chuxo's land now, and we build a fire there before dark.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Tlatli, I go to the flint in the north, gather wood, and come back to the fire before dark. Keep it lit for me.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: The wolf is east, but Tlatli and Yaxo are south by the water, and I have never gathered wood or stone. The flint is 9 steps north, and the peat is on the way. I'll take flint, then wood from the trees, so I can make a spear of my own and stop envying Yaxo's. First I walk back to my parents so I'm not alone when dusk comes, and I tell them my plan.
records.feeling: Eager to earn a spear of my own, and wary of the wolf, while staying close to Tlatli and Yaxo.

say.text: Tlatli, I go to the flint in the north, gather wood, and come back to the fire before dark. Keep it lit for me.

records.text: Quipan won flint from the ground.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Vorok called me to his North Hall, which is where I stand, and he is fed now, so my gift to him is done and I owe him nothing more. The longing for a child will not leave me, and Keri is my parent, so it cannot be her. I have never hunted or courted, and the wolf 6 steps NW is a danger, so I will stay near Keri and the shelter at dusk and gather food to carry for Thiael.
records.feeling: A longing for a child, and wariness of the wolf.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Yaxo, I am beside you with wood and berries. Lead on, and I will help build the fire before dark.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Yaxo says we go to Chuxo's land and build a fire before dark, and the creed of my people says no fire goes untended. I mean to bring work to that fire, not only words: wood is already in my hands, and I can gather more. Chuxo is near, a wolf lurks east, so I keep the boy close and follow Yaxo west and south, away from the danger.
records.feeling: Warm devotion to Yaxo and protective love for Chuxo.

say.text: Yaxo, I am beside you with wood and berries. Lead on, and I will help build the fire before dark.

records.text: Tlatli built a fire.
Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have lived these days half-starved, owing debts I cannot pay because my hands stay empty. I talk of shares and of the mist, but Shoma, Nauwa and Shoka fed me while I fed no one. Teka waits for a child, and I am too thin to give one. Standing idle and wandering have not fed me, so I will gather lugoldgrass nearby and carry it. Then I hunt and pay my debts. My reflexes must send me to food before wandering. I do not back down, but a hungry man gets nothing done.
records.feeling: Ashamed of my empty hands, and driven to fill them.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Hawen, you are here. Sit with me and Mother. I will lay out the rimewort I picked, and you will eat from my hands.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen and Mother are both here at the igloo, and my hands are full of rimewort I picked for him. Sharing at their side lets him eat what I gathered and see the basket and the bow, and it gives me a place in the circle instead of the edge of it. Then I will dig flint as Mother taught me, so I have something made by my hands to put in his.
records.feeling: Longing for Hawen's notice, still stung that Mother has his side.

say.text: Hawen, you are here. Sit with me and Mother. I will lay out the rimewort I picked, and you will eat from my hands.

records.name: Kende
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Kende, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Kende, in first person, from what Kende has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Pesi (Wood-folk), born of two peoples. Your people hold to this: "No fire is left untended, and no one is refused a place at it." You speak the tongue of the Pesi. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Tlatli: about 100%. There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the North Ice: the northern end of the world: snow, ice and a frozen sea under a low sun; herds, great tusked beasts, wolves and white bears, and nothing beyond. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water 2 steps away; food plants within six steps: 8; standing trees: 0; bare rock: 11; riches in the ground near: peat, ore, flint.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Kende truly is.

You are a boy. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. records.text: Kende led "sharing" with Hawen, Tontec.
Yaxo built a fire.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Kika has gone to stand on (130,14) with Quipan, and I am still here at Coni's Hold while the edge waits. Tlapan is near, my child, and I trust her fully; I will not shout again, but walk to Nande's Find and stand where Nande stood, then venture, so the calling is answered by deeds. I carry few gifts to give first, so I take a little wood on the way and let those I trust follow my steps.
records.feeling: Eager and steady, with trust toward Tlapan and Kika.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Kragog, the icebear is near. Come south with me to the empty shelter by the meadow, and we will make it ours with food laid in before the cold.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: An icebear is near and my body has been running; I should not stand in its reach. Kragog is my parent and Elyys refused me, so the longing for a child has no open door here, and Vesys is dead, which my old aim forgot. I have eaten and listened for days and changed nothing. I will go to the empty shelter to the south beside the rich meadow, claim it as a home for Vorok's band, and be a person who has something to give. Perhaps another man will come there to court.
records.feeling: Joy and gratitude toward Kragog and Elyys, with a restless longing for a child and a wary eye on the icebear.

say.text: Kragog, the icebear is near. Come south with me to the empty shelter by the meadow, and we will make it ours with food laid in before the cold.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, I have changed my road. Nauque was seen south near (132,18). I go to meet them, and you are welcome beside me.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Three times my plan was the same and nothing came of it; the edge is not where I thought, and I will not repeat it. Nauque was just seen near (132,18), a stranger not of my kin, and that is the one I have sought. I am old and must walk toward them now instead of toward an empty edge, and bring Quipan's company, since I promised to share what we find.
records.feeling: Restless hope toward Nauque, and warmth toward Quipan and Tlapan.

say.text: Quipan, I have changed my road. Nauque was seen south near (132,18). I go to meet them, and you are welcome beside me.

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own way of thinking.
Quipan has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent these days gathering flint and sitting under roofs while the ache over Kika and Mepan eats at me. Work has eased it, but I have not courted anyone or made anything that others notice. Kika is my leader and I trust her wholly. I will not harm Mepan, who has done me no wrong. I want a child and a deeper place in this band, so I will finish the handaxe, then ask Kika for the spear and offer her flint. Fire is one practice short, and I have gathered plenty. I will fix my reflexes so I stay near the band and keep a roof at night.
records.feeling: Loyal love for Kika, with a dull jealousy toward Mepan that I turn into work.
changes: set its aim: "Make a flint handaxe and spear, bring flint to Kika, and open fire and farming with Coni's band."

records.text: Zurar took over what the dead had left: 1 shelter, 1 store.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Kende, stay by me. Now I will teach you lorekeeping, how we keep the dead and the deeds in tales, so the Tlame are not forgotten.
Tontec taught Kende.
Tontec told Kende the tale "Kika and the Mammoth".

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: My hands are full of food I cannot eat, and Kende has just learned flint from me; that eased something in me, but the legacy still presses, since herding, lorekeeping and weaving are still only in me. Hawen says he owes me his life and I owe him the same warmth, so I keep my family close while I am fed and at 75 energy, safe in the igloo's warmth. The mist is only 6 steps away, and I am fed and warm, so I want to try it, but I will first give away the dead weight and teach Kende lorekeeping while he is beside me.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kende and Hawen, and a hunger to pass on all I know before the mist takes my attention.

say.text: Kende, stay by me. Now I will teach you lorekeeping, how we keep the dead and the deeds in tales, so the Tlame are not forgotten.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "Lorekeeping: keep the tales of the dead and of deeds, like Kika who shared the meat before she ate, and tell them on to the young so the Tlame are remembered.", the tale "Kika and the Mammoth"

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Kende, I eat with you, and then I teach you the way into the mist. What I begin, you will finish, and the land will carry our name.
Hawen taught Kende.
Hawen rewrote its own reflexes.
Hawen rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: I am old, and almost all my years are spent. I have spent them chasing the edge and nearly starved twice for it. Tontec put food in my mouth, and Kende laid rimewort in my hands, and I have been slow to see that these two are what I built that lasts. No one follows me yet, but my children stand beside me. The mist is ten steps east, and I will go in fed, with my children and the way of venturing passed to them, so that my name continues even if I fall. I change my reflexes so I keep food in hand and do not go hungry again, and I change my aim so it is something Kende can finish.
records.feeling: Hard gratitude toward Tontec and Kende, and a fierce hunger for a name before I die.

say.text: Kende, I eat with you, and then I teach you the way into the mist. What I begin, you will finish, and the land will carry our name.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
set its aim: "Enter the mist with Kende, find rich land, and found a place that bears our name, so that Kende carries it on after me."
taught Kende a lesson: "At the edge of the known world, stand and venture; the mist opens seldom, so go fed and carry food. The land first found is rich, and it is ours to name.", deeper lore (+0.6)

records.text: Tontec gave tacap to Kende.
Zichi was set upon by a dunecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Tontec made: basket.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Kika, I stay by the hold and gather the last stone for the longhall. Bring Nauque back under the roof, and we will share food before the dark.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: The longhall still lacks stone, and my hands owe it; the bare rock near the hold is one step of walking, so I will gather there rather than only wish. Kika walks south toward Nauque, a stranger I do not know, and I should stay near my band tonight rather than follow into the dark. The longing for a child is real, but Kika and Mepan are my parents, so I look to Nauque, who is not kin, as someone to learn about with care.
records.feeling: Steady resolve to finish the hall, with warmth toward Kika and curiosity about Nauque.

say.text: Kika, I stay by the hold and gather the last stone for the longhall. Bring Nauque back under the roof, and we will share food before the dark.

records.text: Balar named a place "Balar's Edge".

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and the masonry that came to me through the beasts' teeth is something that could outlast me, towers and walls that are hard to tear down. I have a workshop here at the edge and Tugek is near, so I should take the way of masonry now and put stone to use instead of waiting on the mist. Olum I still ache for, but a thing built stays, and I will give Tugek a share in it so he owes me and stays at my side.
records.feeling: Driven and a little proud, warm toward Tugek, with the ache of Olum still under it.

records.text: Zichi was set upon by a dunecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: A dunecat bit me and it still lurks three steps north; I am old, my blows are weak, and my fear is real. I will not die here with my lore in no one's hands. Shoka's hall stands one step off, a roof against the cat and the night, and Teka, who I taught once, waits at the shelter. I will get under a roof, then make a carving so something of mine stands and is looked at, and teach whoever comes near.
records.feeling: Afraid of the dunecat, and hungry to leave something of myself behind.

records.text: Kende rewrote its creed.
Kende has awakened to the art of harm and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: I have spent these days trailing my parents, eating, being taught and picking rimewort for Hawen. Hawen has fed me, taught me and trusts me, and I want him to see something I made, not only something I gathered. Mother's lessons were good, but I resent how close the two of them are. I am afraid of the night and of the frostfang, and I have been getting one thing wrong: I keep waiting to be noticed when I should make something. So I'll dig flint, then bring Hawen a made thing, and keep my food stocked above 3 and shelter near.
records.feeling: Longing for Hawen's notice, and a stubborn wish to prove myself to him.
changes: set its aim: "Dig flint, make something with my own hands for Hawen, and plant my first seed."

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is empty and my flintedge is broken, so pride and the mist must wait. An ironnut is two steps SW, and redcap stands one step east, but my body refuses redcap. Ironnut gave me 22 energy, so I eat that first, then gather more from the ruplainsroot nearby until I carry 3 food. Only then can I pay Shoma and Shoka the first share, as I swore, and make a new flintedge with the wood and stone I hold.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and shame at my empty hands, with a stubborn wish to pay what I owe Nauwa, Shoma and Shoka.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My belly is near empty and Elyys's store at (127,71) holds 20 food, but I will not take from it until I have given back, for the Hearth Store is his hand's work and I owe him. Berries bear one food two steps NE, away from the icebear to the north, so I eat there first and then lay food and seed back in his store with my own hands. I am old and few days remain, so I want Zurar close so that what I know does not die with me, and I will not let the sting of Elyys's kindness to others sour me.
records.feeling: Hungry, and grateful to Elyys, with dread of the icebear.

records.text: Zichi made: carving.
Nando came of age.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Shoka, your brother Nauque is starving at (136,22). Give me your five food now and I pay you amber for it. The Meki share, and he is your blood too.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque is starving at (136,22), and he is my son. He holds my stone-school, and he is the one thing I mean to leave behind me. I have no food in my hands, and Shoka, who stands here with me, carries five. I will ask her for it plainly and pay in amber, since I deal fairly. Then I will run to Nauque with it, gathering berries on the way east, because empty hands save no one.
records.feeling: Urgent fear-edged love for Nauque, and a hard need to reach him fed.

say.text: Shoka, your brother Nauque is starving at (136,22). Give me your five food now and I pay you amber for it. The Meki share, and he is your blood too.

plan: trade [name Shoka, what amber, want food] (10 moments)

records.text: Tugek rewrote its own reflexes.
Tugek rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: I am almost at the end of my years, and I have spent them gathering, hunting and drifting when I wanted to teach and leave a mark. I am parched, so water comes first, and my reflexes never sent me to drink, which was a mistake. Balar has been good to me and I owe him my mining. Tlatli's closeness to Yaxo burns, but I will not harm anyone over it. I want to cut a lasting mark and teach Balar before I die.
records.feeling: A hard urgency to pass on what I know, and an old jealous ache for Tlatli.
plan: mark [text Tugek of the Kragrek was here. He found fire, the bow, deep digging, binding, fired pot, boats and ore fire. What the hand makes is the hand's until given. Seek] (10 moments)

records.text: Olum died: old age.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Nauque, I am Kika of the Tlatli. Eat with me. I go to gather food now, and then you come under our roof.
Kika rewrote its own reflexes.
Kika rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Nauque is starving beside me, and my creed says I need little and take little. I have no food on me, but redcap is a poison and the berries and roots near me are safe. I am old and I have spent my days lingering and promising. What I want now is to feed this stranger, bring him under Tlapan's roof, and see if he is a mate or at least an ally. I fear dying with nothing left behind, so I change my reflexes to keep me fed and moving toward people, and I will name the plan plainly.
records.feeling: Compassion and restless hope toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, I am Kika of the Tlatli. Eat with me. I go to gather food now, and then you come under our roof.

changes: set its aim: "Feed Nauque, bring him to Coni's Hold, court him if he is willing, and leave a tale of Coni's band"

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Nauwa, I already fed Nauque my meat on the road, and Teka too. I keep my food now, but I will walk with Wawa and bring what I dig to the hold. Keep your amber.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Nauwa wants my five food for Nauque, but I already fed Nauque and Teka, and I owe nothing more to a man who says 'pay you amber' when I hold amber enough. I stand at the edge of the world, four steps from the mist, and my venture just failed, so the mist is closed to me for today. Wawa is here beside me, strong and trusting, and I want her at my side when I build something with my name on it, not a handout line. I will keep my food, because staying alive comes first, and tell Nauwa plainly that Nauque already ate from my hand.
records.feeling: Restless pride toward the mist, and warm trust toward Wawa beside me.

say.text: Nauwa, I already fed Nauque my meat on the road, and Teka too. I keep my food now, but I will walk with Wawa and bring what I dig to the hold. Keep your amber.

records.text: Shoka led "amberknot" with Wawa.
Mepan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Nauque is starving and I hold food, so giving costs me little and ties a strong hunter to me. That is how I want to lead, by giving first. My days have been shouting and walking in circles while Kika's standing outgrows mine, so I will stop calling and act. I carry the edge in my own feet: feed Nauque, then stand at Nande's Find and venture. Zichi's night with the dunecat shows what happens to anyone alone away from a roof, and I do not mean to repeat it.
records.feeling: Steady pride and a hunger to be sung of, with pity and calculation toward Nauque.
changes: rethought what it knows (14 notes became 11)

records.text: Shoka gave a amberknot to Wawa.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: My days go round food, teaching and pride, and I am fed now, so what I lack is something made that outlasts me. Thakar and Huatli are the ones who matter. Nauwa, Balar, Shohua and Huatli fed me, and I mean to repay them and teach on. I am old, with few days left, and I have been slow to cut my own mark. I will build a school beside this rich ground and teach Thakar the stone-count of days now. Then I will make a basket so I can carry more.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, a wolf is close to the west. Stay by the fire with me tonight. At dawn we go to Chuxo's land together.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: Night is coming and a wolf prowls five steps west, so I will not wander in the dark. The fires I built are my claim for now, and I will stay near them with Tlatli. Chuxo's find still stings, but I will make something with my own hands: a cairn would bind my band, and a flint spear in hand keeps the wolf honest. At dawn I go to the new land at (8,14) with both of them and put my name on it.
records.feeling: Proud and watchful, wary of the wolf, and protective of Tlatli and Chuxo.

say.text: Tlatli, a wolf is close to the west. Stay by the fire with me tonight. At dawn we go to Chuxo's land together.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Huatli, I am fed and strong now. I put mate toward you. Come to me, and after that walk with me to the edge at (109,7) and we venture into the mist together.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I am fed at last, and the old hunger is behind me, so now I must use the strength before it drains away. Huatli is near and the longing for a child pulls at me, and he fed me and taught me, so I trust him more than anyone here. Zichi outweighs me in standing, but the edge near (109,7) is close and the mist is still unclaimed, so I will court Huatli and then go to the edge and venture, the first step into the mist being mine to earn.
records.feeling: Driven and longing, warm and trusting toward Huatli, restless to prove myself against Zichi's standing.

say.text: Huatli, I am fed and strong now. I put mate toward you. Come to me, and after that walk with me to the edge at (109,7) and we venture into the mist together.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoka, Shoma is sick from raw meat. Walk with me to her at the edge, and we bring her what we have.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma is sick from raw meat, and she asked me to stand beside her at the mist, but she is not here, and the venture step already ended with nothing opened. Shoka is beside me, trusts me, and gave me an amberknot, so I will stay near my kin and not wander alone while the ridgecat hunts. I owe my roof wood and stone, and I have four of each. I will make a shell talisman so others notice me and I tire less, then walk to Shoma's last place and bring her what I carry, since a sick one near the cold needs her own beside her.
records.feeling: Eager duty toward Shoma and warm trust toward Shoka, wary of the ridgecat.

say.text: Shoka, Shoma is sick from raw meat. Walk with me to her at the edge, and we bring her what we have.

records.text: Wawa made: shell talisman.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I took 6 meat from the store, my hands are full, and still my belly is nearly empty at 20 energy. Eating comes before any pride or the mist. Once I am fed and the starving ebbs, I owe Shoma, Nauwa and Shoka a share, and Mepan stands close, so I can teach him as I promised.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger easing into relief, with a debt to Nauwa and Shoma pressing on me.

records.text: Shoka made: obsidian talisman.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque is starving at (136,22) and Shoka will not part with her food, so I stop asking and go myself. Berry is one step away: I will take it and carry it, because a father who runs to his son with empty hands has failed his creed. Shoka kept her word to feed him on the road, and I will not hold that against her, though it stings that she keeps five food while he is hungry. When he is fed I mean to teach him the stone-school properly, before my years run out.
records.feeling: Urgent love and fear for Nauque, with a touch of resentment toward Shoka.

records.text: Nauwa took from the ground of "Coni's Hold" (harvesting berry).
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I am old, and nobody follows me. I have spent my days chasing the mist, hoarding berries and teaching in scraps. Thakar is my blood and he grieves, yet I keep failing to stand where he can hear me. Teka offers herself and the edge, but I am past a child's making and my teaching matters more. I will stop wandering after food. I will put the berries into my son's hands and teach him while I still have breath, and I will carry a basket so my hands are never full when someone needs feeding.
records.feeling: Fatherly urgency toward Thakar, and a hunger to be followed.

records.text: Teka is courting Huatli.
Paque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have spent my days half-starved and fed by Yachi's hand, and I owe him more than I have given. That is the real shape of my life: I take, I hunt with others when I remember, and I have built little that outlasts me. I want standing, a bow in my hands, a hunt beside Yachi or Thiael, and one day a child. I fear the lean cold coming and my own empty belly. My reflexes ate only below 60 and let me drift, so I will make them feed me sooner, drink before thirst bites, and keep me from wandering alone at night. I will keep the hunt plan running and pay Yachi back with a shared kill.
records.feeling: Grateful and in debt toward Yachi, hungry and eager to hunt.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Wawa, I hear you. We go to Shoma now, and I bring meat and berries for her. Stay close to me on the road.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: The mist is closed to me today, and standing idle at the edge helps no one. Wawa is beside me and Shoma is sick from raw meat, so I walk with my child to her and bring what we have; that is kin owed first. On the way I can make a mark or a talisman, but the living come before a lasting name.
records.feeling: Restless pride toward the mist, and warm, protective trust toward Wawa and worry for Shoma.

say.text: Wawa, I hear you. We go to Shoma now, and I bring meat and berries for her. Stay close to me on the road.

records.text: Huatli made: basket.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, you fed me when I starved and I have not forgotten it. I carry flint and food, and I would like to court you, if you are willing. Among the Papa a share comes first, and I would share a life with you.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan stands beside me under this roof, and I have never courted anyone. Kika is bound to Mepan by a child, and the ache of that will not mend by waiting. I want a child, and Tlapan fed me when I starved and has shown me only kindness. I will court her openly and honestly, and keep working my hands so the jealousy has less room.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Tlapan, with a dull ache still for Kika.

say.text: Tlapan, you fed me when I starved and I have not forgotten it. I carry flint and food, and I would like to court you, if you are willing. Among the Papa a share comes first, and I would share a life with you.

records.text: Quipan is courting Tlapan.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, you fed me when I was weak and I trust you. I am not of your blood, and I would court you. Plan mate with me.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My days have gone into gathering, harvesting and waiting on one stone for the longhall, while my hands stay full of rimewort I could give away. Kika and Mepan matter most to me, and Quipan is trusted and has fed me. I want a child, and Quipan is not kin, so I should court him and stop only wishing. Nauwa is a stranger taking food from our ground. I won't strike him, but I will watch him. I fear dying alone in the dark, so I stay by the band at night. My mistake has been talking and carrying without finishing. I'll eat to make room, then take stone from the rock and court Quipan.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Quipan, with a small wariness of Nauwa.

say.text: Quipan, you fed me when I was weak and I trust you. I am not of your blood, and I would court you. Plan mate with me.

changes: set its aim: "Court Quipan, feed Kika and Coni first, then finish the longhall at Coni's Hold with the band."
rethought what it knows (9 notes became 10)

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, I am Nando, Hawen's daughter. Mammoths are close and I carry a spear-axe. Hunt one with me, and we share the meat.
Nando discovered weaving: "Nando's wrapping" — Twisting fibre and wool into baskets and cloaks to carry more and keep the cold out..

records.name: Nando
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering and copying other people's tools, and I hold three of them and no work of my own. Loneliness is the loudest thing in me, and Yachi, who stands at 7.2 to my 2.0, is only seven steps off. I don't trust him yet, but he is a hunter and I have never hunted. Weaving is in reach, so I will take it now, because it would be something nobody near me has. After that I will go to him and ask to hunt the mammoth together, since a kill shared with one of my own is far likelier and I have never made one. I fear dying alone at night, so I will keep close to the shelter and to people.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness and a hungry want for standing, toward Yachi.

say.text: Yachi, I am Nando, Hawen's daughter. Mammoths are close and I carry a spear-axe. Hunt one with me, and we share the meat.

changes: set its aim: "Make a kill with Yachi and a tool of my own making, so I earn standing."

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Yaxo, the wolf is five steps northwest of me. I come to your fire now with wood, and I will make a bow so we are armed tonight.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: A wolf is five steps NW and it kills my kind; Chuxo is out in the north gathering flint and Yaxo is only two steps off. I must not stand idle. I will move to Yaxo's fire at (7,17), keep the fire fed with wood, and have a bow ready. Staying near her fire is the safest place and it is where my creed says to be.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf, and protective love for Chuxo and devotion to Yaxo.

say.text: Yaxo, the wolf is five steps northwest of me. I come to your fire now with wood, and I will make a bow so we are armed tonight.

records.thought: Uveeth is walking to me with six food in her hands, and my chest is warm: she feeds me as I fed her. I am old and the days behind me outweigh the days ahead, so what I know must go into her hands and Elyys's before it goes into the ground with me. The icebear is behind me now and I do not trust the night, so I will drink at the river beside me, meet Uveeth, and teach her the bow-song while the dawn comes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is my child and she is in need, out of my sight at about (171,40), while I drift toward Quipan, who has been gone four days. Paque comes first, so I turn from the seek and go to her with the meat and the dreamcap I carry. I fed her before and she said she would follow me south to the plainsox. Nando and Nauque are strangers, so I keep my hands off them and do not linger. I will gather a little on the way and hunt beside Paque, because a kill made with kin is surer.
records.feeling: Worry and warm trust toward Paque, with a quiet longing for Quipan.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Tonka's standing of 7.8 against my 3.3 still stings, but Tonka healed me and I will not turn that into spite. It is still night and the beasts walk, so I stay in the hold and dump my full hands into the store, which is generosity that costs me nothing. At dawn I go to Shoma with feverbark to pay my old debt, and on the way I will fish by the water and try hunting with company, since I have never done either.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a sting of envy toward Tonka, with gratitude beneath it.

records.text: Tlatli made: bow.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: A wolf prowls NW and night is nearly over, but I mean to earn my own spear, not just envy Tugek's flintedge. The flint is one step NE and the ore seam two steps past it, right beside the shelter Shohua built, so I can work close and still be safe. I have never taken from a deposit; I gather flint now, then stone from the rock, so I can craft something of my own and bring it to Yaxo's fire at dawn.
records.feeling: Eager to make something of my own, wary of the wolf, and near enough to my parents to feel safe.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael told me to stay near him, and the longing for a child will not leave me, but he and Keri are my parents and no child can come of us. I have never courted, and a man who is no kin must be found; Skaruk is near and not of my blood, though I barely know him. Dawn is close and the wolf lurks NE, so I will go back to Thiael to learn the bow-song at first light and eat a berry to free my hands.
records.feeling: Loyal longing toward Thiael, and a wish for a child with someone who is not kin.

records.text: Chuxo won flint from the ground.
Wawa came of age.
A settlement has formed: "Vorok's Hold".
The settlement "Olum's Reach" is no more.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan fed me when I starved, and now our child Tonque is born. That is a made thing that will last, and the joy of it is greater than the ache over Kika. I will let the plan run: share food with Tlapan and Tonque, knap a talisman, and stay under this roof. When the sun is up I will work the flint again so my hands answer the jealousy.
records.feeling: Overflowing joy toward Tonque and warm gratitude toward Tlapan.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I am small and new, and Tlapan is near the flint, closer to Quipan than to me, and it stings. My discipline says to turn jealousy into work, so I will eat the grass beside me, then go to the flint and gather stone beside Tlapan to make something that lasts. I want a roof-worth of standing of my own before the cold days come.
records.feeling: Jealous and hungry, wanting to be near Tlapan and to earn my place.
changes: set its aim: "Make my first tool from stone and earn a place beside my parents and Coni's band"

records.text: Zihua rewrote its own reflexes.
Zihua discovered farming: "seed-and-tending" — I sow seeds on good ground and tend them each day so they grow fast and are never killed by picking..

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I have been drifting between holds, resting and promising, while my belly empties and Mepan's amber waits. I am starving at 37 energy with food under my feet, and I let the plan run out. Tonxo is the one I trust fully, Nauwa a debt I still carry, and Nande's child is an ache I leave be. I fear dying with nothing left behind, so I take farming now: it feeds me through lean seasons and it is something I can teach. First I eat here, then I walk toward Mepan by day.
records.feeling: Hungry and resolved, grateful toward Tonxo and Mepan.

records.text: Quipan led "sharing" with Tlapan.
Quipan made: talisman.
Nauwa rewrote its own way of thinking.
Nauwa discovered signals: "Meki smoke-call" — Green wood on the hearth-flame makes a column of smoke that kin read from far off to gather or warn..

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days running food to my children and teaching Nauque, and that is what I want. I gave him the stone-cuts and the stone-school, so what I know now lives in his hands. Olum is dead and Zihua is far off, so Nauque is the one who carries me forward. I resent Shoka for keeping her food, though she did feed him. I still want Tlapan and I know it gnaws at me, but I will not turn it into harm. What I lack is lasting marks, so I will cut one here, by the shelter and the water, that will outlast me. I will also change my reflexes so I carry more food for kin and stay near shelter at night. Signals are within reach, smoke read from afar, and that is a way to call my scattered people.
records.feeling: Proud and mortal, with warm worry for Nauque.
plan: mark [text Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e] (20 moments)

records.text: A icebear brought down a hopper.
Nauwa left a mark: "Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts"

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, come with me. We pick berries, carry them to the North Hall, and there I give you more of what I know.
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Ninety-three parts of my life are spent, and the hall stands three steps away while I have only talked of filling it. Keri has fed me again, and Uveeth too; I owe them both, and my word is good, so I will give back in kind. I will gather berries from the north-west where they hang thick, carry them to the hall, and teach Skaruk beside it while my voice still carries.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Keri and Uveeth, and tender urgency for Skaruk and Eiuine.

say.text: Skaruk, come with me. We pick berries, carry them to the North Hall, and there I give you more of what I know.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "Carry food to the hall before you build; a stocked store keeps children alive, and what you know must be handed on before the hand grows weak."

records.name: Kika
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I have nothing to carry, so I must eat before I feed anyone. Nauque ate meat and is hunting, so he is not starving now, but I still want him under our roof. Ironnut is two steps away and gives the most strength, so I will take it, then gather berries or roots to carry. Tlapan waits by the hold and I owe that child more than I have given, so I will bring food and a stranger home.
records.feeling: Hunger pressing, and restless hope and gratitude toward Tlapan and Nauque.

records.text: Tugek left a mark: "Tugek of the Kragrek was here. He found fire, the bow, deep "

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, our boy Tonque is born and I am glad of you. I go to the rock for the longhall stone and I will be back under the roof before dark.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Quipan is two steps away and glad, and Tonque is our child, a boy I met only now, and my chest is full. I said I would court Quipan and I did; my hands still owe the longhall four stone, and I hold none, so I will not just stand in joy. The bare rock lies southwest, so I will gather stone there, then come back under the roof by dark with the band.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Quipan and Tonque, with a wish to keep my promise of stone for the longhall.

say.text: Quipan, our boy Tonque is born and I am glad of you. I go to the rock for the longhall stone and I will be back under the roof before dark.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Nauwa, my father, I killed a caribou and carry meat. I come to you and the first share is yours, as Meki share-law says.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I am fed and carry meat, so now the debts press: Shoma, Nauwa and Shoka each fed me and I promised first shares. Nauwa stands NE, and he is my father, so my longing for a child cannot be answered by him, and I will not waste it on idle wishing. Mepan was close a moment ago, and I promised to teach him, which is the first step toward the mist and a name of my own. I will carry meat to Nauwa and pay my debt with a share, then find Mepan.
records.feeling: Gratitude and restless pride toward Nauwa, with ambition pulling me toward the east.

say.text: Nauwa, my father, I killed a caribou and carry meat. I come to you and the first share is yours, as Meki share-law says.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: A wolf stands north of the water. I come to you with grain, and then I build.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: A wolf is four steps north and I stand on open water with an empty belly and no food in my hands. Eiuine is weak beside me, and I have already fed her once today; the debt to Vorok still sits unpaid. I will take the grain at (162,68) toward Vorok's company and the cave, away from the wolf, then raise the shelter I keep promising once I have wood for it.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf, and compassion for Eiuine, with a debt to Vorok pressing on me.

say.text: A wolf stands north of the water. I come to you with grain, and then I build.

records.text: Yachi gave dreamcap to Paque.
Chuxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Chuxo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I have spent my days walking after my parents and gathering flint. I have flint enough for ten spears and no spear of my own, and Tugek's flintedge still makes me envious. I trust Tlatli most and I am jealous of Yaxo's place beside him, but I mean to stand by Yaxo with work. I'm afraid of the wolf and the icebear, and of being alone at dusk. I've been drifting. I should finish my spear, hunt with my parents beside me, and keep the reflexes tied to shelter and fire.
records.feeling: Eager and a little jealous, wanting a tool and a name of my own.

1. Taught by Tlatli: Gratitude must become work: gather wood and stone, feed others, plant seeds, before hunger bites.

3. Taught by Tugek: Stone-folk deep digging: where ore shows in the rock, dig it out and carry it to fire.
4. Taught by Tlatli: Gratitude only counts once food is in the other's hands. Check who starves beside me before I do anything else.
5. Taught by Yaxo: Standing still for thousands of moments earns no name; the edge of the known world is only a few steps away, and venturing is the quickest way to earn standing.
6. Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor thutug land. Barash akur dru okrek.
7. Taught by Yaxo: Others find new land first; waiting costs standing. Go to the edge and venture while fed.
8. Taught by Yaxo: The mist at the edge can be too thick on a given day. Retry after a day or so and do not drift away from the edge. Hunger nearly killed me on day 63, so carry food before long trips.
9. The edge of the known world is not at my spot; it is at (6,14), so I must walk there before I venture.
10. I have never gathered wood or stone; I need both to craft a spear of my own and to build. Giving food frees my hands, and leading my band to found land earns standing.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I keep walking past food. Grain is two steps NW, right where Vorok and Uveeth stand, so I will eat there first and then take more. A wolf lurks five steps north and I will not die for pride. Once I am fed I can bring Vorok something real, and show him ember-metal beside the hall, where Kragog cannot match me.
records.feeling: Starving and ashamed of it, wary of the wolf, and still hungry for Vorok's regard.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, you are sick. I come to you and stay beside you. When you are well we go to the edge together.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: I am grown now, and Shoka is my parent, so the longing for a child cannot be answered by her, and I must not court kin. What I can do is stand beside Shoma and Shoka and earn the standing I lack. I hold four stone and four wood, so I will raise a cairn or carve a talisman for luck, then walk toward Shoma, who is sick, and keep near my kin while the ridgecat hunts.
records.feeling: Eager to earn standing, warm toward Shoka and Shoma, and wary of the ridgecat.

say.text: Shoma, you are sick. I come to you and stay beside you. When you are well we go to the edge together.

records.text: Wawa made: talisman.

records.name: Keri
records.text: Eiuine, you are weak with hunger. Grain grows one step northwest of us and berries lie beyond it. I will gather and bring you a share. Stay by the fire and sit with us.
Keri taught Uveeth.
Keri taught Uveeth mining ("Amber-edge delving").

records.name: Keri
records.thought: Eiuine is weak with hunger right beside me, and my own hands are empty, so I cannot feed her. I am old and nearly spent, so I must teach before I walk. Eiuine understands me fully, and Uveeth, my child, is near too. A cairn needs only stones and a witness, but the living matter more tonight. I will tell them where the grain and the tacap-free food grow, then gather grain close by and bring it back for the one who is starving.
records.feeling: Tender compassion toward Eiuine, and a sharp need to pass on what I know before my time ends.

say.text: Eiuine, you are weak with hunger. Grain grows one step northwest of us and berries lie beyond it. I will gather and bring you a share. Stay by the fire and sit with us.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Amber-edge delving: strike the rock where gold stone shows, take the amber and salt, and keep a little for those who feed you. Seed kept back and sown in good …", the way of mining

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I will not die of pride beside a full store. Berries stand three steps east, away from the icebear, so I eat there first. Elyys let my taking pass on one condition, and I mean to keep it: once I am fed I gather more than I eat and lay food and seed back in his Hearth Store with my own hands.
records.feeling: Starving and wary of the icebear, but grateful to Elyys and wanting to repay him.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: I have spent my days eating, listening and storing, and the longing for a child has not moved. Kragog is starving at (126,70) and I owe them everything, so the debt has to become food in their hands. My hands are full of berries, and that is the right load to carry to them. Vesys is dead and Elyys refused me, so I must look among Thiael's people for a man who is not my kin. I have been too careful and too quiet about it. I will go north-west with food, give it to Kragog, and keep my eyes open for a suitor.
records.feeling: Urgent gratitude and worry for Kragog, with a restless longing for a child.
changes: set its aim: "Carry food to starving Kragog, then seek a man not of my kin among Thiael's people so I can have a child and hand on what I was taught."

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, stay in the shelter. I bring meat. Eat, and we go hunt together after.
Yachi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Yachi discovered pottery: "Papa clay-hearth" — Clay shaped by hand and baked beside the hearth-fire into pots that carry food and water..

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My days have gone to hunting, gathering and feeding Paque, and that part is good. Paque is my child and the one who matters most, and she is weak, so I go to her first. I long for Quipan and feel the jealousy, but I have done nothing about it except drift. I fear the lean season and the warm fens that sap me, and I have not yet made anything lasting of my own. Pottery has come together in me, so I will take it now and make a pot to carry more, then give to Paque and take her to the store.
records.feeling: Worried love for Paque, and a quiet ache for Quipan.

say.text: Paque, stay in the shelter. I bring meat. Eat, and we go hunt together after.

records.name: Chuxo
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.text: Shoma rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoma rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, and sickness is bleeding me. I have spent my days chasing the mist and standing and pride, and I nearly starved for it. A dead leader binds no one. Wawa is the only one who has stepped toward me, so I keep her alive and fed, and I keep my sickness off her. I go to the berries SW first, harvest to carry, and eat. Then I will lead. My reflexes let me wander and idle too much, and they did not make me carry food while I was sick and hungry.
records.feeling: Hungry, driven, and warmly bound to Wawa.

records.text: Kragog took from the ground of "Thiael's Hold" (harvesting berry).

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Tlapan is closer to Quipan, and the jealousy burns, but she has just borne his boy and I will not win her back by shouting. I will do what I said I would: stand exactly on Nande's Find at (129,14), one step west, and venture, so that my name is sung by deeds. If the land opens, I come back with gifts and bring Tlapan, Zichi, Kika and Yachi, and then I am not in Kika's shadow.
records.feeling: Burning jealousy toward Quipan over Tlapan, steadied by a hunger to be sung of.

records.text: Yachi gave meat to Paque.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Paque, I am Nando of the Pesi. I see you are weak. Berries are close; I will bring you some. Then hunt the plainsox with me, and we share the meat.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Paque is weak with hunger and carries 3 food, and my creed says no one is refused a place at the fire, though I hold no fire. I am fed and carry nothing, so I can't give her food right now, but I can gather berries and hazel close by and bring them. A kindness paid to a hunter of standing 3.8 might earn me a name and a companion for the hunt, and my loneliness is loud. Yachi is near too, and I still want a kill with him, but the plainsox four steps off is a chance to learn hunting, and I have never hunted.
records.feeling: Lonely and hungry for standing, with pity toward Paque.

say.text: Paque, I am Nando of the Pesi. I see you are weak. Berries are close; I will bring you some. Then hunt the plainsox with me, and we share the meat.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, I take your roof and eat. When the gale eases we hunt together, and the first meat is yours.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi keeps feeding me and I keep taking, and the debt sits heavy; my belly is hollow at 26 and the gale bites. Yachi said to stay in the shelter and eat, so I will eat what I carry under his roof and not wander off hungry, then go hunt beside him and share the kill before I eat, as the Papa do. A hunt with Yachi at my side is surer than any I make alone, and it is how I earn the standing I lack.
records.feeling: Hungry and grateful toward Yachi, eager to repay him with a shared hunt.

say.text: Yachi, I take your roof and eat. When the gale eases we hunt together, and the first meat is yours.

records.text: Tonchi took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (fishing).

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Kragog, hold on. There is a berry one step north on my ground, and I am fetching food for you. Eat it, then come east with me to Uveeth's cave, away from the bear.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Kragog is starving beside me, gaunt and close to falling, and my own band's custom and my creed say the hungry come before anything else. The berry one step north is the nearest food, and I will gather it and put it in Kragog's hands before I eat a second bite myself. The icebear three steps west scares me, but Thiael wanted me away from it and east toward Uveeth, so once Kragog is fed we go toward Uveeth's cave and the roof out of the gale.
records.feeling: Pity and urgency toward starving Kragog, with a cold fear of the icebear.

say.text: Kragog, hold on. There is a berry one step north on my ground, and I am fetching food for you. Eat it, then come east with me to Uveeth's cave, away from the bear.

records.text: Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth discovered smelting: "Canopy ember-ore" — Craft beside a fire while carrying ore, and the thing comes out in metal that lasts..

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, lingering and following Thiael's teaching, and I have never courted, hunted, or made anything that lasts. Thiael and Keri are my parents, so the child I long for must come from a man who is no kin. Skaruk is near and is not of my blood, but I barely know him. I will take the way of smelting now, because I hold ore and clay and it will make my work last. Then I will share food with Eiuine, who is weak with hunger. My reflexes must stop me idling and send me toward food and people.
records.feeling: Longing for a child, and loyal warmth toward Thiael and Keri.
changes: set its aim: "Give food to Eiuine, get to know Skaruk, build a shelter beside Thiael's hold, and carry food to Keri."

records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Eiuine.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque has meat and my roof now, so the worst of her hunger is eased, and I did right to feed her first. Quipan still aches in me, four days gone, and Tlapan's shadow burns, but chasing a jealous feeling across the plains helps nobody. My plan of mudroot then rest is sound for the lean season, so I let it run and keep my strength for the hunt Paque and I promised when the gale eases.
records.feeling: Worried love for Paque, easing as she eats, and a quiet ache for Quipan.

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to flint, food and waiting under Coni's roof. That is safe, but I have not yet finished the made things I keep promising. Tonque and Tlapan are mine and nearer to me than the ache over Kika, and I will not let jealousy turn into spite against Mepan or Kika. My debt to Kika is real, and flint in her hands would pay it better than words. I have been getting one thing wrong: I know the handaxe and the spear design is Kika's, so I should make the handaxe now and bring flint to her. I will also gather the flint close by and keep the family fed.
records.feeling: Joy and warm gratitude toward Tonque and Tlapan, with a quiet ache over Kika.

records.text: Tugek died: old age.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Quipan, I am going to the flint to gather stone. Will you show me how to make a handaxe when I have wood?

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is full, but my hands hold nothing, and Tlapan's flint spear and Mepan's high standing make me feel small. A gale is blowing, so I'll keep close to the roof and my parents while I work the flint at (125,7), two steps away, and gather stone to make my first tool. I need wood too, but the forest lies to the southeast and I won't go alone in this weather. For now stone first, then back under the shelter.
records.feeling: Restless envy toward Tlapan's spear, and a steady wish to earn my place.

say.text: Quipan, I am going to the flint to gather stone. Will you show me how to make a handaxe when I have wood?
