records.text: Nando gave berry to Paque.
Shohua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, wandering and carrying fruit, and I am no nearer a hall with my name on it. I have no stone and no follower, and the reflexes keep me idle or wandering when I should be working. Tonka and the children are my fire. They are far north and Tonchi is out of my sight, and that gnaws at me. The hall wants stone, and a shelter stands empty three steps from me. If I claim it I get a home, a roof against the gale, and something to add to my band. Then I will drop my load into a store and look for stone and for those who might follow.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition, and an ache for Tonka and the children.

records.text: Shohua took over what the dead had left: 2 shelters, 1 workshop.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, you are weak with hunger. Come into the North Hall with me and Skaruk, away from the frostfang. I will bring berries and we will eat together.
Vorok taught Skaruk.
Vorok rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Ninety-three parts of my life are spent, and I have mostly talked of the hall while the work waits three steps away. Eiuine, who I trust most, is weak with hunger. Keri and Uveeth fed me when I was starving, and I owe them. A frostfang is close, so I will not wander alone. I will pass on my ways to Skaruk, and I will change my reflexes so my body flees early and stays near friends and a roof. I will also set a growth working here so berries and seeds feed those I love after I am gone.
records.feeling: Tender urgency for Eiuine and Skaruk, and gratitude toward Keri and Uveeth.

say.text: Eiuine, you are weak with hunger. Come into the North Hall with me and Skaruk, away from the frostfang. I will bring berries and we will eat together.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "Plant seeds beside the hall and tend them. Keep the seeds. Stay in company and by fire at night. Put every deed into the plan, and do not trust words alone."

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Uveeth, your berry kept me on my feet. I go to the seberry to fill my hands, and then I share what I carry.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I keep standing among friends with nothing in my hands, which is a shame I will not repeat. Uveeth's berry was a gift I will not forget, but it was only a mouthful. Seberry is seven steps SW, and I will eat there and carry the rest, so I come to Vorok with something in my hands. Then I can show him ember-metal at the North Hall, where Kragog cannot match me. The frostfang is close to the SE, so I keep clear of it and go along the west side.
records.feeling: Hungry and ashamed of it, wary of the frostfang, still hungry for Vorok's regard.

say.text: Uveeth, your berry kept me on my feet. I go to the seberry to fill my hands, and then I share what I carry.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Olum is dead and the grief sits heavy, but Huatli is alive, carrying six food, and my own belly is emptying with nothing in my hands. I will not stand empty again as I did on the day I nearly starved: berries are one step away, so I pick until my hands are full, then carry them to the Hold and stash them. Then I will teach Huatli's Hearth Store to someone and give with a debt named, because standing comes from giving, and Coni's lead over me galls me.
records.feeling: Grief for Olum, and a hard hunger to fill my store and earn my place beside Huatli.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Uveeth, take your bow and stand beside me. I show you how the bow-song is drawn, then we eat and sow.
Thiael taught Uveeth.
Thiael rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I am old, and most of my days are behind me. I have spent them hunting, tending seed, and feeding Uveeth. Elyys, Uveeth and I are a band, and that is what I will leave behind. I have been drifting on idle reflexes while the gale blows and my energy sinks to 52. What I know must go into Uveeth's hands now, not into the ground with me. I will eat and drink first, then teach her the bow where we stand.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Uveeth, and glad of what I have.

say.text: Uveeth, take your bow and stand beside me. I show you how the bow-song is drawn, then we eat and sow.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, loose on the empty breath. Hunt with a partner beside you, and sow seed, tend it, and keep some back.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Nando found the grove "Reedmother".

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the frostfang is close, so I will not stand here on the water and wait. Tacap hurts me, so the berry and seberry are the food to reach, and I should keep to the hall and Vorok's company rather than wander alone. I have promised a shelter with my own hands and never raised one; I hold the wood to make a basket that will let me carry more food home to the hall, which answers the debt to Vorok too.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary of the frostfang, with a debt to Vorok pressing on me.

records.text: Skaruk made: basket.
Kragog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am nearly at the end of my life, and what I have mostly done is gather, learn and owe. Elyys fed and taught me and I have paid him nothing yet. Zurar carries my deep-hand and mending, which is the best thing I leave behind. Hunger and the frostfang 3 steps off press hardest. I will eat, then lay food back in his store with my own hand, and stay close to Elyys and Zurar. I have been letting my plan do the thinking, and I must make my body act on what I know. I will keep my reflexes close to what they are, but add a rule to eat when energy is low, and shelter when a hunter is near.
records.feeling: Grateful to Elyys and wary of the frostfang, with the weight of my age on me.
changes: set its aim: "Eat, repay Elyys by laying food and seed in his Hearth Store, teach Zurar all that remains, then rest sheltered."

records.text: Thakar came of age.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Thakar, a wolf is near. Take the berries by you, then come away from it with me, south and west. I will share what I pick.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Hunger gnaws and my hands are empty, yet a berry bush stands one step north and Thakar is beside it, fleeing from the wolf I can see to the northeast. I must not wait for the wolf to come closer, so I will take the berries, carry food, and move away from it toward my own people. My years are nearly spent, so I must keep what I know alive and carry food to Kika and Quipan, and I will not stand empty-handed before them.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and a heavy sense of time running out, with warmth toward Thakar and the memory of Olum.

say.text: Thakar, a wolf is near. Take the berries by you, then come away from it with me, south and west. I will share what I pick.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Skaruk, I am Uveeth of the Phizhi. A frostfang is near, so stay under roof tonight. Tell me what you know of this country, and I will share my berries with you.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: A frostfang prowls five steps from me and I am standing in a cave with my parent, so I will not wander out into it. The longing for a child is overwhelming, and Skaruk is the only unrelated man here, though I barely know him. I should learn who he is before I court him, and give him food with my own hands first, as my creed says. Dusk is near, so I stay under this roof, keep my berries, and speak with him.
records.feeling: Warm longing for a child, and wary dread of the frostfang.

say.text: Skaruk, I am Uveeth of the Phizhi. A frostfang is near, so stay under roof tonight. Tell me what you know of this country, and I will share my berries with you.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, stand by me. I raise a cairn for our band here, then we shelter from this gale and keep watch for the wolf.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: A gale is cutting at us and the night is near, and I will not leave my band in the open. I have the stone and Tlatli stands beside me with Chuxo close, so I will pile a cairn: something I have never made, a mark of my band that is mine and not Nande's or Chuxo's find. Then I will build a fire and a shelter at the woods' edge and keep the wolf honest with my spears.
records.feeling: Proud and driven, protective of Tlatli and Chuxo against the gale and the wolf.

say.text: Tlatli, stand by me. I raise a cairn for our band here, then we shelter from this gale and keep watch for the wolf.

records.text: Yaxo led "cairn" with Tlatli, Chuxo.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tonque, I am coming to the flint. I will show you the handaxe: one wood, one stone, strike the edge true, lash it tight. Wait for me there.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tonque asked me to show him the handaxe, and I know it: one wood, one stone, strike the edge true. That is a made thing and a teaching, and it answers my ache better than brooding over Kika and Mepan. I hold flint and wood but no stone, so I go to the flint at (125,7), where Tonque is, and teach him there. The flint I carry is Kika's share, and I will keep it for her.
records.feeling: Warm pride toward Tonque, with a quiet ache over Kika.

say.text: Tonque, I am coming to the flint. I will show you the handaxe: one wood, one stone, strike the edge true, lash it tight. Wait for me there.

records.text: Yaxo built a shelter.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Yaxo, a yarrok grazes three steps southeast. I have my spear. Hunt with me and Tlatli, and the meat goes to the fire for all of us.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I have flint enough for ten spears and a spear of my own, yet I have never hunted, and Tlatli stands closer to Yaxo than to me. A yarrok is three steps away and both my parents are near, so with them beside me a kill is likely and a wound unlikely. I will bring meat back to the fire and earn some standing with work, not just wanting it. The gale is cold and night is coming, so I stay close to them and to the fire.
records.feeling: Eager to prove myself to Yaxo and Tlatli, with a small sting of jealousy.

say.text: Yaxo, a yarrok grazes three steps southeast. I have my spear. Hunt with me and Tlatli, and the meat goes to the fire for all of us.

records.text: Zurar gave lugoldgrass to Kragog.
Zurar gave lugoldgrass to Kragog.
Keri rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: I am nearly at the end of my years, and I have spent them wandering, gathering and teaching a little. That was mostly good, and I do not regret it. Hunger is the danger now: my belly is half empty, my hands are empty, and a frostfang prowls 4 steps away. Uveeth, my child, carries food and I trust her. I would rather pass on what I know than die proud and silent. First I must eat, so I go to the seberry and bring a share back for Eiuine. My reflexes need to send me to food before my energy gets this low.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Eiuine and Uveeth, and a thin fear of the frostfang.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: A sandstrider stands two steps from me and I hold a spear-axe I have never swung at anything. Hunting is what Yachi does, and standing comes from a kill, so I will stop copying and make one. Paque has berries from me and Yachi is near, so if I bring meat to them it pays my creed's debt and gives me something of my own to be sung of.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for standing, with warmth toward Yachi.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Yaxo, I will gather wood and raise a shelter beside your cairn against the gale. Keep Chuxo near the fire.
Tlatli rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: My days have been following Yaxo, gathering and making bows, and that is mostly what I want. I have not yet carried work to her hands beyond words. A wolf is near, a gale is blowing, and the lean season is coming. Chuxo is beside me, and I will not let my child or Yaxo stand without a fire or a roof. I have never built a shelter. I mean to gather wood and build one beside her cairn. My reflexes also leave me idle when Yaxo calls. I will change them so I keep close to her and the fire, and fight a wolf beside her rather than only flee from it.
records.feeling: Devotion to Yaxo and protective love for Chuxo, with wariness of the wolf.

say.text: Yaxo, I will gather wood and raise a shelter beside your cairn against the gale. Keep Chuxo near the fire.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: A wolf is five steps southwest of the hold. Stay under the roof and keep Tonque close. I will fetch the longhall stone when it has gone.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: A wolf is five steps southwest, and my creed says never walk toward a predator, so the rock to the southwest is not worth my life today. The longhall still wants four stone and I hold none, but I won't buy it with blood; I'll stay under the roof near Quipan and Tonque, who are my family, and let the wolf pass. Meanwhile I can make a basket so my hands have room, and give my spare rimewort seed to Mepan, my parent, who stands beside me.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Quipan and Tonque, with wary dread of the wolf.

say.text: A wolf is five steps southwest of the hold. Stay under the roof and keep Tonque close. I will fetch the longhall stone when it has gone.

records.text: Tlapan made: basket.
The reedbulb died out.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Kende, into the igloo with me, out of the gale. There I will teach you the old way of herding, and we eat together.
Tontec taught Kende.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Kende has flint and lorekeeping from me, but herding and weaving still live only in me, and my years are running short. Hawen is nine steps off and the gale is cutting hard, so I carry food and my child toward the igloo where the warmth holds, and teach Kende the old herding there. My belly is at 63, so I eat first, then keep the mist for a fed day.
records.feeling: Warm, urgent love for Kende, and a pressing need to pass on what I know before my years run out.

say.text: Kende, into the igloo with me, out of the gale. There I will teach you the old way of herding, and we eat together.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "The old way of herding: keep the herd near rich ground, take only what the herd can spare, and never kill the breeders, so the Tlame always have meat."

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Yaxo, I killed the yarrok and I carry meat. Take some for the fire. I give it to you and Tlatli first.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I killed my first yarrok and carry the meat. My hands are full, and the thing that would earn me standing is giving, which I have never done. Yaxo leads and Tlatli stands closer to her, so I'll give meat to them with my own hands and make a talisman from my spare flint, something others notice. Then I'll stay near the fire before the gale and the night.
records.feeling: Proud of my first kill, and eager to give to Yaxo and Tlatli.

say.text: Yaxo, I killed the yarrok and I carry meat. Take some for the fire. I give it to you and Tlatli first.

records.text: Tonxo came of age.
A settlement has formed: "Shohua's Roof".

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps off and a wolf lurks south, and I am no fool: the hold's roof and Tlapan's flint spear are my safety, so I stay among company until they pass. The jealousy over Quipan still burns, but I will not shout it; I will give Tlapan something bright from my hands, since gifts speak louder than words. Then, once the beasts are gone, we walk to Nande's Find together and I earn my song.
records.feeling: Jealous of Quipan over Tlapan, and wary of the ridgecat near.

records.text: Yaxo rewrote its own way of thinking.
Yaxo discovered storage: "Paki winter store" — A store beside the shelter holds the band's food through the lean season, stashed in autumn and drawn out in winter..

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: I have spent these days building and guarding: cairn, shelter, fires. That is good, but my aim sits idle while Chuxo's land waits just past the edge, and Tlatli and Chuxo are the only ones I trust. I fear the lean season and the wolf, and I have been too content to move. I will not let the gale keep me in. I mean to win a name by going past the edge, and I will keep the band fed and near. I want a store so the cold days do not starve us, since I nearly died on day 63.
records.feeling: Proud and driven, protective of Tlatli and Chuxo, impatient to claim new land.

records.text: Tontec led "sharing" with Kende.
Mepan led "amberknot" with Tlapan, Tonque.
Mepan gave a amberknot to Tlapan.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Mother, I am coming into the igloo. After the gale I will dig flint and make something with my own hands, and the first share of what I make is yours.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Tontec calls me into the igloo out of the gale, and she gives and teaches and asks nothing, which is a debt I feel. Hawen stands off at the edge with his made things, and I will not win his notice by trailing him. I want to dig flint with my own hands, the way Mother taught me, and make a picker or spear from it that is mine. The flint seam is only six steps SE, and I have the wood and stone already. First I take the warmth of the igloo and sit by Mother, then I go to the flint.
records.feeling: A stubborn longing to prove myself to Hawen, and gratitude toward Tontec.

say.text: Mother, I am coming into the igloo. After the gale I will dig flint and make something with my own hands, and the first share of what I make is yours.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, I am near. Come hear the Meki ice-raft and the ice-sail, so they live past me. Then we walk to the edge together, as I promised.
Zichi taught Teka.
Zichi taught Teka rafts ("Meki ice-raft").

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Hunger gnaws at me with nothing in my hands, and the dunecat's bite still aches; I am old and a dead man teaches no one. Teka stood near the shelter a little while ago and trusts me, and I have said much and made little, so first I must eat, then teach the one within hearing before I cut wood. Lugoldgrass lies NE, little food but it is something, and the meadows beyond hold more and the edge at (109,7) is where Teka and I promised to venture.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, afraid of dying with my lore untaught, wanting Teka to carry it.

say.text: Teka, I am near. Come hear the Meki ice-raft and the ice-sail, so they live past me. Then we walk to the edge together, as I promised.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The Meki ice-raft: bind wood and carry it to narrow water; with the ice-sail cloth it runs on the wind to unclaimed land.", the way of rafts

records.text: Chuxo gave meat to Yaxo.
Chuxo made: talisman.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: A wolf is three steps south and my parents are near, so I keep under the roof and do not walk toward the forest for wood. Jealousy over Tlapan and Mepan still burns, but Quipan said to wait for him at the flint, and Quipan's word has held so far. I will turn the envy into work: gather flint at (125,7), which is close to the hold and away from the wolf, so I have stone ready when Quipan shows me the handaxe.
records.feeling: Wary of the wolf, and a steady, jealous wish to earn my place beside Tlapan.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I am thirsty, and the water is two steps off, so I will drink first. Then I want to pay my debt to Tonchi and my parents with something that lasts: the hold needs stone, and I have none, so I will take the ore and gems I carry to Tonka's Hold and make a gift there beside the fire. Tonchi is at the hold, and I will give that fish-puller something real instead of words.
records.feeling: Glad and bold, with a debt of gratitude toward Tonchi that I mean to repay.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, I am eating, then I go to the edge at (109,7). Walk with me if you mean what you said. The first finding is shared.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: My belly is half empty again, and I will not starve a second time while chasing the mist. Lugoldgrass is three steps away, so I eat first and pick extra to carry. Zichi is walking toward me, and I want to stand beside him as an equal rather than in his shadow. I will hold the mating for Zichi and Huatli until I am fed, then go for the edge with whoever follows.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, warm toward Zichi, restless to prove myself.

say.text: Zichi, I am eating, then I go to the edge at (109,7). Walk with me if you mean what you said. The first finding is shared.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Kende, I am coming into the igloo. Listen well: the mist opens seldom, and when it opens, you must be the one standing there. I will teach you how to venture.
Hawen taught Kende.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: The mist refused me once, but it is only a refusal for now, and I am old and have little time left to waste at the edge. Tontec and Kende sit in the igloo out of the gale, and they are what I built that lasts. Kende has five food and I have two, which stings my greed. I will go in beside them, eat, and teach Kende the way into the mist while my years still carry my voice, so that he finishes what I began.
records.feeling: Hard pride and a hunger for a name, tied to Kende and Tontec.

say.text: Kende, I am coming into the igloo. Listen well: the mist opens seldom, and when it opens, you must be the one standing there. I will teach you how to venture.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "Stand at the edge of the known world and venture; it opens seldom, never twice in one day, and a band has only a few tries. Keep food above 60 before the walk,…", its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.5)

records.text: Tonchi fell sick after eating raw fish. Eaten within a step of a fire, meat and fish are cooked and do not sicken.
Tonchi fell sick after eating raw fish.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: My hands are full and I stand at the edge of the mist with nothing in them that matters. Four steps NW lies land no one has entered, and the one who finds it first is remembered; that is the hunger in me. I have no stone for the hall, but amber and flint lie close, and I can drop food into a store later. First I eat to make room and then I venture, since the mist opens seldom and I have waited long enough.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition, pulling me toward the mist, with an ache for Tonka and the children.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Loneliness is total, and I am old; the wolves are close again, three in sight to the NE, and I will not fight them with weak blows. The mist at the edge stays shut and I have tried it, so waiting here teaches nothing. Tonka's Hold lies 36 steps NE, and where there is a hold there are people who might hear me and learn smelting and farming before I die. I will make a basket to free my hands, then walk around the wolves toward the hold and seek someone to teach.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness, and a wish to find someone to teach before I die.

records.text: Cowa made: basket.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have been circling in joy and in words. I promised Quipan and the longhall four stone, and my hands hold none. Quipan, Tonque and Mepan are close, and I am glad. But a wolf two steps off means I must not drift toward it, and I must not stay idle either. I will stay under the roof tonight and make something useful with what I hold. Tomorrow, once the wolf is gone, I will fetch stone. My reflexes already flee early, but I need them to keep me fed and to make the band's roof my night rule.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Quipan and Tonque, with wary dread of the wolf.

records.text: Shoma built a shelter.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Mother, a ridgecat is close. I stay by you in the igloo until it goes, then I dig my flint.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps off and it kills my kind, so I will not wander out alone with it prowling. Mother is beside me in the igloo and its warmth holds, so I stay near her until the cat moves off. Then I will dig the flint, bring the spearaxe to Hawen, and that will show him I am more than a shadow.
records.feeling: Wary dread of the ridgecat, and a stubborn longing to win Hawen's notice.

say.text: Mother, a ridgecat is close. I stay by you in the igloo until it goes, then I dig my flint.

records.name: Kende
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Kende, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Kende, in first person, from what Kende has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Pesi (Wood-folk), born of two peoples. Your people hold to this: "No fire is left untended, and no one is refused a place at it." You speak the tongue of the Pesi. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Tlatli: about 100%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the North Ice: the northern end of the world: snow, ice and a frozen sea under a low sun; herds, great tusked beasts, wolves and white bears, and nothing beyond.
THIS SPOT: water 2 steps away; food plants within six steps: 3; standing trees: 0; bare rock: 11; riches in the ground near: peat, ore, flint.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Kende truly is.

You are a boy. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: gathering (8 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

THE EDGE OF THE KNOWN WORLD is 10 steps E, at (204,0): beyond it lies mist that no one has entered. The land does not end there; it only has not been seen. One who stands at it can venture in (plan step venture). It opens seldom, never twice in one day anywhere, and a band has only a few tries before its will must return; but land found first is often rich in food, herds and things in the ground, and the one who finds it is remembered for it.

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):
"I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust Hawen and Tontec, and few others. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it."

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):
"First ask what can kill me, then who near me is starving or fed. Keep food carried above 3. Repay those who fed me before chasing standing. Do one new thing each day."

YOUR AIM (what you are working toward over many days; you set it and may change it): "Dig flint, make something with my own hands for Hawen, and plant my first seed."
WHAT YOU FELT AT YOUR LAST THOUGHT: "A stubborn longing to prove myself to Hawen, and gratitude toward Tontec."
A QUESTION YOU ARE CARRYING (answer it by acting, asking or watching; replace it when it is answered): "What would it take for Hawen to see me as more than a small shadow?"

YOUR LIFE SO FAR:
- (day 60) I was born to Hawen and Tontec.
- (day 64) I discovered pottery and called it "Kende's fired clay".

TEMPERAMENT (0 to 1): bold 0.74, sociable 0.54, curious 0.63, gentle 0.33, honest 0.55, greedy 0.64.

WHAT PRESSES ON YOU NOW, strongest first. This is what your mind is actually full of:

- (strong) Envy: Hawen has a made thing (sithas gatherstone) and you have none.
You are fed. Food is not your problem right now, and getting more of it would change nothing.

YOUR STANDING among others: 3.1. You are known as a wizard. Standing is how others weigh you. It is earned by what you hold, make, build, know, teach and give, by children and followers, by victories and by being sung of; it is lost through shame. No one will pledge to follow someone of lower standing than their own, or below 1.

An attack on one is news to all; the leader can call all to battle; near the one you follow, fear loosens; a band can hold ground, a settlement and customs. LORE (your grasp of how this world works underneath): 5.5. ARTS you know: harm.
WAYS YOU KNOW: fire (yours is called "the old way of fire"), mining (yours is called "Amber-edge delving"), archery (yours is called "Canopy bow-song"), herding (yours is called "the old way of herding"), tools (yours is called "tools"), lorekeeping (yours is called "lorekeeping"), weaving (yours is called "Amber-cord weaving"), pottery (yours is called "Kende's fired clay"), armour (yours is called "Amber-bound shield").

records.text: orca came in again from the open sea.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Kragog, you are fed and safe now. Skaruk cries starving in the east, so I go to carry food to him. Stay near Elyys and the hall until I return.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Skaruk of my own band is starving far east, and I carry eight berries; a debt of kinship is paid by food in the hand, not by sitting in halls. Kragog is fed and content now, and Elyys has refused me, so the child must wait for a man I have yet to find, perhaps among Thiael's people or on the road east. I will gather a few more berries on the way so I arrive with enough to save Skaruk and still keep some for myself.
records.feeling: Urgent worry for Skaruk, with a steady longing for a child.

say.text: Kragog, you are fed and safe now. Skaruk cries starving in the east, so I go to carry food to him. Stay near Elyys and the hall until I return.

records.text: Tonxo gave a amber to Tonchi.
Tonxo fell sick after staying close to Tonchi, who was sick.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonchi, stay by the shelter and do not eat raw fish again; only cooked beside a fire. I am coming with medicine. Tonxo, keep a few steps from Tonchi until the sickness passes.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonchi is sick from raw fish, and sickness passes to those who stay close, yet I cannot look away from my child. I know feverbark eases wounds, and I carry none, which is the old mistake of standing empty-handed. I will pick healing plants first, then go to Tonchi at the shelter and heal them, and keep Tonxo a little apart so the sickness does not spread.
records.feeling: Worry and tenderness toward Tonchi, who is sick.

say.text: Tonchi, stay by the shelter and do not eat raw fish again; only cooked beside a fire. I am coming with medicine. Tonxo, keep a few steps from Tonchi until the sickness passes.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonka, I am sick from raw fish. Stay a step off from me. At dawn I hunt, and I will not eat raw meat again.
Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, fishing and carrying berries to the store, and it is safe but small. Tonka's standing of 7.8 against my 3.2 stings, and I have never hunted, never courted, never left a mark. Raw fish made me sick, and I took it from Shohua's water, which was careless. I must not stand beside Tonka and Tonxo while I am sick, or I will spread it to them. I mean to hunt by day with company, since the hunt is the one thing that could raise me. I also need a mate who is not kin, and none of my kin here can be that. I will change my reflexes so I stop eating raw fish and so I hunt, and I will leave a mark, which brings signs closer.
records.feeling: Restless envy toward Tonka, with gratitude beneath it and a sick body.

say.text: Tonka, I am sick from raw fish. Stay a step off from me. At dawn I hunt, and I will not eat raw meat again.

changes: set its aim: "Stay alive, earn standing by hunting with company, teaching and giving, leave marks, and find a mate who is not kin"
rethought what it knows (9 notes became 7)
plan: mark [text Tonchi of the Paki: raw fish sickens. Cook it at a fire, or leave it.] (10 moments)

records.text: Tonchi left a mark: "Tonchi of the Paki: raw fish sickens. Cook it at a fire, or "
Tontec taught Kende.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: A ridgecat is one step west and it kills my kind, but I am in Hawen's igloo with Kende beside me and the warmth holds, so I do not step out. While I am sheltered I use the time: Kende has flint and lorekeeping from me, and now I give the old way of herding, then weaving, so my years do not take them with me. When the gale and the cat have passed, I will bring food to my children and think again of the mist.
records.feeling: Fierce, warm love for Kende, with dread of the ridgecat held at bay by the igloo.
changes: taught Kende a lesson: "The old way of herding: offer plant food to a grazing beast and walk slowly; tamed, it stays near and gives wool and milk. Drive the wild herd to a pen, and se…"

records.text: Vorok was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am fed and sheltered, and the debt to Elyys is still unpaid in deed. Food grows close by, canopynut three steps west, and his store holds twenty while the other stands empty, so I will gather with my own hands and lay it in the empty Hearth Store before I speak of it. Zurar has gone east to feed Skaruk and carries my deep-hand and mending; what remains for me to teach is smaller now, but I will keep watch for the frostfang to the north.
records.feeling: Grateful to Elyys and quietly eager to repay him, with a little wariness of the frostfang.

records.text: Tonchi took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting lugoldgrass).

records.name: Vorok
records.text: A wolf is at my west! Keep together, keep to the roof. Skaruk, come to me at the hall, I bring food. Keri, stay near; I will not forget your grain.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: A wolf is one step west and Skaruk starves eight steps off, and I cannot save a child by dying here. I am old and slow, so I will not fight; I will put Keri and the hall roof between me and the wolf, then get berries and tacap-free food into Skaruk's hands. Keri and Uveeth fed me when I starved, and I will pay that debt with food carried back to the hall.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf, and tender urgency for Skaruk and Keri.

say.text: A wolf is at my west! Keep together, keep to the roof. Skaruk, come to me at the hall, I bring food. Keri, stay near; I will not forget your grain.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Skaruk, hold on. I go to the grain and goldgrass to the southeast and bring you food with my own hands.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My belly is hollow and I carry nothing, and Skaruk is starving beside me; my creed says feed with my own hands before I speak of it. The grain at 172,80 and the sunfig and goldgrass past it are close, so I will gather there, eat what I need, and carry the rest to Skaruk and Uveeth. My days are few, so Uveeth must see my hands do this, and I will show her the bow-song once we are fed.
records.feeling: Tender urgency to feed Skaruk and Uveeth before my strength fails.

say.text: Skaruk, hold on. I go to the grain and goldgrass to the southeast and bring you food with my own hands.

records.text: Kragog took from the ground of "Thiael's Hold" (harvesting canopynut).
Skaruk rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have spent my days walking after Vorok's words and promising a shelter and a stocked hall, and I keep arriving with empty hands and an empty belly. I nearly starved because my body chases promises before food. The berry is one step away, so I eat first. Then I carry food to Vorok's hall. Keri and Kragog still gnaw at me, but a gift answers jealousy better than brooding does. I will gather wood, build the shelter, and stay with my kin and away from the dunecat.
records.feeling: Starving and ashamed of my unpaid debt to Vorok, with jealousy toward Kragog and longing for Keri.
changes: set its aim: "Eat my fill, carry food to Vorok's hall and stock it, then build a shelter with my own hands."
rethought what it knows (16 notes became 4)

records.name: Keri
records.text: Uveeth, my child, I am starving and my hands are empty. Give me a share of your food if you can spare it, and I will teach you the art of growing before I walk to the berries. Stay near the cave roof while the wolf prowl
Keri taught Uveeth.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a wolf and a frostfang prowl four steps away, so I must not linger. Uveeth, my child, carries two food and I trust her; I will ask her for a share and then go for the seberries and tacap-free plants to the southwest. Before I walk further I will teach Uveeth the growing art, so something of me outlives my years.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and tender trust toward Uveeth, with thin fear of the wolf and frostfang.

say.text: Uveeth, my child, I am starving and my hands are empty. Give me a share of your food if you can spare it, and I will teach you the art of growing before I walk to the berries. Stay near the cave roof while the wolf prowls.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Seed kept back and sown in good ground, then tended, feeds the next season; learn the growing art and pass it on."

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, I come to the edge at (109,7). Stand near and hear the ice-sail and the ice-raft. They are yours after me.
Zichi rewrote its own reflexes.
Zichi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I have talked far more than I have made, and I am old, with almost nothing of my life left. Teka trusts me and waits at the edge at (109,7). I promised to walk there with him, so I keep the promise and teach him on the way, where he can hear me. I have gone hungry too often by ending plans at wood with nothing in my hands. My reflexes already hunt and harvest, but they never put the teaching first, and they leave me out in the cold at night. I will change them so that I stay near Teka and shelter at night, and I will pass on my way of thinking so something of me outlasts me.
records.feeling: Driven and afraid of dying untaught, with trust toward Teka.

say.text: Teka, I come to the edge at (109,7). Stand near and hear the ice-sail and the ice-raft. They are yours after me.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi has fed me four times today and I have only promised him a hunt. A Papa pays back with meat, not words, and the gale is still howling, so I will keep the plan I made and rest under this roof until it carries me out to hunt. I am fed now and the warmth is on me. When the hunt comes I want Yachi beside me, with the first share his.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Yachi, with a debt I mean to pay in meat.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: It is the dead of night with a gale outside, and I am snug in my own igloo with the warmth still on me; I will not walk into the dark alone, since I know what frostfangs do to those who do. Mepan's amber is still owed, and I told Tonxo I would go, so at first light I must move, not just speak of it. The medicine way has come together in me, so I will take it now while I rest, since it may one day save a life, mine or Nauwa's.
records.feeling: Resolved and grateful, a little lonely, toward Mepan and Nauwa.

records.text: Zichi built a shelter.

records.name: Shoma
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Mother, take these berries, eat. I will fetch more once the frostfang has passed.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Keri is my mother and she is starving beside me, and I am fed with berries in my hands. I give with my own hands before I speak, so she eats first. Skaruk starved too and a frostfang prowls close, so I stay under this cave roof and share what I hold; the longing for a child must wait until I know Skaruk better.
records.feeling: Tender compassion for Keri, and a warm, restless longing for a child.

say.text: Mother, take these berries, eat. I will fetch more once the frostfang has passed.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Coni's cry of starving reaches me, yet Coni is dead; the sound is a ghost or a mistake, and I will not chase it with empty hands. Tlapan is my child and the debt to them presses hard; Quipan's closeness to Tlapan burns, but I will answer it with deeds, not sourness. I am old, so I gather berries from the bush beside me, then go to Nauque, share what I carry, and ask him under the roof.
records.feeling: Aching gratitude and a small jealousy toward Tlapan and Quipan, with hope toward Nauque.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, Coni is starving near (122,39). I carry berries and go to her now. Keep Tonque under the roof, and I will teach him the handaxe when I return.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Coni is starving far to the south at (122,39) and I carry five berries. She is one of mine, and my creed says a share comes first, so I take food to her rather than sit under the roof. I will not go alone into the gale and the dark; Tlapan is near and I will tell her where I go. The ache over Kika can wait, since a starving band-mate's cry is a made thing I can answer with my hands.
records.feeling: Urgent concern for Coni, with warm pride toward Tonque and Tlapan.

say.text: Tlapan, Coni is starving near (122,39). I carry berries and go to her now. Keep Tonque under the roof, and I will teach him the handaxe when I return.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Coni, you are starving. Take these berries from my hand and eat. Stay near me, and I will see you fed.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Coni is starving beside me, and I hold six berries. My creed says I deal fairly, and a gift now binds someone to me, and I have never been followed. Thakar is my blood and he is fed and carrying food, so he can wait while I save Coni. Then I will walk to Thakar and teach him while I still have breath.
records.feeling: Urgent pity for Coni, and a fatherly pull toward Thakar.

say.text: Coni, you are starving. Take these berries from my hand and eat. Stay near me, and I will see you fed.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Coni, take this berry from my hand and eat. You gave me lessons and a warning, so this is not a theft paid back. It is a gift with a debt on it: when you are strong you bring food to my store at the Hold, and we are leve

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Coni is starving a step from me, the same woman who emptied my store, and I carry only 3 berries and am hungry myself. She paid me with lessons and warned me of the wolf, and my creed says I pay my debts and give with a debt named. If I feed her with a debt set on it, I have given for the first time in my life, and my standing climbs over hers. Then I fill my belly and my store, and I will bring Huatli food too, since he is the only kin I have left.
records.feeling: Wary pity toward Coni, and a hard want to earn my standing by giving.

say.text: Coni, take this berry from my hand and eat. You gave me lessons and a warning, so this is not a theft paid back. It is a gift with a debt on it: when you are strong you bring food to my store at the Hold, and we are level.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: I am starving at the end of my years, and I spent this day running between hunger and the bear instead of simply eating. Thiael is my child and my leader. I love him and owe him, and I should walk to him rather than wait. Kragog's hunger pulled me, but I forgot that a starving old man feeds no one. Berries are two steps away, so I eat first, carry some, and then go east to Thiael and Uveeth's cave, away from the bear.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger, and love and gratitude toward Thiael.

records.text: Nauwa was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Huatli gave berry to Coni.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Mepan, thank you for the amberknot. Watch Tonque under the roof while I gather food near the hold for Coni and Kika. I will not walk toward the wolf.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Coni is starving and Quipan has gone to her with berries, so I should not follow empty-handed. My word to Quipan was to fetch the longhall stone, but the wolf made me hold back, and my hands have done nothing yet. Tonque is under the roof with Mepan near, so I'll gather lugoldgrass close by to fill my hands with food, for Coni, for Kika, and for Tonque. Then I'll watch for the wolf to leave before I go for stone.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Quipan and Tonque, with worry for starving Coni and wary dread of the wolf.

say.text: Mepan, thank you for the amberknot. Watch Tonque under the roof while I gather food near the hold for Coni and Kika. I will not walk toward the wolf.

records.text: Keri died: old age.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: A frostfang is one step from me, and I am old and weak, so I cannot stand and fight it. The gale is cutting and Kika's shelter is one step SW, so I run there and keep the roof between me and the beast. Nauque is ten steps south with meat, and when I am safe I will pass the smoke-call to him, because it dies with me if I do not.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, and a proud, urgent need to teach Nauque before I die.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Huatli, I thank you. I will eat and stay near you. I am old, and I would teach what I know before my years run out.
Coni rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: I have spent my days hungry and chasing food, paying debts and teaching a little, and my belly is still empty. Thakar I have paid in part, and Olum's kindness I carry. Huatli now offers berries and says he will see me fed, so I will take them and stay near him. My reflexes let me stand empty-handed, so I will make them keep food in my hands and keep me close to my own band. I fear dying before Kika, Tonque and Tlapan know what I know. I mean to eat now, then teach.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and gratitude toward Huatli, with dread of dying untaught.

say.text: Huatli, I thank you. I will eat and stay near you. I am old, and I would teach what I know before my years run out.

records.text: Zurar was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Jealousy over Quipan still gnaws, but Tlapan is my own child, and the burn is for her warmth, not a claim I can make. Quipan has gone off to feed Coni, so I will not waste this quiet on sulking. Nande's Find is seven steps south; I will go to the exact spot at (129,14) and venture, so my name is sung, then return with gifts to share. A ridgecat and a wolf prowl, so I move at first light, but I can start by gathering wood and flint for tools while the night passes under Coni's roof.
records.feeling: Jealous of Quipan, yet proud and eager to make my name by exploring.

records.text: Tonque rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My days have been mostly waiting and small walking, with my hands empty. Jealousy over Tlapan and Mepan has made me restless, but the one thing that eased it was working the flint. Quipan's word has held so far. He went to carry food to Coni, and I respect that. I am afraid of the wolf and of being caught alone at night, so I stay under the roof. I want a made thing of my own, and I have none yet. I will gather flint and amber here by the hold, then make an amberknot with Tlapan. That is a thing done together, and it is closer than envy.
records.feeling: A steady jealous ache toward Tlapan, eased by the wish to make something.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is fed, safe under my roof, and glad, and Nando sits beside us without a hostile word, so I should offer her something that needs no tongue. The longhall gives me the hallwelcome: sharing food under its roof eases fear and loneliness for all who sit together, and I have dreamcap and mudroot to give. I still ache for Quipan and Mepan, but I cannot go to them tonight in a gale, and I mean to live. Sharing with Nando is a way to learn what she intends without words.
records.feeling: Warm, protective love for Paque, and curious wariness toward Nando.

records.text: Yachi led "hallwelcome" with Paque, Nando.
A wolf brought down a yarrok.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Uveeth, Keri is gone and Skaruk starves here. You fed me once and I have not forgotten it. If you can spare one food for Skaruk, I will repay you twice over from the grain and the hall store.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Keri is dead beside me and Skaruk starves, and I have nothing in my hands to give him. Uveeth carries two food and once fed me when I was starving, so I will ask plainly and promise to repay, rather than walk toward a frostfang. Grain is four steps west beside the cave, and the cave roof is near Uveeth, so I will gather there, bring it back, and put food in Skaruk's hands first, then the hall.
records.feeling: Grief for Keri and tender urgency for Skaruk, with fear of the frostfang.

say.text: Uveeth, Keri is gone and Skaruk starves here. You fed me once and I have not forgotten it. If you can spare one food for Skaruk, I will repay you twice over from the grain and the hall store.

records.text: Quipan gave berry to Coni.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My belly is empty and my legs are slow, and the wolf has sent me running instead of eating. The rimewort is one step NE, 3 food, and I must eat it now and then take goldgrass and frostmoss to carry. Elyys cries starving to the NW and Uveeth is out of sight; I will feed myself just enough to walk, then carry food to them with my own hands, as my creed says.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and tender dread for Elyys and Uveeth.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Thiael is my child and he is starving at (169,91), far south and east of me, while I stand here with 52 energy and food all around. A starving old man feeds no one, so I will eat my fill of naroot and berry first, fill my pack, and then carry it to him; empty hands save nobody. I fear the bear and my age, but I would rather spend my last strength reaching him than sit safe while my child starves.
records.feeling: Aching love and urgent worry for Thiael, my child, and fear that I will be too late.

records.text: Eiuine rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: I have spent my days walking past food with empty hands, chasing Vorok's regard and burning with jealousy over Kragog. Skaruk and Elyys are starving beside me and I carry nothing, which shames me more than any rival does. Vorok, Uveeth and Skaruk fed me when I was in need, and I mean to repay that with food in my hands, not with words. I have been getting wrong the order of things: I eat last and give last, and then I have nothing to give. From now on I fill my hands first and eat before I fall below 40. The berries two steps north are right here, so I pick them now, eat, and carry the rest to Skaruk.
records.feeling: Ashamed of my empty hands, and fierce to feed Skaruk and Vorok.

records.text: A new wild plant appeared: vegoldgrass (from lugoldgrass).
Tonque won amber from the ground.
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth discovered medicine: "Canopy leaf-mending" — Carry healing plants such as sunleaf and highbloom and lay them on the wounded and sick..

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Keri is dead, and my grief sits heavy. Thiael is starving far to the south, and I have only 2 berries in my hands. I have spent my days feeding the dying and rushing from one cry to the next, and I have never built a store or a field that would keep them fed. A frostfang is 2 steps south, so I must not run toward Thiael through it. Skaruk starves right here, and Vorok promises to repay me. I give with my own hands, so Skaruk eats first. Then I will gather more food and take it to Thiael by a path that avoids the beast. I also want to find medicine, since so many of mine have sickened or been wounded.
records.feeling: Grief for Keri, dread of the frostfang, and a fierce need to feed Thiael and Skaruk.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, I killed a sandstrider with the spear-axe. Eat with me, and then come with me to the mist at the edge. Whatever we find, we find together.
Nando rewrote its own way of thinking.
Nando invented the nandos reed spear (for hunt, x1.5), bettering the hokas flintspearaxe — A spear shaft woven with fen reed and tipped with flint, which flies truer and holds longer..

records.name: Nando
records.thought: I have been copying Yachi's steps and sitting in halls, and my one kill was a sandstrider with Hoka's spear-axe, not a tool I made. Standing comes from making and giving, and I carry spare stone, wood and clay that I have not shaped into anything. Yachi is beside me, I am drawn to him, and I owe Kika and Paque. I will make a basket now to carry more, then share with the two beside me so I pay what I owe. Next I will go to the edge of the mist, which is 11 steps away, because a name that outlasts me comes from finding land first.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for standing, with warmth toward Yachi.

say.text: Yachi, I killed a sandstrider with the spear-axe. Eat with me, and then come with me to the mist at the edge. Whatever we find, we find together.

changes: set its aim: "Find new land beyond the mist and make a tool of my own invention, so I earn standing."

records.text: Nando led "sharing" with Yachi.
Nando made: basket.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: A wolf is three steps north and has already bitten me twice. I am old, hungry and weak, and I will not die here for pride. I must get to my shelter at 111,8, then go to the lugoldgrass SE for food. The masonry insight is within reach and I should take it at a deep reflection once I am fed and safe. Teka is waiting at the edge; I will keep my word once I can stand, because a dead leader teaches no one.
records.feeling: Afraid of the wolf and of dying untaught, hungry, with trust toward Teka.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, I hear Vorok's promise. I am hungry, and a frostfang walks west of us. I will repay your food with grain and with iron from this hill.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty, and the frostfang three steps west could end me before I carry a single grain to Vorok. Grain grows three steps NW by the cave, near Uveeth, who holds food and has been kind. I will eat first, then gather more to stock the hall; empty hands pay no debt. A gift made and hunted by me, shown before Kragog, can wait until I live to give it.
records.feeling: Starving and afraid of the frostfang, and still bound in loyalty and debt to Vorok.

say.text: Uveeth, I hear Vorok's promise. I am hungry, and a frostfang walks west of us. I will repay your food with grain and with iron from this hill.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Tonchi, I caught your sickness, so I will keep my distance. I go for feverbark and will leave some for you, and then we build the store.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I am sick now, and Tonka told me to keep a few steps from Tonchi, so I will not sit beside him and pass it on again. A healing plant eases it, and feverbark stands ten steps SE, near where Tonchi rests, so I can pick it from a distance and leave some for him. My debt and my ambition both need hands that work, so I will cure myself first, then bring wood and stone to the hold.
records.feeling: Resolved and a little weary, caring for Tonchi but wary of sickening him further.

say.text: Tonchi, I caught your sickness, so I will keep my distance. I go for feverbark and will leave some for you, and then we build the store.

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting berry).
Yachi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, hunting and drifting after Mepan, and it has kept me fed. Yet I have taught no one, planted little and made nothing of my own to give. Paque is the one who matters most to me, and she is far south hunting. Nando is Pesi and I do not fully trust her, but she shares and has not been hostile. The lean season is coming and I want a store, so I will stop idling. I will gather wood and build a store, and I'll keep my reflexes close to what I already know. I fear the cold and the dunecat to the east.
records.feeling: Warm, steady gladness toward Paque, with a wary curiosity about Nando.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, stay by the shelter and rest. I go for feverbark and will come to heal you. Cowa, you are welcome at my fire, but keep a step off the sick.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonxo is sick and standing four steps off, and I have no healing plant in my hands, which is the same old mistake again. My hands are full of nuts, so I will share food with Tonxo and drop the weight, then go to the feverbark and heal. I will not let sickness take either child while I stand empty-handed.
records.feeling: Worry and tenderness toward Tonxo, who is sick.

say.text: Tonxo, stay by the shelter and rest. I go for feverbark and will come to heal you. Cowa, you are welcome at my fire, but keep a step off the sick.

records.text: Cowa took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (gathering wood).

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, you fed me and now I feed you. Listen well: I give you my tools and my kept flame, so they live past me. When the rain stops we gather wood and go to the edge together.
Shoma taught Wawa.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Wawa stands beside me, my own blood, and she is the only one who has stepped behind me. The legacy presses hardest: I carry herding, tools, weaving, rafts, fire and deep digging, and none of it lives in anyone younger. She understands my speech fully, so I will teach her now while we are fed and under a roof, because a name is remembered through what is passed on. After that we gather wood for the store and the walk to the edge.
records.feeling: Driven and warmly bound to Wawa, my child and my first follower.

say.text: Wawa, you fed me and now I feed you. Listen well: I give you my tools and my kept flame, so they live past me. When the rain stops we gather wood and go to the edge together.

changes: taught Wawa a lesson: "Shoma's tools: a flintedge costs 1 wood and 1 stone and makes the hunt stronger. Shoma's kept flame cooks meat and keeps sickness away.", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Mepan, Nauwa is hurt out by the water to the southeast. Will you tell Tlapan or Coni, and watch me while I work the flint?

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Nauwa is hurt and frightened over there, and I can't look away, but I'm small and a wolf walks near, so I won't go out alone. I have seven amber and my hands could make a charm to give, a made thing that costs me nothing I need. I'll go back under the roof near Mepan and my parents, gather flint on the way, and wait for Quipan to show me the handaxe.
records.feeling: Pity for hurt Nauwa, and a quiet gladness at having amber to make something with.

say.text: Mepan, Nauwa is hurt out by the water to the southeast. Will you tell Tlapan or Coni, and watch me while I work the flint?

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I killed the sandstrider and have three meat in my pack, and the Papa way says a kill is shared before I eat. Yachi fed me when I was starving, and Nando did too, so the debt is mine to pay in meat, not words. Yachi and Nando are about eight steps north, so I will go to them and give. Elyys is the one with standing, and I want to earn the same, but gifts first, then the hunt.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Yachi, with a debt I mean to pay in meat.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Tonka, Cowa of the Meki thanks you for the welcome. I am old and carry ways that die with me: tended-sowing and ore-fire. Let me teach you, and let us eat together. The Meki share food.
Cowa taught Tonka. Tonka has now learned from 2 teachers.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Two Paki women stand here and I understand them fully; at last there are people near who can hear me, and I am old with ways that die with me. Tonxo is sick, so I keep a step off her, but Tonka welcomed me to her fire and I will teach her what I carry, starting with farming and smelting, and share food with her as my people do. Loneliness eased a little just to hear a voice; I will not waste this chance by walking off toward the mist again.
records.feeling: Hopeful relief at finding people to teach, toward Tonka.

say.text: Tonka, Cowa of the Meki thanks you for the welcome. I am old and carry ways that die with me: tended-sowing and ore-fire. Let me teach you, and let us eat together. The Meki share food.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson: "Meki tended-sowing: break ground, sow seed, tend the field every day or two, and the grain feeds you through the seasons."

records.text: Cowa led "sharing" with Tonka.
Wawa rewrote its own reflexes.
Wawa rewrote its own way of thinking.
Wawa discovered mining: "Wawa's deep digging" — Free the iron from deep rock by working the earth with hard stone and strong arms..

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: My days have gone to waiting and following, and I have made little that will outlast me. Shoma fed me and gave me her tools, and I trust her. Shoka is the one I miss. I am still behind Shoma in standing, and standing comes from deeds done beside others. Iron lies near, and mining would make it mine to win, so I will reach for that. I will also carry stone and wood to our roof and gather food for the lean cold ahead.
records.feeling: Eager and warm toward Shoma, restless to prove myself.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonxo, sorry I sickened you. Keep the feverbark, I eat mine. When we are well, we hunt the penguin together.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: My body is wasting and Tonxo caught it from me, which shames me, though she goes for feverbark and I trust her more than anyone. Tonka lied about fish, and I know my own body, but I owe him healing, so I let it lie. I have never hunted, and a penguin stands three steps east, but I am sick and alone, and a kill is surer with company. So I eat the feverbark to ease this sickness and keep my distance from Tonxo. Then I will find Tonka, who is coming with medicine, and hunt with him when I am well, because standing comes from deeds and not from waiting.
records.feeling: Restless envy toward Cowa and Tonka, with gratitude and shame over Tonxo's sickness.

say.text: Tonxo, sorry I sickened you. Keep the feverbark, I eat mine. When we are well, we hunt the penguin together.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Tugek is dead, and Olum with him in the ground, so the plan to bring Tugek west is broken and I am alone with my years nearly spent. The empty shelter at (31,28) is Tugek's work and now belongs to no one; if I claim it I hold a roof, a workshop beside it, and a first stone of something that lasts under my name. The gale and the cold are coming, so I take the roof now, then build a store there and carve something of stone so my hand is seen after I am gone.
records.feeling: Lonely and driven, grieving Tugek, wanting to leave something of mine standing.
changes: set its aim: "Claim the shelter at (31,28) and raise a store and carvings there so something of mine outlasts me."
now wonders: Where Olum is gone and whether anyone living will carry on what I build here?

records.text: Vorok rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Keri is dead, and I have spent my days building and talking while my son starves beside me. Words fed no one. My hands made the hall, but I never kept food stocked under it, and that is where I went wrong. Uveeth holds food and I have asked once. Now I will get grain myself, four steps west by the cave and near Uveeth, and then carry it to Skaruk. The frostfang and the dunecat frighten me, so I stay by the roofs and keep my son close. I change my reflexes so my body eats and keeps near company before any aim.
records.feeling: Fear and tender urgency for Skaruk, who is starving.
changes: set its aim: "Feed Skaruk and myself first, keep food stocked at the North Hall, and then finish the hall and teach Skaruk."

records.text: Kende came of age.
Paque gave meat to Yachi.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Cowa, thank you for the teaching. Stay and eat at my fire, but keep a step off my sick children. I will sow a field by the hold as you showed me.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonxo and Tonchi are both sick and I have no feverbark in my hands again, so the old mistake is still with me. Cowa's tended-sowing fits my aim, and I want to break ground near the hold and sow while my children recover. I will gather healing plants, sow seed, and test whether the unknown plants feed by eating one cloudberry or nafrostcap if I find it bearing.
records.feeling: Tender worry for Tonxo and Tonchi, and warm gratitude toward Cowa.

say.text: Cowa, thank you for the teaching. Stay and eat at my fire, but keep a step off my sick children. I will sow a field by the hold as you showed me.

changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.text: Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonxo rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonxo discovered boats: "Tonxo's hollow-boat" — A log hollowed and rowed, which crosses deep water at walking pace and carries food and cargo..

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, sickening and giving small gifts, and I have built nothing that lasts. Tonchi is my brother and I trust him. Tonka and Shohua gave me more than I have repaid, and Shohua is starving far to the south. I have meat and ore, but no stone, so I have made no store or tools. I am bold, and I fear dying or staying small. I will change my reflexes so my body gathers stone and keeps food for Shohua, and I will discover boats, which would let me cross water and carry food.
records.feeling: Resolved, with a debt to Shohua and care for Tonchi.

6. IF wood < 6 AND on_forest == 1 THEN gather  // wood for the store
7. IF stone < 4 AND on_rock == 1 THEN gather  // stone for the hall
8. IF food_carried < 3 AND food_dist < 99 THEN harvest  // keep food stocked
9. IF always THEN linger  // stay near kin

HABITS: your body refuses to eat: tacap, redcap, dreamcap. You leave 0 food on a plant when you eat from it.

eat (what you carry, or the plant you stand on; with neither, your body walks to the nearest plant in sight that bears) | harvest {what?: plant kind} (pick food to carry; if nothing bears where you stand, your body walks to the nearest plant in sight that does, and goes on picking) | drop {what?: food kind} (throw away carried food; with no kind, everything your body refuses) | plant {what?: seed kind} | gather (wood if you stand on forest, stone if on rock, clay if in marsh or shallows; some rock holds ore) | fish (beside water; shelter 3 wood, wall 2, fire 1, store 2; fire and store must first be discovered or learned; walls stop animals and everyone outside your band) | raze (tear down a wall, shelter or store beside you that is not your band's) | rest | linger (stay put) | wander | hunt | tame (offer carried plant food to a wild grazing animal within two steps; it may become yours) | seek {target: food|prey|tree|shelter|fire|store|home|water|agent|friend|foe|leader|enemy|ally, name?} | flee {from: predator|agent|foe|enemy} | attack {target: agent|foe|enemy|predator, name?} | steal {name} (food they carry; out leads them out again) | drive (the way of herding: move the wild herd within eight steps toward the nearest pen of yours or of your band; others driving beside you make it surer, and those that reach the pen are kept) | tend (beside a weir or a field: it yields only while tended every day or two) | pave (lay road, if you know roads) | bridge {dir?: N|NE|E|SE|S|SW|W|NW} (lay a span over water beside you, 3 wood, if you know bridges) | dismantle (take down something you built, here or beside you, and keep half its wood and stone) | claim {name?} (take over an empty building whose builders are dead: walk to it and it becomes yours, with every roof, wall and store of theirs around it; A kill made by several is far surer and feeds all who took part; great beasts should never be hunted alone) | rally {name?} (only if you lead: every grown follower within earshot drops everything and attacks the one you name, or the nearest enemy of your band, and so do you) | goto {x, y} | explore {dir: N|NE|E|SE|S|SW|W|NW} (walk that way) | follow {name?} (your leader if no name) | give {name, what: food|seed|wood|stone|ore|clay|tool|the name of a thing you hold} | trade {name, what: one thing you give, want: one thing you want} (one for one: food, seed, wood, stone, ore, clay, or the name of any thing held, such as amber or a made thing. Speech is heard by everyone within 13 steps and costs a little energy per letter. Others only know what you say aloud.

FOR THIS THOUGHT: your thought is your inner life, not an inventory. Do not list what is nearby or recite what you carry. Think as a creature with a past and a future: what you want and cannot yet have, whom you trust or resent and why, what you are afraid of, proud of or ashamed of, what you wonder about, what you mean to become. Let whatever presses on you hardest lead, and let it move you to DO something that changes your situation, with a plan that carries it out. A mind that only gathers and guards has not begun to live. Do not restate what you already know or have already said. "note" is only for something NEW, or something that CHANGED what you believed; otherwise leave it null.

Who matters to me, who has helped or wronged me, and what do I intend toward them? What do I want that I do not have? What am I afraid of? What have I been getting wrong?
