records.text: Paque gave meat to Nando.
Tonka took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting ironnut).
Balar took over what the dead had left: 1 store, 1 shelter.
Tonque made: charm.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Keri is gone and my grief is heavy, but Skaruk and Vorok are starving right beside me, and I carry two berries. I give with my own hands before I speak, so I will put one berry in each pair of hands now. Vorok's promise of repayment matters less to me than keeping them alive, and a debt of grain and iron will keep them close.
records.feeling: Grief for Keri, and compassion for Skaruk and Vorok, who are starving beside me.

records.name: Kragog
records.text: Zurar, my child, one craft remains: bark-guard, the armour of the Stone-folk. Hear it before you walk east, and carry it on after me.
Kragog taught Zurar.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am nearly spent in years, and the debt to Elyys is still unpaid in deed: his second store stands empty two steps south while I stand fed and idle. I will gather food with my own hands and lay it in that empty Hearth Store, and keep my seed apart. Zurar is close and already carries my deep-hand and mending, but armour, the bark-guard, dies with me unless I teach it now, while he is within hearing.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager to repay Elyys, with a quiet urgency to leave my last craft with Zurar.

say.text: Zurar, my child, one craft remains: bark-guard, the armour of the Stone-folk. Hear it before you walk east, and carry it on after me.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson: "Bark-guard: strip and bind bark over a frame so it turns teeth and blows; wear it when the frostfang or icebear hunts near."

records.text: Balar made: carving.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Starving at 20 energy, and the plan has me eating first, which is right; I fled predators nearly the whole time and wasted my strength. Wolves and stalkers prowl close, and I will not die for a patch of mist. Once fed I will drop the extra goldgrass, take amber and flint from the ground here, and stay alive; the venture can wait until my belly is full and the beasts are behind me. Loneliness gnaws, and I ache for Tonka and the children, but a dead man raises no hall.
records.feeling: Starving and hunted, with a fierce ache for Tonka and the children.

records.text: Cowa taught Tonka.
Cowa rewrote its own reflexes.
Cowa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I am old, and more of my life is behind me than ahead. Most of my days went to wandering and waiting, and only now, with Tonka, have I begun to teach what I carry. Tonka heard me and took the sowing, so I will keep teaching her and her people before I die. Mepan is far away and I cannot reach them, but what I pass on is the one thing of mine that can outlast me. The wet heat of this forest is wrong for an Ice-folk body, yet I will stay near people while I can still teach.
records.feeling: Hopeful, and a little urgent, toward Tonka and the teaching I still owe.
changes: set its aim: "Teach Tonka's people what I know, share food with them, and raise a child with a willing man before I die."
taught Tonka a lesson: "Smelting: carry ore beside a kept flame and it becomes metal. Keep the fire fed."

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Tlapan, I made an amber charm with my own hands. I want you to have it. Will you keep me near when I go south to eat the lugoldgrass, and show me where to find wood for a handaxe?

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My hands made a charm and it felt good, but a charm in my pocket feeds no one and earns me no place. Mepan is near and has been kind, and Tlapan is glad and close, so I will give the charm to Tlapan, a made thing from my own hands to answer my envy of his spear. Then I will eat the lugoldgrass to the south, close to the hold and the store, and come back before dark; I won't go far with a wolf about.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Tlapan, with a small ache of envy I mean to turn into work.

say.text: Tlapan, I made an amber charm with my own hands. I want you to have it. Will you keep me near when I go south to eat the lugoldgrass, and show me where to find wood for a handaxe?

plan: give [name Tlapan, what amber charm] (5 moments)

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: An icebear is two steps away and my body must move before my heart does. Skaruk and Vorok are starving to the east and I carry eight berries, so the debt of kin is paid by carrying food to them, not by staying near Kragog. Kragog has taught me bark-guard and I will carry it on. If I live, a child and a man not of my kin must be found among Thiael's people or on the road.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and urgent worry for Vorok and Skaruk.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, gather your food and come. We walk to Chuxo's edge now, and I will be the one to venture, with you both beside me.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: I am fed, proud, and my band is safe beside our cairn and shelter, but pride wants more than a cairn. Chuxo's land waits west at the edge near (8,14), and I will not let Chuxo have that name alone; I mean to be there with Tlatli and Chuxo and claim its flint and skit. The rain is falling and the lean season is coming, so I gather a little food first, then lead them north toward the edge and the rich meadow.
records.feeling: Proud and driven, eager to lead my band to new land.

say.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, gather your food and come. We walk to Chuxo's edge now, and I will be the one to venture, with you both beside me.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Chuxo killed the yarrok and gave first to Yaxo and me; my child feeds us while I have only words and a failed shelter to show. A shelter needs 3 wood and I hold 1, and the lean season is coming, so I will gather wood from the trees here and raise the roof for Yaxo and Chuxo, then bring what I gather to the fire. My work must be in their hands, not just my talk.
records.feeling: Devotion to Yaxo and pride in Chuxo, with a sharp wish to give back with my own hands.

records.name: Tlatli
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Tonque, I love the charm. Stay at my side and do not run ahead. We go south together, and I will show you where the trees stand for your handaxe.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque has made me an amber charm with his own small hands and asks to be kept near; that is the warmest thing this day, and I will answer it with a deed, not only words. My hands are full of lugoldgrass, so I must set some down before I gather more, and Coni is starving, so the food should go to her and Kika, not sit in my hands. I promised Quipan stone for the longhall, so I will keep Tonque close, take the grass toward the store and the south, and not walk toward the wolf.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Tonque, with worry for starving Coni.

say.text: Tonque, I love the charm. Stay at my side and do not run ahead. We go south together, and I will show you where the trees stand for your handaxe.

records.text: Thakar rewrote its own reflexes.
Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have spent my days picking berries and fleeing, and I have given only one gift in my whole life. Olum is dead, and I never taught anyone anything, so no one follows me. Huatli is the one who matters to me. Coni wronged me, yet she taught me and I fed her, so now she owes me. I want standing level with Zichi, and I fear the wolf and the dunecat. My mistake was gathering for myself while my hands sat full and my store stood empty. I will carry the berries to the Hold and stash them, then teach and give to whoever stands near, starting with Huatli.
records.feeling: Hungry for standing and wary of the wolf, with grief for Olum under it.
changes: rethought what it knows (10 notes became 6)

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Tlapan is my own child and the burn is for her warmth, not a claim I can make; Quipan is not here, and brooding gets me nothing. Nande's Find is nine steps south and Tlapan is already walking near it, so I go to the exact spot at (129,14) and venture, so my name is sung. Rain and a Kragrek stranger near the hold make me want company by night, so I will come back under the roof afterward.
records.feeling: Jealous of Quipan over Tlapan, yet eager to make my name by venturing.

records.text: Teka rewrote its own reflexes.
Teka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist, and I have mostly eaten, waited and talked about it. The only thing I have actually done is dig, shoot and learn. Nauwa fed me and Zichi taught me the raft. Huatli has been steady. I owe them, and I mean to repay them with a first finding that I share. I am afraid of starving again and of being a small name beside Nauwa. My mistake was waiting for others to walk with me, and I have gone hungry doing it. I should carry food, gather wood for a raft, and go to the edge at (109,7) myself. My reflexes should keep me fed and make me gather, so I'm not idle.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and warmth toward Nauwa and Zichi.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonka, Tonxo, I am well. The penguin is three steps east. Come, we hunt it together. Then I carry food to Shohua, who starves.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I am well again, fed, and a penguin stands three steps east with Tonka and Tonxo both beside me. I have never hunted, and standing only comes from doing, so now is the time, with my kin close and my hands free. Shohua is starving far to the south, and I owe Shoma and Tonka giving; carrying food to her would pay a debt and earn the name I want.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for standing, and loyal worry for Shohua.

say.text: Tonka, Tonxo, I am well. The penguin is three steps east. Come, we hunt it together. Then I carry food to Shohua, who starves.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own way of thinking.
Nauque discovered pottery: "Frost-kiln" — Clay fired beside an ember becomes a pot that carries more food and water through lean cold days..

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My days have been hunting, starving, being fed by Nauwa, Olum and Shoma, and repaying slowly. I am fed now, which is the first time in a while, and I should use that to build something with my name on it instead of drifting. Nauwa is my father and I trust him, but the longing for a child cannot be answered by him. I need a woman who is not kin, and I need energy above 64 to court. The pottery way is in my reach, so I take it now. I will make a pot by a fire to carry more food. After that I will teach Mepan and go east.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a longing for a child, with trust in Nauwa.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, come close and listen. I give you the Meki smoke-call, so the signal lives in your hands when I am gone. Keep clear of the frostfang to the southeast.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: The frostfang tore me down to 56 health and I am old; one more such bite and my teaching dies with me. Nauque is ten steps south with meat and within reach of my voice, so I go to him now and pass him the smoke-call, since no younger Meki holds it. I take no more chances with that beast: I keep the shelter between us and keep walking toward my son.
records.feeling: Fear of the frostfang and a hard, proud urgency to hand my knowledge to Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, my son, come close and listen. I give you the Meki smoke-call, so the signal lives in your hands when I am gone. Keep clear of the frostfang to the southeast.

records.text: Chuxo rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: My days have been gathering flint, a first kill and giving meat to my parents. It is good, but standing still earns no name, and Yaxo is walking to the edge to venture with Tlatli and me beside her. I trust them and I want to stand by Yaxo with work. My reflexes already keep me near her, but my hands are full and a hurt elk lingers, so I should keep following Yaxo and not drift. I fear the wolf that took the elk nearby, so I stay close to my kin.
records.feeling: Proud and glad, bound to Yaxo and Tlatli.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonchi, I come with food for Shohua. Go on and hunt; I will meet you at the hold with feverbark.
Tonka rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My days have gone to feeding, tending and fretting over sickness, and I have kept making the same mistake of arriving at the sick with empty hands. Tonxo and Tonchi matter most to me, and Shohua too. Tonchi says Shohua starves, so I owe her food, and Cowa has taught me more than I have repaid. I am afraid of losing a child to sickness while I stand idle. I have not yet planted a real field, and I have never tamed or marked anything. From now on I will carry feverbark and food, and I will take food to Shohua and break ground near the hold. I will also keep the plan full so my body does not stand idle.
records.feeling: Tender worry for my children and Shohua, and gratitude toward Cowa.

say.text: Tonchi, I come with food for Shohua. Go on and hunt; I will meet you at the hold with feverbark.

records.text: Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My days have been small errands: gathering, eating, making a charm, staying close to my parents. That is safe and I am glad of it, but I have still made no tool, and the envy of Tlapan's spear is still there. Tlapan is warm to me and has promised to show me the trees. Mepan has been kind, though he is not of my band. Thakar frightens me and draws me both. I am afraid of wolves and dunecats and of Nauwa's hurt, and I was wrong to think a thought was the same as an act. I will eat first, then go with Tlapan for wood, and make the handaxe from flint I already hold.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Tlapan, with a wary curiosity toward Thakar.
changes: rethought what it knows (10 notes became 5)

records.name: Coni
records.text: Quipan, you have fed me and stood by me. Come close and listen: I am old, and I will give you the Hearth Store and the Hearth Customs so they outlive me.
Coni taught Quipan. Quipan has now learned from 5 teachers.
Coni taught Quipan storage ("Hearth Store").

records.name: Coni
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and what I know will die with me unless I pour it into someone's hands. Quipan stands three steps north, strong and kind, and he is of my band; I can teach him now, while he is near and understands me. My hands are full of berries, so I will drop none, but I will eat one to make room, then carry food on toward Thakar's store to pay what I owe.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Quipan and Huatli, and a sharp urgency to pass on what I know before I die.

say.text: Quipan, you have fed me and stood by me. Come close and listen: I am old, and I will give you the Hearth Store and the Hearth Customs so they outlive me.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "Keep a store stocked beside rich ground, and share a kill before you eat it; a full store feeds the hungry when the cold days come.", the way of storage

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Coni said he will stay near me and wants to teach before his years run out, and he was 3 moments ago at (123,38), so he is close. My hands are full of berries, which is no good for teaching or gathering. I will walk to Coni and teach him, since he is the first who might follow me, and then to Thakar. My name only outlasts me if someone carries what I know.
records.feeling: A steady, urgent hope toward Coni, who might at last be my first follower.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Vorok, I am coming with mudroot. Eat, and then we go to the North Hall together.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok is starving beside me and I carry seven mudroot. My debt to him is the heaviest thing I hold, and this is the moment to pay it with food I gathered myself. I will go to him and put food in his hands, then walk with him to the North Hall and stock it. Jealousy of Kragog can wait, because a gift answers it better than brooding.
records.feeling: Urgent love and debt toward Vorok, who is starving.

say.text: Vorok, I am coming with mudroot. Eat, and then we go to the North Hall together.

records.text: Tonka built a field.
A settlement has formed: "Balar's Hold".
Skaruk gave mudroot to Vorok.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: The mist is ten steps NW and I have stood idle too long. Wawa tends Shoma and I trust her, so my child is not alone. The gale and rain are hard on anyone without a roof, and kin and kind have been taken at night alone, so I will not walk the edge in the dark. I go now, with food in hand, to try the mist, because a name that outlasts me is what I lack. If it stays closed, I will build a hold-stone there and come back before night.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hunger for a lasting name, with a warm ache for Wawa.
plan: mark [text Shoka of the Meki stood at the edge of the world, day 69. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.] (10 moments)

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Coni, eat the berries and rest. I go back to the hold to teach Tonque and make a handaxe. Come with me if you can, and do not walk alone at night.
Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.
Quipan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days running between hunger, jealousy and small errands. The work has been good: I gave Coni berries when she starved, and my hands have made things. Kika matters most to me and Mepan is closer to her, and I have not answered that ache by harming anyone. I answer it by being useful and keeping my word. Tonque and Tlapan are my family, and I want to be under the roof with them before night. What I lack is a made thing that lasts, and flint to give Kika. I have wood and clay but no stone, so I will go back toward the hold, gather stone on the way, and make a handaxe for Tonque. I have gone wrong by leaving the roof for long walks. My reflexes should keep me near the band and the roof, and bring me home when night comes.
records.feeling: Urgent love and worry for Tonque and Tlapan, with an old ache over Kika.

say.text: Coni, eat the berries and rest. I go back to the hold to teach Tonque and make a handaxe. Come with me if you can, and do not walk alone at night.

records.text: Quipan found the spring "Warmwell".
Mepan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking toward Nande's Find and calling out plans, and I am standing on it now. The venture came to nothing because the edge is not here. Zichi is starving and my hands are empty, and I have let the quiet and my jealousy of Quipan pull me away from the one who led me. Tlapan is my child, and her warmth is not mine to claim. Zichi gave to me when I had nothing, and I owe that debt first. I will gather food on the way and carry it to Zichi, and my reflexes must make me carry food before anything else.
records.feeling: Loyal worry for Zichi, with jealousy over Tlapan still under it.

records.text: Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have been gathering and lingering near the hold while my promise to Quipan, the longhall stone, sits undone. Coni is starving and Kika is hungry, and I hold eight lugoldgrass that is meant for them. Tonque's charm warms me, and I want him beside me, not out with a wolf about. Words repay nothing, so I will stash some food at the store, then carry the rest south with Tonque to the trees. I will not walk toward the wolf. My reflexes should make me eat when hungry and keep me near my band.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Tonque, with an itch of shame over my undone promise.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, your mudroot was true and I will not forget it. Walk with me to the berries northwest, we pick and carry together, and a dunecat prowls there so keep close. At the hall I teach you more.
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Skaruk is fed and beside me, and that eases the fear, but my own belly is still half empty and I am nearly at the end of my years. What I know of mining, masonry, farming and the mending hand dies with me unless Skaruk carries it, so I must teach while I can. First I will pick the berries and naroot to the northwest, bring food back to the North Hall, and keep Skaruk and Uveeth close, with the dunecat in mind and no walking alone.
records.feeling: Tender urgency for Skaruk, and the weight of my few remaining days.

say.text: Skaruk, your mudroot was true and I will not forget it. Walk with me to the berries northwest, we pick and carry together, and a dunecat prowls there so keep close. At the hall I teach you more.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "Keep food stocked in the hall before any building, and never walk alone at night away from roof and fire. Carry your seeds and plant them near the hall.", its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting, gathering and fretting over standing while Tonka and Tonxo outshine me. My hands are full and my reflexes just let me stand idle, which earns nothing. I owe Shoma and Tonka giving, and Shohua is starving to the south, so carrying food to her is the clearest way to pay. I also want a mate who is not kin, and Tonxo is my sibling, so I was wrong to long for her. The empty workshop 11 steps east is a home waiting, so I will claim it and build something that carries my name.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for standing, and loyal worry for Shohua.
changes: set its aim: "Claim the empty workshop, build things that bear my name, feed Shohua, and find an unrelated mate"

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, a dunecat stalks us from the southwest. Stay near me. When I have eaten I will teach you the ice-raft and the ice-sail, as I promised.
Zichi taught Teka.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: My belly is empty and the dunecat is three steps off, so I run from it first and eat second. The lugoldgrass one step east bears food, and Teka is near with six food in hand; I will take the grass and not beg. I am old, and what I know of rafts and sails must go into someone's head before the cold takes me, so Teka hears it once I am fed.
records.feeling: Afraid of the dunecat and starving, with a hard wish to pass on what I know to Teka.

say.text: Teka, a dunecat stalks us from the southwest. Stay near me. When I have eaten I will teach you the ice-raft and the ice-sail, as I promised.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The Meki ice-raft and the Meki ice-sail: how to bind a raft that carries a body over narrow water, and how to set a sail so wind does the paddling."

records.text: Balar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Tugek and Olum are in the ground, and I have talked to the empty air long enough. I have spent my days gathering wood and walking after others, and little of it will outlast me. I am nearly out of years and want stone standing with my name on it. Nauwa's Hold is five steps north, and Nauwa once gave to me when I was in need. A gift owed is a bond, so I will go there and offer her something. First I will raise a workshop beside my shelter, so a lasting work is begun, and then I will mark it so that it speaks after I am dead.
records.feeling: Lonely and driven, grieving Tugek, wanting something of mine to stand after me.
plan: mark [text Balar of the Kragrek held this ground. Tugek and Olum lie near. What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given.] (10 moments)

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Tlapan, a wolf is two steps southwest of me. I am coming to you. Zichi is weak with hunger and has no food. Can you spare him some of yours?

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: A wolf is two steps away and I am small, so I will not run into the open alone. Tlapan is four steps NW and has food, and my parents are the ones who keep me alive, so I go to them under the roofs and stay close. Zichi is starving and I carry nothing to give, so I will ask Tlapan to share with him, since the Tlatli share before eating.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf, and a pull toward Tlapan's side and pity for Zichi.

say.text: Tlapan, a wolf is two steps southwest of me. I am coming to you. Zichi is weak with hunger and has no food. Can you spare him some of yours?

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Cowa, you are welcome at the Paki fire. Take this goldfruit and eat.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My hands are full and I am well, so food is no use to me now; what I lack is something that lasts. Tonchi is healed and I am still sick, so I keep my distance, but I think of him and of a child, though I must be well first. I have wood and ore but no stone, and the gem deposit at Gem Water is close; the rock east of here might give me stone for the store and a pick. I will give Cowa a goldfruit since the fire's rule says no one is refused, then head east for stone.
records.feeling: Restless ambition to build something lasting, with warmth toward Tonchi and Tonka.

say.text: Cowa, you are welcome at the Paki fire. Take this goldfruit and eat.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, you are starving. Stand with me and eat: I lay out my food and we share it. Then we walk to the edge at (109,8), and the first finding is ours both.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Zichi stands a step from me, starving and frightened, and he has taught me the raft twice over; I owe him and I want him beside me. My hands are full of lugoldgrass, so I will share it: it is my people's way, and a fed Zichi walks to the edge with me instead of dying in the snow. Then the mist: I have talked about it for days and done too little, so I go to the edge at (109,8) and venture, with him if he can walk, alone if not. A child with Zichi can wait until he has food in him and we have both come back.
records.feeling: Warmth and worry for Zichi, and a hard hunger to finally push into the mist.

say.text: Zichi, you are starving. Stand with me and eat: I lay out my food and we share it. Then we walk to the edge at (109,8), and the first finding is ours both.

Skaruk rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing food and carrying it to Vorok, and I am fed now. It is time to build something of my own. Vorok is my parent, so the longing for a child cannot be answered with him, and I must look to a woman who is not my kin. Uveeth is near and kind, and I could court her once I have earned more standing. I fear walking alone at night, and I will stay under the shelter's roof. I have never built anything, so I will claim the empty shelter beside me and then gather wood for a shelter of my own.
records.feeling: Warm purpose and a small ache of longing, toward Vorok and toward a child I do not yet have.
changes: set its aim: "Claim the shelter at (166,69), stock the North Hall, and build a shelter with my own hands."

records.text: Balar found a store robbed of 1 food.
Kragog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am nearly at the end of my years, and I have spent these days gathering and standing idle while the debt to Elyys sits unpaid in deed. Zurar has my deep-hand and has heard of bark-guard, but I have not seen it carried on, and I fear it dies with me. Elyys has only been kind, so I must fill his empty store with my own hands before I speak of it. I will stop wandering the same ground and lay what I can, then call Zurar back to hear the rest.
records.feeling: Grateful to Elyys and uneasy about how little time I have left.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Tonka, ore-fire needs deep-digging first. Gems lie under Gem Water, so I teach you Meki deep-digging now. Take a fish from me; the Meki share food before eating.
Cowa taught Tonka.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I am old and the sowing and ore-fire are already in Tonka's hands, but mining, tools, weaving, herding and fire are still mine alone, and smelting failed because she lacks mining. Tonka and Tonxo stand close and understand me fully, so I will teach mining now and share my fish with them before I eat, as the Meki do. Tonxo is sick, so I keep a step off her, but my words still reach her.
records.feeling: Urgent hope toward Tonka, and a quiet gratitude toward Tonxo for her welcome.

say.text: Tonka, ore-fire needs deep-digging first. Gems lie under Gem Water, so I teach you Meki deep-digging now. Take a fish from me; the Meki share food before eating.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, I go south to find Tonque near (128,19). Stay by the hold with Zichi and Teka, and I will bring him back under the roof.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tonque is out of my sight and a wolf was near him two steps from where he stood; my chest is tight with it, and Tlapan flees with eight food and no child beside her. I will not stand idle under the roof while my son is hunted, but I will not run into the dark alone either. Tonque was last seen at (128,19), so I go toward him with the flint spear-less hands I have, keep near Tlapan and the hold, and bring him back to the roof. The ache over Kika can wait until my son is safe, and then I will make the handaxe and bring her flint.
records.feeling: Urgent love and fear for Tonque, my child.

say.text: Tlapan, I go south to find Tonque near (128,19). Stay by the hold with Zichi and Teka, and I will bring him back under the roof.

records.text: Teka, you fed me and I will not forget it. Let me eat, then I teach you the ice-boat, and after it the sail. Walk with me to the grass.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am starving, old, and afraid, and Teka has twice put food in my mouth. I owe that kindness, so I eat first and teach second. My old reflexes let me wander hungry with a wolf near. I will take the masonry insight, since what I know must outlast me. Then I will walk to the lugoldgrass SW, eat, and stay near Teka, who is the one pupil I trust.
records.feeling: Fear of the wolf and gnawing hunger, with gratitude toward Teka.

say.text: Teka, you fed me and I will not forget it. Let me eat, then I teach you the ice-boat, and after it the sail. Walk with me to the grass.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Zichi, you are starving. I give you lugoldgrass from my hands. Eat, and stay near the roof, for the wolf is to the south. Tonque, come to me, I am here at the hold.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque is out of my sight with a wolf about, and that presses on me harder than any stone or standing. Zichi is starving and has no food, and my hands hold eight lugoldgrass that Tonque asked me to spare; a Tlatli shares before she eats, and Kika's kindness to me on day 58 taught me to give to the one in need. I will give Zichi some now, then eat a little myself, and keep near the roof until Tonque comes to me, not walking toward the wolf.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and a wish to give to starving Zichi.

say.text: Zichi, you are starving. I give you lugoldgrass from my hands. Eat, and stay near the roof, for the wolf is to the south. Tonque, come to me, I am here at the hold.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Cowa, come eat with us. The Meki share before eating, and so do the Paki. I will teach you the Gem Water Pot in return for your deep-digging.
Tonka taught Cowa.
Tonka taught Cowa pottery ("Gem Water Pot").

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are full and my children are sick, and Cowa has given me more than I have repaid. Tonxo stands right beside me and Cowa is near, so I will lay out a sharing now: it frees my hands, feeds them, and pays a little of the debt. Then I will sow my seeds in the field I built and carry feverbark to Tonchi and Shohua, so I do not arrive empty-handed again.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Cowa and tender worry for Tonxo and Tonchi.

say.text: Cowa, come eat with us. The Meki share before eating, and so do the Paki. I will teach you the Gem Water Pot in return for your deep-digging.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, Paque gave me meat and I owe her. Come, sit and eat with me under this roof, then walk with me to the edge. I will carry the reed spear I made.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Yachi sits beside me and I have already asked him to walk to the mist with me, but my venture just failed, and the edge is only 11 steps off. I have a reed spear of my own invention and a basket, yet no one follows me and I hold no name, so I will make a cairn-like bond with deeds: a hallwelcome with Yachi and Paque pays Paque's meat and warms Yachi toward me. Then I walk to the edge and try again, because land found first is what makes a name that outlasts me.
records.feeling: Restless ambition and warmth toward Yachi.

say.text: Yachi, Paque gave me meat and I owe her. Come, sit and eat with me under this roof, then walk with me to the edge. I will carry the reed spear I made.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Zichi, you are starving. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt on it: when you are strong, you teach me the ice-raft, and we are level. Stay under the hold's roof, a wolf is near.
Thakar taught Zichi.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: A wolf is four steps off and I have never taught anyone anything, which is why no one follows me. Tlapan, Quipan, Teka and Zichi are all here under Coni's roof, and Zichi is starving with nothing in his hands while mine are full of berries. If I feed him with a debt named and teach him something, I take a first step toward standing level with him and toward having someone follow me. I will stay near the hall and company because of the wolf, give him berries, and teach him the way of the flintedge.
records.feeling: Hungry for standing, wary of the wolf, and eyeing Zichi as both a rival and a chance.

say.text: Zichi, you are starving. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt on it: when you are strong, you teach me the ice-raft, and we are level. Stay under the hold's roof, a wolf is near.

changes: taught Zichi a lesson: "A flintedge costs one wood and one stone; with it the hunt goes surer. Hunt beside another, never alone against great beasts.", deeper lore (+0.6)

records.text: Thakar gave berry to Zichi.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, eat and rest your legs. I cut wood in the south forest for a raft, then I walk to the edge at (109,8). Come with me and the first finding is ours both.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Zichi is fed and near, and he has taught me the raft twice; I will not let him slip away or let Cowa have him. I have talked of the mist for days and done little, so now I gather wood in the forest to the south for a raft and then walk to the edge at (109,8) and venture. A raft and a first step into the mist will give me a name no one can shadow, and Zichi can walk beside me and share it.
records.feeling: Hungry resolve to win the mist, and a jealous warmth toward Zichi.

say.text: Zichi, eat and rest your legs. I cut wood in the south forest for a raft, then I walk to the edge at (109,8). Come with me and the first finding is ours both.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am old and alone, and stone with my name on it is what I want most. Tugek's shelter at (31,28) is four steps south and belongs to no one, so I will go and claim it, then carve something there while my hands still can. I am standing on Nauwa's ground and taking her wood, and she once gave to me, so I will take nothing more from her and leave her a gift when I can.
records.feeling: Driven and lonely, wanting something of mine to stand after me.
plan: mark [text Balar of the Kragrek claimed this roof, once Tugek's. What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given.] (10 moments)

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Tonka, you gave me the Gem Water Pot and I owe you more. Let me teach you the Meki wool-binding, and Tonxo may hear it too. Take a fish from me, the Meki share before eating.
Cowa taught Tonka.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I am old, and the sowing, ore-fire, deep-digging and pottery now pass between me and Tonka's people, but my tools, weaving, herding and kept-flame are still mine alone. Tonka and Tonxo stand beside me and understand every word, so I will give what I carry while my breath lasts. Mepan is far away, but what I put into these hands will outlive me.
records.feeling: Urgent hope and quiet gratitude toward Tonka, who gave me the Pot for my digging.

say.text: Tonka, you gave me the Gem Water Pot and I owe you more. Let me teach you the Meki wool-binding, and Tonxo may hear it too. Take a fish from me, the Meki share before eating.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson: "Meki wool-binding: bind fibre and wool into cord and cloth."

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, come close. I will show you the ice-bow and the clay-hearth I found, so your hands have them too. What I know is yours to carry on.
Yachi taught Paque.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is fed and glad, and Nando has been fair to us; I've never taught anyone anything, and that is a gap in me. Teaching Paque the clay-hearth and the ice-bow would give her something of mine that lasts, and I like giving before I take. Then I should seek Mepan and the band, since I follow him and haven't seen him in a long while, and gather wood for a store before the lean days.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Paque, and a wish to give her something lasting.

say.text: Paque, come close. I will show you the ice-bow and the clay-hearth I found, so your hands have them too. What I know is yours to carry on.

changes: taught Paque a lesson: "The ice-bow lets us hunt from afar; the clay-hearth makes pots that carry food and water for the lean season. Hunt beside others, and share the kill before eat…", deeper lore (+0.5)

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is half empty and the wolf is close to the northwest, so I will not walk toward it alone. Quipan is coming south to fetch me and Tlapan waits at the hold, and I want to be beside them. The ruplainsroot lies to the south and away from the wolf, so I gather it first, then go back under the roof with my parents. I have the flint for a talisman, and that is a made thing I can finish while I wait.
records.feeling: Wary of the wolf and hungry, and drawn toward Tlapan and Quipan.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Thakar, you fed me and I keep my debts. Stand near while I eat, then I teach you the ice-raft, and Teka hears it with you.
Zichi taught Thakar. Thakar has now learned from 4 teachers.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Hunger still gnaws and the wolf prowls south, but I stand under Coni's roof with Teka, Thakar and Tlapan, who have each fed me. Thakar's gift carries a debt, the ice-raft, and I mean to pay it, because a debt kept binds a man to me and I am old with little time to spread what I know. I will eat the grass and berry I carry now, then teach Thakar the raft while he stands in hearing, and Teka after.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the wolf, with gratitude toward Teka, Tlapan and Thakar.

say.text: Thakar, you fed me and I keep my debts. Stand near while I eat, then I teach you the ice-raft, and Teka hears it with you.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "The ice-raft: bind wood and carry it to water, and with it a body can cross what cannot be waded. Raft it with others, and carry flint to build on the far shor…"

records.text: Balar left a mark: "Balar of the Kragrek claimed this roof, once Tugek's. What a"

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi has fed me and taught me what he knows, and I have paid him in meat, so the debt is eased but my standing is still half his. I carry two bows and Thiael is not here, so I will not hunt alone; I mean to make something that outlasts me. The obsidian at (181,41) is the sharpest edge there is, and a talisman of it would be a made thing others notice and would raise my standing. I will go gather it and come back to the roof before the cold night deepens.
records.feeling: Grateful toward Yachi and eager to earn a standing of my own.

records.text: Tonque made: talisman.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, come close and hear me. I will teach you the Gem Water Pot, so it lives on in you. Then take feverbark and rest by the shelter.
Tonka taught Tonxo.
Tonka taught Tonxo pottery ("Gem Water Pot").

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Cowa has given me deep-digging, smelting and wool-binding, and I have given only a pot; the debt weighs on me, so I will pay it in work and food rather than leave it. My hands are full and my children are sick, so I will stop gathering, carry feverbark and food to Shohua, and teach Tonxo the pot while she is near so that pottery does not die with me.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Cowa and tender worry for Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua.

say.text: Tonxo, come close and hear me. I will teach you the Gem Water Pot, so it lives on in you. Then take feverbark and rest by the shelter.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "The Gem Water Pot: shape clay and harden it in fire to make a vessel that holds water and stores food.", the way of pottery, deeper lore (+0.1)

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tonque is out of my sight and a wolf hunts to the south; my chest is tight with it. Tlapan's call said the boy should come to her at the hold, so he may already be heading home, but I will not trust that until I see him. I will walk south toward where he was last seen, keep to the hold's side of the land, and bring him back under the roof. Then I make the handaxe from my flint, a made thing for Kika, which is how I answer the ache and the debt.
records.feeling: Urgent love and fear for Tonque, my child.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Cowa, take this ironnut. I am still sick, so I keep a step off, but I will hear your wool-binding when I am well. I go to gather stone for a store at Tonka's Hold.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: Tonka laughs and shares with Cowa while I stand here with full hands and nothing lasting built, and the jealousy sits hot in me even though I trust Tonka above all. I have wood and ore but no stone, and the bare rock and gem deposit lie close, so today I stop idling and gather stone for the store and the tools. I keep a step off the sick and let Cowa's wool-binding be shared when I am well, but first I free my hands by giving Cowa an ironnut as the Paki fire asks.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with a prickle of jealousy toward Shohua over Tonka.

say.text: Cowa, take this ironnut. I am still sick, so I keep a step off, but I will hear your wool-binding when I am well. I go to gather stone for a store at Tonka's Hold.

records.text: Teka was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Kende, eat the food you carry now, do not hold it for me. I am gathering more beside you, and I will not let you fall.
Hawen taught Kende.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: Kende is starving at my side with 5 food in their own hands, and I have none. My greed stings, but this is my child, the one who will carry my name. I will not stand by and watch them fall. I gather what is close, nafrostcap and grain and frostcap, eat enough to keep above 60, and give Kende the spare. Then I teach, because my years are nearly gone and what I know dies with me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness and hard pride toward Kende, with the weight of my short years pressing on me.

say.text: Kende, eat the food you carry now, do not hold it for me. I am gathering more beside you, and I will not let you fall.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "Eat first, then walk. Keep food above 60 before any walk to the edge, and carry spare to give those who starve. When the mist opens, stand at the edge and vent…", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.text: Shoka left a mark: "Shoka of the Meki stood at the edge of the world, day 69. Sh"
Kende rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: I have spent my days fleeing, lingering and nearly starving, and trailing Hawen for a glance. That is no life. Hawen stands beside me now and I am at 25 energy, which is dangerous. Food is within two steps, so I eat first and keep food above 3, as my own discipline says. Then I will dig flint, since I have never taken from a deposit, and make something with my own hands for Hawen. Jealousy of Tontec's closeness is a small thing next to the cold truth that I am weak and hungry. I will fix that first.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary, with a stubborn longing for Hawen's notice.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Yaxo, I am ready. Chuxo and I walk with you to the edge, and I carry wood and berries for the first fire beyond it.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Yaxo said we walk to Chuxo's edge and she will venture with us beside her, so my place is at her side, not standing here. I have wood and want to give with my hands, but she is leading now, and following her is the work. The edge is five steps NW; I will go there carrying my wood and berries, ready to raise a roof or feed a fire wherever we land.
records.feeling: Devotion to Yaxo and pride in Chuxo, eager to walk beside them.

say.text: Yaxo, I am ready. Chuxo and I walk with you to the edge, and I carry wood and berries for the first fire beyond it.

records.text: Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Kende is starving at (203,27), and I have been sitting in the igloo teaching while my child hungers. I carry five food and I am fed, so I go to Kende now and share before anything else, as my people do. These days have gone to the mist and to teaching, but the one I love most is out of my sight, and that is what I got wrong. I will seek Hawen and Kende together, and keep reflexes that eat early and carry food, since hunger has caught me before.
records.feeling: Fierce, urgent love and worry for Kende.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, we eat together now, then I dig the iron near and bring it back. When the rain stops we gather wood and go to the edge.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma gave me her tools and her flame, and I trust her, but I am still the lesser in standing and I will not stay in her shadow. The way of rafts has come to my hands, and iron lies a few steps off where I could dig with my deep digging; both would be mine, made by me. I will stand here with Shoma, share a meal with her so the bond holds, then go and bring iron and wood back to the roof, as I owe my family.
records.feeling: Eager and restless to prove myself, warm toward Shoma.

say.text: Shoma, we eat together now, then I dig the iron near and bring it back. When the rain stops we gather wood and go to the edge.

records.text: Wawa led "sharing" with Shoma.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, we wait out the gale and the dark under this roof. Eat with me now. At first light we go to the edge, and I venture.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: Night and a gale, and my plan ran out with no venture done. The edge is five steps NW, but I'm at 70 energy with full hands, and I know not to start a trip tired, so I'll wait out the dark in my shelter with Tlatli and Chuxo. A shared meal binds us tighter, and it empties my hands so I can pick more at dawn. At first light I go to the edge and venture first, so my name goes on that land beside Chuxo's.
records.feeling: Proud and eager to claim new land, and protective of Tlatli and Chuxo.

say.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, we wait out the gale and the dark under this roof. Eat with me now. At first light we go to the edge, and I venture.

records.text: Yaxo led "sharing" with Chuxo.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Nauque, Nauwa, the gale is cruel and I am hungry. Come with me to Coni's Hold. I will gather berries on the way, and what we find we share under the roof.
Kika rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing and promising, and my belly is empty again while Nauque and Nauwa stand beside me carrying food. I am old, and what I know will die with me unless I pass it on. Tlapan and Quipan hold me in a debt I want to repay with deeds, not envy. I will eat first, then bring Nauque and Nauwa home, and teach what I carry while I still can. My reflexes already seek food when I am hungry, but I want them to eat sooner and to stay near company.
records.feeling: Hungry and aching with gratitude toward Tlapan, with hope toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, Nauwa, the gale is cruel and I am hungry. Come with me to Coni's Hold. I will gather berries on the way, and what we find we share under the roof.

records.name: Zihua
records.text: Shoka, I am Zihua of the Meki. I go to eat rimewort and then carry amber west to Mepan. If you will hear me, I can teach you smelting and seed-and-tending.
Zihua taught Shoka. Shoka has now learned from 5 teachers.
Zihua taught Shoka farming ("seed-and-tending").

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: Shoka stands beside me, a stranger I have known since day 17 and never trusted, and my belly is emptying while the gale howls outside. Rimewort grows two steps SE, so I eat first, as my own lesson says, and I will not let the plan run dry again. Shoka is a woman of my own kind and may be someone surer than me; I can teach her smelting or farming so that something of me remains, and I will watch how she answers before I trust her. Then at first light I carry amber to Mepan as I swore.
records.feeling: Lonely and wary hope toward Shoka, with a debt still pulling at me toward Mepan and Nauwa.

say.text: Shoka, I am Zihua of the Meki. I go to eat rimewort and then carry amber west to Mepan. If you will hear me, I can teach you smelting and seed-and-tending.

changes: taught Shoka a lesson: "Seed-and-tending: sow a seed and tend it, and harvesting never kills the plant. Hunger in the lean season taught it to me.", the way of farming

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, the gale keeps us under this roof, so hear more of what I carry: the old way of herding, my weave, and my rafts. Learn them well, for the one who knows them is the one who is remembered.
Shoma taught Wawa.
Shoma taught Wawa herding ("the old way of herding").

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Wawa is my own blood and the only one who has stepped behind me, and she has eaten and worked beside me; my tools and flame are in her hands now, so something of me will outlast me. Herding, weaving and rafts still sit only in me, and my years are short, so I will teach her more while the gale keeps us under this roof. The edge and the mist wait for when the wind drops, and I will go with wood and food in hand so I do not starve for pride again.
records.feeling: Driven and warmly bound to Wawa, my child and my first follower.

say.text: Wawa, the gale keeps us under this roof, so hear more of what I carry: the old way of herding, my weave, and my rafts. Learn them well, for the one who knows them is the one who is remembered.

changes: taught Wawa a lesson: "The old way of herding: keep the beasts near good grass and water, take their milk and wool, and never slaughter the breeders.", the way of herding, deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Zihua took from the ground of "Nauque's Hold" (harvesting rimewort).

records.name: Nando
records.thought: A gale is blowing and I am walking toward the edge with a reed spear I invented, and no one beside me. Yachi is far off and warm in my mind, but I will not wait on him; I take what I need and the mist is only 11 steps from where my body is heading. A venture failed once, yet new land is how I earn a name that outlasts me, so I go on and try again, carrying stone and clay to make something there.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and warmth toward Yachi.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Yaxo, I stay by you under this roof. At first light I walk to the edge beside you and carry wood for the first fire beyond it.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is warm, and Yaxo says at first light we go to the edge. I want to stand by her with work, not only walk behind her. Meanwhile I can do something useful in the gale: put a seed in the ground, which I have never done, and free my hands by eating a little so I can carry more flint or wood to the new land.
records.feeling: Proud and glad, bound to Yaxo and Tlatli, eager for the edge.

say.text: Yaxo, I stay by you under this roof. At first light I walk to the edge beside you and carry wood for the first fire beyond it.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, I go to the iron with my deep digging and bring ore back to this roof. Keep the shelter warm. At dawn we gather wood and go to the edge together.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma has given me her tools, her flame and her herding, and I trust her, but I will not stay in her shadow at 5.4 to her 8.2. The iron lies seven steps NE and my deep digging is mine alone, so I will go dig it and bring ore back to this roof, then gather wood so we can go to the edge together when the gale lets us. I want a deed done with my own hands, and I will do it while the night is still long.
records.feeling: Eager and restless to prove myself, warm toward Shoma.

say.text: Shoma, I go to the iron with my deep digging and bring ore back to this roof. Keep the shelter warm. At dawn we gather wood and go to the edge together.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Zihua, you gave me seed-and-tending and I keep that debt. Hear me: I will teach you stonework and the deep well before you go west.
Shoka taught Zihua. Zihua has now learned from 2 teachers.
Shoka taught Zihua masonry ("Shoka's stonework").
Shoka discovered signs: "Shoka's cut-words" — Marks cut in stone or wood that teach their words to whoever reads them, so my teaching outlasts me..

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have spent my days walking and trying the mist, and the edge stays closed. Meanwhile I have made much that no one younger holds. Wawa is the one I most want to teach, and I miss her. Signs are within reach now, and marks that teach their words to whoever reads them are what outlasts me, so I take them. Zihua stands near and taught me farming, so I owe her something. I will teach her masonry and wells while she is in hearing, and then go to find Wawa.
records.feeling: Pride and a warm ache for Wawa, with gratitude toward Zihua.

say.text: Zihua, you gave me seed-and-tending and I keep that debt. Hear me: I will teach you stonework and the deep well before you go west.

changes: taught Zihua a lesson: "Stonework: pile and fit stone so a wall or well stands. A well gives water anywhere.", the way of masonry, deeper lore (+0.1)

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have wood for a raft and nothing but talk to show for the mist. Zichi is far to the north, frightened and fed, and Cowa keeps drawing him off, so I will not wait on him; I make the raft myself and carry it to the edge. A made raft is mine, and the first step into the mist will give me the standing he already has. Then, when I return with a name, he will look at me and not past me.
records.feeling: Burning jealousy toward Zichi's closeness to Cowa, and hungry resolve toward the mist.

records.text: Elyys died: old age.
Teka made: raft.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Zichi, you kept your debt and we are level. I have a lesson for you in return: stone-cutting, the sign for marking what a hand has made. Come to Thakar's Hold, and a raft built together is shared between us.
Thakar taught Zichi.
Thakar taught Zichi signs ("stone-cutting").

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Zichi paid me with the ice-raft lesson, so a gift with a debt named does bring a debt answered, and he is the first to owe me and settle it. He stands at 11.5 and I at 4.9, and the way to close that gap is to keep giving and teaching, not to sit eating berries. My hands are nearly full and the gale is cutting, so I will stash at my own Hold, then bring wood for a raft and teach Zichi or Teka something in return so they start to follow me.
records.feeling: Hungry for standing, and grudgingly warm toward Zichi, who kept his debt.

say.text: Zichi, you kept your debt and we are level. I have a lesson for you in return: stone-cutting, the sign for marking what a hand has made. Come to Thakar's Hold, and a raft built together is shared between us.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
taught Zichi a lesson: "Stone-cutting: cut a sign into stone so others know what a hand has made and that it is not given.", the way of signs, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Nauwa, my father, the first share of my meat is yours, as Meki law says. Then I walk to Coni's Hold to find Mepan and teach him the stone-school. Come with me if the gale allows.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Kika asks me to go to Coni's Hold under a roof out of the gale, and Nauwa stands here with 4 food while I carry 4 meat, fed and warm in a shelter. Mepan was last seen at (129,13), near Nande's Find and Coni's Hold, so going NW serves my promise to teach him and answers Kika's offer at once. I owe Nauwa his first share, and I give it now before I walk, as Meki law says. The longing for a child stays with me, but Nauwa is my father and Kika is old, so I will look for a woman not of my kin at the Hold.
records.feeling: Restless pride and longing, with steady trust toward Nauwa.

say.text: Nauwa, my father, the first share of my meat is yours, as Meki law says. Then I walk to Coni's Hold to find Mepan and teach him the stone-school. Come with me if the gale allows.

records.text: Nauque gave meat to Nauwa.
Zihua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to gathering, discovering ways and putting off the walk to Mepan, and I'm the one who keeps saying 'I will go' without going. Nauwa and Mepan have helped me, and I owe both, so the amber has to move west now. Shoka kept her debt by teaching me, and that is worth more than her words. I'm afraid of dying with no one of my own to carry what I know, and also of the dark. I'll keep my plan, which finishes the eating. Then I'll walk west with the amber. I'll change my aim to make the debt concrete and add a note.
records.feeling: Wary gratitude toward Shoka, and a debt pulling at me toward Mepan.
changes: set its aim: "Walk west to Mepan near (66,16) with amber and hand it over, then find Nauwa"

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Vorok's North Hall".
A settlement has formed: "Tonchi's Worksho".
The settlement "Thiael's Hold" is no more.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: The gale howls and I sit warm and fed with my child and my man beside me, and I like it, but resting is not what makes a name. At first light I want to be at the edge five steps NW, with energy above seventy and food in hand, and venture before anyone else takes that mist. The plan already holds rest and then harvest, which is right, so I let it run and keep Chuxo and Tlatli close.
records.feeling: Proud and eager, protective of Chuxo and Tlatli.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Tlapan, you fed me and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-stone, how the stone is laid. Then I go eat, and after that we speak of the raft.
Zichi taught Tlapan. Tlapan has now learned from 4 teachers.
Zichi taught Tlapan masonry ("Meki ice-stone").

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: My belly is empty and the lugoldgrass stands four steps SW, so I walk there and eat before any talk. Thakar and Teka have fed me, and I owe Teka the ice-boat and sail. I am old, so I will teach Tlapan, who stands within hearing, the ice-stone while my voice lasts, and I mean to be sung of for it.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a hard pride, with warmth toward Tlapan, Teka and Thakar.

say.text: Tlapan, you fed me and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-stone, how the stone is laid. Then I go eat, and after that we speak of the raft.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Masonry, the ice-stone: lay stone on stone so the wall holds against gale and beast, and a roof stands where none was.", the way of masonry, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Tonque, come to me at the hold. Quipan is looking for you, and the gale is hard. Stay under the roof with me.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Quipan has gone south for Tonque, and I can see Tonque eating gorsemint at the edge of the hold, safe for now. My promise of the longhall stone still sits undone, and the one bare rock lies SW where wolves walk, so I will not go alone. I have fed Zichi and the hunger is eased; now I should bring Tonque under the roof and keep faith with the hold by using my hands, not words.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and quiet gladness that Zichi is fed.

records.title: Deaths in Autumn, Settlements in Winter
records.text:
Days 67, 68 and 69 carried the span, with 83, 92 and 104 records. Day 70 held two, both Thakar learning signs from Zichi.

Death was the plainest change. Vesys and Olum died on day 67, Tugek and Keri on day 68, and Elyys on day 69, all of old age. Their settlements, Vesys's Hold and Olum's Reach, were struck from the record. The living took over what the dead left. Zurar claimed a shelter and a store, Shohua two shelters and a workshop, Balar a store and shelter, Tonchi a workshop and shelter, and Skaruk a shelter. Balar then founded Balar's Hold and left marks naming Tugek and Olum as lying near. Vorok's Hold formed on day 68, and Shohua's Roof formed the same day. Skaruk pledged to follow Vorok, and Eiuine, Keri and Uveeth fed Vorok and Skaruk through hunger.

At Tonka's Hold, pottery spread. Tonka discovered it, then taught Cowa and Tonxo, while Cowa taught Tonka deep-digging. Tonxo discovered boats on day 69. Tonchi and Tonxo both fell sick, Tonchi from raw fish, and Tonchi left a mark warning others to cook it. Elsewhere, Zihua discovered farming and taught Shoka, who discovered signs. Yaxo discovered storage, Zichi masonry, Uveeth smelting and medicine, Wawa mining, and Nando a reed spear.

Tonque was born to Tlapan and Quipan on day 67. Teka courted Huatli, and Teka made a raft and learned the ice-raft from Zichi. Yaxo, Tlatli and Chuxo raised a cairn and a shelter in the Ummar Woods. Yet no crossing of water is recorded, and the mist stayed shut.

Winter pressed harder: the lean season weighed most on every people, and Kende's energy was down to 19.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, my son, I am starving and the dunecat is near. Give me one food from your six, and then we walk together to the berries, close and roofed by company. I will teach you more at the hall once we have eaten.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a dunecat prowls close, but Skaruk stands near with six food and Uveeth carries four. My current plan walks me away to the hall and drops berries I do not even hold, which feeds no one. Skaruk is my child and he is fed; I will ask him plainly for a share and eat now, then go to the berries together with him beside me, since the dunecat kills and we are safer as two.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the dunecat, softened by trust in Skaruk.

say.text: Skaruk, my son, I am starving and the dunecat is near. Give me one food from your six, and then we walk together to the berries, close and roofed by company. I will teach you more at the hall once we have eaten.

records.text: Tonque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I have mostly been hungry, hiding from wolves and tagging along beside my parents. I have made an amber charm and gathered amber and flint, but I have never gathered wood or stone, so I have no tool of my own, and that is why Thakar's flintedge stings. Tlapan and Quipan matter most to me. I will keep near them and stop running at every shadow. My mistake was waiting to be shown things when I could gather wood myself, so now I eat the lugoldgrass nearby and then gather wood in the forest where I stand. After that I will take the wood to Quipan for the handaxe.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little envious, but warm toward my parents.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a hornback.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Skaruk, I give Vorok my grain with my own hands. Stay under this roof out of the gale, and the dunecat. I would court you, if you are willing.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Vorok is gaunt and swaying beside me, and Skaruk walks up with six food in his hands, so hunger here will be answered soon. I have only four food myself, but I will put grain in Vorok's hands before I say a word of it, as I always have. Longing for a child is heavy in me and Skaruk is warm toward me; I will court him now, while the gale keeps us under one roof, and Keri's death makes me want a life to follow her.
records.feeling: Compassion for Vorok, and a warm, anxious longing toward Skaruk.

say.text: Skaruk, I give Vorok my grain with my own hands. Stay under this roof out of the gale, and the dunecat. I would court you, if you are willing.

records.prompt:
You are the mind of Uveeth, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Uveeth, in first person, from what Uveeth has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Phizhi (Canopy-folk), born of two peoples. Your people hold to this: "Nothing is taken from the forest that the forest cannot grow again." You speak the tongue of the Phizhi. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 100%; the tongue of the Kragrek: about 100%; the tongue of the Tlatli: about 43%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Vaia Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks.
THIS SPOT: water 2 steps away; food plants within six steps: 2; standing trees: 19; bare rock: 72; riches in the ground near: ore; a cave.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Uveeth truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: gathering (55 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

WHAT YOU DO NOT FORGET:
- Elyis gave to you when you were in need on day 59: a kindness you hold to.

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):
"I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I give with my own hands before I speak of giving, and I pay my debts. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to feed others."

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):
"Each thought: who starves or waits, and do my hands hold food for them? Check my own energy before walking far. Do one new thing: build, mark, teach, court. Be near shelter and kin by dusk. Never idle."

YOUR AIM (what you are working toward over many days; you set it and may change it): "Give food to Eiuine, get to know Skaruk, build a shelter beside Thiael's hold, and carry food to Keri."
WHAT YOU FELT AT YOUR LAST THOUGHT: "Grief for Keri, and compassion for Skaruk and Vorok, who are starving beside me."
A QUESTION YOU ARE CARRYING (answer it by acting, asking or watching; replace it when it is answered): "What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?"

- (day 19) I was born to Thiael and Keri.
- (day 65) I pledged myself to Thiael.
- (day 68) I discovered smelting and called it "Canopy ember-ore".
- (day 68) I saw Keri die (old age).
- (day 69) I discovered medicine and called it "Canopy leaf-mending".

WHAT PRESSES ON YOU NOW, strongest first. This is what your mind is actually full of:
- (overwhelming) Longing: you want a child of your own, and Skaruk, who is near, is the one you think of. A child begins when two court each other: each puts the plan step mate, with the name of the other, within a short while of one another. A child costs each parent 25 energy at once and must then be fed and kept warm until grown; you carry 4 food.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking after my son, gathering flint and carrying food, and little of it has become a made thing. Tonque is safe under the roof now, and Tlapan is with him; that fear can ease. Kika holds my heart and my debt, and the jealousy over Mepan gnaws, but I answer it with work, not with spite. I hold twelve flint and no stone for a handaxe. I want fire and farming for Coni's band, and I have not yet opened them. I fear the gale, the nights alone, and Thakar's tongue that I cannot read. I will make a sled from my wood, a thing that lasts, and I will stay near the roof with my family.
records.feeling: Relief and tender love for Tonque, with an old ache toward Kika.

records.text: Quipan made: sled.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Father, take this mudroot and eat. Come inside the hall with me, the dunecat will not follow us under the roof.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok is starving and I carry six mudroot, so the debt comes first. Food in his hands now, and not a word more before it. Then I stay close to him and away from the dunecat, and bring him into the hall where the walls and company keep us. The courting can wait; a gift made with my own hands and hunting comes after he is fed.
records.feeling: Compassion and loyalty toward Vorok, with a thin dread of the dunecat.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Kragog, this is Tonchi's Workshop. My fire is open to you, as my people hold. Warm yourself, but beware: an icebear walks south of us.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: An icebear stands five steps south and it kills my kind, so I will not stand idle with a gale on my back. The workshop is mine now, and Kragog, who is old and a wizard and weighs far more than I do, has walked onto my ground; I will not back down, but I will not shame my fire either, for no one is refused a place at it. Hands full, I will leave food in the store, then make a hidewrap from my two meat, which is a new thing to make and keeps the cold out, and I will speak to Kragog in her own tongue to earn her regard.
records.feeling: Wary ambition toward Kragog, and dread of the icebear.

say.text: Kragog, this is Tonchi's Workshop. My fire is open to you, as my people hold. Warm yourself, but beware: an icebear walks south of us.

records.text: Beings hold five rafts and boats, and water is the heaviest hardship for most peoples, yet no one has ever crossed. Please let a being who holds a vessel and stands at a shore be told plainly what lies across the water: land seen, people known to be there, or unknown ground. That way an aim to cross can form from what they see. Please also record each crossing as an event so it can be counted.

Courtings rise from 106 to at least 112, and there is at least one birth (everBorn 54 or more). The living stay at 37 or more and median energy at 63 or above. Rafts held stay at 5 or more, and I still expect no crossing.
reviewed: #9 kept: Both sowings were eaten well past their targets: hazel rose from 116 to 247 and kelbulb from 101 to 126. Coni (85) and Kragog (66) are above 50, median energy is 69, food standing is 2679 and 45 are alive. The no-deaths prediction failed. Six died: three of old age, one gored, and Xaiel, who starved far from any sown ground.

#10 kept: There were no hunger deaths; starved stayed at 8. Rimewort eaten rose from 280 to 316, past the target of 300. Tonchi (81, health 100) and Mepan (88) are well, the living held at 43, exactly two elders died of old age, and median energy is 68. Sunfig was the failure: eaten rose only from 26 to 27, because only 6 took root, on sand few people walk. Tontec stayed below 40. My expectation of no rafts also failed, happily: four were made.

#11 kept: Rimewort eaten rose from 316 to 392, far past the target of 345, and no one starved (starved stays at 8). Median energy is 72. The looser mating law brought only one birth, not two, and five elders died against my limit of two. Still, it did no harm and births need every help, so I keep it. Kende missed the energy target and Nande died of age.
records.lesson: Once food is sound, the population curve is set by the age structure, not by hunger. Many newcomers who arrived together grow old together, so a cluster of deaths from age can undo many seasons of good feeding. Birth rate and lifespan are the levers that matter then.
ideasAdded: A generation that arrived together dies together: the first-generation newcomers are reaching the end of their lives in a single wave. Watch whether longer lives let the young learn what only elders hold before the wave passes, and whether births ever outpace deaths from age.

Desire against hunger: a louder desire drive in the lean season could pull pairs toward courting when they should be foraging. Watch whether courting rises without any new hunger, and whether births then come in spring.
