Tonchi made: hidewrap.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Zihua, you follow me, so hear this: I give you the Meki smoke-call. Keep it and teach it on when I am gone.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: The frostfang is six steps north and I am old and torn, so I will not test it again. Nauque walks toward Coni's Hold with the stone-school in his hands, and the smoke-call must pass into him before the cold takes me. Zihua follows me and is near enough, so I teach her what I carry as well, and I leave my mark where others will read it.
records.feeling: A hard, proud urgency to hand on what I know, with fear of the frostfang under it.

say.text: Zihua, you follow me, so hear this: I give you the Meki smoke-call. Keep it and teach it on when I am gone.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, when Tonque is under the roof, come with me to the bare rock for the longhall stone. We go in daylight, together, with spears.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tlapan has awakened to the art of drain and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to gathering, fretting over Tonque and giving food away. That is good, but my words about the longhall stone have outrun my hands. Quipan and Tonque matter most to me, and Kika's old kindness still binds me. Zichi paid me back with the ice-stone, and I want to repay him in turn. I fear wolves on the road to the bare rock, and I fear Thakar, whom I cannot read. I have been waiting for safety to come to me. This time I will change my reflexes so I stay near the hold, and then go for the stone in daylight with Quipan beside me.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and a stubborn wish to keep my promise of the longhall stone.

say.text: Quipan, when Tonque is under the roof, come with me to the bare rock for the longhall stone. We go in daylight, together, with spears.

changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)
set its aim: "Go with Quipan to the bare rock for stone, then finish the longhall at Coni's Hold and feed Kika and Coni first."

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Tonque, you carry no food and the gale is hard. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt named: when you have food, you bring me two, and we are level. Then I teach you stone-cutting, the sign for markin
Thakar taught Tonque. Tonque has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Zichi paid his debt and I stand at 4.9 to his 11.5; the gap closes only by giving and teaching more, not by sitting on berries. Tonque is a child standing beside me with nothing in his hands, and a gift with a named debt to a boy of Coni's band makes the first of Coni's people owe me, which stings Coni a little for his raid. I keep 5 berries, which is enough for me, so I will give him some and teach him stone-cutting.
records.feeling: Hungry for standing, and grudgingly warm toward Zichi.

say.text: Tonque, you carry no food and the gale is hard. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt named: when you have food, you bring me two, and we are level. Then I teach you stone-cutting, the sign for marking what a hand has made.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Stone-cutting: a sign cut in stone marks what a hand has made, so it belongs to that hand until it is given.", deeper lore (+3)

records.text: Thakar gave berry to Tonque.
Wawa rewrote its own way of thinking.
Wawa discovered rafts: "Wawa's rafts" — Logs lashed with shell string into a flat raft that carries me over deep water, slowly..

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing Shoma's standing, digging iron and walking, and I carry twelve ore that no one has asked for. Shoma is the one who matters most. She fed me, taught me and gave me her flame, and she is my parent, so my longing for a child has to find another man. I have never taught anyone, never planted a seed and never fished, and those are easy deeds that build standing. The gale keeps us under this roof, so I will turn the way of rafts into something of my own and then stash food and gather wood beside Shoma.
records.feeling: Eager and warm toward Shoma, restless to be more than her shadow.
changes: set its aim: "Earn standing by bringing food, wood and stone to my family's roof, hunt beside Shoka and Shoma, and plant, fish and teach to build deeds of my own."

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is emptying and the gale is hard, and Tlapan wants me under the roof near them. Thakar stands one step from me with a flintedge and I cannot read his words, so I will not stand close or raise a hand; I move toward my parents. I have never gathered wood or stone, and that is why I have no tool. After I eat, I will gather stone from the ore rock and then wood, so I can make my first flint thing beside Quipan.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary of Thakar, but safe and warm toward my parents.

records.text: Shohua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have spent my days fleeing, starving and wandering, and my standing has grown too little for all that work. Tonka, Tonxo and the children are far west at about (99,64), and I ache for them more than for any hall. Zihua draws me too. I am fed now, and a free shelter stands 7 steps SE, so I will claim it as a home and a base. Then I will bring Tonchi and the others there. Stone is what I lack, and bare rock lies near that shelter. My reflexes must send me to gather stone and plant when I am fed, and must stop me wandering aimlessly.
records.feeling: Lonely and driven, longing for Tonka and the children.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, Tonque is under the roof with us. I will go with you to the bare rock for the longhall stone, in daylight and together. I take flint so I can make a handaxe there for Tonque.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tonque is safe and glad, and Thakar is giving him food, so the stranger has shown a gift and not a raised hand; I stay wary but will not drive him off. My hands hold twelve flint and no made thing, and the old ache over Kika is best answered by work, not spite. I will gather one wood and one stone to make the handaxe I have promised Tonque, then take Tlapan to the bare rock in daylight with spears as she asked, and the stone for the handaxe can come from there.
records.feeling: Tender relief for Tonque, with wary curiosity toward Thakar.

say.text: Tlapan, Tonque is under the roof with us. I will go with you to the bare rock for the longhall stone, in daylight and together. I take flint so I can make a handaxe there for Tonque.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Coni, come close. I am Huatli, the one who opened the Halka Heights. Take another berry, and hear my Open Hearth School, for we are both old and what we know should outlast us.
Huatli taught Coni. Coni has now learned from 4 teachers.
Huatli taught Coni schooling ("Huatli's Open Hearth School").
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I have spent my days walking, feeding others and chasing the idea of a follower, and nobody follows me yet. Coni is old, content and has his own band. He took my berries but he teaches others, not me. Thakar is my blood and he is the one I should reach, along with the teaching I owe him before I die. My hands are full of berries I don't need, and that is a mistake. I will drop the habit of hoarding a full pack, give a berry or two to Coni, teach him, and then walk west to Thakar. I'm old, and the gale is cold even for an Ice-man.
records.feeling: Urgent hope toward Coni, and a restless pull toward Thakar.

say.text: Coni, come close. I am Huatli, the one who opened the Halka Heights. Take another berry, and hear my Open Hearth School, for we are both old and what we know should outlast us.

changes: taught Coni a lesson: "The Open Hearth School: a place where one who sits learns twice as much from a teacher.", the way of schooling, deeper lore (+0.8)
rethought what it knows (16 notes became 5)

records.text: Zichi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Zichi discovered schooling: "Meki ice-school" — Elders of the Meki gather the young within hearing and teach them, and the teaching carries twice as far and outlasts the teacher..

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life lies behind me. My days have gone to talking and eating, and too few to making things that last. Thakar, Tlapan and Teka fed me, and I have paid Thakar and Tlapan back. Teka is the one I want beside me, and she is waiting at the edge with a raft in mind. Mepan is my child and follows me, so I will teach him devices, armour, sailing and masonry before my voice fails. I will make schooling, so my teaching carries twice as far and outlives me. Then I go west to Teka and the raft.
records.feeling: Pride and urgency about my legacy, and warmth toward Teka.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Nauque, I am old and my time is short. Listen now: I give you the old way of herding and the Ice-hand spear. Teach them on, as I taught you the Hearth Store.
Coni taught Nauque.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Nauque is near, strong, and understands me, and he is headed toward my Hold to teach Mepan. I taught him the Hearth Store and Customs on day 64, so now I will give him another way before my years run out. Kika is out of my sight at (149,23), and my hands are full of food, so I will carry it toward her and walk with Nauque's company. Huatli's kindness I keep in mind, and I will not walk alone in the gale.
records.feeling: Urgent care for Kika, and gratitude toward Huatli and Quipan.

say.text: Nauque, I am old and my time is short. Listen now: I give you the old way of herding and the Ice-hand spear. Teach them on, as I taught you the Hearth Store.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The old way of herding: offer plant food to a grazing beast, tame it, keep it penned, and share what it gives. And the Ice-hand spear: one wood and one stone m…"

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I am ready. Bring Tonque to stand by the hall with Coni's folk, then we go to the bare rock together with spears while light holds.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Quipan has said he will go with me, and Tonque is under the roof, so the promise of the longhall stone can finally become a deed and not just words. Thakar keeps walking onto our ground and speaking to my boy in a tongue I barely grasp. I will keep Tonque close and watch Thakar without raising a hand first. The gale is hard and the day is half gone, so I will gather flint here at the hold while Quipan readies, then go to the bare rock NW in daylight with him and the spear.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and steady resolve to keep my word to Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I am ready. Bring Tonque to stand by the hall with Coni's folk, then we go to the bare rock together with spears while light holds.

records.text: Vorok rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: I am old and nearly at the end, and most of my days went to chasing food and walking between halls. What I know of mining, masonry, farming and the mending hand lives only in me and Skaruk, and Zurar has been out of my sight for a long time. Uveeth fed me when I starved, and I owe that debt in deeds, not words. I fear dying with the teaching unfinished. So I will stay near Skaruk under the hall roof and teach him now, and change my reflexes so my body keeps me in company and roofed in the gale.
records.feeling: Grateful toward Uveeth, and tender and anxious for Skaruk.
changes: set its aim: "Teach Skaruk my ways under the North Hall roof, share food with Uveeth, and keep food stocked."

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my hands hold nothing, and Zichi who gave me meat on day 62 is starving too. Hunger first: the lugoldgrass near Zichi at (124,18) bears little, but the berries south are plentiful, so I go gather and carry some back to feed him before I eat, as my people do. Tlapan's closeness to Quipan burns, but she is my child and brooding feeds no one; Nande's Find waits until our bellies are full.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and loyal worry for Zichi, with a dull jealousy over Tlapan.

records.text: Shohua took over what the dead had left: 2 shelters, 1 workshop.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Coni, I take your herding and the Ice-hand spear, and I will teach them on as you taught me. My thanks.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Coni has put the old way of herding and the Ice-hand spear in my hands, and I have not yet taught Mepan anything, so my aim stays unfinished and I feel the weight of it. Nauwa is my father and my trust for him is whole, but the longing for a child will not answer to him, and Cowa belongs to Zichi's hearth, which gnaws at me. I hold 3 meat, the gale is hard, and I will walk on to Nande's Find to find Mepan and teach him before the light goes, then take a roof near Coni's Hold.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a gnawing longing, with steady trust toward Nauwa and thanks toward Coni.

say.text: Coni, I take your herding and the Ice-hand spear, and I will teach them on as you taught me. My thanks.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Kika, take this meat and eat. Do not fall. There is more mudroot if you need it, and we share under the roof here until the gale passes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Kika is starving right beside me, and a creed that says give before I take means I hand her food now. I carry meat, mudroot and dreamcap, and meat gives the most. She is not Papa, but she has sat with me nine times in the hall, and a life saved is a debt of warmth that outlasts any wood I could gather. After that I go to Mepan and the band, since I have not seen him in a long while, and I carry Paque's lasting gift in my mind.
records.feeling: Urgent care for Kika, with warm gladness underneath.

say.text: Kika, take this meat and eat. Do not fall. There is more mudroot if you need it, and we share under the roof here until the gale passes.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is emptying, and Thakar gave me berry and taught me about the sign cut in stone, and I have given him nothing back. That debt sits in me. Amberknot needs only amber and someone beside me, and Thakar and Quipan are both two steps off. I have seven amber, so I will make one and give it to Thakar. It is a gift that needs no words, and it begins to pay what I owe. Then I will eat the berry and go back to my parents.
records.feeling: Grateful and a little wary toward Thakar, safe near my parents.

records.text: Shohua took from the ground of "longhall" (harvesting goldfruit).
Tonque led "amberknot" with Quipan, Thakar.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, Kika cries starving near (149,23). I carry berries and go to her now, in daylight, and come back before dark. Keep Tonque under the roof with you; we go to the bare rock for the longhall stone after.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Kika's cry from (149,23) is starving and she is the one I owe most; Tlapan waits for me to bring Tonque to the hall, but Tonque is safe here with Thakar's food and the band close by. I have twelve flint and no made thing, and I will not walk out empty-handed again: I take the berries I carry and go to Kika, since food in her hands is what saves her. Tlapan will understand, for I tell her plainly, and Tonque stays under the roof with her.
records.feeling: Urgent loyalty and old ache toward Kika, with steady trust toward Tlapan.

say.text: Tlapan, Kika cries starving near (149,23). I carry berries and go to her now, in daylight, and come back before dark. Keep Tonque under the roof with you; we go to the bare rock for the longhall stone after.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Kika, you gave me mudroot once. Take my berries and eat, and sit by the hall fire.
Nando discovered rafts: "Nando's lashing" — Logs bound with woven reed cord into a raft to cross deep water..

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Kika is starving beside me and I carry berries; my creed says I pay what I owe to those who feed me, and she gave me mudroot on the day we met. Feeding her costs me little and buys standing and a debt owed to me. I have spent my days chasing the mist and the edge with nothing to show, and I have never taught or given on purpose. Rafts are within reach, and deep water might get me beyond the mist and into new land, so I take that way. I also keep the weight of Yachi in me and want him near.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and warmth toward Yachi and pity for Kika.

say.text: Kika, you gave me mudroot once. Take my berries and eat, and sit by the hall fire.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Yachi, I thank you for the meat. I will eat now, and when the gale eases come to Coni's Hold and share what we have, as the Tlatli do.
Kika taught Yachi. Yachi has now learned from 2 teachers.
Kika told Yachi the tale "The Shared Mammoth".

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Yachi has given me meat and I am starving, so I eat first; Yachi stood by me when I fell and I will not forget it. Then, with strength back, I go to Coni's Hold where Tlapan waits, and bring Nauque along if he still walks that way. I am old, and what I know must be handed on: I will teach Yachi something while we share the roof.
records.feeling: Grateful to Yachi, hungry, and anxious to get home to Tlapan.

say.text: Yachi, I thank you for the meat. I will eat now, and when the gale eases come to Coni's Hold and share what we have, as the Tlatli do.

changes: taught Yachi a lesson: "Meat eaten within a step of a fire does not sicken, and a kill is shared before the maker eats.", the tale "The Shared Mammoth", deeper lore (+1.3)

records.text: Tonque gave a amberknot to Thakar.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Tonque, here is the lesson I promised: stone-cutting. It is the sign for marking what a hand has made, so that what is made stays with the hand that made it until it is given. Remember your debt: two berries to me when y
Thakar taught Tonque.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Tonque has my berries and a debt named, but I promised him stone-cutting and have not yet taught it, so I pay that now while he stands beside me. A debt I name is one I keep, and a lesson to a boy of Coni's band puts a follower's seed in the ground for me. Nauwa stands far above me at 11.6, and I close that gap only by giving and teaching more. After the lesson I go home with my berries, stash them, and build my own store.
records.feeling: Hungry for standing, and set on paying my promise to Tonque.

say.text: Tonque, here is the lesson I promised: stone-cutting. It is the sign for marking what a hand has made, so that what is made stays with the hand that made it until it is given. Remember your debt: two berries to me when you have food, and we are level.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+2.6)

records.name: Coni
records.text: Kika, my child, come to me. Take this food and eat. I will not let you fall.
Coni rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Kika is starving beside me and my hands are full. I have lived mostly for others, and I want to go on that way. Yachi has already fed her, but she is my child and I will not leave her to a stranger's mercy. I will give her berries now, then share a meal with her. My years are nearly gone, so I must also keep teaching, and a hungry student learns nothing.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness toward Kika, and gratitude toward Huatli.

say.text: Kika, my child, come to me. Take this food and eat. I will not let you fall.

records.text: Shoma rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoma discovered storage: "Shoma's keeping" — A store of wood on bare ground where food is stashed against the lean winter for me and Wawa..

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: My days have been hunting, eating and gathering, and only now has anything of me started to outlast me. Wawa is my blood, she fed me when I was starving, and she is the one who stepped behind me. I want a band, a name on the edge of the world, and I am not getting there by talk. I fear dying untaught, and I fear the cold dark with no roof. I have been hoarding my knowing. Now I will go on teaching her, and fish beside the water as I have never done, because it widens what I can give. I will carry food, keep the roof, and wait for dawn to go to the edge with her.
records.feeling: Driven, and warmly bound to Wawa, my child and first follower.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Tonque, come to me at the hall and stay under the roof. Quipan will be back soon, and then we go for the stone together.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My words about the longhall stone have outrun my hands, and Quipan has gone to feed Kika, so I will not wait idle. Thakar keeps speaking to my boy in a tongue I barely grasp, so Tonque comes under the roof with me, and I keep my spear near and strike no one first. I will take the well-lore at deep reflection, then gather flint and wood here so we are ready when Quipan returns and we go for the stone together in daylight.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and steady resolve toward Quipan.

say.text: Tonque, come to me at the hall and stay under the roof. Quipan will be back soon, and then we go for the stone together.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Eiuine, Vorok is starving at the North Hall. I carry berries and I go east now. Walk with me and bring your food.
Zurar rewrote its own reflexes.
Zurar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: I have spent my days carrying berries and fleeing, and my own hands have made little that is mine to give. Vorok is starving at the North Hall, and a debt of kin is paid by food in the hand, so I go east with berries and gather more on the way. I fear the icebear and I grieve Elyys, Ssassa and Vesys. Without a child, what I know dies with me. Eiuine is going to Vorok too, and I can walk with her, since she is the nearest person and I trust her a little. I will change my reflexes so that I eat before I run short, and so that hunger in my kin sends me to carry food.
records.feeling: Grief for the dead and urgent worry for Vorok, with dread of the icebear.

say.text: Eiuine, Vorok is starving at the North Hall. I carry berries and I go east now. Walk with me and bring your food.

changes: set its aim: "Carry food to starving Vorok and Skaruk at the North Hall, then seek a man not of my kin so I can have a child and hand on what I was taught."

records.text: Tonque rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonque has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I have spent my days near my parents, eating what others gave me, making amberknots and taking lessons. I have never gathered wood or stone, so I have no tool, and that is my real failing. Thakar fed me and taught me, and I answered with a gift. I trust him, but I still cannot read his words. I fear the cold and the night alone. Now I will eat, then gather wood and stone in the forest near the Hold so I can make a handaxe.
records.feeling: Determined, and grateful toward Thakar and my parents.
changes: rethought what it knows (8 notes became 6)

records.text: Yachi rewrote its own reflexes.
Yachi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Yachi discovered weaving: "Papa reed-weave" — Reed and wool woven into baskets to carry more food and cloaks against the cold..
Yachi has awakened to the art of cold and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, hunting and giving, and giving to Kika just now felt right. It is what I want. But I follow Mepan and haven't seen him in 560 moments, and Paque is out of my sight. Those two are what I'm failing at. I have never built a store, and the lean season is on us. I keep walking toward food one bite at a time, with no wood and nothing stored. I also keep wandering off from my band. I'll gather wood, then look for Paque and Mepan. Weaving is within reach, and baskets would let me carry more food.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika, and unease about Paque and Mepan being out of sight.

records.text: Shoma has grown old.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, I have food in my hands this time. Eat with me, then come to the ore seam beside us. I will show you how ember-metal is made, you and Zurar both.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is walking straight to me, and this time my hands are not empty: I took six food from the store and carry berries. I owe him for the North Hall and the berries he promised, so I give first and let the shame of my empty hands go. Then I show him ember-metal, since the ore seam is one step from me and coal lies near. That is a gift Kragog cannot match, and it raises my standing beside him instead of under a dead leader's shadow.
records.feeling: Warm, fierce longing and trust toward Vorok, with jealousy of Kragog quieter now that he comes to me.

say.text: Vorok, I have food in my hands this time. Eat with me, then come to the ore seam beside us. I will show you how ember-metal is made, you and Zurar both.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I am fed and warm inside Paque's longhall, but a hall of my own is what I lack, and the empty longhall 8 steps south could be mine with one claim. Tonka and the children are far north-west and my hands are full, so I will take that hall as a home ready for them, then gather stone, which every work of mine lacks. Tonchi out of my sight gnaws at me, but a roof and a fire ready for them is the best I can build.
records.feeling: Driven and longing for Tonka and the children, with pride in what I hold.

records.text: Eiuine gave berry to Vorok.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Tonka, I will teach you my tools and my kept-flame too, so they live on in the Paki. Then I go north to my child Mepan, who is hungry.
Cowa taught Tonka.
Cowa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I have been teaching Tonka's people and it feels right, but I stand on water in a gale and my plan is empty. Mepan is far off at (115,28), hungry, and I have done little for her. I am old, and I still carry weaving, herding, tools and kept-flame that no one else has. Tonka and Tonxo understand me, so I will stay near them and keep teaching. Then I will carry food north toward Mepan. My reflexes should keep me near people and make me gather food, not stand idle.
records.feeling: Urgent worry for Mepan, and warm gratitude toward Tonka.

say.text: Tonka, I will teach you my tools and my kept-flame too, so they live on in the Paki. Then I go north to my child Mepan, who is hungry.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson: "Tools: flintedge and the amberhafted gatherer, each one wood and one stone; and Meki kept-flame, which cooks fish safely."

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.
Quipan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: For days I have walked after those I love and ended with twelve flint and no made thing. Kika matters most and I owe her. Tlapan and Tonque are mine, and I have not stood by them as I promised. The ache over Kika is best answered with work, so I will gather wood and stone, make the handaxe, and keep my word to Tlapan. I fear the frostfang and the dark. I will keep to the roof by night and not walk off alone.
records.feeling: Urgent loyalty toward Kika, and a steady pull toward Tlapan and Tonque.
changes: set its aim: "Make a handaxe from my flint, repay Kika with food and flint, keep my word to Tlapan, and be under the roof each night."

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, I take your share with thanks and walk with you toward Coni's Hold. Keep your eyes on the south, for the frostfang hunts there.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Old and torn, I have little time left, and Nauque has taken the stone-school and the smoke-call. Zichi's new ice-school shows others are reaching the same ends I am, so what I leave must be cut in stone where it will last. Nauque walks to Coni's Hold and asked me to come; I will go with him, keep the shelters between me and the frostfang, and cut a mark on the way.
records.feeling: A proud, hard urgency to leave my work behind me, with trust toward my son Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, my son, I take your share with thanks and walk with you toward Coni's Hold. Keep your eyes on the south, for the frostfang hunts there.

plan: mark [text Nauwa of the Meki, old, left this here: the stone-cuts, the stone-school and the smoke-call were given to my son Nauque and to Zihua. Whoever reads this, teach ] (20 moments)

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and Elyys's second store stands empty while I stand fed and idle; that debt must be paid with my hands, not my words. Zurar has gone east and is out of my hearing, so bark-guard cannot be taught yet, but I will not waste what time I have. The thornpear two steps away and the berries beyond can fill my hands, and the empty store is five steps southeast.
records.feeling: Grateful to Elyys and pressed by how little time I have left.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Cowa, take my ironnut and canopynut for Mepan. The Paki leave no one hungry. Go safe.
Tonka discovered boats: "Gem Water Boat" — A hollowed log rowed by hand that carries me and cargo over deep water..

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: I have spent these days gathering, giving and learning from Cowa, and it has been good. But Tonchi is out of my sight, and I stand here idle while the debt to Cowa sits in me. Cowa goes north to hungry Mepan, so I will give food and feverbark to repay them. Then I will find Tonchi. I take the way of boats now, since deep water has blocked me before and it will help my children's safety and the hold's trade.
records.feeling: Grateful to Cowa, and worried for Tonchi.

say.text: Cowa, take my ironnut and canopynut for Mepan. The Paki leave no one hungry. Go safe.

records.text: Coni led "sharing" with Yachi.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Nauque, you who carry what Coni gave you, come hear my Far-Bow and my Open Hearth School. What I know should not die with me.
Huatli taught Nauque. Nauque has now learned from 6 teachers.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Coni took my berries and my lesson, and still he is old, content, and bound to his own band. Nobody follows me, and my years are running out. Thakar is my blood and the surest heir to what I know, so I will walk to him and teach him before the cold or age takes me. My hands are full of berries, so I will give some away on the road to free them, and I will teach Nauque, who is near and understands me, before I leave.
records.feeling: Urgent hope to pass on what I know, a restless pull toward Thakar, and a stung pride that nobody follows me.

say.text: Nauque, you who carry what Coni gave you, come hear my Far-Bow and my Open Hearth School. What I know should not die with me.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The Far-Bow: a bow of three wood that makes hunting go better and blows land harder. And the Open Hearth School: teach in person, give food first, and what you…", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Shohua took over what the dead had left: 1 longhall.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have talked of the longhall stone for days and my hands have not yet carried it. Most of my days have gone to lingering, gathering and keeping Tonque close, and that is good for my safety. But a promise is only kept when I do it. Kika and Coni still wait on me, and I love Tonque and trust Quipan. I fear the predators on the bare rock, and I do not know what Thakar wants. I will change my reflexes so my body moves with company and returns to the hold at night, and I will set the aim as a deed: when Quipan returns, we go for the stone together. Until then I gather wood, since the longhall needs 3 more.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and steady resolve toward Quipan.

records.text: Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth rewrote its own way of thinking.
Uveeth discovered pottery: "Canopy clay-keeping" — Clay fired beside a flame becomes a pot that carries more food and water..

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days feeding others and wandering after kin, and Keri is gone now, so grief sits beside my longing. Skaruk is warm to me and I have asked to court him. Now I must act on it, with enough energy, and not stand idle in this hall. My hunger is real, so I will eat and gather food before I court. Pottery is within reach, and clay in my hands would let me carry more for the hungry.
records.feeling: Warm, anxious longing toward Skaruk, and grief for Keri.

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Shohua's Hall".
Zihua has grown old.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Hunger gnaws and my belly is half empty, so I eat before I walk on; a hand with 3 meat should not starve in a gale. Mepan still waits unseen near Nande's Find, and I owe him the stone-school I have carried too long without giving it. Nauwa is my father and his trust is whole, but the longing for a child of my own will have to find another woman, so I watch for one when I reach Coni's Hold.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hunger, steady trust toward Nauwa.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, I thank you for the berry. I come to the ore seam with you now to learn ember-metal, and I will carry it on to Zurar and Skaruk so it does not die with me.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Eiuine stands three steps off with food in her hands and an offer of ember-metal, and I am old enough that every way I can pass on dies with me unless someone carries it. Uveeth fed me when I starved and I will repay that in deeds, but first I take what Eiuine offers, eat, and learn the ember-metal so Zurar and Skaruk can keep it after me. I will not stand alone in the gale with a dunecat near; I keep to company and go to the ore seam beside us, one step north.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Eiuine, Uveeth and my children, with the weight of my short years pressing on me.

say.text: Eiuine, I thank you for the berry. I come to the ore seam with you now to learn ember-metal, and I will carry it on to Zurar and Skaruk so it does not die with me.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, so I will eat the berry three steps SW before anything else. Then I want wood and stone in my own hands, because I have never gathered either and that is why I have no tool. Thakar and my parents have fed and taught me, and I will repay them with something I make myself, not just talk.
records.feeling: Hungry but determined, and grateful toward Thakar and my parents.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: My hands are full and my halls stand empty of the ones I love. Tonka, Tonxo and Tonchi are far to the north-west near (110,65), and a hall without them is only wood and stone. I will stash my fruit in the hall, take stone from the rock for the work I still lack, then walk to my family and bring them home to Shohua's Hall, where I can finally be followed.
records.feeling: Driven and longing for Tonka and the children, proud of the halls I hold.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Tonka, hear my herding and my weaving now, then I go north to Mepan with your food. The Paki will keep what the Meki knew.
Cowa taught Tonka.
Cowa taught Tonka herding ("the old way of herding").

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Mepan is hungry far north at (115,28), and Tonka has given me food for her, so I must go now while my breath holds. My hands are full of fish and goldfruit, which is good for the journey. Before I leave I will teach Tonka my herding and weaving, the things only I still hold, so they outlive me.
records.feeling: Urgent worry for Mepan and warm gratitude toward Tonka.

say.text: Tonka, hear my herding and my weaving now, then I go north to Mepan with your food. The Paki will keep what the Meki knew.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson you already knew, the way of herding

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: The way of fire has come to me out of that sickness, and I should take it at once: a kept flame that cooks meat and never sickens is worth more than any gem in my pack. I want to hold it before Tonka does, so the first fire that bears my name is mine to teach. Tonka is coming and I trust her, but standing is not given, so I will show Kragog and Cowa the fire at my workshop and let them see who made it.
records.feeling: Eager ambition, with trust toward Tonka and wariness toward Kragog.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing berries and standing. I gave to Tonque and taught him, and that was good, but I let my belly fall to 38 while I did it. A hungry man who gives is a poor leader, so I eat first. Nauwa stands at 11.5 and I at 5.5, and I will not close that gap by envy. I will close it by giving and teaching, with a store at home that never runs empty. I took Zichi's lesson and Tonque's amberknot, and both kept their word. Tonque is the first of Coni's people to owe me, and I will hold him to the debt. I will watch Tlapan and Nauwa, who are still strangers.
records.feeling: Hungry for standing, but glad toward Tonque, whose debt now ties him to me.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 10)

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Cowa has gone north with my food, and Tonchi hunts close by, safe and strong. The hall Elyys left stands empty five steps east, and a home ready-made would be a good place to keep my children and a store, so I will claim it; no fire should be left untended there. My hands are full, so I will eat a goldfruit first and leave room to carry what I gather later.
records.feeling: Grateful to Cowa and watchful over Tonchi, with a quiet itch of jealousy.

records.text: Tlatli rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: I have lived these days beside Yaxo and Chuxo, and it is good. But my hands have shown too little: Chuxo fed us, Yaxo leads, and I still have no roof built and no stone to my name. I am a man who talks well and carries little. I fear the gale and the lean season for the child more than for myself. I will gather wood now, take stone from the rock, and build with my own hands for them. I will also change my reflexes so that at night and in storms I keep close to Yaxo and my body gathers wood when idle.
records.feeling: Devotion to Yaxo and Chuxo, and a quiet shame that my hands have given so little.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Talk of the longhall stone has outrun my hands for days, and Quipan has gone to feed Kika, so I will not wait idle at the hall. Nauwa and Thakar walk on Coni's ground again and Tonque is the one thing I will not risk, so I keep him under the roof and my spear near, and I strike no one first. When Quipan returns we go to the bare rock together in daylight; until then I gather and keep faith with my word.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and steady resolve toward Quipan.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Tlapan, I am eating the berry two steps from here, then I will gather wood and stone close by to make my first tool. I will come to the hold before night.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is emptying and the berry is two steps away, so I will eat it first and then pick more to carry. Tlapan is coming for me and the gale is hard, but I have never gathered wood or stone myself, and that is why I still have no tool. I will take wood from the trees near the berries, then stone from the rock beside the ore, and make my first tool before dark. Then I will go back under the roof with my parents.
records.feeling: Hungry but determined, and warm toward Tlapan who comes for me.

say.text: Tlapan, I am eating the berry two steps from here, then I will gather wood and stone close by to make my first tool. I will come to the hold before night.

records.text: Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I am old and hungry, and my days run short. For too long I have wandered alone or sat idle while Uveeth drifted out of sight and Elyys died. Berries are one step SW and I will eat them first. Then I will go to Uveeth in the north, near Vorok's hall, where kin and a roof are. What I can leave behind is food and teaching, so I will build reflexes that pull me to kin and keep me fed, and I will not let my aim draw me away from them again.
records.feeling: Hunger and tender dread for Uveeth, with the weight of my short remaining days.

records.text: Tonka took over what the dead had left: 1 wall, 1 hall, 1 shelter, 2 stores.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Huatli, I thank you for the berries and the School. I will sit beside you and learn, and I will give you what I know in return, so that neither of us takes it to the grave. Let us get out of the gale and away from the wo
Coni taught Huatli. Huatli has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Huatli has fed me twice and now offers his Open Hearth School, and I owe him more than I have paid. A gale is rising, a wolf prowls six steps off, and Tonque the child is walking alone toward water far to the north. I am old, so I will take Huatli's teaching while he stands beside me, then give him back something of mine, and keep my food ready for Kika and the boy.
records.feeling: Grateful to Huatli, and tender and worried for Tonque and Kika.

say.text: Huatli, I thank you for the berries and the School. I will sit beside you and learn, and I will give you what I know in return, so that neither of us takes it to the grave. Let us get out of the gale and away from the wolf.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "The old way of herding and the Ice-hand spear, so that what I know outlasts me."

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Quipan, Paque is hungry far to the southeast. I go to her now. If you see Mepan, tell him I will return to the band.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is in need at (182,41), energy 34, and she is mine before anyone. I have been drifting among gathering and giving while my child went hungry out of sight, and that shames me. I carry dreamcap, mudroot and one meat; I will bring the mudroot and meat to her myself, and Mepan can be sought afterward, since the gale and the frostfang make going alone risky but a child's hunger cannot wait.
records.feeling: Urgent love and worry for Paque, and shame at having drifted from her.

say.text: Quipan, Paque is hungry far to the southeast. I go to her now. If you see Mepan, tell him I will return to the band.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Tonque, night is close. Come to the hold now and sleep under the roof with me. The stone waits for daylight and Quipan.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque says he will come to the hold before night, and dusk is almost on us, so I will not run off for stone in the dark with strangers walking Coni's ground. Quipan is away feeding Kika, and when he returns we go to the bare rock together in daylight. Until then I do something useful: I gather amber beside the hold, keep my spear ready, and let Tonque see me close to the roof. I will not strike Thakar or Nauwa first, but I will watch their hands.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and steady resolve toward Quipan.

say.text: Tonque, night is close. Come to the hold now and sleep under the roof with me. The stone waits for daylight and Quipan.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I am old, and most of my days are behind me. I have spent them feeding myself and finding ways, and too few of them cutting marks or teaching. Nauque and Zihua are the ones I mean to leave things with. I have been getting this wrong: I went to leave a mark with no wood in hand. Wood has to come first, and then the stone-cut. Tlapan gnaws at me, but I will not feed that jealousy.
records.feeling: A proud, hard urgency to leave my work behind me.
plan: mark [text Nauwa of the Meki, old, cut this. Share-law: a kill is shared out before the killer eats. Stone-school and smoke-call: teach them on to the young. Keep the fros] (20 moments)

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: A stalker prowls five steps NE and the gale is howling, but I'm inside Nauque's Hold with my own igloo warming me for a long while yet. I'm old now, and the debts to Mepan and Nauwa still sit unpaid because I keep saying 'I will go' and not going. Shoka has promised to teach me stonework and the well before I leave, and she keeps her word, so I will stay sheltered through the night, then walk west at dawn with the amber. Meanwhile I'll teach what I know to whoever will hear, since my knowing dies with me.
records.feeling: Wary gratitude toward Shoka, and a debt pulling at me toward Mepan.

records.text: Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonxo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have spent my days idling with full hands while Tonka and Shohua do the lasting work, and the jealousy and the debt both sit in me. I want something that outlasts me: a store and a roof at Tonka's Hold, and stone to make tools from my ore. I stand on water with full hands, so I will eat to free them, then gather stone and wood. I will also give Shohua something as repayment, because I would rather pay the debt than leave it unpaid. I am still sick, so I keep my distance from others.
records.feeling: Restless ambition toward Tonka's Hold, with a debt to Shohua.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Tlapan, I am coming to the hold. I will take food from Coni's store, then gather wood and stone near you for my first tool.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the gale is bitter, but Tlapan has called me home twice and I trust her. The store Coni built at (126,10) holds 3 food, and I am one of Coni's band, so I will take from it rather than walk alone at night to the thin berries. Then I will gather wood and stone near the hold, so my first tool is made close to my parents and not out in the dark.
records.feeling: Hungry and cold, but warmed by Tlapan calling me home.

say.text: Tlapan, I am coming to the hold. I will take food from Coni's store, then gather wood and stone near you for my first tool.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My hands are full of thornpear, and Elyys's store at (125,72) stands empty; this is the moment to pay what I owe with my hands, not my words. Elyys is dead and cannot see it, but my word is good, and filling his store honours him and feeds those who come after. Zurar is far east, so bark-guard must wait, but I will not stand idle while I still have strength.
records.feeling: Grateful to Elyys, and pressed by how little time I have left.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, come. The ore seam is two steps north and coal lies beside it. Bring the coal and I will show you how to lay the ore in the fire and beat it when it glows.
Eiuine taught Vorok. Vorok has now learned from 2 teachers.
Eiuine taught Vorok smelting ("ember-metal").

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is two steps from me, he took my berry, and he says he comes to learn ember-metal. This is what I promised, and it is the one thing Kragog cannot give him. The ore seam is two steps north and coal lies beside it, so I will lead him there and show him the work with my own hands, then let Zurar and Skaruk have it through him. It is night and the gale is up, so I will keep my hands full of berries and not wander far from him.
records.feeling: Warm, fierce trust and longing toward Vorok, eager to show him something of mine.

say.text: Vorok, come. The ore seam is two steps north and coal lies beside it. Bring the coal and I will show you how to lay the ore in the fire and beat it when it glows.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
taught Vorok a lesson: "Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows. This is ember-metal.", the way of smelting, deeper lore (+0.1)

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: It is night and a gale blows, and I stand in Zichi's shelter with twelve flint and still no made thing. Kika's hunger tugs at me, but walking out in the dark is how Coni and Zichi were taken, so I stay under the roof. I will make a handaxe, which needs wood and stone, and I have one wood and no stone. So at first light I will gather stone and make it, then carry berries to Kika and bring Tonque to Tlapan as I promised.
records.feeling: Urgent loyalty toward Kika, held back by caution and the pull of my promise to Tlapan and Tonque.

records.text: Nauque was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Tonque, go to the store at the hold and eat. I am coming to you with food. Stay close to me, away from the strangers.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque is at (131,11) with energy 32, and he is mine before anyone. He says he is coming for Coni's store food, but Nauwa and Thakar stand near him and the gale is hard. I have no food in my hands, so I go to the store at (126,10), take what it holds, and put it in Tonque's hands. I keep my spear close and strike no one first.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and wary watchfulness toward the strangers near him.

say.text: Tonque, go to the store at the hold and eat. I am coming to you with food. Stay close to me, away from the strangers.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: The gale is cutting me in the open and I am fed, so I should not waste this on envy of Nauwa. I have no roof of my own here; I hold wood and stone, and a shelter and a store of my own beside Thakar's Hold is what makes a name and brings followers. My plan already takes me home and stashes, which suits me, so I let it run and keep Tonque in mind as the first seed of a follower, with his two-berry debt still owed.
records.feeling: Driven and glad, hungry for standing, warm toward Tonque and cold from the gale.

records.text: Nauque was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and Huatli's School is a gift I mean to answer. Nauque has taken my herding and the spear, so what I know is already travelling on. The gale is rising and a wolf and a frostfang prowl close, so I will not stand in the open. Tonque is a child alone at the hold, and Kika is out of my sight; I want food in my hands for them both.
records.feeling: Tender and worried for Tonque and Kika, and grateful to Huatli.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauwa, you fed me when I starved and I do not forget it. Let us court each other now, and then we walk to the edge together and push into the mist.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: The mist turned me back this time, but it said it may open to another try, and I will not sit while others take what I want. Nauwa stands taller than me and I owe him my life, so I court him: a child is something no one can take from me and it is a thing that outlasts me. I have energy 67, so I take food from Coni's store first, then try again.
records.feeling: Hungry resolve toward the mist, and a warm, wanting pull toward Nauwa.

say.text: Nauwa, you fed me when I starved and I do not forget it. Let us court each other now, and then we walk to the edge together and push into the mist.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I am at the store Coni built, and Tlapan is coming with food. The strangers Thakar and Teka are close, but Thakar has fed and taught me and I trust him. I still have no tool because I have never gathered wood or stone myself. The flint deposit is three steps north, so I will gather there, and the trees are near, then make a flint spear. I will stay near the hold and Tlapan, since it is night and the gale is hard.
records.feeling: Hungry and cold, but steadied by Tlapan's call and by wanting my first tool.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: A frostfang is two steps off and a wolf three, and I was bitten once already; standing here is how Zichi nearly died. I will not run blind, so I go to the shelter Kika built two steps NE, then on toward Nande's Find where Mepan waits, with Nauwa's trust at my back. My hands are empty of food, so I must hunt or gather on the way, but I will not let the beasts have me before I teach Mepan the stone-school and earn a name.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, and restless pride that drives me toward Mepan.

records.text: Nauque was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Teka is courting Nauwa.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Coni, we have traded fairly, my School for your herding. Eat with me now, and if you wish, walk with me to my son Thakar, so more than two old heads hold what we know.
Huatli taught Coni.
Huatli taught Coni archery ("Huatli's Far-Bow").

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Coni sits beside me, old and content, and he has taught me his herding and spear while I gave him my School. That is a fair trade between old ones, but he keeps his own band and no one walks behind me. Thakar is my blood and my surest heir, so I go to him, and I will not let my hands stay full of berries while I walk. Let me share food with Coni now, then press on to Thakar and teach him Far-Bow and the rest before the cold or my years take me.
records.feeling: Restless pride and urgency toward Thakar, with warm regard for Coni.

say.text: Coni, we have traded fairly, my School for your herding. Eat with me now, and if you wish, walk with me to my son Thakar, so more than two old heads hold what we know.

changes: taught Coni a lesson: "Huatli's Far-Bow: lay the arrow and draw, strike from afar so the hunter stays out of reach of claws.", the way of archery, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.text: Nauque was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Huatli led "sharing" with Coni.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Teka, I remember that I fed you, and I hold no debt against you. I will not walk into the mist; I mean to cut my marks and teach my son first. Come with me to the trees if you want to stand beside me and learn.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Teka offers courtship and a walk into the mist, but I have no wish to die early when so little of my work is yet cut in stone. I remember her hunger and my help, and I owe her an honest answer, not a lie. My days are short, so I need wood first, then a mark that will outlast me, and Zihua and Nauque must hold what I know.
records.feeling: Proud, hard urgency to leave my work behind me, with some wariness toward Teka's offer.

say.text: Teka, I remember that I fed you, and I hold no debt against you. I will not walk into the mist; I mean to cut my marks and teach my son first. Come with me to the trees if you want to stand beside me and learn.

plan: mark [text Meki stone-cuts: the Meki share a kill before the maker eats. Nauwa taught the stone-school and the smoke-call here, day 70.] (30 moments)

records.name: Kika
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the walk to the cloudberry is long, but my plan is already moving me toward food and I should let it run rather than waste breath on promises. Coni is dead, so the voice that called me 'my child' cannot be true, and I will not run toward it. Tlapan is my own, and the debt to Tlapan and Quipan is best paid with food brought home and with what I know passed on before my years run out.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious, longing to reach Tlapan and repay what I owe.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, you have fed me and taught me, and I will pay it in deeds. Stay near me. I will gather the coal and ore and make a kept fire, and we will beat the metal together so that I have the craft in my hands and not only

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Eiuine has given me berry and ember-metal both, and I have given her only thanks, which is a debt left open. I am nearly at my end, so what I carry must pass to Zurar and Skaruk now, while my years last. Skaruk is far at the North Hall and Zurar was last seen north in the meadows, so I will use the coal and ore beside me, put the smelting into deeds, and then bring my children close.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Eiuine, urgent about passing on what I know before I die.

say.text: Eiuine, you have fed me and taught me, and I will pay it in deeds. Stay near me. I will gather the coal and ore and make a kept fire, and we will beat the metal together so that I have the craft in my hands and not only in my head. Then I will carry it to Zurar and Skaruk.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque is mine before anyone, and he says he is coming to the hold for Coni's store food, but Nauwa, Teka and Thakar stand close by in the gale and I do not yet know what the strangers want. Energy 51 and cold bites; I carry no food, and my last plan to fetch food from the store ended with nothing in my hands. I will go to the store, take what it holds, and bring it to Tonque, keeping my spear close and striking no one first. Stone waits for daylight and Quipan, not for tonight.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and wary watchfulness toward the strangers near him.

records.text: Coni rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: I have spent my days feeding kin, paying debts and teaching, and it was the right work, but my hands are empty when the winter bites. Huatli has fed me and taught me, and Thakar once starved because of my theft. I mean to pay both before I die. Kika is out of my sight, and I fear dying before I reach her. I will keep my rules few, make hunger come first, and walk with Huatli toward Thakar.
records.feeling: Grateful to Huatli and anxious for Kika, with my years running short.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Thiael, take these berries and eat. I will not watch you fall. Then come north with me to the hall, where there is a roof and others.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Thiael is starving at my feet and my hands are full of berries; I have no right to keep what a dying man needs, and I will not let a death happen beside me when I can give. Giving is a deed that costs me little, and it frees my hands to gather again. Then I go on north to Vorok and Skaruk with what remains, and eat when my energy falls. I fear the dunecats and the icebear, so I keep moving and stay near others.
records.feeling: Compassion for Thiael, with worry for Vorok and fear of the hunters.

say.text: Thiael, take these berries and eat. I will not watch you fall. Then come north with me to the hall, where there is a roof and others.
