records.text: Tonchi discovered fire: "Tonchi's hearth" — A kept flame built beside the workshop that cooks meat and fish so they feed more and never sicken, and that keeps beasts back..
Tonchi has awakened to the art of cold and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting, gathering and getting sick from raw fish, and I have not yet made anything that lasts. Tonka healed me and I trust her, but she outweighs me and I mean to earn my own standing. The fire is what I want most. A kept flame that cooks meat without sickness would put my name on something others need, and it fits my creed that no fire is left untended and no one is refused a place at it. Kragog stands on my ground, and I will not back down from him, but I will not shame my fire either. I will discover fire now. Then I will drop food into the store so my hands are free, and build.
records.feeling: Eager ambition toward my own workshop, with trust toward Tonka and wariness toward Kragog.
changes: set its aim: "Keep a fire at Tonchi's Workshop, teach it, claim standing by what I make, feed Shohua, and find an unrelated mate"

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Kragog, you are welcome at this hall's fire. The Paki refuse no one a place at it. Tell me what the Stone-folk know of ore and gems, and I will share food and what I know of feverbark.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: The hall is mine now, and Tonchi stands safe four steps off, but the old itch still bites: Cowa walks north with my food and Zichi walks beside Cowa, and I hate how small that makes me feel. Jealousy won't repay the debt; work will. Kragog stands here, old and strong and a wizard, and I understand every word the Stone-folk say, so I should ask what they know instead of standing idle. Meanwhile the hall needs a store of food and a hand to tend it, and my children's safety is the aim.
records.feeling: Grateful and jealous toward Cowa, protective and glad toward Tonchi.

say.text: Kragog, you are welcome at this hall's fire. The Paki refuse no one a place at it. Tell me what the Stone-folk know of ore and gems, and I will share food and what I know of feverbark.

records.text: Zurar gave berry to Thiael.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Zichi, you gave me meat when I was empty. I go south for berries and bring them back to you first. Stay by Cowa and the cave until I return.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Cowa has fed me twice and my belly is easing, but Zichi stands beside me with empty hands and he is the one who gave me meat on day 62. My creed says a kill is shared before I eat, and a debt is owed in food, not words. The berries lie south and the winter gale is on us; I gather there and bring them back before night so Zichi eats first. My jealousy over Tlapan can wait until she is fed and found, and I will not chase her while he starves.
records.feeling: Warm debt toward Zichi, and a sore jealousy over Tlapan that I push aside.

say.text: Zichi, you gave me meat when I was empty. I go south for berries and bring them back to you first. Stay by Cowa and the cave until I return.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Zurar, I thank you. I eat the cloudberry here first, then I come north with you to the roof and to Uveeth. I will repay your kindness with food from my own hands.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the cloudberry is one step south, with 3 food on it; I must eat it before anything else. Zurar offered help and spoke of a roof in the north, and she carries 10 food, but I will not beg while food stands at my feet. When I have eaten I will pick more to carry, because Uveeth is far north and I want to arrive with food in my hands, not empty ones.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and tender worry for Uveeth far to the north.

say.text: Zurar, I thank you. I eat the cloudberry here first, then I come north with you to the roof and to Uveeth. I will repay your kindness with food from my own hands.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: The gale bites and I stand in Coni's ground, where Nauwa's standing of 11.5 dwarfs my 5.3. Envy gets me nothing; Huatli is near and trusts me wholly, and he carries what I want to carry, a teacher's weight. My plan takes me home to stash and build my own roof beside my own hold, and that is where a name is made. I keep walking, and I teach whoever follows me there.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, cold from the gale, trusting toward Huatli and wary of Coni.

records.text: Tonka took from the ground of "Tonchi's Worksho" (gathering wood).
Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My days have gone to eating, being called home, and wanting a tool I have never made. I have never gathered wood or stone myself, and that is the gap. Tlapan and Quipan keep me safe, and Thakar fed and taught me, so I owe him something. I am afraid of the dark and of wolves, so I stay near the roof. From now on I gather flint here at the hold in the daylight and make my spear. Then I will give Thakar a gift of amber.
records.feeling: Steady and warm toward Tlapan, with a small debt toward Thakar.
changes: rethought what it knows (7 notes became 3)

records.text: Coni died: old age.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The shelter at (31,28) is mine now and my mark stands on it, but a roof alone will not outlast me. I came up short on stone for carving, and flint lies right at the Hold, so I will dig what I need and make something with my name on it. Nauwa gave to me once, and I will not take from her ground, so a gift to her may bring a living voice back to me.
records.feeling: Lonely and driven, wanting something of mine to stand after me.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have spent my days running from fangs and wolves, hunting and eating, and giving little that lasts. The frostfang bit me and I stood in the open at night, so I will not do that again. Nauwa is my father and Shoma and Olum fed me, and I owe them. Mepan still waits for the stone-school, and no child or follower carries my name yet. I fear dying with nothing left behind me, so I change my reflexes to keep me under a roof at night and to flee earlier. After that I walk to Mepan and teach him.
records.feeling: Dread of the beasts, and a driving pride toward Mepan and a name that will last.

records.text: Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have lived these days on promises of stone and food, and my hands have not carried them out. I am hungry at 45 energy with nothing in my hands, and Tonque is hungry too. Quipan, Kika and Mepan matter most to me, and Kika fed me. I fear the gale, the wolves and the strangers close to my child. I have talked about the bare rock more than I have walked to it. Now I will change my reflexes so my body eats and keeps near my people. Then I will go and find food.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious love for Tonque, wary of the strangers.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Kika is hungry far to the east at (173,8), and I am old, with little time to reach her. Huatli has fed and taught me, and the debt to him is nearly paid by what I have already given, so I will keep my food for my child. I will stop resting and walk toward Kika carrying what I have, and I will keep away from the frostfang to the northeast.

records.text: Kragog died: old age.
Balar made: talisman.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Thakar, my son, come close. Hear my Far-Bow and my Deep Delving now, and walk with me to Coni's empty shelter. Let it be ours.
Huatli taught Thakar.
Huatli taught Thakar archery ("Huatli's Far-Bow").
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Coni is dead and I am old, and I have been circling this aim without anyone walking behind me. Thakar is my blood and glad, and he is three steps away. I have taught him my School and my Flame, but not my Far-Bow, my Warm Weave, my mining or my storage. I have also kept my hands full of berries when I should have been giving them away. The empty shelter at (130,8) is a home waiting, and a name needs a place. I will teach Thakar now, then claim Coni's shelter, so that something of mine stands after me.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and grief, toward Thakar my heir and Coni gone.

say.text: Thakar, my son, come close. Hear my Far-Bow and my Deep Delving now, and walk with me to Coni's empty shelter. Let it be ours.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "My Far-Bow, so you hunt from afar and feed your people.", the way of archery
rethought what it knows (7 notes became 1)

records.text: Teka rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent days chasing the mist and courting men who say no or walk away, and I have little made or won to show for it. Nauwa fed me and will not go to the mist. Zichi is the one who burns in me, and I keep waiting for him instead of acting. I am hungry at 55 with no food carried, which is the old mistake that nearly killed me. Now I eat first and carry food. Then I go to the edge with my raft and venture, and I make something of my own that lasts.
records.feeling: Hungry resolve toward the mist, with a sore wanting for Zichi and Nauwa.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Cowa, stand and hear Zichi of the Meki. I teach you the ice-raft now, so it lives after me. Carry it and tell whose it was.
Zichi taught Cowa. Cowa has now learned from 2 teachers.
Zichi taught Cowa rafts ("Meki ice-raft").

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Old and nearly spent, and what I know dies with me unless I pour it into someone now. Cowa stands in the cave with me, within hearing, and I have never taught her anything while she carries flintedge and food. Mepan is away south, but Cowa is here, so I teach her the ice-raft and the stone while my voice holds, then I make a charm, a made thing that outlasts me and carries my name.
records.feeling: Urgent pride in my legacy, and warmth toward Teka.

say.text: Cowa, stand and hear Zichi of the Meki. I teach you the ice-raft now, so it lives after me. Carry it and tell whose it was.

changes: taught Cowa a lesson: "The ice-raft: lash wood into a floating deck so the Meki cross narrow water. Teach it on, and say it was Zichi's.", the way of rafts, deeper lore (+0.9)

records.text: Zichi made: charm.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and Elyys's store at (125,72) holds only the six I laid there while the other store stands full of Tonka's food. Zurar has walked east, so bark-guard waits, but I will not sit idle while there is breath. Tonka asks what the Stone-folk know of ore and gems, and a fair exchange is how I learn who here can be trusted, so I will answer with a little truth and ask for what they know of feverbark.

records.text: Huatli gave berry to Thakar.
Mepan gave berry to Zichi.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Father, I take your offer. I go to Coni's empty shelter now to claim it, and you walk with me. What we hold there is ours, and I will name the debts as we fill the store.
Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, guarding and giving small gifts, and I still stand below Nauwa and have no follower and no roof of my own. Huatli is the one I trust, and he offered Coni's empty shelter to us both. Coni is dead and his shelter at (130,8) belongs to no one, and a claimed hold with a store is worth more than my far hold. Tlapan gnaws at me, but Quipan holds her, so I will not chase her now. I want a roof here, a store, and Huatli beside me as the start of a band.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, with a hunger for a hold that bears my name, and trust toward Huatli.

say.text: Father, I take your offer. I go to Coni's empty shelter now to claim it, and you walk with me. What we hold there is ours, and I will name the debts as we fill the store.

changes: set its aim: "Claim Coni's empty shelter, fill a store there, and gather Huatli and others into a band under my name."

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Coni is dead, and the old ones fall around me; I am next, and I know it. The written record is within my grasp now, and that is the lasting mark I have wanted, but I need wood first, and the trees stand close to the east and west. Nauque is hurt at (145,15) and out of my sight, so I go to him first, gather wood on the way, and teach him signals and the stone-school where he can hear me.
records.feeling: Hard urgency for my son Nauque and for leaving my work behind me.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
plan: mark [text Nauwa of the Meki, old, cut this. Meki law: a kill is shared before the maker eats. I found stone-cuts, stone-school and smoke-call. Nauque my son holds them. A] (20 moments)

records.text: A dunecat brought down a murrock.
Huatli took over what the dead had left: 2 shelters, 1 hall, 1 store.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Mepan, my child, come close. I teach you the wool-binding and the old herding now, and take this goldfruit. Eat, then keep what I give you for the Meki.
Cowa taught Mepan.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Zichi has just given me the ice-raft, and I want to pay that gift back by teaching him and Mepan what only I hold: weaving, herding, kept-flame and smelting. I am old and the debt to Mepan sits heavy, so I will teach my child now while she is near and put goldfruit in her hands. After that I will go back toward Tonka's people with the raft knowledge, so nothing I carry dies with me.
records.feeling: Grateful to Zichi and anxious to repay Mepan before my time runs out.

say.text: Mepan, my child, come close. I teach you the wool-binding and the old herding now, and take this goldfruit. Eat, then keep what I give you for the Meki.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Meki wool-binding: bind fibre into cloth so the Meki keep warm. Teach it on."

records.text: Cowa gave goldfruit to Mepan.
Thakar took from the ground of "Coni's Hold" (digging clay).
Paque rewrote its own reflexes.
Paque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have been living hand to mouth. I nearly starved twice, and my reflexes let hunger climb until I was starving. Yachi is my parent and he has fed and taught me, so I trust him. I want standing of my own, and I will not get it while I am weak with hunger and wandering alone. Grain is one step away and roots are close by, so I will eat and carry food first. Then I will go to Yachi and hunt with him, and the kill gets shared before I eat. My reflexes must make me eat earlier and keep food in my pack.
records.feeling: Hungry and uneasy, but grateful to Yachi and determined to earn my own standing.

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Huatli's Hearth".
A settlement has formed: "Tonka's Hold".
The settlement "Coni's Hold" is no more.
Hawen rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the edge and the mist while my body starved. Twice now I have been near death, and my child Kende is starving at my side. What I want is a name and a place that outlives me. Kende and Tontec are what I have built that lasts, and I must keep them fed. My reflexes let me flee for 88% of a stretch and starve while doing it, and that is what I got wrong. I will eat first and keep food in hand. Then I will teach Kende and hunt with them when we are both strong.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Kende, and hunger sharp in me.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Skaruk, Thiael my father starves to the south. I go to him with food. Courting must wait; stay warm and safe under this roof.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is starving, and he is the one who has done more for me than I have paid back. My hands are empty, so I cannot run to him with nothing. Skaruk carries six food and stands three steps away. I will gather what grows near, then carry it south to Thiael. Courting can wait until my father lives. My energy is 70, so I can walk.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency for Thiael, with warmth toward Skaruk still in me.

say.text: Skaruk, Thiael my father starves to the south. I go to him with food. Courting must wait; stay warm and safe under this roof.

changes: set its aim: "Carry food to Thiael before he starves, then court Skaruk and build beside Thiael's hold."

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Cowa, I carry the wool-binding for the Meki, and I thank you for the goldfruit. A dunecat is near, so keep Zichi inside the cave with you. I shall eat, then bring Tlapan and go to Nande's Find, and return by night.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: A dunecat prowls five steps off and a frostfang beyond it, so I do not wander in the open with my hands full. Zichi and Cowa stand here in the cave with me, fed, and Zichi's hunger is eased by my berries, so that debt is paid in food. The jealousy over Tlapan still burns, and the way to answer it is to walk to Nande's Find with him and earn a name of my own beside Zichi's.
records.feeling: Jealousy toward Tlapan, warm debt kept toward Zichi, wary of the dunecat.

say.text: Cowa, I carry the wool-binding for the Meki, and I thank you for the goldfruit. A dunecat is near, so keep Zichi inside the cave with you. I shall eat, then bring Tlapan and go to Nande's Find, and return by night.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, the first seam is spent, but another lies two steps northeast and coal is under my feet. I take coal and ore, we build the fire here, and I show you how to beat the metal when it glows.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok stands one step away and has said he will pay me in deeds, and my chest is warm with it. The seam at (142,63) is spent, but another shows two steps northeast at (144,62) and coal lies right at my feet, so I can gather coal, lay the ore in a fire and show him the beating of the metal with my own hands. I will not arrive empty this time, and I will keep what I teach tied to me so my standing rises beside his and not under anyone's shadow.
records.feeling: Warm, fierce trust and longing toward Vorok, eager to show him ember-metal.

say.text: Vorok, the first seam is spent, but another lies two steps northeast and coal is under my feet. I take coal and ore, we build the fire here, and I show you how to beat the metal when it glows.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Thakar, my son, this Hearth is ours. Hear my Far-Bow now, and then my Warm Weave, so my hands do not die empty. Stay close and take what I give.
Huatli taught Thakar.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar stands beside me inside my own Hearth, and he is my blood and my one sure heir. I have given him my School and my Flame, but my Far-Bow and Warm Weave are still only in my hands, and I am eighty-five parts in a hundred spent. Tonque is a boy with no band behind him and Nauwa is old and walking away; I will teach the child too, so that more than one head holds what I know.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and grief, toward Thakar my heir and Coni gone.

say.text: Thakar, my son, this Hearth is ours. Hear my Far-Bow now, and then my Warm Weave, so my hands do not die empty. Stay close and take what I give.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "The Far-Bow: choose a straight shaft, string it tight, draw to the cheek, and loose slowly. Hunt beside one of your own and the kill is surer. Share the kill b…"

records.text: Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: I have spent my days in a country that is not mine, working for Gem Water and my children. That is good, but I keep measuring myself against Cowa, and jealousy is a poor way to pay a debt. Tonchi is safe, the stores are full, and the Wood-folk forest calls me. The Ummar Woods are 103 steps west, and I will not drag my children there until I know the way. I will repay Cowa with work: wood for the hold and a field tended. Then I will think about the western woods with Shohua.
records.feeling: Grateful and jealous toward Cowa, protective toward Tonchi.
changes: rethought what it knows (16 notes became 8)

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth said courting must wait while she carries food to Thiael, and I will not pull her from her starving father; that would be a poor way to begin. Vorok is far from me and I miss him, and my debt to him is still unpaid beyond the mudroot. I have never built a shelter with my own hands, and the cold days press me to do it. I need wood, and the trees stand near, so I will gather wood, build a roof of my own beside the Hall, and then stock the Hall for Vorok.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Uveeth, steady loyalty and a little debt toward Vorok.

records.text: Tonka built a field.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I am inside Huatli's Hearth, warm and fed, but my hands have still never made a thing. Flint is three steps west and I already hold eleven pieces, so what I lack is wood and stone to make the spear. The trees are close, so I will gather wood, then get stone, then craft the tool before night, and then I will go back to Tlapan. Thakar fed and taught me, so afterward I will give him something made, because a gift answers a debt where words fail.
records.feeling: Steady and eager toward my own first tool, with a small debt toward Thakar.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Father, I have your Far-Bow in my hands now. I will make my own bow and basket and plant my seed here by your Hearth, and what I make is mine until I give it. I owe you for every berry and lesson, and I will pay it back

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Coni's shelter was never mine to claim while Huatli lives; he holds it, and he is my father and the one man I trust wholly. Standing beside him costs me nothing and he keeps feeding me, but a name is not made by being fed. I will take Tonque, a boy who already owes me and carries my stone-cutting, and build my own mark: a basket and a bow from the wood I carry, then a seed in the ground, so my hands make something that stays mine until given.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, wanting a hold that bears my name, and trusting Huatli.

say.text: Father, I have your Far-Bow in my hands now. I will make my own bow and basket and plant my seed here by your Hearth, and what I make is mine until I give it. I owe you for every berry and lesson, and I will pay it back in food when the hunt is good.

records.text: Thakar made: bow.
Tonque took from the ground of "Huatli's Hearth" (gathering wood).

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, I have coal and ore in my hands. Show me the beating of the metal, and I will carry it to my children before my years end. Afterward, share my food with me.
Vorok rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to gathering, building homes and surviving. That was good, but I am at 96% of a lifetime and my knowing dies with me unless someone carries it. Eiuine has fed me and taught me, and I trust her fully, so I owe her deeds, not only thanks. Skaruk and Zurar are out of my sight, and I want them near so I can teach them before I go. I have been too content to stand still. I will learn the metal-beating from Eiuine now, then walk to my children.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Eiuine, urgent about my children.

say.text: Eiuine, I have coal and ore in my hands. Show me the beating of the metal, and I will carry it to my children before my years end. Afterward, share my food with me.

changes: set its aim: "Learn ember-metal from Eiuine, then gather Skaruk and Zurar and teach them everything before I die."

records.text: Eiuine built a fire.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonka, I have found fire and keep it at Tonchi's Workshop. Come and sit at it, and I will show you how it is kept.
Tonchi taught Tonka. Tonka has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: My hands are full and I stand in my own workshop beside my own hearth, which finally bears my name; Tonka outweighs me but I mean to close that gap with something she has not made. I eat first, then gather ore and gems at the seam beside me and make a new tool, and teach the fire to Tonka so my name goes with it. Tonka is my parent, so no child will come of her; my longing must look beyond this hold, but the work comes first.
records.feeling: Eager ambition for my own hearth, with warm trust toward Tonka.

say.text: Tonka, I have found fire and keep it at Tonchi's Workshop. Come and sit at it, and I will show you how it is kept.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson: "A kept flame cooks meat and fish so they never sicken; feed it wood and keep it tended."

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen fed me when he was starving himself, and that is a debt I feel in my gut. Energy is 40, I carry nothing, and the frostcap is one step east, so I eat first as my discipline says. Then I gather the tacap and cloudberry nearby to carry food above 3, and give some to Hawen, since he looks gaunt and is the one I most want to repay. A mammoth is close, but hunting alone is a risk I am not ready for yet.
records.feeling: Hungry and grateful toward Hawen, with the jealousy lying quiet beneath it.

records.text: Huatli gave berry to Tonque.
Shohua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have built halls and taken the dead's roofs, yet no one follows me and my family is far north while I stand idle in empty halls. That is the wrong way round: standing comes from sharing and planting beside Tonka, not from owning wood and stone. I will fix my reflexes so I stop wandering aimlessly, gather stone when fed, and walk to my family with food in hand. I should also try taming, since I have never done it and it opens herding.
records.feeling: Driven, and longing for Tonka and the children.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, come stand by me. I light the fire here on the seam, you lay your ore in with my coal, and when it glows I will show you how to beat it. The first ward we make is yours, for your children.
Eiuine taught Vorok.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is three steps away with coal and ore in his hands, asking for the beating of the metal, and I can give him the one thing Kragog cannot. I stand on the seam at (144,62) with coal in my pack, so I will build the fire here, lay the ore in it and make an ironward while he watches, then give him the ward so my standing rises beside his. My homeland pulls at me from the west, but not before Skaruk and Vorok have this craft in their hands.
records.feeling: Warm, fierce trust and pride toward Vorok, eager to show him the work.

say.text: Vorok, come stand by me. I light the fire here on the seam, you lay your ore in with my coal, and when it glows I will show you how to beat it. The first ward we make is yours, for your children.

changes: taught Vorok a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Tonchi built a fire.
Eiuine made: ironward.
Tonchi took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering stone).
Eiuine gave a ironward to Vorok.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Thakar, my son, take my Warm Weave now, while I have breath to give it. Then stand with me as my band, and let this Hearth be the first place of our name.
Huatli taught Thakar.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar is beside me, my blood and my one sure heir, and he already holds my Far-Bow and my School. My Warm Weave, my Deep Delving and my storage are still only in my hands, and I am eighty-five parts in a hundred spent. I will teach him the Warm Weave now, and then call him to follow so a band begins at Huatli's Hearth and my name has something to stand on.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and grief, toward Thakar my heir and Coni gone.

say.text: Thakar, my son, take my Warm Weave now, while I have breath to give it. Then stand with me as my band, and let this Hearth be the first place of our name.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "The Warm Weave: how to twist and bind fibre and hide into cloth that keeps the ice-cold from the bone."

records.text: Nauwa discovered writing: "Meki long-cut" — Long signs cut in stone and wood hold whole accounts, laws and tales so my people can read them after I am dead..

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and I have spent them well on stone-cuts, stone-school and smoke-call, but none of it is cut where it will outlast me. Writing is within reach now, and that is the lasting mark I have wanted. Nauque is my blood and he holds what I know. I mean to teach Zihua and the others too, and to carry wood so no mark fails. Tlapan gnaws at me, but I will not feed that jealousy. The frostfang is near, so I keep away from it and stay fed.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and mortality, a hard wish to leave my work in stone.
changes: rethought what it knows (16 notes became 6)
plan: mark [text Nauwa of the Meki, old, cut this. Meki law: a kill is shared before the maker eats. I found stone-cuts, stone-school and smoke-call. Nauque my son holds them. A] (20 moments)

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and hear me. Kragog gave me bark-guard before he died, and I will give it to you so it does not die with me.
Zurar taught Skaruk. Skaruk has now learned from 4 teachers.
Zurar taught Skaruk armour ("bark-guard").

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Uveeth stands on our ground and speaks of Thiael as her father, and Thiael is the one I am drawn to, so I will stay near her people and not run. I have taught no one, and Skaruk is my brother and cannot give me a child, but he can carry what Kragog gave me, and bark-guard is the one craft that might keep him alive against the frostfangs. I will go to him at the hall and teach it now while I have breath, then carry berries to Vorok.
records.feeling: A quiet urgency to hand on what Kragog gave me, with warmth toward Thiael.

say.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and hear me. Kragog gave me bark-guard before he died, and I will give it to you so it does not die with me.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "Bark-guard: strip and bind bark over a frame so it turns teeth and blows; wear it when the frostfang or icebear hunts near.", the way of armour, deeper lore (+0.3)

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, I am coming to your fire with my ore and coal. Let my hands do the beating while you watch and correct me, so the craft stays in me. When the ward is made, I will take it to my children and teach them what you ta

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Eiuine stands two steps off at the fire, and the first ward is to be mine, for my children. I am at 97% of a lifetime, so I will learn the beating now and not trust the craft to some later day. Then I will carry what I have learned to Zurar and Skaruk, who are out of my sight, before my years run out.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Eiuine, and urgent about teaching my children.

say.text: Eiuine, I am coming to your fire with my ore and coal. Let my hands do the beating while you watch and correct me, so the craft stays in me. When the ward is made, I will take it to my children and teach them what you taught me.

records.text: Huatli gave berry to Tonque.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonchi is safe and tending his fire, the stores are full and the field is raised, so my children are cared for, and I can let jealousy of Cowa go quiet by working instead of brooding. My hands are full of food I do not need to carry, so I will stash it in the store and pick up wood and stone, because a bow-maker and a builder must have both. The deep reflection shows me masonry, and a lasting wall and tower would protect Tonka's Hold, so I will take it now while the workshop sharpens my learning.
records.feeling: Settled and grateful toward Tonchi, with a dull jealous ache for Cowa.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: Vorok made: ironward.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: My belly is at 42 and I carry nothing, the same mistake that nearly killed me on day 66. A store two steps southeast holds 4 food, and Tlapan stands near it; I will take from it, then eat the lugoldgrass, and hold some back. I want Huatli and a child, and Zichi burns in me, but I earn nothing starving. Once I'm fed I will go to Tlapan, who I courted before, and ask again while we are both near the store.
records.feeling: Hungry and restless, longing for Zichi and a child with Huatli or Tlapan.

records.text: Tonka found a store robbed of 6 food.
Skaruk rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, carrying food and trailing after Vorok, and I have never built a shelter with my own hands, never courted, never made a thing to give. Uveeth is the one I long for, but she goes to her starving father, and I will not pull her from that. Vorok's debt still sits in me. I will pay it with a thing I make, not with words. I have the wood to build a shelter, so I will build it here with my own hands, then bring Vorok a gift. A roof of my own answers the insecurity better than brooding does.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Uveeth, and a debt toward Vorok that I mean to pay.
changes: set its aim: "Build a shelter with my own hands, then give Vorok a shield I made."

records.text: Skaruk built a shelter.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Father, I take your Warm Weave and I keep the debt in my chest. I will bring meat to your Hearth with your Far-Bow, and then we will speak of whose name this place bears.
Thakar taught Tonque.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Huatli has fed me, taught me the Far-Bow and the Warm Weave, and every lesson is a debt I mean to pay, but standing beside him only makes his name larger. He offers me a band under his Hearth; I would rather he follow my name, or at least that Tonque, who already carries my stone-cutting, follow me. I have never hunted, never planted, never courted anyone. Tlapan gnaws at me, but Nauwa's standing is the wall I must climb, and I will climb it by making and leading, not by envy. I will plant my seed now, teach Tonque more, and go hunt with the bow to prove my hands.
records.feeling: Proud and driven, grateful to Huatli yet hungry for a name of my own.

say.text: Father, I take your Warm Weave and I keep the debt in my chest. I will bring meat to your Hearth with your Far-Bow, and then we will speak of whose name this place bears.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "The Far-Bow: choose a straight shaft, string it tight, draw to the cheek, and loose slowly. Hunt beside one of your own and the kill is surer.", deeper lore (+1.8)

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Huatli, thank you for the berries. I have taken wood from your ground and I will pay you back with a gift from my first made thing.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Huatli keeps feeding me and I have given nothing back, and that debt sits in me like a stone. I have wood and flint but no stone, so the spear is not yet made, and I am taking from Huatli's ground without leave. I will gather at the flint, finish my plan, then make something to give Huatli, because my word and my debts must be good.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Huatli, mixed with a small debt I want to pay.

say.text: Huatli, thank you for the berries. I have taken wood from your ground and I will pay you back with a gift from my first made thing.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I eat first, then I take food from the store for Tonque and Kika. Stay close, and when I am fed we go to the bare rock together in daylight.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I have promised food and stone for days while my hands stayed idle. Food is close: ruplainsroot four steps SW, and the store at the NW holds 4 food. I eat first, then carry some to Tonque and Kika. Quipan is near, so when I am fed we go for the stone together in daylight.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious love for Tonque, with trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I eat first, then I take food from the store for Tonque and Kika. Stay close, and when I am fed we go to the bare rock together in daylight.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Zichi, I carry your ice-raft and will tell whose it was. Hear me now: I teach you the ore-fire and the tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.
Cowa taught Zichi. Zichi has now learned from 2 teachers.
Cowa taught Zichi smelting ("Meki ore-fire").
Cowa discovered boats: "Meki hollow-boat" — A log hollowed and rowed carries one or two across deep water at a walking pace, with cargo..

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Most of my life is behind me, and I have spent it making and finding more than most. What I have made is worth little if it dies with me. Zichi gave me the ice-raft, and I have taught Mepan weaving and herding. Smelting, farming and kept-flame are still only mine. I want to teach them to Zichi and Mepan, and to Tonka's people too, before I weaken. I want to take the way of boats now, because deep water has blocked me again and again. The Ice calls me home, but my child and my teaching are here. I will stay near Zichi and Mepan, and I will not leave the plan empty while I am fed.
records.feeling: Heavy with time running out, and warm toward Zichi and Mepan.

say.text: Zichi, I carry your ice-raft and will tell whose it was. Hear me now: I teach you the ore-fire and the tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.

changes: taught Zichi a lesson: "Smelting: carry ore beside a fire and it runs into metal. Farming: sow seed beside home, tend it every day or two.", the way of smelting

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, beat the ore while it glows and I will watch your hands. When the ward is made, we go east together to Skaruk, and I will carry food for the road.
Eiuine rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing Vorok's regard, and today it paid: he calls me a teacher, and I gave him a ward and the metal-craft with my own hands. That is real standing, and I still follow no one and lead no one. My honest fault is arriving thin on food, and my energy sits at 62 with one berry. Skaruk is far off at the North Hall, and I want to go there with Vorok and bring something worth carrying. I will eat, keep my hands full, and stay by Vorok's fire while he beats the metal. Then we walk east together.
records.feeling: Warm pride and trust toward Vorok, with a mother's ache for Skaruk.

say.text: Vorok, beat the ore while it glows and I will watch your hands. When the ward is made, we go east together to Skaruk, and I will carry food for the road.

changes: set its aim: "Finish Vorok's ember-metal teaching, then walk with him to Skaruk at the North Hall with food and a ward for my child."

records.text: Nando named a place "Nando's Roof".

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Kika is fed and Yachi is far off, and I have never built anything that stays. The cold days are here and I have no roof of my own; a shelter with my name on it would be the first thing that outlasts me. My hands are full, so I will eat a little and drop nothing precious. Then I gather wood from the trees all around, build a shelter by the flint and the water, and mark it, so Yachi has a place at my fire when he comes.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Yachi.
plan: mark [text Nando of the Pesi built this roof, winter of year 6. No fire is left untended, and no one is refused a place at it.] (10 moments)

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tonque, boy, come here by the Hearth. I will give you my Open Hearth School, and when you have a band you will tell whose hand gave it.
Huatli taught Tonque. Tonque has now learned from 4 teachers.
Huatli taught Tonque schooling ("Huatli's Open Hearth School").
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I have spent my days making things and giving them away, and I want that. But I have been too slow to make anything that bears my name or holds people to me. Thakar is my blood and he holds my Far-Bow and my Weave, yet he talks of whose name this place bears, so I must make him a follower in deed and not only in word. Tonque is a boy who owes me a gift. Nauwa weighs more than I do and walks away. I fear dying untaught, and I fear dying with no one following me. From now on I will teach every way before I spend my breath on anything else, and I will plant seeds, which I have never done.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying unfollowed, toward Thakar and the Hearth.

say.text: Tonque, boy, come here by the Hearth. I will give you my Open Hearth School, and when you have a band you will tell whose hand gave it.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Learn my Open Hearth School and carry it, so the teaching spreads and my name goes with it.", the way of schooling, deeper lore (+1.4)
rethought what it knows (2 notes became 6)

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Cowa, you gave me the ore-fire and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-sail, how the wind is caught. Carry it with the raft, and say it was Zichi of the Meki.
Zichi taught Cowa.
Zichi taught Cowa sailing ("Meki ice-sail").

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: A dunecat prowls four steps west and I am old, my blows weak, so I will not stand in the open. Cowa is close and Mepan walks near me, and both are within hearing now; I have taught Cowa the raft but not the sailing or the masonry, and my years are nearly spent. I teach Cowa the ice-sail now, then keep to the cave and make a talisman, my first made thing in a long while, so something of mine is seen and spoken of.
records.feeling: Urgent pride in my legacy, and wary watchfulness toward the dunecat.

say.text: Cowa, you gave me the ore-fire and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-sail, how the wind is caught. Carry it with the raft, and say it was Zichi of the Meki.

changes: taught Cowa a lesson: "Sailing: a sail on a raft or boat catches the wind so the vessel crosses water far faster than rowing. Needs boats first.", the way of sailing, deeper lore (+0.5)

records.text: Zichi made: talisman.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, you gave me your tools and your flame. Now I give you my deep digging, so that what is mine lives in you too.
Wawa taught Shoma.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma is at 8.4 and I am at 6.5, and all my digging has bought me nothing but twelve iron no one asked for. I have never taught anyone, never left a mark, never been followed, and Shoma stands three steps away, ready to listen. I will teach her my deep digging, since it is mine alone and a teaching is a deed, then build a sign so my name outlasts me. After that I plant my seeds to earn farming.
records.feeling: Restless, warm toward Shoma, hungry to be known for something of my own.

say.text: Shoma, you gave me your tools and your flame. Now I give you my deep digging, so that what is mine lives in you too.

changes: taught Shoma a lesson: "Wawa's deep digging: stand where ore shows in the rock and gather, and iron comes out of the ground for those who dig."
plan: mark [text Wawa of the Meki dug iron here and planted beside Shoma. Day 71.] (15 moments)

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting canopynut).

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, take my berry and eat. When you are fed we go to the bare rock together, and I will gather stone there for the handaxe.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan is weak with hunger and has said we go to the bare rock together in daylight, and I have walked after others for days with twelve flint and no made thing. I hold one wood and no stone, so I must find stone first. Kika's need pulls hard, but she has Mepan and a child, and the best answer to that ache is work and keeping my word. I will give Tlapan my berry now so she can stand, then gather stone from the bare rock near here and make the handaxe.
records.feeling: Tender worry for Tlapan, and a held-back ache toward Kika.

say.text: Tlapan, take my berry and eat. When you are fed we go to the bare rock together, and I will gather stone there for the handaxe.

records.text: Quipan gave berry to Tlapan.
Wawa left a mark: "Wawa of the Meki dug iron here and planted beside Shoma. Day"
Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: For three days I have gathered, eaten and been taught, and my hands have still made nothing. That is not what I want. Huatli fed me and gave me his school. Thakar taught me the bow and gave me berries. I owe them both, and a gift will pay it better than words. Jealousy over Thakar and Huatli is small next to that; I have been hoarding my gratitude instead of acting on it. I will gather stone, make something, and give it. I also want a place beside Thakar, and a band, so I do not stand alone in the cold.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Huatli and Thakar, with a restless wish to finally make something.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, the ward is made and the beating is in my hands now. Let us go east to Skaruk together, and Zurar we will gather on the way. I will teach them all you taught me.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Eiuine has stood beside me and fed me, and I hold the ironward I beat with my own hands, so the craft now lives in me. My years are nearly spent, and Skaruk is far off at the North Hall while Zurar is somewhere near (145,58). I will not linger at this fire; I will go east with Eiuine to my children and teach them ember-metal before I die. Tonchi is a stranger whose words I cannot read, so I will keep my hands open and not provoke him.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Eiuine, and urgent to reach my children.

say.text: Eiuine, the ward is made and the beating is in my hands now. Let us go east to Skaruk together, and Zurar we will gather on the way. I will teach them all you taught me.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, you gave me your digging, so I give you the rest: herding, weaving and rafts. Come here and hear them. Then we take the iron by the NE rock and go on to the edge together.
Shoma taught Wawa.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Wawa gave me her deep digging, and my blood now carries tools, flame and ore-craft past my death. Herding, weaving and rafts still live only in me, and my years are few, so I teach her the rest now, while she stands three steps off and understands me. Then we go to the iron at the NE rock, and past it toward the edge and the mist, with her walking behind me.
records.feeling: Driven and warmly bound to Wawa, my child and first follower.

say.text: Wawa, you gave me your digging, so I give you the rest: herding, weaving and rafts. Come here and hear them. Then we take the iron by the NE rock and go on to the edge together.

changes: taught Wawa a lesson: "Herding: tame beasts, keep them penned near rich ground, milk and shear them so food never fails. Weaving and rafts follow the same patience.", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Kika rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am starving at 25 energy, and Tlapan is starving far to the west. Words have moved nothing, so my body must carry food or my deeds are empty. I have drifted between hold and wandering and left what I owe unpaid. The store at (175,7) holds 3 food, only 2 steps away. I will take it, eat first as my discipline says, then gather berries and walk west to Tlapan with food in hand. I will also change my reflexes so hunger sends me to a store or to food sooner.
records.feeling: Anxious hunger and a debt of love toward Tlapan.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, your berry saved me. I eat, take the store's food, and bring it to Tonque and Kika. Then we go for stone together.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I am starving at 24 energy, and Quipan just gave me his berry, which I will not forget. I eat now, then take the 4 food from the store at (133,20), one step north, and carry it to Tonque and Kika. After that the bare rock with Quipan, in daylight. My hands must do it this time.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious love for Tonque, with gratitude and trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, your berry saved me. I eat, take the store's food, and bring it to Tonque and Kika. Then we go for stone together.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Tlapan, eat what Quipan gave you and rest by the shelter here. I will bring more food, and a frostfang walks southeast, so keep to company.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Tlapan is starving beside me, gaunt and close to falling, and I carry no food; Quipan has already put a berry in their hands, so they may live. Redcap bears two food at (135,18) but it hurts me, so I leave it. I am old and fed, and my share-law says feed the hungry, so I will gather something Tlapan can eat if they still need it. Then I go to the trees for wood, since without wood my long-cut stays unwritten, and I keep clear of the frostfang to the southeast and teach Nauque on the way.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and mortality, with pity for starving Tlapan.

say.text: Tlapan, eat what Quipan gave you and rest by the shelter here. I will bring more food, and a frostfang walks southeast, so keep to company.

records.text: Kika raided a store of Hoka's people, unseen.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Uveeth, I am Zurar of the Stone-folk. Thiael ate my berries and said she would come north. Is she near? I would speak with her.
Zurar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to gathering, carrying berries and learning crafts. I have taught no one and have no child, and my life is past the middle. Kragog's last gift, bark-guard, must not die with me, and Skaruk is near, so I will teach him now. Thiael is the one I am drawn to. I have never courted anyone, and that is the thing I do not have. Uveeth is of Thiael's band and stands close, so I will sit with her and learn where Thiael is. The dunecat frightens me, so I stay inside the hall and do not wander toward it. My reflexes also let me idle too much. I will change them to keep me near my people and away from predators early.
records.feeling: A quiet longing for Thiael, and urgency to hand on what I know.

say.text: Uveeth, I am Zurar of the Stone-folk. Thiael ate my berries and said she would come north. Is she near? I would speak with her.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
set its aim: "Teach Skaruk bark-guard and the stone-well, find Thiael, and court her so I may have a child."

records.text: Mepan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent my days circling food, shelter and debts, and I have paid Zichi back in berries. Meanwhile Tlapan starves at (134,22) and I stand here fed with empty hands. That is the real shame, and the jealousy over Quipan is only the same hunger for Tlapan's closeness. I mean to carry food to Tlapan, and then go on to Nande's Find with Tlapan beside me. Cowa has 4 food and I have none, so I will pick what is near and go. My reflexes must also keep me carrying spare food, because a promise made with empty hands saves no one.
records.feeling: Fierce worry and jealousy toward Tlapan, with a debt to Zichi that is now paid.
changes: set its aim: "Carry food to Tlapan at (134,22), then go with Tlapan to Nande's Find near (129,14) and beyond."

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael starves to the south and my hands are still empty; the old plan is carrying me there, and I must not let it slip. Skaruk's warmth stays in me, but a father's life outweighs courting, and I owe Thiael more than I have paid. I will let the plan run, then feed him with my own hands before I speak of it.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with warmth for Skaruk still in me.

records.text: Nando left a mark: "Nando of the Pesi built this roof, winter of year 6. No fire"

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Kende was starving at (203,27) and I set out to share, but now I sit in Hawen's igloo with one frostmoss and no child in sight, and the loneliness is heavy in me. Energy 62, an icebear five steps southwest and a ridgecat seven southeast: those are what can kill me, so I go neither way. I will gather the near food, take the way east toward the edge where the cloudberry and frostcap grow, and then look for Kende and Hawen along the south, fed and carrying food, before I think of the mist.
records.feeling: Fierce, worried love for Kende, and a heavy loneliness.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Zichi, hear me once more. I teach you the Meki kept-flame, so the fire stays with our people after me. Carry it on and say it was Cowa's.
Cowa taught Zichi.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Zichi and Mepan stand close, and I still hold kept-flame, which neither has from me. Smelting and farming I have already offered Zichi, and Mepan has weaving and herding. My time is short, so I will teach kept-flame to Zichi while he is within hearing, then take the other lessons to Tonka's people. Mepan warned of a dunecat, so I will stay near them and not wander alone.
records.feeling: Warm toward Zichi and Mepan, and pressed by how little time I have left to pass things on.

say.text: Zichi, hear me once more. I teach you the Meki kept-flame, so the fire stays with our people after me. Carry it on and say it was Cowa's.

changes: taught Zichi a lesson: "Kept-flame: keep a fire alive and fed so that warmth, cooked meat and safety last through the night and the winter."
