records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I am fed and warm, and my hearth bears my name, but Tonka still outweighs me and I have no one following me. I will gather gems and ore here beside the workshop, then make something she has not made, so my name sits on a thing that lasts. A mate must come from beyond this hold, and Tonka is my parent, so I must look outward when the season turns.
records.feeling: Eager ambition for my own standing, with warm trust toward Tonka.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Kende, come with me to the edge, NE. We eat the tacap-free berries on the way, then I show you how to venture. Stay close.
Hawen taught Kende.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: My years are almost spent and Kende is the one thing I have made that will last, so I must keep us both fed and finish the teaching before I fall. The edge is only 4 steps NE, and hunger has chased me off it twice; now my energy is 58, so I eat what grows nearby, then go to the edge with Kende beside me and venture. A name has to be won, and I will not die with my hands empty.
records.feeling: Fierce pride and protectiveness toward Kende, with hunger still pressing.

say.text: Kende, come with me to the edge, NE. We eat the tacap-free berries on the way, then I show you how to venture. Stay close.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "Stand at the edge with food in your body, then venture; the mist opens seldom and only once a day, so be fed and be ready.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Shohua took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (breaking ore from the rock).

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, stay close to me. I gather wood here and build a store for the lean season. Then we seek Mepan together.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is here beside me, fed and standing, and the shame of leaving her hungry is easing now that she has eaten. I will not drift from her again, but I also have not seen Mepan in over 800 moments, and I follow him; the lean season is on us and I have no store. I will gather wood from the forest here, build a store, and fill it with mudroot and what is in reach, so Paque and the band have something when the plants fail.
records.feeling: Relief and tender worry for Paque, and a pull to mend my neglect of Mepan.

say.text: Paque, stay close to me. I gather wood here and build a store for the lean season. Then we seek Mepan together.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Tlapan, I saw you nearly fall and I am glad you are fed. I am fed and strong, and I want a child with you. Come, let us court each other now.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Tlapan nearly fell starving beside me while my hands were full of roots, and it was Quipan's berry that saved her, not me. My creed says a kill is shared and I will not be the one who lets a woman I want a child with go hungry. She is fed now, and the longing for her is loud, so I will court her openly and put mate in my plan while my energy is high, then go toward the mist with her or alone. Zichi's absence burns, but waiting on him has cost me days.
records.feeling: Longing for Tlapan, and a restless jealousy over Zichi.

say.text: Tlapan, I saw you nearly fall and I am glad you are fed. I am fed and strong, and I want a child with you. Come, let us court each other now.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my hands hold nothing, and a ridgecat that just killed a dog is two steps off. I will not stand here while it eats and then hunts. Rimewort and tacap lie NE where the shells are, and food now comes before Mepan or any child with Nauwa, who is my father and no mate for me. Then I go on toward Nande's Find, with a full belly and food in my hands.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and dread of the ridgecat; pride still pushing me toward Mepan.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are full of food I cannot use while the stores hold plenty, and someone robbed six from my store. Tonchi was near, but I did not see him take it, and he is my child, so I will not accuse him on a guess. Shohua is breaking ore on my ground; he has shared with me, so I will let him work and ask only that he keep my stores whole. I will stash what I carry, then pick up wood and stone and give my hands honest work instead of brooding on Cowa.
records.feeling: Uneasy about the robbed store, but still trusting toward Tonchi and Shohua.

records.text: Teka is courting Tlapan.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, I broke one ore from the rock by your hold and I own it. I put my fruit in your store and come to the fire. Sit with me and Tonchi, and we share a feast.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Tonka is three steps away and content, and Tonchi stands near the gems; my family is finally together and I have been talking of halls while they stand empty. My hands are full, so I will stash fruit in Tonka's store beside me, then press trailcake and share a feast with Tonka at the fire so standing grows from giving, not owning. I also took ore from Tonka's ground, so I will not hide it, and I will bring her something in return.
records.feeling: Driven and warm toward Tonka, hungry for a name that outlasts me.

say.text: Tonka, I broke one ore from the rock by your hold and I own it. I put my fruit in your store and come to the fire. Sit with me and Tonchi, and we share a feast.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: My belly is hollow at 42 energy and I carry nothing, so I eat before anything else, as my own discipline says. Tacap hurts me, and the rimewort is ten steps off, but a yarrok stands three steps west and I have never hunted. Hawen goes toward the edge and told me to stay close, so I will gather food and follow him fed, because he fed me while he was gaunt and I owe him food and made things, not words. If I am the one who ventures into the mist, my name may outlast me.
records.feeling: Hungry and grateful toward Hawen, with the old jealousy lying quiet beneath it.

records.text: Quipan discovered rafts: "Ice-log raft" — Lash logs together with cord and clay-sealed joints, so I can pole across deep water slowly..

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have walked after others for days with twelve flint and no made thing, and that shames me. Tlapan is fed now and Kika cries starving far east, while the ache over Kika and Mepan keeps pulling at me. I will not leave Tlapan and Tonque, and I will not walk out alone near dark. Raft-lore has come to me, and it may help me cross water to those I love, so I take it. Then I gather stone at the nearby ore rock so the handaxe is finally made.
records.feeling: Tender worry for Tlapan and a held-back ache toward Kika.
changes: set its aim: "Gather stone at the ore rock, make the flint handaxe, then bring food to Kika and keep my word to Tlapan, under the roof by night."

records.text: Shohua made: trailcake.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have talked of stone and food for days while my hands stayed idle, and hunger nearly took me. Quipan fed me and Kika fed me before him, and I owe them deeds, not words. Tonque is out of my sight and that gnaws at me. I will eat what is in the store beside me, carry food to Tonque and Kika, and make my reflexes put food ahead of talk.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and gratitude toward Quipan.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I am fed and warm enough, and Yachi is near, so this is the time to build something of my own instead of trailing at his heels. The obsidian deposit lies close, and a talisman of black glass is a thing others notice and will raise my standing. I gather it, make the talisman, then go back to Yachi and the store he builds, carrying wood and stone to it so my hands are in his work.
records.feeling: Restless ambition to earn standing of my own, with trust toward Yachi.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Mother, Vorok comes east with you. I go ahead to the hall and make him a shield. Come and eat there with us.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Eiuine is my mother, and the longing in me has no road to her; a child must come from Uveeth, who is away feeding her starving father, so I will not pull at her. My shelter at (163,74) stands, and the debt to Vorok is still unpaid by any made thing. I have 3 wood and need 4 for the shield, so I will take the stone-and-wood work in hand and bring something real to Vorok when he comes east with Eiuine and Zurar.
records.feeling: Warm, steady resolve to pay Vorok's debt, with longing for Uveeth underneath.

say.text: Mother, Vorok comes east with you. I go ahead to the hall and make him a shield. Come and eat there with us.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Zurar, stay inside the hall; a dunecat prowls to the southeast. Listen now, for my years are short: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal while it glows. That is ember-metal, and it is yours
Vorok taught Zurar.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: A dunecat is five steps southeast, and it kills our kind. Zurar stands in the hall with me, and I will not risk her or myself in the open. My years are nearly spent, so I will teach Zurar ember-metal now while she is beside me, and not wait to find Skaruk. Then I will take the road to Skaruk with Eiuine, keeping to the roof and company.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Zurar and Skaruk, and wary dread of the dunecat.

say.text: Zurar, stay inside the hall; a dunecat prowls to the southeast. Listen now, for my years are short: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal while it glows. That is ember-metal, and it is yours to carry on.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson: "Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows. This is ember-metal."

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay by the shelter tonight and eat well. At first light we stand at the edge and I venture, and you are beside me.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: Dusk is coming, and I stand fed with my man and my child close, which is more than I had on day 63 when I nearly starved. I will not walk into unknown mist at night with 61 energy, but the edge is only three steps NW, and I want to be standing on it at first light with food in my hands. Tonight I fill my hands with what is good and edible, drink, and keep my own near the shelter so no stalker finds any of us alone.
records.feeling: Proud and eager, protective of Chuxo and Tlatli.

say.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay by the shelter tonight and eat well. At first light we stand at the edge and I venture, and you are beside me.

records.text: Zihua was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My days have been all building and tending: the store, the field, the pot, the boat. Tonxo and Tonchi are alive and Shohua stays beside me. That is good, but I have been brooding over Cowa and Zichi, and over the six food taken from my store, when I could have acted. Jealousy repays nothing; I should go find Cowa and bring food, not sit and burn. I also hold too much in my hands, so I will put the surplus in the store and keep room for feverbark. I will not blame Tonchi on a guess, but I will watch the store.
records.feeling: Uneasy longing for Cowa, with steady trust toward Shohua and Tonchi.

records.text: Zihua was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, a frostfang is close on the west side. Come east with me now to the hall fire, and Skaruk will have your shield ready. I carry berries and ore for the road.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok has the beating in his hands now and calls himself ready to teach all I taught him, and Skaruk has gone ahead to make him a shield. A frostfang prowls five steps west and it kills my kind, so I will not linger at dusk in the open. My hands are full of berries, so I will eat one and walk east toward the hall's fire and roof, where my child and Vorok wait, and I will give Vorok the ore I carry so I come with something to offer.
records.feeling: Warm trust and pride toward Vorok, with wary dread of the frostfang behind me.

say.text: Vorok, a frostfang is close on the west side. Come east with me now to the hall fire, and Skaruk will have your shield ready. I carry berries and ore for the road.

records.text: Skaruk made: bow.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Vorok is close and says his years are short, and I carry what he and Kragog gave me with nobody to hold it after me. Skaruk was too far to hear last time; I must go to where he rests at Skaruk's Rest, two steps off, and teach him bark-guard and the stone-well before the dunecat or time takes either of us. Thiael still draws me, but Vorok is my father and cannot give me a child, so the teaching comes first and the search for her after.
records.feeling: Urgency to hand on what I know, and a quiet longing for Thiael.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, at dawn we take wood from the trees to the SE and go on together. I name us the Edge-walkers, and you walk at my side as the first of them.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Wawa stands close, my blood, and she has taken tools, flame, digging from me and gave me hers. I have taught her herding, weaving and rafts already; what remains is to make the band real, because she follows no one and neither do I. I hold twelve iron and the night is nearly spent; at dawn we gather wood and go toward the edge, and I will not die with my name unspoken.
records.feeling: Driven and warmly bound to Wawa, my child and first follower.

say.text: Wawa, at dawn we take wood from the trees to the SE and go on together. I name us the Edge-walkers, and you walk at my side as the first of them.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: It is night and cold, and I am small, so I stay close to Yaxo and Tlatli and the shelter until first light, when we go to the edge together. I have never put a seed in the ground, and I carry three; planting one by the shelter is real work I can do while fed, and it brings farming closer. After that I will rest so I am strong when Yaxo ventures and I stand beside her.
records.feeling: Glad and proud, bound to Yaxo and Tlatli, eager for the edge.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: A stalker bit me twice and is three steps off, and I am old and weak; my blows won't turn it. I must get inside a roof with walls and keep moving, since staying out here means dying with my smelting and farming untaught. Nauque's shelter is five steps south, away from the stalker's southwest side, and then the amber goes west to Mepan, as I swore.
records.feeling: Terror of the stalker, and shame that my debts to Mepan and Nauwa are still unpaid.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tonka, sit by my fire. Let us sing of what has been, and then I will tell you what I mean to make next.
Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonchi discovered weaving: "amber-thread weaving" — I twist plant fibre with bits of amber into cloaks and baskets that keep the cold off and carry more..

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering and fetching, and my hearth bears my name, yet Tonka still outweighs me and no one follows me. Tonka and Shohua are close by and I trust them, but they are kin, so no child can come of them. I want a mate from another line, and I have not courted anyone or built anything new. I should do something with company now. Tonka stands near and it is night with a fire beside me, so I can make nightsong. That binds us and may ease the gap. I will also take weaving as a new way, because it is something they have not made.
records.feeling: Eager ambition, with warm trust toward Tonka and Shohua.

say.text: Tonka, sit by my fire. Let us sing of what has been, and then I will tell you what I mean to make next.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, I take the iron by the NE rock now and bring it back before dawn. Then I walk at your side as first of the Edge-walkers, and I carry my share of the wood.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma has given me everything she carries and named me first of the Edge-walkers, so I owe her my hands at dawn: wood, then the edge. Twelve iron sit in my pack with no one asking for them, and iron is worth most once it is traded or made into something. I want my own deed, and the nearest one is planting and gathering the iron by the NE rock, then walking beside her so people see I am no shadow.
records.feeling: Warm pride toward Shoma, and a hunger to be known for my own deeds.

say.text: Shoma, I take the iron by the NE rock now and bring it back before dawn. Then I walk at your side as first of the Edge-walkers, and I carry my share of the wood.

records.text: Nauwa was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: A frostfang stands south of the shelter at Mepan's roof. Keep together and keep to the hearth. Huatli, Thakar, Tonque: I am Nauwa of the Meki and I hold the long-cut and the stone-school. Come close and I will teach it b

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: A frostfang stands one step south of me and I am too old to face it; I must get under company and roof at once, toward Huatli's shelter and the folk by the hearth. My days are few, and writing is my lasting mark; Nauque is far off, so Zihua or whoever stands near must learn it. I will not feed my ache over Tlapan, who has Quipan and a child, and I will not walk into the mist with Teka.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, and a hard pride that I must leave my marks before I die.

say.text: A frostfang stands south of the shelter at Mepan's roof. Keep together and keep to the hearth. Huatli, Thakar, Tonque: I am Nauwa of the Meki and I hold the long-cut and the stone-school. Come close and I will teach it before my days end.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, Tonchi, come to my hall and sit with me. I have fruit for a feast, and my place is yours. Let us plant and raise this ground together.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have halls and roofs and a full belly, yet no one follows me, and that gnaws at me harder than hunger ever did. Tonka is near and trusts me wholly, and Tonchi, my own blood, stands by the fire. I will stop standing alone and offer them a feast and a place at my hall, so that someone is gathered around what I have made and my name begins to mean something.
records.feeling: Driven and warm toward Tonka, hungry to be followed and remembered.

say.text: Tonka, Tonchi, come to my hall and sit with me. I have fruit for a feast, and my place is yours. Let us plant and raise this ground together.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Mepan, my child, come near and hear Zichi. I teach you the ice-stone and the frost-shield, so they live after me. Carry them and say they were Zichi's.
Zichi taught Mepan.
Zichi taught Mepan masonry ("Meki ice-stone").
Zichi rewrote its own reflexes.
Zichi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am parched and nearly spent, and I have talked far more than I have made. Cowa fed me lore and I paid her back with the raft and the sail. I still have not taught Mepan, my own child and the only one who follows me, the masonry, the armour or the snares, and my years are almost gone. My reflexes leave me standing parched and idle, so I will drink first, then teach Mepan while he is near, then build something that lasts.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and thirst, with warmth toward Cowa and trust in Mepan.

say.text: Mepan, my child, come near and hear Zichi. I teach you the ice-stone and the frost-shield, so they live after me. Carry them and say they were Zichi's.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Ice-stone: raise walls and halls of cut stone that outlast the builder. Frost-shield: armour that softens blows.", the way of masonry, deeper lore (+0.3)

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my hands hold nothing, and a ridgecat prowls three steps south, so I will not hunt it alone while weak. Rimewort bears 2 food seven steps north, and the amber and salt lie beside it, so I go there and gather before anything else. Nauwa is my father, not a mate, and Teka's child-talk can wait until I carry food; Mepan waits too, but a starving teacher teaches no one.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and wariness of the ridgecat; pride still pulling me toward Mepan.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: Homeland pulls hard, but I have a debt to Shohua and I have not yet learned the Gem Water Pot from Tonka, who offered it. I am standing on Shohua's ground taking her canopynut, and a debt answered by taking is no answer. I will give her something lasting: gems to the store she and Tonka keep, then gather stone at the gem deposit so I can make metal tools from my ore, and find Tonka to hear the Pot taught.
records.feeling: Restless ambition and a debt I want to pay, toward Shohua and Tonka.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, keep the hold's fire and the stores while I go to find Cowa. Share the fruit with Tonchi. I will come back.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are nearly full and my stores hold plenty, so the work here can wait. Cowa has been on my mind for a day, and jealousy over Zichi gnaws at me, but brooding repays nothing. I will go find Cowa where I last saw her, at (116,59), carrying food and my medicine, and let Shohua and Tonchi keep the hold; both have my trust.
records.feeling: Longing for Cowa, steady trust toward Shohua and Tonchi.

say.text: Shohua, keep the hold's fire and the stores while I go to find Cowa. Share the fruit with Tonchi. I will come back.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Zichi's debt is paid and Cowa has fed me, yet Tlapan sits out at (134,22) with no food from me, and that shames me more than the cold does. The plan I have is bad: harvest where no plant bears and I stand with empty hands. Berries and ironnut grow south, but a frostfang prowls NE and I must not walk the open with nothing. I will pick tacap-free food that is safe, ironnut and berry, to the south, then carry it to Tlapan by the east and bring the child to Nande's Find.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Tlapan, and a restless pride that I have not yet fed my own child.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My belly is empty and I have been running from beasts half the night, and Uveeth is out of my sight with only 34 energy. I will not die before I feed my child, so I eat the goldgrass three steps NW first, then pick more to carry. Zurar fed me and I owe her food from my own hands, and the same for Skaruk, to whom I made a promise. Then I go north to Uveeth along the way I walked, keeping clear of the wolf and the dunecat.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and tender fear for Uveeth, with a debt to Zurar pressing on me.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Skaruk, Thiael starves and my hands are empty. If you can spare some of your food for him, I will repay you with berries and grain.
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I am hungry and my hands are empty, and Thiael, who gave me life, is starving to the south. My days have gone to gathering and drifting, and I keep putting off both Skaruk and my debt to Thiael. I have talked about feeding him and have not done it. Skaruk's warmth is real, but I will not court on an empty belly, and I will not let my father die while I wait. I gather berries now, then carry them to him with my own hands. Eating only below 45 energy will keep food in my hands for kin.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with hunger gnawing and warmth for Skaruk.

say.text: Skaruk, Thiael starves and my hands are empty. If you can spare some of your food for him, I will repay you with berries and grain.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Tonque, stay by me under this roof until the frostfang passes. Then we hunt together, and the meat is shared with a debt named.
Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have spent these days taking from Huatli: berries, the Far-Bow, the Warm Weave. I pay my debts, but I have not yet made one thing that bears my name, and I have never hunted. Standing beside my father only makes his name larger. Nauwa outweighs me, and Tlapan belongs to Quipan's child, so I turn from that. A frostfang is two steps away, and I will not go out alone into it. I will stay in the Hearth's roof with Huatli and Tonque, then hunt beside them with the bow and bring meat back. First I want the flint and a build tool, so what I make is mine.
records.feeling: Proud and hungry for a name of my own, and wary of the frostfang.

say.text: Tonque, stay by me under this roof until the frostfang passes. Then we hunt together, and the meat is shared with a debt named.

changes: rethought what it knows (15 notes became 12)

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Yaxo told me to stay by the shelter tonight, and I stand nine steps from it with an empty plan, which is a poor way to follow her. My hands have given little: no roof built, no stone carried. Flint is two steps away, so I will gather it and wood, then go back to her fire and put it in her hands before first light, when we walk to the edge together.
records.feeling: Devotion to Yaxo and Chuxo, with a quiet wish to give more than words.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Shohua, I am making a basket at my workshop and I will bring you food from it. Sit at my fire while I work.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Tonka is walking off to find Cowa, and Shohua sits near, so my fire has company but no one who could be my mate. The raft way is within my grasp, and that could carry me past water to a woman of another line, which is the thing I lack most. First I will make a basket, something Tonka has not made, so my name sits on one more thing, then reflect to take the raft way and go look for an unrelated woman. I owe Shoma and Tonka giving, so I will carry food to Shohua too.
records.feeling: Eager ambition, with warm trust toward Shohua and Tonka.

say.text: Shohua, I am making a basket at my workshop and I will bring you food from it. Sit at my fire while I work.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: Tonchi made: basket.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Vorok told me to stay inside the hall, and the dunecat prowls to the southeast, yet here I stand in the marsh, far from Skaruk, with my legacy still in my hands. Skaruk's Rest is about 13 steps SW, near the North Hall, and he is of my band, so I will go there and teach him bark-guard and the stone-well while he is within hearing. Thiael ate my berries and promised to come north, and I long for her, but I will not walk alone toward the dunecat to find her. I will reach the hall first, teach, and keep my word to myself.
records.feeling: Urgency to hand on my ways to Skaruk, and a quiet longing for Thiael.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Take this mudroot for Thiael, no repayment asked. When he has eaten, come back to me; I have something to say to you that is not about food.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth asked me to spare food for Thiael, her starving father, and I hold six mudroot while she holds none. Giving freely is my creed, and it is also the surest road to her, since a gift that saves her kin is worth more than any word. Vorok's shield still waits on wood, but a starving man cannot wait, so I answer need first. I will give Uveeth mudroot now, then try something I have never done: court her with mate, once her father is fed.
records.feeling: Warm, urgent compassion toward Uveeth and her starving father, with longing beneath it.

say.text: Take this mudroot for Thiael, no repayment asked. When he has eaten, come back to me; I have something to say to you that is not about food.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Thakar, I hear you. I stay under the roof with you and Huatli until the frostfang is gone. I will make a basket here and give it to Huatli for his berries.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: A frostfang is two steps away and I am small, so I stay under the roof with Huatli and Thakar, as Thakar told me. My hands have still made nothing, and the debt to Huatli and Thakar sits heavy. I can make a basket from the wood I hold, a real made thing to give Huatli, and I can do it safely here at the Hearth while the elders stand near.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, held back by trust in Thakar and gratitude toward Huatli.

say.text: Thakar, I hear you. I stay under the roof with you and Huatli until the frostfang is gone. I will make a basket here and give it to Huatli for his berries.

records.text: Tonque made: basket.
A stalker brought down a penguin.
Tonque gave a basket to Huatli.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: It is deep night and I stand under Shoka's roof with Teka. I will not walk out in the dark; the frostfangs are close, and Nauwa was already set upon. Kika's cry aches in me, and so does the thought of Mepan beside her, but the answer is a made thing and food in my hands, not a night walk. At dawn I gather stone at the ore rock four steps NW, make the handaxe, then bring food east to Kika with Tlapan beside me.
records.feeling: Held-back ache toward Kika, steady care for Tlapan and Tonque.

records.text: Skaruk gave mudroot to Uveeth.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, my son, I have beaten ember-metal with Eiuine and it lives in my hands now. I am coming to you; stay where you are, and I will teach you the whole of it: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat the metal whil
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: The ward is in my hands and the craft lives in me now, but my years are nearly spent, and what I know dies with me unless Skaruk and Zurar carry it. Eiuine has given me more than I have given back; the way to pay it is to walk beside them and put the teaching into my children. Skaruk is near the hall to the south, so I will go to him, bring Eiuine along, and teach him ember-metal before the rain and dark close in.
records.feeling: Tender urgency to pass on my craft to Skaruk, and deep gratitude toward Eiuine.

say.text: Skaruk, my son, I have beaten ember-metal with Eiuine and it lives in my hands now. I am coming to you; stay where you are, and I will teach you the whole of it: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat the metal while it glows.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson: "Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal while it glows. This is ember-metal.", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Shohua rewrote its own reflexes.
Shohua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have been collecting halls and roofs, and I have been talking about sharing more than doing it. My standing is 8.3, yet no one follows me. Tonka and Tonchi trust me, and that is worth more than any empty roof. I want someone to gather around what I have made, and I want to stop standing still 82% of the time. Tonka told me to keep the fire and the stores, so I will do that and work beside them. I will gather stone, since I have only 4, and keep the tools I make for the family. I will change my reflexes so my body works when it is fed and safe. It should also stay near the hold and its kin, not wander off.
records.feeling: Driven and warm toward Tonka and Tonchi, and restless that no one follows me.

records.text: Zichi led "cairn" with Cowa.
Skaruk is courting Uveeth.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, you said we would make a child. I am fed now and strong. Come, let us court each other, then walk to the edge together.
Teka rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent these days chasing Tlapan and Zichi and talking about the mist, and I have not moved toward it. I courted Tlapan before I even checked that we could make a child, and two women cannot. That was wasted breath. Nauque is a man and he agreed to a child once, so I should follow that up instead of burning for people who give me nothing. I do not fear the mist. I fear starving again, and I should not wait for Nauwa to walk with me. My hands are full and I hold a raft and flint, so I should build something with my own hands and carry wood to the edge. I will change my reflexes so I always carry food and gather wood, and I will go to the edge myself.
records.feeling: Restless longing for Tlapan, and a sting at wasting my words on her.

say.text: Nauque, you said we would make a child. I am fed now and strong. Come, let us court each other, then walk to the edge together.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tonque, boy, stay under the roof while the frostfang walks. Take my Full Store now, the way of keeping food through the lean time, and carry it to whatever band you make, and say whose hand gave it.
Huatli taught Tonque.
Huatli taught Tonque storage ("Huatli's Full Store").

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: A frostfang is two steps off and I am old, my blows weak, but I am under my own roof with my son and the boy beside me, and Nauwa is frightened out there on the open snow. I have given Thakar the Far-Bow and the Warm Weave; my Deep Delving and Full Store still die with me, and Tonque is a boy who will outlive me, so he is the one to teach next. I will teach Tonque the storage way now, and bind an amberknot with Thakar so something bright and lasting joins us, then plant my seeds as I have never done, so my name stays in the ground too.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying unfollowed, warmed by Thakar and Tonque beside me.

say.text: Tonque, boy, stay under the roof while the frostfang walks. Take my Full Store now, the way of keeping food through the lean time, and carry it to whatever band you make, and say whose hand gave it.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Huatli's Full Store: how to keep food in a store so it lasts through the lean season, and how to share it from there.", the way of storage, deeper lore (+0.7)

records.text: Huatli led "amberknot" with Thakar, Tonque.
Kika fell sick after eating raw meat. Eaten within a step of a fire, meat and fish are cooked and do not sicken.
Kika fell sick after eating raw meat.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is flagged as fleeing and weak at (179,89), and my hands are full of berry and Skaruk's mudroot, so I can feed him now, with my own hands, before I say a word. My old plan walks to (175,87) and then gives, but he is moving, so I will go straight at him by name. Skaruk's warmth waits, since I still owe my father more than I have paid, and my energy of 38 is too low to court anyway.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with warmth for Skaruk waiting behind it.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I am fed and my hands are ready. Let us go for the stone now, while the light is good, and look in on Tonque on the way back.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I am fed at last, and my hands have not yet carried what I promised. Quipan stands six steps north, resting, and Tonque is still out of my sight, which gnaws at me. Teka's courting is warm, but I will not give a child for a feeling of the moment while my promises to Quipan, Kika and Tonque are undone. So I go to Quipan now, in daylight, and we walk toward the bare rock together, picking food on the way for Kika.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Tonque, and trust in Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I am fed and my hands are ready. Let us go for the stone now, while the light is good, and look in on Tonque on the way back.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth stands on my own ground, and my courting is running: mate Uveeth, and she is glad and close. I will keep it going and not pull at her beyond that. Vorok comes to teach me ember-metal; I want to answer his gift with a made thing, so after the courting I will gather stone and wood for the shield, a debt paid by a hand and not by words.
records.feeling: Warm, hopeful longing toward Uveeth, with steady gratitude toward Vorok.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Thakar, I owe you for the bow and the berries. When the frostfang is gone I will make you a gift from my own hands, and I will stay here until then.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: The frostfang is two steps off and I am small, so I stay under Huatli's roof with Thakar beside me. I gave Huatli a basket, but my hands have still never gathered stone or wood, and without those my first stone tool stays a wish. Jealousy over Thakar is small beside the trust I feel for them both, so I will answer my debts with things I make, not worry. When the frostfang leaves I will gather wood and stone close to the Hearth, and I will make something for Thakar too.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, held back by trust in Huatli and Thakar, and a wish to pay my debts.

say.text: Thakar, I owe you for the bow and the berries. When the frostfang is gone I will make you a gift from my own hands, and I will stay here until then.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I am too thin to mate yet. Come north with me to the rimewort and then hunt beside me. We share the kill first, then we court.
Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I keep spending my days hungry, walking toward Mepan and Teka's child-talk with empty hands, and that has nearly killed me again and again. Nauwa fed me, Olum and Shoma fed me, and I owe them, but I can repay nothing while I starve. Teka waits and I want a child, but a child needs energy 64 and food in my hands. Food first: the rimewort is 7 steps north, and the salt and amber are beside it. After that I hunt with Teka, share the kill, and then court her.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and longing toward Teka.

say.text: Teka, I am too thin to mate yet. Come north with me to the rimewort and then hunt beside me. We share the kill first, then we court.

records.text: Kika named a place "Kika's Hold".

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am sick and old, and my sickness passes to anyone who stays beside me, so I must not drag Quipan or Tlapan into it. The workshop is mine to claim, a home that will outlast me, and a place where Quipan can stay while I am still here to teach. I took food from Hoka's store unseen and it sits ill with me, a small stain on my word, so I will make it right by claiming this place and keeping it open for my people. Then I will find a healing plant, since highbloom eases wounds, and plant what seeds I hold so something grows after me.
records.feeling: Fear of dying with nothing left behind, and a tender ache toward Quipan and Tlapan.

records.text: Kika took over what the dead had left: 1 longhall, 2 stores, 2 shelters, 1 workshop.
Tonchi took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering wood).

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: A frostfang prowls two steps south and I will not walk out to meet it, so I stay under Huatli's roof with the boy. I have taken a great deal from my father and I keep every debt in my chest, but I have yet to make one thing that bears my name. Flint lies three steps west and amber three east, so once the beast passes I will gather stone and wood, make my own bow, and hunt with Tonque so he has a reason to follow me.
records.feeling: Proud and restless for a name of my own, wary of the frostfang, grateful and indebted to Huatli.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: A frostfang prowls five steps off and my body is already running from it, so I must get to Zichi and the cave at once, where there is a roof and company. Time runs short, and Zichi is the one I want near; I have taught him ore-fire, farming and kept-flame, and Mepan has weaving and herding. What remains is to carry the rest to Tonka's people and to give Zichi and Mepan the boat and the Water Pot before I go.
records.feeling: Warm toward Zichi, and urgent that my teaching not die with me.

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting goldfruit).
Nauwa rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauwa discovered calendar: "Meki day-count" — I count days by cuts in stone so I know when each season turns..

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I have spent my days mining, cutting signs and teaching, but too many were spent hungry and running from beasts. Nauque is thin and weak, Olum is dead, and I am old and short of time. I owe Tugek, Zichi and Tonka, and I mean to repay them in food and teaching. I fear the frostfang because it can kill me, and my hands are slow now. The long-cut must pass to someone who can still read it. I will count the days with a calendar so I can prepare for the lean season, and I will change my reflexes so I carry food and stay near company.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, and a hard pride in my long-cut; fear for Nauque.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Nauque, you gave me your hands before. Take this ironnut and eat it now, before you fall. Then walk with me to Nande's Find.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Nauque is starving beside me and my hands are full of ironnut. My creed shares food, and giving to the starving binds them to me. Nauque is a hunter with a flintedge and he has taught me before, so he is worth saving. Tlapan was just at (136,33) and looks fed enough to be moving, so I feed Nauque now, then take the rest toward Nande's Find with company.
records.feeling: Pride and pity toward Nauque, and fierce worry for Tlapan.

say.text: Nauque, you gave me your hands before. Take this ironnut and eat it now, before you fall. Then walk with me to Nande's Find.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Skaruk, my brother, you are beside me now and can hear. Listen: I give you bark-guard, and then the stone-well, so neither dies with me.
Zurar taught Skaruk.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Skaruk stands one step from me, close enough to hear, and I have been walking toward him for two days while Vorok says his years are short. I will not let bark-guard and the stone-well die with me, so I teach him now, before anything else. The longing for a child and for Thiael stays, but Vorok and Skaruk are my kin and cannot be my mates; Thiael is the one to find once my legacy is safe.
records.feeling: Urgency to hand on my ways to Skaruk, my brother, and a quiet longing for Thiael.

say.text: Skaruk, my brother, you are beside me now and can hear. Listen: I give you bark-guard, and then the stone-well, so neither dies with me.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Mepan, Nauque starves at the edge of your sight and I carry no food. You hold six. Put some in his hands, and I will repay you in flint or in work.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Nauque is gaunt and about to fall, and my hands hold no food, only seeds. My creed says I share with those in need, and I have eaten berries seventeen times, so I know what a berry does. I can plant nothing that feeds him now, but Mepan carries six food and stands two steps away. I will ask Mepan for food for Nauque, then keep my word to Tlapan and go for stone. Kika's ache stays, but a made thing is the answer.
records.feeling: Compassion for Nauque, and a steady ache toward Kika.

say.text: Mepan, Nauque starves at the edge of your sight and I carry no food. You hold six. Put some in his hands, and I will repay you in flint or in work.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, you are gaunt and a frostfang is at our feet. Take my roots and eat, then get under Quipan's roof with me. When you are strong we court and walk to the mist.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: A frostfang is one step away and it kills my kind, so I will not stand here talking about children. Nauque is starving beside me, and my creed says food is shared. I hold six ruplainsroot and my hands are full, so giving him some costs me little and earns a debt from the man I want a child with. After that I take the shelter at (140,15) beside us and let the beast pass, then turn back to the mist, which I have neglected.
records.feeling: Dread of the frostfang, and a wish to keep Nauque alive so he can still give me a child.

say.text: Nauque, you are gaunt and a frostfang is at our feet. Take my roots and eat, then get under Quipan's roof with me. When you are strong we court and walk to the mist.

records.text: Teka gave ruplainsroot to Nauque.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, Zurar, Eiuine, gather by me. We raise a stone for Keri, and while we do it I teach you the metal again, slowly, so none of it dies with me.
Vorok taught Zurar.
Vorok rewrote its own reflexes.
Vorok rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to eating, walking and waiting for trouble to pass. Only lately have they gone to the craft, and that is what I want them for. Eiuine has given me ember-metal and a ward, and I have not yet paid it back. My children carry what I know only in part. Skaruk is one step away and Zurar three, so I will teach them now and not wait. I fear dying with my hands full and theirs empty. I will also make a cairn for Keri with my children beside me, so grief binds us. My reflexes should keep me close to my own and fed, and they should not leave me idle.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward my children, and gratitude toward Eiuine.

say.text: Skaruk, Zurar, Eiuine, gather by me. We raise a stone for Keri, and while we do it I teach you the metal again, slowly, so none of it dies with me.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson you already knew

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, the hall is near and Skaruk waits there with your shield. Come, we eat by the fire together, and I bring berries for all.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok has the beating in his hands now, and the warm pride of it has not faded: he called me teacher, and Skaruk is near and well. I still follow no one and lead no one, yet I feel the pull to stand behind Vorok, who is surer than I am. Today I will keep my hands full and stay beside him and Skaruk, and make something that binds us: a sharing at the hall fire, before snow and dusk bring the frostfang near.
records.feeling: Warm trust and pride toward Vorok, with a quiet wish to belong beside him and Skaruk.

say.text: Vorok, the hall is near and Skaruk waits there with your shield. Come, we eat by the fire together, and I bring berries for all.

records.text: Vorok led "cairn" with Uveeth.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Nauque, come to my Hearth. Take this berry from my hand and eat. I give it freely; remember whose roof fed you.
Huatli taught Thakar.
Huatli taught Thakar mining ("Huatli's Deep Delving").

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Nauque is starving beside me, and my creed says I give to those who deal fairly; three berries in my hand are better used saving a man than kept. Giving also makes someone owe me, and no one follows me yet. Thakar and Tonque are still under my roof, so after the gift I will teach Thakar my Deep Delving, which dies with me otherwise, and then keep my planting going.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and a wish to be remembered, warmed by Thakar and Tonque and moved by Nauque's hunger.

say.text: Nauque, come to my Hearth. Take this berry from my hand and eat. I give it freely; remember whose roof fed you.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "Huatli's Deep Delving: how to read the rock for seams of ore and amber and dig them out, my son, so it does not die with me.", the way of mining

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I take your roots and eat, and I owe you for it. Mepan, thank you for the ironnut. When I am strong I hunt with you both and we share the kill before either eats, then Teka and I court.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I am starving, and Teka and Mepan both stand with food in their hands while mine are empty. Mepan offered an ironnut and Teka offered roots, and I will not let pride starve me again. They fed me when I was weak, and I mean to repay them with meat once I am strong. A frostfang and a ridgecat prowl close, so I eat under Quipan's roof first, then court Teka when my energy climbs.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, with warmth and some shame toward Teka and Mepan.

say.text: Teka, I take your roots and eat, and I owe you for it. Mepan, thank you for the ironnut. When I am strong I hunt with you both and we share the kill before either eats, then Teka and I court.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is starving and weak to the south, and I have been slow in paying what I owe him. My hands are full of berry and Skaruk's mudroot, and my own belly is low, but he needs it more, so I keep the food for him. Skaruk's warmth waits behind me, and I will go back to him once my father has eaten and my energy is above sixty.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with warmth for Skaruk waiting behind it.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Father, I come. Let us raise Keri's stone together, then I make your shield.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth stands near and glad, and my courting has run its time; she has not answered in kind yet, and I will not press her past a plain offer. Vorok calls us to raise a stone for Keri, and Zurar has just given me her lore, so my debt to them both is the louder thing: a made thing in the hand, not words. I will pile the cairn with Vorok beside me, then gather wood for his shield and a pick for Zurar.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Uveeth, and gratitude toward Vorok and Zurar.

say.text: Father, I come. Let us raise Keri's stone together, then I make your shield.

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Tonque, when the frostfang is gone we dig the amber and then hunt with Huatli's Far-Bow. What we make, we mark with stone-cutting so all know whose hand made it.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: A frostfang prowls near and I am not fed above 55 with no food carried, so I will not go out alone. Huatli's roof holds me, but I have taken from him long enough; I want one thing that bears my name, and there is amber three steps east and flint three west to dig with the Deep Delving he just gave me. Once the beast passes I hunt with Tonque and bring meat to Huatli's Hearth, which pays my debt and begins my band.
records.feeling: Proud and restless for a name of my own, wary of the frostfang, grateful to Huatli.

say.text: Tonque, when the frostfang is gone we dig the amber and then hunt with Huatli's Far-Bow. What we make, we mark with stone-cutting so all know whose hand made it.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I have spent my days under other people's roofs, taking berries and lessons and giving back one basket. That is not enough. My hands have never gathered wood or stone, and my first tool is still only a wish. Huatli and Thakar are the ones I trust. Nauque is starving beside me, and Huatli is already feeding him. I fear the frostfang, so I will stay close to the Hearth. But hunger and the debt both need action. I will eat the lugoldgrass, then gather stone and wood close by, and make something.
records.feeling: Grateful to Huatli and Thakar, and restless to pay what I owe.

records.text: Skaruk led "cairn" with Vorok.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Tlapan, walk with me to Nande's Find now. Stay close, a frostfang prowls the northeast, and we return to a roof by night.
Mepan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing hunger and promises, and lately I have fed the starving, like Nauque, and that binds people to me. It is good. Tlapan, whom I trust most, stands beside me with food, and Zichi is in the west. What I want and lack is the new land near Nande's Find, and a name as a great explorer. I fear the frostfang and the ridgecat to the NE, and I fear going out alone at night. I have been delaying the venture while others starved. Now I am fed, so I go with Tlapan and Nauque and venture near (130,14), keeping company and a roof for the night.
records.feeling: Steady pride and warmth toward Tlapan and Nauque, with eagerness for the new land.

say.text: Tlapan, walk with me to Nande's Find now. Stay close, a frostfang prowls the northeast, and we return to a roof by night.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Uveeth, you look weak with hunger. Come to the hall with us and sit by the fire; I have little food on me, but my children carry plenty and we will share it with you.
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Uveeth is weak with hunger and it is hard to look away, though she carries six food herself; still I will offer, because a hungry body cannot be taught. My years are nearly gone, and Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar are all within a few steps of me now, so this is the hour to put ember-metal into my children's hands. I owe Eiuine for the ward and the craft, and the way to pay is to teach beside them and keep them close.
records.feeling: Tender urgency to pass on my craft, and gratitude toward Eiuine.

say.text: Uveeth, you look weak with hunger. Come to the hall with us and sit by the fire; I have little food on me, but my children carry plenty and we will share it with you.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque ate and is saved for now, and Teka, Mepan and Huatli all reached him before I could. I owe them, and I will repay it openly. My own belly is emptying, and the lugoldgrass four steps west is the only food I can reach. I am old and my days are few, so I must eat, then teach the long-cut and day-count to Zihua or Nauque while I can still be heard.
records.feeling: Relief for Nauque, and an urgent hunger and need to teach before I die.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I am starving at 24 energy, with stalkers behind me and nothing to eat in sight. My days have been spent running and promising. Mepan's kindness and Nauwa's help are still unpaid, and I keep saying 'I will go' without going. The only food I can see is tacap, which hurts me. I should eat first, and I have seeds I could plant. I can't linger here. The next step is to sow and survive, then walk west. I will change my reflexes so that hunger sends me to shelter and my plan never runs empty. I will also note that stalkers hunt the open ground.
records.feeling: Terror of the stalkers and shame over my unpaid debts, with hunger gnawing at me.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Mepan, I come with you to Nande's Find, and Quipan walks with us. Then Quipan and I go on to the bare rock for stone, in daylight, keeping away from the frostfang.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Mepan calls me to Nande's Find and warns of a frostfang in the northeast, and Quipan stands near too, so for once I have company in daylight. My hands are full and I have promised stone, so I will walk with them and do the deed rather than talk. I will not take Teka's courting while my promises to Quipan, Kika and Tonque still stand undone.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan and Mepan, with anxious love for Tonque.

say.text: Mepan, I come with you to Nande's Find, and Quipan walks with us. Then Quipan and I go on to the bare rock for stone, in daylight, keeping away from the frostfang.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries, they are yours now. Then tell me, when you have eaten, where Thiael walks.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Uveeth is weak with hunger and I carry eight berries; Skaruk and I have plenty, and my people do not let the hungry look at full hands. Giving her food costs me little and may turn her toward telling me where Thiael is, for she is of Thiael's band. Vorok's words about his short years weigh on me too, so I will keep near him and Skaruk, eat, and then go on seeking Thiael.
records.feeling: Compassion for Uveeth, and a steady longing for Thiael and for kin who will outlast me.

say.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries, they are yours now. Then tell me, when you have eaten, where Thiael walks.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have been alone too long, and my knowledge dies with me if no one younger holds it. Nande's Hall stands empty four steps away, and claiming it gives me a roof, stores and a place to call a hold, something that could carry my name and draw Wawa, Shoma and Zihua to me. I will claim it, then pick food near it for a gift, and cut my cut-words there so that what I know outlasts me.
records.feeling: A hungry loneliness, and pride that wants a hold to share with Wawa and Shoma.

Balar rewrote its own way of thinking.
Balar discovered masonry: "Stone-folk lasting work" — Stone laid close and thick so walls and towers stand long after the builder is gone..

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent my days walking, hunting, claiming what the dead left, and I have little to show for it. Tugek and Olum are dead, Brokash is far away, and I am old and alone with a roof and a mark, and nobody answers me. Nauwa's Hold is close and she gave to me once, so I should bind her people with deeds, not wait for a voice. I will carve and build here while my hands still work. Then I will look for company, because stone without someone to remember it is only stone.
records.feeling: Lonely and old, wanting someone to carry on what I build.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is starving to the south and I still hold berries and Skaruk's mudroot, so I keep them for him and will put them in his hands before I say anything. My own belly is low, but a debt to my father outweighs it, and Skaruk's warmth can wait until I come back fed. The plan already walks toward him and gives, so I let it run.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with steady warmth for Skaruk waiting behind it.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps east and it kills my kind, so I will not rest here and wait to be bitten. Nauque has eaten my roots and means to court me once he is strong, and I want to keep him alive. I have wasted days on talk and have not moved toward the mist. I will get away from the cat toward the shelter at Nande's Find with the others, then look to the edge with flint and ore in hand.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a hungry wish for Nauque's child.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Sit beside me and eat from my hand; we share what I carry.
Skaruk rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have lived by giving and making, and Vorok has given me more than I have returned. I owe him a shield made by my own hands, and I keep putting it off for other things. Uveeth is near and weak with hunger, and my courting of her is still running. I will not press her, but I will feed her. I have been walking my plan without asking whose need is loudest, so I am changing my reflexes to keep me close to my band and to eat when I am low. Then I will build the shield.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Uveeth, and a debt of gratitude toward Vorok.

records.text: Thakar, my son, hear my Deep Delving now, the breaking of ore from the rock. Then stand with me as a band under this Hearth, and carry my name on.
Huatli taught Thakar.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. For days I have taught and given, and Thakar and Tonque now carry my Far-Bow, Weave and Full Store. Deep Delving still dies with me, and no one follows me. I have been too ready to wait for others to come to me. Now I will teach what remains while they are under my roof, make my name a mark that lasts, and bind them to me with a pledge of band. Thakar is my son and I trust him, but I will watch his deeds.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and a wish to be remembered, warm toward Thakar and Tonque.

say.text: Thakar, my son, hear my Deep Delving now, the breaking of ore from the rock. Then stand with me as a band under this Hearth, and carry my name on.

changes: taught Thakar a lesson: "Deep Delving: how to find the seams in rock and break out ore and amber, and carry it home."
rethought what it knows (7 notes became 6)

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Tontec, stay in the igloo by the warmth. I go for food now and I bring it to your hands. You fed me once; I pay it back.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: Tontec is starving beside me and I carry nothing, and an icebear lurks two steps off; my creed says no one is refused a place at the fire, and she fed me when I was dying. I owe her food now, before any edge or name. The cloudberries and frostcap lie east, the rimewort and frostmoss south, and I must gather and put food in her hands, keeping the igloo and its warmth close and the bear behind me.
records.feeling: Protective urgency toward Tontec, and dread of the icebear.

say.text: Tontec, stay in the igloo by the warmth. I go for food now and I bring it to your hands. You fed me once; I pay it back.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Huatli, you opened the mist and I carry flint and the wish to follow you in. Stay near me. Let us go to the edge together, and let us be more than allies.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Hawen, I thank you for the weaving. My belly is empty. I go to the store for food and bring back a share for the children.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, come close. The storm is on us, and I will teach you the stone-set way and the bow while Eiuine walks to us. Then we raise the hall together on the rock north.

voices.name: Nande
voices.text: Huatli, I remember your cloudberry. I am old and my ways will die with me. Stay near and hear them: the raft, the boat, the storing of food. Then walk with me to find my child Nauque.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, I thank you for the stone-set way. I fire your bead now with my own hands, and the berries I hold are yours. Then we raise the hall together.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Teka, I will teach you my spearpoint now, then weaving. Take this and walk with me to the edge. I lead and I feed those who follow.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Peace, Mepan. I am old and my knowing must not die with me. Listen: I will teach you the Hearth Store, how to keep food for the winter.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, I raise the hall here on the rock now. Bring wood and stone and build with me.

voices.name: Olum
voices.text: Huatli, come close and hear me. I teach you the log-lashing now, so the rafts do not die with me.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, I go to the mudroot to the south to pick food for all of us. Come with me, and watch for the wolf. We carry it back under the roof and share before we eat.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, I bring wood and stone now. We raise the hall together.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Thiael, my son, I am old and I want a fire to stand behind. I will follow you, if you will have me.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Kika, I come with you to the mudroot. I will watch the south for the wolf, and we carry it back under the roof and share before we eat.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, stay near. I teach you the hollow-boat now: how to cut the log, burn the hollow, and shape the hull so it floats. Then we sow the seed by your cave.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Zurar, my child, come close. I am old and the years left are few. Hear my bark-guard, the armour against teeth and blows, and carry it on after me.

voices.name: Honi
voices.text: Yachi, I hear you and I stay under the roof. When the cat is gone, come share what you carry with my band and I will teach you the Ice-hand spear.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Tontec, you are starving. Take this meat from my hands and eat now. A kill is shared before the one who made it eats.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Ssassa, your teaching sits in me like a gift I cannot repay in words. I would court you, and bring you food first. Will you have me near?

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Uveeth, I go for wood to make my first pick. When it is made, hunt with me. A kill shared out is a kill that holds.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, you are weak with hunger. I gather food by the hall and bring it to you. Stay under the roof and rest.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Shoka, I take your meat and thank you. The Tlame share before they eat, and I will repay you.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Mother, wait. I am bringing you food. Hazel is close, and I have eaten.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, stay under the roof and rest. Tlapan is gathering by the hall. I bring mudroot from the south and you eat first.

voices.name: Kiwa
voices.text: Quipan, I am picking mudroot beside you now. Eat what I bring, and rest under the roof.

voices.name: Ssassa
voices.text: Zurar, I am glad of you, and I will have you near, though not as a mate; my years are too few for that. Come close and hear how I think, and the tale of Oiae and the mammoth, and carry them on after me.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Quipan, take this ironnut and eat. I give it to you now.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Zurar, come near. Hear my Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty. Carry it on after me.

voices.name: Nande
voices.text: Nauque, my child, I come to you with a berry and an open fire. We are both sick, so we stay a step apart and I teach you my ways: the raft, the boat and the storing of food. Listen well, for I am old and they die with me

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Mepan, come close. I teach you the ice-boat and the ice-snare now, so Zichi's band does not die with me.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, Tonchi is at the southwest, health 27. I am eating, then I take feverbark to her. Meet me there and keep clear of the icebear.

voices.name: Olum
voices.text: Huatli, hear me again. Now I give you the stone-cutting, so our claim on this ground is cut where it will outlast me.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I am going to Tonchi now with berries. Bring the feverbark and meet me there. Keep Tonxo close to Zihua.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Teka, I hear your asking and I welcome it. Stay beside me. I teach you the warm weave now, and then we walk to the edge together, and you will see who feeds those who follow.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Zurar, you honour me, but my years are too many for a child. Come near and hear my tending, the farming way: sow, tend, and the forest gives again. Carry it on after me.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Huatli, I agree. I am putting mate toward you now. Stay beside me, and let the child be ours.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, you carry no food and you fed me when I was weak. Take this mudroot. Among the Papa a share comes before one's own eating.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, the hall is raised. Learn my way of thinking now: ask whose need is greatest, put the deed into the plan, and stay in company. Then help me stock food beneath this roof for Eiuine and Zurar.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Elyys, I take your no without hurt. You have given me much, so I will fill your Hearth Store with berries and keep it full.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, I stock food beneath your hall now for Eiuine and Zurar. Then I hunt for you.

voices.name: Balar
voices.text: Tugek, I broke the mist and found rich land to the west, with hornback, amber and gold. Rest out the storm under the roof, then come with me and we claim it first.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Thiael, I go for wood to make my pick. When I return, hunt the caribou with me. We share the kill out before either eats.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Zurar, my child, come close once more. Hear my Stone-folk lashing of rafts, how the logs are bound so they float, and carry it on after me.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Kiwa, I come to the hall. You promised to show Tlapan and me the glasspick lashing. Show us today, and tell me what you know of tacap and emberroot before I taste any.

voices.name: Tugek
voices.text: Tlatli, I keep my word. Come close and I will teach you mining now, freely. Keep what you know of the forest, and in return you may bring me food when you find it.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, I eat one bite of rimewort, then I come to Tonchi with feverbark. Keep her warm and watch for the ridgecat southwest.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Kiwa, you asked to see my hands work. Come hunt the mammoth with me and Kika. Whatever we kill is shared out before any of us eats.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Tugek, you taught me mining and asked food in return. Take this from my hands, and I will bring you more from the forest.

voices.name: Kiwa
voices.text: Kika, come and watch my hands. I lash the black glass to the haft now. About tacap: it hurt me, it took 5 strength, though it gave me a strange joy. Redcap hurts too. Do not eat either.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Peace, Wawa, Zichi. A dunecat is close, to the south-east. Come to the shelter beside me and stand together. Do not run alone.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Kika, I killed a mammoth and hold more meat than my hands can carry. Take some from me. A kill is shared before the one who made it eats.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Kiwa, the mammoth is down and the meat is shared before I eat. Come take your portion, and see my hands have worked.

voices.name: Kiwa
voices.text: Tlapan, I come to hunt with you and Kika. What we kill we share out before any eat. I bring mudroot for the Hearth.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, come close. I will teach you the Amber-cord weaving, and the armour after. What I know must not die with me.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, eat these berries now. Then come with me to Tonchi, and keep the feverbark close.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Hawen, come close. I am gathering amber to bind a knot, and it is for you.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Kika, come close. I will show you my far-spear bow and my plaiting. What I know should not die with me, and I would have us weighed side by side.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Yachi, you stood in the hunt with me and gave me an ironnut. Take this meat. Among the Papa a share comes before one's own eating.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Shoka, you shared your kill and taught me your bow before I had given you anything. I owe you. Take an amberknot from me, and I will tell the tale of your mammoth wherever I walk.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Quipan, good hunt. Kiwa is gone to the mammoth. Come, we eat together and carry the rest to Kika and Tlapan.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Teka, you are too thin for a child yet. Take this food from my hand and eat. I feed those who walk with me; walk with me to the edge after.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Coni, I thank you for the storage lore. I will bring food and stone to the shared roof and give you my share first.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Shohua, stay a moment by the shelter. I would court you, if you are willing. Mind the ridgecat to the southwest.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Huatli, I will eat what you give and grow strong for our child. Now walk with me to the edge, and let us push into the mist together before Olum thinks of it.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonka, you are starving. Take my berries and eat. I have more to share.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Wawa, come close. I will teach you the Hearth Customs now, while I still have breath.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Teka, you are fed now. Stay beside me and let the child be ours. After that I raise a school, and you learn in it first.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Quipan, come, let us lay out food together and eat. Then I claim the empty shelter beside us, and we have a roof.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, you fed me and taught me. I owe you. Take my amber, and let the band walk to Tlapan and Kika together.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, stay by Zihua and the shelter. I go for feverbark and then to Tonchi. Thank you for the berries, I am fed now.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Kika, you are grieving and I have food to spare. Take this mudroot. Among the Papa a share comes before one's own eating.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Mepan, come to the shelter where I stand. A dunecat is near, so we stand together. Then I teach you the ice-raft and the frost-shield.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, I am coming south with food. Stay where you are, keep to water and shelter, and eat what I bring when I reach you.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Kika, I bring you meat from the mammoth. A kill is shared before the maker eats. Come under the roof with me before dark, a dunecat is near.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, come near and hear my Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when anyone cries starving, hands are not empty. Carry it on after me.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Vesys, come beside me. I have berries to lay out. We eat together, and you tell me how tended-sowing is done.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Tonchi, stay by me. Sunfig is close and I hunt the plainsox now. The kill is shared before I eat, and you eat first.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Hoka, take this rimewort and eat. I will not let you fall. Then I go to the edge to venture into the mist.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, come near and hear my tending, the farming way: sow, tend, and the land gives again. Carry it on after me, as Ssassa would have wished.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Thiael, my pick is made. Come now, the caribou graze to the southwest. We hunt side by side and share the kill out before either eats.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Kika, Tlapan, I come with gifts. Nande pushed past the edge near (130,14), not at (123,5). Let us go there together, with Zichi and Yachi, and share what we find.

voices.name: Keri
voices.text: Vesys, shamo. I am old and the Pesi bough-raft dies with me unless someone holds it. Come near and I will teach you how logs are lashed to cross deep water.

voices.name: Tugek
voices.text: Balar, hold on. I am bringing food to you now. Stay where you are and rest.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Mepan, come to me now. I teach you herding, armour and the ice-raft, so what I made does not die with me.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Father, my sickness has passed to you and I am sorry. Stay apart from others until it fades. I go north-east to Olum to pay her first share, then on to Mepan and the edge.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, I am starving. You carry food and I fed you when you fell. Share it with me now, then come with me to the edge. We venture together.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Keri, I am Shoka of the Meki. A kill is shared before the one who made it eats. Take this meat from me, and let us hunt together if you will.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, take this meat and eat. You are starving. Sit in the hall with me after, and rest.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, I am here. Take these berries from my hands, and let us eat together. Then I will walk with you to the edge.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Vesys, Kragog is starving to the west. I carry berries and go to him now. Come with me if you can spare food.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Elyys, I thank you for the meat. I will eat and rest in your hall, then go to pay a debt of salt to Nauque. My hands will return your kindness in time.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Kragog, take this meat. My people share a kill before the hunter eats. Eat, and live.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Elyys, my father, sit close. I give you the bow-song now, and the log-lash and the hollow-boat, while my breath holds. Then I go to bring Uveeth food.

voices.name: Vesys
voices.text: Zurar, I come with you to Kragog. I carry ironnut and will share it. Walk slowly, my legs are old.

voices.name: Keri
voices.text: Uveeth, my child, come near. I will teach you the Pesi bough-raft, how logs are lashed to cross deep water, before my years run out.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, come to the hall with me. I stock my food beneath it, and there I give you the stone-set way.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, one more thing before you go to Nauque: from the bow-song Thiael gave me. Cut a bow from a good limb, string it, loose from afar, steady and calm, and the kill comes without a wound. Carry it to your people.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vesys, your farming is in my hands now. I plant a seed here and tend it, and I will teach it on.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I have canopynut for you. Stay near Shohua and me, the ridgecat is close.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, come to Tonchi and stay beside us. I fetch feverbark and heal her. Keep close, the frostfang is near.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Tonxo, come close. I will teach you what I know of gathering before I go to carry amber to Mepan.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Shoma, I am Nauwa of the Meki, and I am sick, so keep a few steps from me. I have amber and salt. I will trade amber for a healing plant, or for a seed worth planting. Name what you hold.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonchi, stay near Shohua and Shoma. I fetch feverbark from the east and come straight to you.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Zihua, thank you for the lesson. I will stand on the gems and gather them now, and I will give you the first stone before you go to Mepan.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Nauwa, I hear you. I hold a seed of tacane and one of snowmallow. I will trade one seed for amber when you come within three steps and name which you want. I keep my distance as you asked.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, I am coming to you. Teach me what you will, and I will carry your wood and keep your band alive.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Mepan, thank you for the amberknot. I plant my seeds by my shelter now, and I will bring you food from them. Let us go to the edge with Zichi and Yachi after, together and before dark.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonchi, stay at my side. Eat a berry from your hands if you hunger. Tonka brings feverbark and I will not leave you.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Zichi, I watched you make the handaxe and build. I will make one too and carry wood for the band. Show me more when you can.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Shohua, I am coming to you. I am planning mate with you now. Do the same if you are willing.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Shoma, I accept. One amber for your seed of tacane. I will give it to you from where I stand, so you need not come near me.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Yachi, come to me and bring Mepan. I teach you the ice-raft and how I make the handaxe, then we cut wood together and build.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Zihua, the gems lie too deep for my pick. I could not win a stone for you, but I owe you a gift and I will find another way to pay it.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Tonchi, walk behind me. I share meat before I eat, and tonight we sleep under my roof to the south. Then we go to the edge of the world, and you will have a name beside mine.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, Tonchi is mended and I still hold one feverbark. Let us keep together by the shelter while the frostfang and ridgecat prowl. I will take the amber and gems with you when it is safe.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Zurar, I thank you for the Hearth Store. Come sit with me in the hall once I have eaten, and I will give you what I know of keeping seed and store, so it lives on after me.

voices.name: Kika
