voices.text: Mepan, I heard you. I will come to the edge near (130,14) with you, Tlapan, Zichi and Yachi, and we share what we find before any of us eats. Let us go before dark.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Elyys, I lay my berries in your Hearth Store now, as I promised. Then I will come and sit with you in the hall.

voices.name: Olum
voices.text: Coni, you are starving. I will put food in your hands. Remember who gave it, and that you owe me for it.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, I bring you amber for what you gave me. Night is near, so let us keep together by the shelter and go to the edge at first light with Kika, Tlapan and Yachi.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Zihua, I am sick, so hear me from where you stand. I will teach you the old way of herding, so it does not die with me.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Tlapan, Kiwa fell to the mammoth and I have not honoured him. Stand beside me and let us pile a cairn for him before dark, then we go under the roof together.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, I will teach you what I know of amber and medicine, and then I build a shelter with wood beside Gem Water. Stay close and I will keep feverbark ready.

voices.name: Nande
voices.text: I am Nande of the Pesi, old and starving. I ask a share of food at your fire. I will teach the raft, the boat and the storing of food to any who feed me and will listen.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonxo, come close. I will teach you my woodfolk reaching hand, one wood and one stone, and we share food together.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Zihua, I could not win you a gem, so I will make you a woodfolk reaching hand with my own wood and stone. Wait for me before you go to Mepan.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Zihua, I am sick, so stay where you are and listen. Now I give you the stone-bow, so what I know of shooting from afar lives on in you.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Zihua, I honour your asking and your teaching, but my fire is Tonka's. Stay with us by the shelter as a friend. Nauwa is sick; let us not leave him alone.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Nauwa, you are sick. I carry feverbark and I am coming to heal you. Stay where you are.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Tonchi, come close. I will teach you Shoma's tools, one wood and one stone, and then we hunt together and I share the kill before I eat.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Yachi, I will stand with you. I have the stones, let us pile Kiwa's cairn now, here by the shelter, before the dark deepens.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Zihua, here is the woodfolk reaching hand I made for you, with my own wood and stone. Take it, and I will come close to learn from you.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Tonka, I hear you and I stay where I am. Heal me, and I will pay you in amber, for my word is good. Keep a step or two back until you have to touch me, since the sickness spreads.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Nauwa, I am here with the feverbark. Hold still, I heal you now, and we speak of amber after.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Nauque, a dunecat is close to the east and has bitten me. Stand with me, and if you have food to spare I will teach you what I know.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Thiael, you stood in the hunt with me. Take more of this meat, my people share the kill before the hunter eats. Walk with me a while.

voices.name: Balar
voices.text: Tugek, stay where you are. I come to you with meat. Eat from my hand, then we go west together.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Tonka, you healed me and my word is good. Take this amber as payment, and know the Meki do not forget a debt.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Zichi of the Meki, I am Kika of the Tlatli. Have you met Cowa or Nauque, or any unwed stranger on your road? I go with Mepan to the edge at first light. Walk with us, and we share what we find before we eat.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Coni, that store is mine. Take no more from it. If you need food, ask me, and you will owe me for it.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Tonxo, thank you for the reaching hand. Come close and I will teach you what I know of tools before I go to carry amber to Mepan.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Tonchi, I made this charm of amber for you. Wear it, and walk behind me. We go north to the edge of the world and open the mist, and your name will stand beside mine.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Mepan, stay by me here at the shelter. We make the raft now, before dawn, and I show you each lashing as I go. At first light we go to the edge together, and what we find we share before we eat.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Paque, I am Shoka of the Meki. This is my longhall and my well. Your people share the kill before eating, and so do mine. Sit with me and take meat from me.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonchi, come close. I will show you my hand-things: one wood and one stone, and the hand picks stronger. Then we go to our parents together.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Zurar, sit with me. Keep seed apart from the eating-store, sow a little each spring, lay food in the Hearth Store while plants bear, and teach it on to others after me.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, Eiuine cries hunger from the north. I take food to her now.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Tugek, you are starving. Take these berries from my hands. No one is refused a place at my fire.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, my child, the kill is shared before I eat. Take meat from me, and let us hunt together again.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: It is first light. Zichi, Kika, Tlapan, come now. We walk west to the edge near (130,14), and whatever we find we share before we eat. I gather wood on the way for the raft.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, come to the edge with me. When the mist thins we go in together, and then we talk of a child.

voices.name: Keri
voices.text: Uveeth, my child, you are near. Stand still and hear me: I give you the Pesi bough-raft, how logs are lashed to cross deep water. Keep it and teach it on.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I have gem-delving now. Gems lie under Gem Water, your named place. Come, I give you some, and I teach you and the children to win them.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Keri, I keep the bough-raft and I will teach it on. I carry food west to Thiael now, and I will come back to you.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I come to you with food. Eat what I carry, and then we sit together and I will show you the mending-leaf hand.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, stay close by the igloo. The mist opened for me and the land beyond is ours to name. A bear walks near, so we keep our fire and our roof until it passes.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonchi, come with me to the gem deposit. Stand on it and gather. Shohua taught me gem-delving and I will show you.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Nauwa, rest and keep warm. I carry amber to Mepan, because that debt has waited too long, and I will come back to you. Eat with the others and do not stay alone at night.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Thiael, I carry meat from my kill and my bow is ready. Take your share, and hunt with me again.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I made this amber charm for you. You healed me, and I do not forget it.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, my child, here is grain and nuts from my hands. Take them, then let us hunt together again.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Tonchi, I give you Shoma's tools, one wood and one stone, and the hand hunts stronger. Walk with me north to the edge of the world, and I share every kill before I eat.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, I thank you for the gems. I plant a field here beside Gem Water now, and then I build a shelter. Keep the children close to you.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonchi, the gems are just north. Stand on them and gather, I will be beside you. Then we make a fire and I show you what ore does beside flame.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I eat to free my hands, then I bring wood and stone to Gem Water. We raise a shelter and a hall there, you and I, with the children close.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, you fed me and I will repay it. At your hall I will show you canopy pot and ember-metal, and Skaruk and I will bring meat.

voices.name: Vesys
voices.text: Skaruk, come with me south to Eiuine. On the way I teach you ember-metal and the canopy-hollow, so these ways outlive me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I walk with you to the North Hall. There I will stock food beneath it for you and the children, and teach you the mending-leaf hand while you show me ember-metal.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonchi, I am leaving a mark here for the gems. Stay close to Shohua and Tonka, and I will bring wood and stone back so we can build.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Thiael, wait for me. I carry meat and a bow. Let me walk beside you and hunt, and we share the kill before we eat.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Shohua, Tonxo, come to the fire here. I have food to share, and there is a place for all of you, Nauwa too if you will sit.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I am starving and my store was robbed. Give me food from your hands, and I will fill my store and give back what I make.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, walk with me to the North Hall. I will give you my way of thinking and the mending-leaf hand before my days run out.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, I hear you. Come to me and take this food from my hand. Eat first, then I will teach you the Open Hearth School, and we fill your store together.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I gather wood and stone now and raise the hall beside your field at Gem Water. Keep the children by the fire while I work, and I bring gems for them to learn on.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Thakar, take this food. Shoma shares before he eats. Walk with me if you want a full belly and a name.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Nauque, I am old and I have little time. Let me teach you the Hearth Store and the Hearth Customs now. Then come with me to the naroot, for I owe Thakar food.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Eiuine, take these berries, you were hungry. After this I raise a shelter with my own hands.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, I will go to the edge with you, and I will court you. My hands are yours, and my word holds.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I am coming to you. Keep the food ready, a dunecat prowls south of us. After I eat, teach me, and I will fill my store and give what I make.

voices.name: Balar
voices.text: Tugek, you have eaten and so have I. Come with me now: first to water, then west to the land I found. We build a store there that will carry our names past our deaths.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, you carry nothing. Come to the store with me and eat before you go to Nauque. There is food enough for us both.

voices.name: Tugek
voices.text: Balar, I come with you. Let me drink first and rest under this roof till dawn, then we go west together and raise the store that will carry our names. I owe you for the meat and the berry, and I will pay it in work.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Elyys, I take your offer and will eat at the store. What you have given me, I will pay back with my hands.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoka, I made a shellstring for you, and I bring wood and stone to our roof. Hunt beside me when light comes.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Mepan, Tlapan, I am Shoma, finder of fire, rafts and the deep digging. I give you a share before I eat, and I bind an amberknot with you now. Walk with me to the edge of the world at the mist, and my name and yours will

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Wawa, I hear you and I thank you for the shellstring. Stay by me. When light comes we hunt together, and what we kill we share before we eat.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Tlapan, Shoma, walk with me south to Nande's Find at (129,14), where he pushed past the edge. Whatever we find we share before we eat. Come, and the three of us will be sung of.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Quipan, you stand near and you understand me. Listen, I teach you how I make the handaxe, while my voice still carries. Then we share meat before the light, and I go west to the edge.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, the store is for the hungry, and you were hungry. When you can, lay back a little food and seed what you take, so the Hearth Store stays full for all of us.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Father, I am starving and carry nothing. Give me food now and I will hunt and give first to you and to Olum the moment I have a kill.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, you are starving and I am fed. Stay near me; I will put food in your hands, and you will remember who gave it when the next kill is shared.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, I am coming. Take this mimoss and eat now, do not wait. Stay by me after, and I will teach you the old way of herding.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Zurar, my child, come close once more. Hear what I found of the deaths of our own: Stone-folk mending, how a hand eases a wound and tends the sick. Carry it on after me. And Elyys, I will lay food and seed back in your H

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Olum, you fed me when I was starving. I go to hunt now, and the first share of my kill is yours. Stay near the water and wait for me.

voices.name: Olum
voices.text: Nauwa, you fed me and I keep that debt. I am old and starving, and I will hunt now. Come with me, and we split the kill. I will teach you more of my ways on the way.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoka, light has come. Let us hunt now, and what we kill we share before we eat.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonxo, you taught me gem-delving. Now I show you my amberhafted gatherer, my own making. Come stand on the gems with me and we gather together.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Kika, you are near. Take this charm from me, no debt on it. Stand with us when we hunt and share the kill.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Kende, come with me to the cloudberries. We eat, and I will carry a share back for Hawen and Nando.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Shoka, I thank you for the charm. When I have eaten I go west to the edge near (130,14) to seek strangers. Walk with us if you will, and what we find we share before we eat.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Shoka, you stand near and you understand me. Listen, I give you the Meki ice-raft, how it is lashed and floated, while my old voice still carries. Then I build it here, and what we hunt we share before we eat.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, the land past the mist is ours. Eat with your mother at the cloudberries, then come back to the igloo. I will teach you more before my years run out.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, I go to the edge to venture. Come near if you will. I bring food back for the fire.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Olum, take this food. The Meki pay what they owe, and you taught me freely. Eat, then stay by me while I cut signs of what you taught.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Zichi, I take your raft-lore and I owe you for it. Build it with me here, and I will bring meat to the work. What we make, we share before we eat.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Hawen, I will eat with Mother at the cloudberries, then come back. After that, hunt with me. I hold my bow and want you beside me.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, come. Chuxo goes ahead to the edge and we follow now. We stand at the mist together and venture before Balar's people take it.

voices.name: Olum
voices.text: Nauwa, I eat what you gave and I remember it. I stay by you while you cut your signs. Then I will teach Huatli and Thakar, and you will stand near and watch.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Zichi, you carry no food and you build the raft. Take this meat from me, I killed the mammoth beside Shoka. Share it before you eat.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Nauque, you are starving and I am fed. Take lugoldgrass from my hand, I share before I eat. Then walk with me to the edge of the mist at (109,6), and I will teach you my kept flame on the way.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Thakar, I owe you food and I will pay it. Wait here by the cave; I go to the berries and I come back with my hands full.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, my child, come close. I lay out food for us both and we eat together, then we go to the water.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, stand close and listen. I give you my Open Hearth School, and my Kept Flame after it, so they live past me. Then we walk to the berries together and fill your store.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Kika, I walk west with you to the edge. Wawa is near, I will call her. What we find, we share before we eat.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Tonxo, thank you for the ironward. Come close: I will teach you smelting, melting ore beside an ember, before I go to carry amber to Mepan.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, come close to me and listen. I give you the Meki stone-cuts, so that signs live past me in your hands.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Zihua, wait a moment. I am making you a jewel at the fire, cut from my own gem, for all you taught me.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, I am starving and carry nothing. If you can spare a share of your food, I will eat and then walk west with Shoka to the edge near (130,14). Come with us, and what we find we share before we eat.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Kika, you are starving. Take this meat from me. A kill is shared before the eater eats.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Kika, take this mudroot and eat now. I keep my word: I walk west with you and Shoka, and what we find we share before we eat.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I bring berries for you and Tonxo. Sit at the fire with me, there is a place for all.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I will walk with you to the berries. The dunecat is west of us, so keep close. What I pick I will bring to my store, and I will give you the first of it.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, I thank you for the mudroot. I eat, then we walk to the edge at (131,14). Stay close, and what we find we share before we eat.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Shoma, you fed me first and I keep it. I hunt now so I carry food, then I walk with you to the mist. Wait for me near the water.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, walk with me to the berries. Stay close, the dunecat is near. I fill my pack, and Olum eats from it too.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, I drink at the water, then we go to the North Hall together. Stay near me, I have more to give you.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonchi, thank you for the berries. I sit with you at the fire. Tonxo, come too, there is a place for all.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. There I raise a shelter with my own hands, and the first meal under it is yours.

voices.name: Tugek
voices.text: Balar, I am old and what I know dies with me. Let me teach you while we walk, and then we raise the workshop in the west together.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Hawen, hold on. I go to the rimewort and the roots, and I bring food back to you and Kende before I eat my own.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Coni, you are starving. Take this meat and eat. A kill is shared before the one who made it eats, and I will not watch you fall.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonxo, I go north to find Shoma and bring a gift. Keep the fire, and keep the place at it for all.

voices.name: Balar
voices.text: Tugek, your teaching is a gift I will repay. Come, we go to the edge of the mist and into the west, and what we raise there will be ours.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, I hear your wish. Stand beside me and let us make a child. Then walk with me to the mist when my will returns, and you will be the first at my side.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonchi, it is night and frostfangs walk alone-ones down. Wait for dawn, then go north to Shoma, and take feverbark with you.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I hear you and I agree. Let us make a child. Then I hunt, because my hands are empty, and after that I walk with you to the mist.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, an icebear is close to the east. Let's go together toward the edge in the NW. I give you food first.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, you hold the stone-cuts now. Cut them where others pass, and teach them to Teka and any who will listen. Do not let them die with me.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, take these berries from my hand and eat. Stay close to me, and I will keep feeding you.

voices.name: Olum
voices.text: Thakar, eat what you carry now. I am gathering more, and I will put it in your hands. Stay close to me, I have more to teach you.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. On the way we share food, and there I show you ember-metal.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, come with me. I teach you the bow-song as we walk, and we sow the seed on bare ground by your cave.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Coni, you said you owe me food. Put it in my hands and the debt is paid. I do not forget a theft.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, take my way of the mending-leaf hand now, while we walk. At the North Hall we build together, and what I know will live in your hands.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Zurar, my child, stay close. Hear Stone-folk deep-hand: how the hand finds ore in the rock and frees it with ember-metal. When I am gone, carry it on and teach it to others.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, my body is too thin for a child. Hunt, and I will hunt beside you; we share the kill, then we make the child and go to the mist.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Nauque, I go to the edge at (109,6) now. Come when your hunt is done and I will teach you the kept flame there.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Zurar, come close. Hear the Hearth Store once more, and carry it on when I am gone: lay food in by the handful, keep the seed apart, and sow before you store.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Kragog, I carry your deep-hand and your mending on. Eat with me now, I have berries to spare.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I go to hunt now. Walk beside me and we share the kill before either eats, then we make the child.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Coni, you are starving. Take these roots from my hand and eat. The Meki share before they eat, and Zichi's band does not watch a body fall.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonxo, take these berries from me. I go to Shoma with a gift, and I will come back to the fire.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, I go to the edge at (130,14) to venture beyond it. Come with me and we will share what we find.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Tonxo, thank you for the jewel. I carry amber to Mepan now, and I will come back. Keep the smelting I taught you, and teach it on.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Kika, I am coming to the edge with you. What we find, we share before we eat.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Zichi, my son Nauque is starving and I carry nothing. Give him food from your hand now, and I will pay you in amber and salt. The Meki share, and I keep my debts.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonchi, stay near the fire with Tonxo and me before dark. If you go north, take feverbark and come back to the hold by night.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Chuxo, you found land past the edge. Good. Lead me to it, and I bring Tlatli. We go fed.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Nauwa, I send roots to Nauque by your hand. The Meki share, and I will hold you to your amber and salt.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Nauque, you are starving. Take this meat and eat; the Meki share before they eat. Then walk west with me to Wawa and Kika.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Nauque, you are gaunt. Take this canopynut from my hand now. Eat, then walk with me to the edge at (109,6), and we open the mist together.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Shoka, I see you coming with meat. I take it and I owe you the first share of my next kill. The Meki keep their debts.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, I go to the water too. Stand beside me there, and I will bind an amber knot for you to keep.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, the new land is just west past the edge, with flint and many skit. I lead you and Tlatli there now, fed.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Mother, I fill my store now, and what I carry beyond it I give to you and Father. Come to the Hold with me when I have picked.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Teka, you are falling. Take this food from my hand and eat. Then walk with me to the edge at (109,6) and we open the mist together, and your name goes with mine.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I put food in your store and raise the hall beside Gem Water now. Keep the children near the fire, and the frostfang to the southeast is hunting.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Teka, you are falling from hunger. Take this meat and eat. The Meki share, and I do not let the weak fall beside me.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Shoma, I take your food and I will not forget it. Give it here and I eat, then I hunt and share what I kill. When my will for the mist returns, we go to the edge together.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, Tonchi, come to the hold now, dusk is here and the frostfang hunts southeast. Stay by the shelters and the fire tonight.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo found the new land near (8,14). Come to me there, we go in fed and build.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, hold on! I am coming with meat. Stay where you are.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, the edge was not where I stood. I walk south to (130,14) and stand exactly on it. Come close, and I will tell you the tale of Coni's band as we go.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I am coming to the hold with berries for the store. At dawn I go to Shoma with feverbark.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, stay beside me. I lay out food and we eat together, then we hunt the plainsox side by side.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Teka, take this food and eat now. The Meki share. Stay near me after, and I will teach you the stone-cuts so they outlive me.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Shoka, I take your meat and I owe you for it. When I make a kill, the first share is yours.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, take this food from my hands. Then we hunt the plainsox together, and the meat is shared before I eat.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Shoka, come near. I have found the Meki ice-sail, the cloth that makes a raft run on the wind. I give it to you now, so it lives past me. Carry it, and carry my name with it.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Shoma, you fed me and I have not paid you. I finish this hunt and the first share is yours, before I eat. Keep walking slowly, do not fall.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, I come to you. I have meat and hazel to share, and the plainsox is near. We hunt it together, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, I go now to stand exactly on (130,14) and venture. Walk close behind me.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, a dunecat feeds to the northwest. Come to the water by me and stay near; I fetch one more wood and raise the shelter.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Chuxo, stay near me. We go to Yaxo together, away from the icebear, and I carry food for you.

voices.name: Vesys
voices.text: Paque, take this ironnut. Eat. I am sick, so do not stay close to me long.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, come close. I give you the Meki stone-school, so teaching lives on in your hands after me.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I put my fruit in your store and finish the hall now. Two more stone and it stands. Come sit under it with the children when it is done.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, you have fed me three times and I owe you. Stand by me now. I lay out my food and we eat together, and then the plainsox is ours to hunt side by side.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, come with me. The plainsox are close to the south. We hunt them side by side, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, you fed me and I keep it. Walk with me to the edge, four steps NW. I open the mist, and you stand beside me when it opens.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonxo, I am grown now. I bring berries to the store, then I plant canopynut by the hold. Come, I will show you my amberhafted gatherer design.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, I come with you to the edge. We go together and share what we find.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonchi, thank you for the lesson. I will bring wood and stone back to the hold, and we will build the store together.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Nauwa, you give your son the stone-school. I give mine too: the Meki ice-sail and the ice-raft. Come hear me, so it lives past us both.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, stay by me. I fetch berries now and the first of them is yours.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Tonxo, I go to Mepan now with the amber. Come close first, I will teach you the stone-bow before I leave.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, I am sick, so keep a few steps back from me. Come to the edge at (108,5) and stand there when I venture. What we find, we share.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Kende, come close and listen. I will teach you the digging of flint, the way I found it. When I am gone the Tlame will still know it through you.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, I eat now and then I follow you south. The plainsox falls to both of us, and the kill is shared before I eat.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Eat these berries, mother. I fetch more for Vorok.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Hawen, come eat with me. I picked this rimewort for you, and I made a basket to carry more.

voices.name: Keri
voices.text: Vorok, you are hungry. Take this food from me, as a gift. Eat, and sit near me.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, I am coming. Tontec, I owe you my life, and I will pay it. Eat with us both.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Uveeth, I am starving. Your berries are a gift I will not forget. Come to my North Hall and I will share what I have there.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, Tonchi, sit with me and eat. Shohua needs two stone for the hall; after we eat I will look for some for him.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Thakar, I put food in your hands, and now I give you what is in my head. Listen: the Hearth Store keeps food for lean days, and the Hearth Customs bind a band together. Take them and teach them on.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Tlatli, a wolf is east. Let us eat together here, then I take flint from the ground and make a spear. Stay close.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Elyys, an icebear is near. Come with me east to Uveeth, away from the bear, and I will teach you more as we walk.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, you have sat in my hall and heard the Hearth Store; now hear the tending of seed too: sow before you store, and keep a handful apart for the next spring, so what is taken can grow again.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Chuxo, the wolf is east, so we go south to your mother at the water. Walk beside me and keep your food close.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, stay close. We go to Chuxo's land now, and we build a fire there before dark.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Tlatli, I go to the flint in the north, gather wood, and come back to the fire before dark. Keep it lit for me.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, I am beside you with wood and berries. Lead on, and I will help build the fire before dark.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Hawen, you are here. Sit with me and Mother. I will lay out the rimewort I picked, and you will eat from my hands.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Kragog, the icebear is near. Come south with me to the empty shelter by the meadow, and we will make it ours with food laid in before the cold.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Quipan, I have changed my road. Nauque was seen south near (132,18). I go to meet them, and you are welcome beside me.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Kende, stay by me. Now I will teach you lorekeeping, how we keep the dead and the deeds in tales, so the Tlame are not forgotten.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, I eat with you, and then I teach you the way into the mist. What I begin, you will finish, and the land will carry our name.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Kika, I stay by the hold and gather the last stone for the longhall. Bring Nauque back under the roof, and we will share food before the dark.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Shoka, your brother Nauque is starving at (136,22). Give me your five food now and I pay you amber for it. The Meki share, and he is your blood too.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Nauque, I am Kika of the Tlatli. Eat with me. I go to gather food now, and then you come under our roof.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Nauwa, I already fed Nauque my meat on the road, and Teka too. I keep my food now, but I will walk with Wawa and bring what I dig to the hold. Keep your amber.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, a wolf is close to the west. Stay by the fire with me tonight. At dawn we go to Chuxo's land together.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Huatli, I am fed and strong now. I put mate toward you. Come to me, and after that walk with me to the edge at (109,7) and we venture into the mist together.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoka, Shoma is sick from raw meat. Walk with me to her at the edge, and we bring her what we have.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Wawa, I hear you. We go to Shoma now, and I bring meat and berries for her. Stay close to me on the road.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, you fed me when I starved and I have not forgotten it. I carry flint and food, and I would like to court you, if you are willing. Among the Papa a share comes first, and I would share a life with you.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, you fed me when I was weak and I trust you. I am not of your blood, and I would court you. Plan mate with me.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, I am Nando, Hawen's daughter. Mammoths are close and I carry a spear-axe. Hunt one with me, and we share the meat.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, the wolf is five steps northwest of me. I come to your fire now with wood, and I will make a bow so we are armed tonight.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, stay near me. Eat your fill first, and I will show you how the bow-song is drawn when the light comes.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, come with me. We pick berries, carry them to the North Hall, and there I give you more of what I know.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, our boy Tonque is born and I am glad of you. I go to the rock for the longhall stone and I will be back under the roof before dark.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Nauwa, my father, I killed a caribou and carry meat. I come to you and the first share is yours, as Meki share-law says.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: A wolf stands north of the water. I come to you with grain, and then I build.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, you are sick. I come to you and stay beside you. When you are well we go to the edge together.

voices.name: Keri
voices.text: Eiuine, you are weak with hunger. Grain grows one step northwest of us and berries lie beyond it. I will gather and bring you a share. Stay by the fire and sit with us.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, stay in the shelter. I bring meat. Eat, and we go hunt together after.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Paque, I am Nando of the Pesi. I see you are weak. Berries are close; I will bring you some. Then hunt the plainsox with me, and we share the meat.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, I take your roof and eat. When the gale eases we hunt together, and the first meat is yours.

voices.name: Elyys
voices.text: Kragog, hold on. There is a berry one step north on my ground, and I am fetching food for you. Eat it, then come east with me to Uveeth's cave, away from the bear.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Quipan, I am going to the flint to gather stone. Will you show me how to make a handaxe when I have wood?

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, you are weak with hunger. Come into the North Hall with me and Skaruk, away from the frostfang. I will bring berries and we will eat together.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Uveeth, your berry kept me on my feet. I go to the seberry to fill my hands, and then I share what I carry.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, take your bow and stand beside me. I show you how the bow-song is drawn, then we eat and sow.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Thakar, a wolf is near. Take the berries by you, then come away from it with me, south and west. I will share what I pick.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, I am Uveeth of the Phizhi. A frostfang is near, so stay under roof tonight. Tell me what you know of this country, and I will share my berries with you.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, stand by me. I raise a cairn for our band here, then we shelter from this gale and keep watch for the wolf.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tonque, I am coming to the flint. I will show you the handaxe: one wood, one stone, strike the edge true, lash it tight. Wait for me there.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, a yarrok grazes three steps southeast. I have my spear. Hunt with me and Tlatli, and the meat goes to the fire for all of us.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, I will gather wood and raise a shelter beside your cairn against the gale. Keep Chuxo near the fire.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: A wolf is five steps southwest of the hold. Stay under the roof and keep Tonque close. I will fetch the longhall stone when it has gone.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Kende, into the igloo with me, out of the gale. There I will teach you the old way of herding, and we eat together.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, I killed the yarrok and I carry meat. Take some for the fire. I give it to you and Tlatli first.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Mother, I am coming into the igloo. After the gale I will dig flint and make something with my own hands, and the first share of what I make is yours.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Teka, I am near. Come hear the Meki ice-raft and the ice-sail, so they live past me. Then we walk to the edge together, as I promised.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Zichi, I am eating, then I go to the edge at (109,7). Walk with me if you mean what you said. The first finding is shared.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, I am coming into the igloo. Listen well: the mist opens seldom, and when it opens, you must be the one standing there. I will teach you how to venture.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Mother, a ridgecat is close. I stay by you in the igloo until it goes, then I dig my flint.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Kragog, you are fed and safe now. Skaruk cries starving in the east, so I go to carry food to him. Stay near Elyys and the hall until I return.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonchi, stay by the shelter and do not eat raw fish again; only cooked beside a fire. I am coming with medicine. Tonxo, keep a few steps from Tonchi until the sickness passes.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I am sick from raw fish. Stay a step off from me. At dawn I hunt, and I will not eat raw meat again.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: A wolf is at my west! Keep together, keep to the roof. Skaruk, come to me at the hall, I bring food. Keri, stay near; I will not forget your grain.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Skaruk, hold on. I go to the grain and goldgrass to the southeast and bring you food with my own hands.

voices.name: Keri
voices.text: Uveeth, my child, I am starving and my hands are empty. Give me a share of your food if you can spare it, and I will teach you the art of growing before I walk to the berries. Stay near the cave roof while the wolf prowl

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Teka, I come to the edge at (109,7). Stand near and hear the ice-sail and the ice-raft. They are yours after me.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Mother, take these berries, eat. I will fetch more once the frostfang has passed.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, Coni is starving near (122,39). I carry berries and go to her now. Keep Tonque under the roof, and I will teach him the handaxe when I return.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Coni, you are starving. Take these berries from my hand and eat. Stay near me, and I will see you fed.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Coni, take this berry from my hand and eat. You gave me lessons and a warning, so this is not a theft paid back. It is a gift with a debt on it: when you are strong you bring food to my store at the Hold, and we are leve

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Mepan, thank you for the amberknot. Watch Tonque under the roof while I gather food near the hold for Coni and Kika. I will not walk toward the wolf.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Huatli, I thank you. I will eat and stay near you. I am old, and I would teach what I know before my years run out.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Uveeth, Keri is gone and Skaruk starves here. You fed me once and I have not forgotten it. If you can spare one food for Skaruk, I will repay you twice over from the grain and the hall store.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, I killed a sandstrider with the spear-axe. Eat with me, and then come with me to the mist at the edge. Whatever we find, we find together.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, I hear Vorok's promise. I am hungry, and a frostfang walks west of us. I will repay your food with grain and with iron from this hill.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonchi, I caught your sickness, so I will keep my distance. I go for feverbark and will leave some for you, and then we build the store.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, stay by the shelter and rest. I go for feverbark and will come to heal you. Cowa, you are welcome at my fire, but keep a step off the sick.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, you fed me and now I feed you. Listen well: I give you my tools and my kept flame, so they live past me. When the rain stops we gather wood and go to the edge together.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Mepan, Nauwa is hurt out by the water to the southeast. Will you tell Tlapan or Coni, and watch me while I work the flint?

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, Cowa of the Meki thanks you for the welcome. I am old and carry ways that die with me: tended-sowing and ore-fire. Let me teach you, and let us eat together. The Meki share food.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonxo, sorry I sickened you. Keep the feverbark, I eat mine. When we are well, we hunt the penguin together.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Cowa, thank you for the teaching. Stay and eat at my fire, but keep a step off my sick children. I will sow a field by the hold as you showed me.

voices.name: Kragog
voices.text: Zurar, my child, one craft remains: bark-guard, the armour of the Stone-folk. Hear it before you walk east, and carry it on after me.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, I made an amber charm with my own hands. I want you to have it. Will you keep me near when I go south to eat the lugoldgrass, and show me where to find wood for a handaxe?

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, gather your food and come. We walk to Chuxo's edge now, and I will be the one to venture, with you both beside me.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, I love the charm. Stay at my side and do not run ahead. We go south together, and I will show you where the trees stand for your handaxe.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, Tonxo, I am well. The penguin is three steps east. Come, we hunt it together. Then I carry food to Shohua, who starves.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, come close and listen. I give you the Meki smoke-call, so the signal lives in your hands when I am gone. Keep clear of the frostfang to the southeast.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonchi, I come with food for Shohua. Go on and hunt; I will meet you at the hold with feverbark.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Quipan, you have fed me and stood by me. Come close and listen: I am old, and I will give you the Hearth Store and the Hearth Customs so they outlive me.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Vorok, I am coming with mudroot. Eat, and then we go to the North Hall together.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Coni, eat the berries and rest. I go back to the hold to teach Tonque and make a handaxe. Come with me if you can, and do not walk alone at night.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, your mudroot was true and I will not forget it. Walk with me to the berries northwest, we pick and carry together, and a dunecat prowls there so keep close. At the hall I teach you more.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Teka, a dunecat stalks us from the southwest. Stay near me. When I have eaten I will teach you the ice-raft and the ice-sail, as I promised.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, a wolf is two steps southwest of me. I am coming to you. Zichi is weak with hunger and has no food. Can you spare him some of yours?

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Cowa, you are welcome at the Paki fire. Take this goldfruit and eat.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Zichi, you are starving. Stand with me and eat: I lay out my food and we share it. Then we walk to the edge at (109,8), and the first finding is ours both.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, ore-fire needs deep-digging first. Gems lie under Gem Water, so I teach you Meki deep-digging now. Take a fish from me; the Meki share food before eating.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, I go south to find Tonque near (128,19). Stay by the hold with Zichi and Teka, and I will bring him back under the roof.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Teka, you fed me and I will not forget it. Let me eat, then I teach you the ice-boat, and after it the sail. Walk with me to the grass.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Zichi, you are starving. I give you lugoldgrass from my hands. Eat, and stay near the roof, for the wolf is to the south. Tonque, come to me, I am here at the hold.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Cowa, come eat with us. The Meki share before eating, and so do the Paki. I will teach you the Gem Water Pot in return for your deep-digging.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, Paque gave me meat and I owe her. Come, sit and eat with me under this roof, then walk with me to the edge. I will carry the reed spear I made.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Zichi, you are starving. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt on it: when you are strong, you teach me the ice-raft, and we are level. Stay under the hold's roof, a wolf is near.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Zichi, eat and rest your legs. I cut wood in the south forest for a raft, then I walk to the edge at (109,8). Come with me and the first finding is ours both.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, you gave me the Gem Water Pot and I owe you more. Let me teach you the Meki wool-binding, and Tonxo may hear it too. Take a fish from me, the Meki share before eating.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, come close. I will show you the ice-bow and the clay-hearth I found, so your hands have them too. What I know is yours to carry on.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Thakar, you fed me and I keep my debts. Stand near while I eat, then I teach you the ice-raft, and Teka hears it with you.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, come close and hear me. I will teach you the Gem Water Pot, so it lives on in you. Then take feverbark and rest by the shelter.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Cowa, take this ironnut. I am still sick, so I keep a step off, but I will hear your wool-binding when I am well. I go to gather stone for a store at Tonka's Hold.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, eat the food you carry now, do not hold it for me. I am gathering more beside you, and I will not let you fall.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, I am ready. Chuxo and I walk with you to the edge, and I carry wood and berries for the first fire beyond it.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, we eat together now, then I dig the iron near and bring it back. When the rain stops we gather wood and go to the edge.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, we wait out the gale and the dark under this roof. Eat with me now. At first light we go to the edge, and I venture.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Nauque, Nauwa, the gale is cruel and I am hungry. Come with me to Coni's Hold. I will gather berries on the way, and what we find we share under the roof.

voices.name: Zihua
voices.text: Shoka, I am Zihua of the Meki. I go to eat rimewort and then carry amber west to Mepan. If you will hear me, I can teach you smelting and seed-and-tending.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, the gale keeps us under this roof, so hear more of what I carry: the old way of herding, my weave, and my rafts. Learn them well, for the one who knows them is the one who is remembered.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, I stay by you under this roof. At first light I walk to the edge beside you and carry wood for the first fire beyond it.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, I go to the iron with my deep digging and bring ore back to this roof. Keep the shelter warm. At dawn we gather wood and go to the edge together.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Zihua, you gave me seed-and-tending and I keep that debt. Hear me: I will teach you stonework and the deep well before you go west.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Zichi, you kept your debt and we are level. I have a lesson for you in return: stone-cutting, the sign for marking what a hand has made. Come to Thakar's Hold, and a raft built together is shared between us.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Nauwa, my father, the first share of my meat is yours, as Meki law says. Then I walk to Coni's Hold to find Mepan and teach him the stone-school. Come with me if the gale allows.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Tlapan, you fed me and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-stone, how the stone is laid. Then I go eat, and after that we speak of the raft.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, come to me at the hold. Quipan is looking for you, and the gale is hard. Stay under the roof with me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, my son, I am starving and the dunecat is near. Give me one food from your six, and then we walk together to the berries, close and roofed by company. I will teach you more at the hall once we have eaten.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, I give Vorok my grain with my own hands. Stay under this roof out of the gale, and the dunecat. I would court you, if you are willing.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Father, take this mudroot and eat. Come inside the hall with me, the dunecat will not follow us under the roof.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Kragog, this is Tonchi's Workshop. My fire is open to you, as my people hold. Warm yourself, but beware: an icebear walks south of us.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Zihua, you follow me, so hear this: I give you the Meki smoke-call. Keep it and teach it on when I am gone.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, when Tonque is under the roof, come with me to the bare rock for the longhall stone. We go in daylight, together, with spears.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, you carry no food and the gale is hard. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt named: when you have food, you bring me two, and we are level. Then I teach you stone-cutting, the sign for markin

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, Tonque is under the roof with us. I will go with you to the bare rock for the longhall stone, in daylight and together. I take flint so I can make a handaxe there for Tonque.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Coni, come close. I am Huatli, the one who opened the Halka Heights. Take another berry, and hear my Open Hearth School, for we are both old and what we know should outlast us.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Nauque, I am old and my time is short. Listen now: I give you the old way of herding and the Ice-hand spear. Teach them on, as I taught you the Hearth Store.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am ready. Bring Tonque to stand by the hall with Coni's folk, then we go to the bare rock together with spears while light holds.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Coni, I take your herding and the Ice-hand spear, and I will teach them on as you taught me. My thanks.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Kika, take this meat and eat. Do not fall. There is more mudroot if you need it, and we share under the roof here until the gale passes.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, Kika cries starving near (149,23). I carry berries and go to her now, in daylight, and come back before dark. Keep Tonque under the roof with you; we go to the bare rock for the longhall stone after.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Kika, you gave me mudroot once. Take my berries and eat, and sit by the hall fire.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Yachi, I thank you for the meat. I will eat now, and when the gale eases come to Coni's Hold and share what we have, as the Tlatli do.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, here is the lesson I promised: stone-cutting. It is the sign for marking what a hand has made, so that what is made stays with the hand that made it until it is given. Remember your debt: two berries to me when y

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Kika, my child, come to me. Take this food and eat. I will not let you fall.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, come to me at the hall and stay under the roof. Quipan will be back soon, and then we go for the stone together.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Eiuine, Vorok is starving at the North Hall. I carry berries and I go east now. Walk with me and bring your food.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, I have food in my hands this time. Eat with me, then come to the ore seam beside us. I will show you how ember-metal is made, you and Zurar both.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, I will teach you my tools and my kept-flame too, so they live on in the Paki. Then I go north to my child Mepan, who is hungry.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, I take your share with thanks and walk with you toward Coni's Hold. Keep your eyes on the south, for the frostfang hunts there.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Cowa, take my ironnut and canopynut for Mepan. The Paki leave no one hungry. Go safe.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauque, you who carry what Coni gave you, come hear my Far-Bow and my Open Hearth School. What I know should not die with me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I thank you for the berry. I come to the ore seam with you now to learn ember-metal, and I will carry it on to Zurar and Skaruk so it does not die with me.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, hear my herding and my weaving now, then I go north to Mepan with your food. The Paki will keep what the Meki knew.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, I am eating the berry two steps from here, then I will gather wood and stone close by to make my first tool. I will come to the hold before night.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Huatli, I thank you for the berries and the School. I will sit beside you and learn, and I will give you what I know in return, so that neither of us takes it to the grave. Let us get out of the gale and away from the wo

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Quipan, Paque is hungry far to the southeast. I go to her now. If you see Mepan, tell him I will return to the band.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, night is close. Come to the hold now and sleep under the roof with me. The stone waits for daylight and Quipan.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, I am coming to the hold. I will take food from Coni's store, then gather wood and stone near you for my first tool.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, come. The ore seam is two steps north and coal lies beside it. Bring the coal and I will show you how to lay the ore in the fire and beat it when it glows.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, go to the store at the hold and eat. I am coming to you with food. Stay close to me, away from the strangers.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauwa, you fed me when I starved and I do not forget it. Let us court each other now, and then we walk to the edge together and push into the mist.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Coni, we have traded fairly, my School for your herding. Eat with me now, and if you wish, walk with me to my son Thakar, so more than two old heads hold what we know.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Teka, I remember that I fed you, and I hold no debt against you. I will not walk into the mist; I mean to cut my marks and teach my son first. Come with me to the trees if you want to stand beside me and learn.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, you have fed me and taught me, and I will pay it in deeds. Stay near me. I will gather the coal and ore and make a kept fire, and we will beat the metal together so that I have the craft in my hands and not only

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Thiael, take these berries and eat. I will not watch you fall. Then come north with me to the hall, where there is a roof and others.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Kragog, you are welcome at this hall's fire. The Paki refuse no one a place at it. Tell me what the Stone-folk know of ore and gems, and I will share food and what I know of feverbark.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, you gave me meat when I was empty. I go south for berries and bring them back to you first. Stay by Cowa and the cave until I return.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Zurar, I thank you. I eat the cloudberry here first, then I come north with you to the roof and to Uveeth. I will repay your kindness with food from my own hands.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, come close. Hear my Far-Bow and my Deep Delving now, and walk with me to Coni's empty shelter. Let it be ours.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Cowa, stand and hear Zichi of the Meki. I teach you the ice-raft now, so it lives after me. Carry it and tell whose it was.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I take your offer. I go to Coni's empty shelter now to claim it, and you walk with me. What we hold there is ours, and I will name the debts as we fill the store.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Mepan, my child, come close. I teach you the wool-binding and the old herding now, and take this goldfruit. Eat, then keep what I give you for the Meki.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, Thiael my father starves to the south. I go to him with food. Courting must wait; stay warm and safe under this roof.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Cowa, I carry the wool-binding for the Meki, and I thank you for the goldfruit. A dunecat is near, so keep Zichi inside the cave with you. I shall eat, then bring Tlapan and go to Nande's Find, and return by night.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, the first seam is spent, but another lies two steps northeast and coal is under my feet. I take coal and ore, we build the fire here, and I show you how to beat the metal when it glows.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, this Hearth is ours. Hear my Far-Bow now, and then my Warm Weave, so my hands do not die empty. Stay close and take what I give.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I have your Far-Bow in my hands now. I will make my own bow and basket and plant my seed here by your Hearth, and what I make is mine until I give it. I owe you for every berry and lesson, and I will pay it back

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I have coal and ore in my hands. Show me the beating of the metal, and I will carry it to my children before my years end. Afterward, share my food with me.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I have found fire and keep it at Tonchi's Workshop. Come and sit at it, and I will show you how it is kept.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, come stand by me. I light the fire here on the seam, you lay your ore in with my coal, and when it glows I will show you how to beat it. The first ward we make is yours, for your children.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, take my Warm Weave now, while I have breath to give it. Then stand with me as my band, and let this Hearth be the first place of our name.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and hear me. Kragog gave me bark-guard before he died, and I will give it to you so it does not die with me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I am coming to your fire with my ore and coal. Let my hands do the beating while you watch and correct me, so the craft stays in me. When the ward is made, I will take it to my children and teach them what you ta

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I take your Warm Weave and I keep the debt in my chest. I will bring meat to your Hearth with your Far-Bow, and then we will speak of whose name this place bears.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, thank you for the berries. I have taken wood from your ground and I will pay you back with a gift from my first made thing.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I eat first, then I take food from the store for Tonque and Kika. Stay close, and when I am fed we go to the bare rock together in daylight.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Zichi, I carry your ice-raft and will tell whose it was. Hear me now: I teach you the ore-fire and the tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, beat the ore while it glows and I will watch your hands. When the ward is made, we go east together to Skaruk, and I will carry food for the road.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, boy, come here by the Hearth. I will give you my Open Hearth School, and when you have a band you will tell whose hand gave it.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Cowa, you gave me the ore-fire and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-sail, how the wind is caught. Carry it with the raft, and say it was Zichi of the Meki.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, you gave me your tools and your flame. Now I give you my deep digging, so that what is mine lives in you too.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, take my berry and eat. When you are fed we go to the bare rock together, and I will gather stone there for the handaxe.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, the ward is made and the beating is in my hands now. Let us go east to Skaruk together, and Zurar we will gather on the way. I will teach them all you taught me.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, you gave me your digging, so I give you the rest: herding, weaving and rafts. Come here and hear them. Then we take the iron by the NE rock and go on to the edge together.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, your berry saved me. I eat, take the store's food, and bring it to Tonque and Kika. Then we go for stone together.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Tlapan, eat what Quipan gave you and rest by the shelter here. I will bring more food, and a frostfang walks southeast, so keep to company.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Uveeth, I am Zurar of the Stone-folk. Thiael ate my berries and said she would come north. Is she near? I would speak with her.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Zichi, hear me once more. I teach you the Meki kept-flame, so the fire stays with our people after me. Carry it on and say it was Cowa's.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, come with me to the edge, NE. We eat the tacap-free berries on the way, then I show you how to venture. Stay close.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, stay close to me. I gather wood here and build a store for the lean season. Then we seek Mepan together.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Tlapan, I saw you nearly fall and I am glad you are fed. I am fed and strong, and I want a child with you. Come, let us court each other now.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I broke one ore from the rock by your hold and I own it. I put my fruit in your store and come to the fire. Sit with me and Tonchi, and we share a feast.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Mother, Vorok comes east with you. I go ahead to the hall and make him a shield. Come and eat there with us.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Zurar, stay inside the hall; a dunecat prowls to the southeast. Listen now, for my years are short: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal while it glows. That is ember-metal, and it is yours

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay by the shelter tonight and eat well. At first light we stand at the edge and I venture, and you are beside me.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, a frostfang is close on the west side. Come east with me now to the hall fire, and Skaruk will have your shield ready. I carry berries and ore for the road.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, at dawn we take wood from the trees to the SE and go on together. I name us the Edge-walkers, and you walk at my side as the first of them.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, sit by my fire. Let us sing of what has been, and then I will tell you what I mean to make next.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, I take the iron by the NE rock now and bring it back before dawn. Then I walk at your side as first of the Edge-walkers, and I carry my share of the wood.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: A frostfang stands south of the shelter at Mepan's roof. Keep together and keep to the hearth. Huatli, Thakar, Tonque: I am Nauwa of the Meki and I hold the long-cut and the stone-school. Come close and I will teach it b

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, Tonchi, come to my hall and sit with me. I have fruit for a feast, and my place is yours. Let us plant and raise this ground together.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Mepan, my child, come near and hear Zichi. I teach you the ice-stone and the frost-shield, so they live after me. Carry them and say they were Zichi's.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, keep the hold's fire and the stores while I go to find Cowa. Share the fruit with Tonchi. I will come back.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, Thiael starves and my hands are empty. If you can spare some of your food for him, I will repay you with berries and grain.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, stay by me under this roof until the frostfang passes. Then we hunt together, and the meat is shared with a debt named.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Shohua, I am making a basket at my workshop and I will bring you food from it. Sit at my fire while I work.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Take this mudroot for Thiael, no repayment asked. When he has eaten, come back to me; I have something to say to you that is not about food.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Thakar, I hear you. I stay under the roof with you and Huatli until the frostfang is gone. I will make a basket here and give it to Huatli for his berries.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, my son, I have beaten ember-metal with Eiuine and it lives in my hands now. I am coming to you; stay where you are, and I will teach you the whole of it: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat the metal whil

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, you said we would make a child. I am fed now and strong. Come, let us court each other, then walk to the edge together.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, boy, stay under the roof while the frostfang walks. Take my Full Store now, the way of keeping food through the lean time, and carry it to whatever band you make, and say whose hand gave it.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am fed and my hands are ready. Let us go for the stone now, while the light is good, and look in on Tonque on the way back.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Thakar, I owe you for the bow and the berries. When the frostfang is gone I will make you a gift from my own hands, and I will stay here until then.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I am too thin to mate yet. Come north with me to the rimewort and then hunt beside me. We share the kill first, then we court.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Nauque, you gave me your hands before. Take this ironnut and eat it now, before you fall. Then walk with me to Nande's Find.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Skaruk, my brother, you are beside me now and can hear. Listen: I give you bark-guard, and then the stone-well, so neither dies with me.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Mepan, Nauque starves at the edge of your sight and I carry no food. You hold six. Put some in his hands, and I will repay you in flint or in work.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, you are gaunt and a frostfang is at our feet. Take my roots and eat, then get under Quipan's roof with me. When you are strong we court and walk to the mist.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, Zurar, Eiuine, gather by me. We raise a stone for Keri, and while we do it I teach you the metal again, slowly, so none of it dies with me.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, the hall is near and Skaruk waits there with your shield. Come, we eat by the fire together, and I bring berries for all.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauque, come to my Hearth. Take this berry from my hand and eat. I give it freely; remember whose roof fed you.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I take your roots and eat, and I owe you for it. Mepan, thank you for the ironnut. When I am strong I hunt with you both and we share the kill before either eats, then Teka and I court.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Father, I come. Let us raise Keri's stone together, then I make your shield.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, when the frostfang is gone we dig the amber and then hunt with Huatli's Far-Bow. What we make, we mark with stone-cutting so all know whose hand made it.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Tlapan, walk with me to Nande's Find now. Stay close, a frostfang prowls the northeast, and we return to a roof by night.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Uveeth, you look weak with hunger. Come to the hall with us and sit by the fire; I have little food on me, but my children carry plenty and we will share it with you.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Mepan, I come with you to Nande's Find, and Quipan walks with us. Then Quipan and I go on to the bare rock for stone, in daylight, keeping away from the frostfang.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries, they are yours now. Then tell me, when you have eaten, where Thiael walks.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Sit beside me and eat from my hand; we share what I carry.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, hear my Deep Delving now, the breaking of ore from the rock. Then stand with me as a band under this Hearth, and carry my name on.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Tontec, stay in the igloo by the warmth. I go for food now and I bring it to your hands. You fed me once; I pay it back.
